q_1_1_directa: The National Regulatory Authority (NRA) for clinical trials is the State Agency for Medicines and Health Technologies (AGEMED).
q_1_1_ampliada: The NRA is responsible for authorizing clinical studies involving substances used in medicines, medical devices, and investigational products conducted within national territory. The Ministry of Health and Sports, through this directorate, must ensure that subjects' rights are respected and that ethical and legal principles are complied with, including Good Clinical Practice (GCP).
q_1_1_fuente: Norma para Estudios Clínicos (NEC), Chapter 20, Article 77; Manual de Inspección de Buenas Prácticas Clínicas, Definitions.
q_1_2_directa: The main regulations include the Constitución Política del Estado Plurinacional de Bolivia, the Declaration of Helsinki, the Ley del Medicamento (Ley N° 1737), its implementing regulation (Decreto Supremo Nº 25235), and the Norma para Estudios Clínicos (NEC).
q_1_2_ampliada: Biomedical research must be framed within ethical and human-rights principles, with those contained in the Declaration of Helsinki being fundamental. The Constitution guarantees the development of science and research for the general interest. Ley N° 1737 establishes the general framework for the regulation of medicines for human use, including research, and its implementing regulation (DS Nº 25235) sets out the operational provisions for its implementation. The Norma para Estudios Clínicos (NEC) is the specific regulatory instrument for conducting clinical trials in the country.
q_1_2_fuente: Constitución Política del Estado, Article 103, paragraph I; Norma para Estudios Clínicos (NEC), Chapter 4, Article 6; Chapter 5, Article 11; Ley del Medicamento N° 1737, Article 2; Reglamento a la Ley del Medicamento DS Nº 25235.
q_1_3_directa: The main regulation specific to clinical trials is the Norma para Estudios Clínicos (NEC), which incorporates the Good Clinical Practice (GCP) standards issued by the International Council for Harmonisation (ICH) and the World Health Organization (WHO).
q_1_3_ampliada: The Norma para Estudios Clínicos (NEC), issued through Resolución Ministerial Nº 0834 of November 23, 2004, sets out ethical, legal, and procedural guidelines, including protocol development, informed consent, clinical trial authorization, and the composition of committees. Compliance with GCP standards, the international standard for the design, conduct, and documentation of clinical trials, is mandatory.
q_1_3_fuente: Norma para Estudios Clínicos (NEC), Chapter 13, Article 49; Manual de Inspección de Buenas Prácticas Clínicas, LEGAL BASIS; Norma para Estudios Clínicos (NEC), Chapter 39, Article 131.
q_1_4_directa: Yes, all clinical studies must obtain, before they may be conducted, a prior favorable opinion from the corresponding Clinical Research Ethics Committee (CEIC).
q_1_4_ampliada: The CEIC's opinion is a fundamental requirement and must weigh the methodological, ethical, and legal aspects of the proposed protocol, as well as the risk-benefit balance for subjects. This approval is necessary to ensure that the research is conducted in a manner that respects individuals' fundamental rights and the ethical principles of the Declaration of Helsinki.
q_1_4_fuente: Norma para Estudios Clínicos (NEC), Chapter 4, Article 5; Chapter 37, Article 119.
q_1_5_directa: Yes, authorization by the Directorate of Medicines and Health Technology (AGEMED) to conduct clinical studies requires a prior opinion from an accredited Clinical Research Ethics Committee (CEIC).
q_1_5_ampliada: The clinical study authorization application submitted to the NRA must be accompanied, among other documents, by the duly accredited CEIC's report on the conduct and follow-up of the study (Annex 4). The ethical review process therefore precedes, or takes place simultaneously with, the formal regulatory submission for administrative authorization.
q_1_5_fuente: Norma para Estudios Clínicos (NEC), Chapter 20, Article 77; Chapter 20, Article 79, item c).
q_1_6_directa: Yes. Clinical Research Ethics Committees must be accredited by the Minister of Health and Sports through a Ministerial Resolution.
q_1_6_ampliada: The regulation establishes that the Ministry of Health and Sports coordinates and sets the criteria for CEIC accreditation. This accreditation is formalized through a specific Ministerial Resolution and must be renewed periodically according to time frames set by the Ministry. Renewal confirms that the committee meets the minimum requirements for composition and resources.
q_1_6_fuente: Norma para Estudios Clínicos (NEC), Title III, Chapter 34, Articles 111 and 113.
q_1_7_directa: No publicly searchable registry of Clinical Research Ethics Committees (CEICs) in Bolivia has been found to exist. Regulations provide that each CEIC is accredited before the Ministry of Health and Sports through a Ministerial Resolution, an administrative act of which AGEMED is aware; however, at the time of this review, no official list published online or public directory of accredited committees was identified.
q_1_7_ampliada: Although the regulation does not mention a real-time, publicly accessible list, it does establish a formal administrative registry with the authority. The accreditation process produces a Ministerial Resolution held by the Directorate of Medicines and Health Technology, which coordinates accreditation and thereby centralizes information on the committees authorized to operate in the country.
q_1_7_fuente: Norma para Estudios Clínicos (NEC), Title III, Chapter 34, Articles 111 and 112.
q_1_8_directa: Yes. All clinical studies conducted in Bolivia involving medicines or investigational clinical trial products (including radiopharmaceuticals, blood products, allergens, and medicinal plants) must be authorized by the NRA. Studies with no therapeutic benefit for subjects must be conducted at sites specifically authorized by AGEMED.
q_1_8_ampliada: The regulation establishes two administrative authorization regimes: prior (express) authorization, and an abbreviated procedure (tacit approval if there are no objections within 60 days). Prior authorization is mandatory for the first clinical study of a substance classified as a Clinical Trial Investigational Product (PEI), the first study of a new therapeutic indication, and clinical studies with no therapeutic benefit (except bioequivalence studies with generics).
q_1_8_fuente: Norma para Estudios Clínicos (NEC), Chapter 1, Article 1; Chapter 20, Article 77; Chapter 21, Article 82; Chapter 33, Article 108.
q_2_1_directa: Yes. The sponsor is defined as the individual, group of individuals, company, institution, or organization — including academic institutions — with legal representation in the country and duly registered in the corresponding public registries, that is responsible for the initiation, management, completion, and financing of a clinical trial.
q_2_1_ampliada: The sponsor is the entity responsible for managing the clinical trial, from its initiation through to its completion and financing. Current regulations require the sponsor to have legal representation in Bolivia and to be registered in the corresponding public registries. This definition covers both natural persons and legal entities, including academic institutions, broadening the range of entities that may act as sponsors of clinical research in the country.
q_2_1_fuente: Norma para Estudios Clínicos (NEC), Chapter 10, Article 41; Manual de Inspección de Buenas Prácticas Clínicas, Definitions.
q_2_2_directa: Yes, the sponsor must have legal representation in the country and be duly registered. If the sponsor is located outside Bolivia, it must identify and provide the details of an authorized representative in Bolivia.
q_2_2_ampliada: This requirement ensures that a local legal entity assumes responsibility before the Bolivian authorities for the initiation, management, completion, and financing of the clinical trial, facilitating communications and compliance with regulatory and ethical obligations.
q_2_2_fuente: Manual de Inspección de Buenas Prácticas Clínicas, Definitions; Norma para Estudios Clínicos (NEC), ANNEX 1, III. GENERAL INFORMATION, D.
q_2_3_directa: Yes. The sponsor must establish Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs); select investigators and ensure their qualifications; supply the investigational medicine in accordance with Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP); appoint a monitor; and provide financial compensation and legal coverage to subjects in the event of injury or death related to the study.
q_2_3_ampliada: The sponsor is obligated to guarantee the integrity of the study and the protection of subjects. This includes ensuring that the investigational product (IP) meets quality standards (GMP) and that documentation (protocols, reports, publications) is properly managed and communicated to the NRA and the CEIC, particularly with regard to serious and unexpected adverse reactions.
q_2_3_fuente: Norma para Estudios Clínicos (NEC), Chapter 10, Article 42 (items a, c, f, g, j).
q_2_4_directa: Yes. The sponsor may engage a Contract Research Organization (CRO) to carry out one or more of its obligations. Agreements or contracts with the CRO must be documented, and these essential documents must be kept on file.
q_2_4_ampliada: Although the sponsor may delegate specific tasks to a CRO, the Manual de Inspección de Buenas Prácticas Clínicas emphasizes that the sponsor remains ultimately responsible for the quality and compliance of the trial. The manual applies to everyone involved, including CROs, and during inspection the list of study activities is reviewed together with the parties responsible for each (activities carried out by the sponsor, the CRO, etc.).
q_2_4_fuente: Manual de Inspección de Buenas Prácticas Clínicas, Definitions; Manual de Inspección de Buenas Prácticas Clínicas, SCOPE; Manual de Inspección de Buenas Prácticas Clínicas, ANNEX 1.
q_2_5_directa: Yes. Approval from the site's management is required, and for studies with no therapeutic purpose, express authorization of the site by the health authority is also required.
q_2_5_ampliada: For every study, the sponsor must select sites with adequate resources and obtain written approval from the medical site's management. In addition, for studies with no particular therapeutic benefit (Phase I or bioequivalence studies), the research site must request and obtain specific authorization from the Directorate of Medicines and Health Technology to conduct the study.
q_2_5_fuente: Norma para Estudios Clínicos (NEC), Articles 42 and 79, and Chapter 33, Articles 108 and 109.
q_2_6_directa: Yes. The Principal Investigator must be a qualified healthcare professional responsible for the team at the research site. Their competence must be documented, evidencing formal training in Good Clinical Practice (GCP), knowledge of the protocol, and training in the handling of biological samples.
q_2_6_ampliada: The Principal Investigator must be a qualified healthcare professional who takes responsibility for the research team at the site. Their qualifications must be documented through an up-to-date curriculum vitae, and they must provide evidence of formal training in Good Clinical Practice (GCP), detailed knowledge of the study protocol, and specific training in the handling of biological samples. In addition, they must formally document the delegation of functions to team members through a written record. These training and delegation records are essential documents that must be kept on file and available for inspection by AGEMED.
q_2_6_fuente: Norma para Estudios Clínicos (NEC), Chapter 12, Article 46; Manual de Inspección de Buenas Prácticas Clínicas, GCP Principles; Manual de Inspección de Buenas Prácticas Clínicas, ANNEX 1.
q_2_7_directa: Yes. Bolivian regulations mandate that the sponsor provide financial compensation to subjects in the event of injury or death related to the clinical trial. This requires taking out professional civil liability insurance covering potential adverse reactions, with the policy to be submitted as part of the initial file before both the CEIC and AGEMED.
q_2_7_ampliada: The CEIC must verify the provision for compensation and treatment that will be offered to subjects in the event of injury or death attributable to the clinical study. Taking out insurance is a requirement that must be documented from the initial submission of the file to the Ethics Committee and the regulatory authority. In studies with no particular therapeutic benefit, subjects must receive agreed compensation for the inconvenience suffered, although the amount may not be so high as to constitute undue inducement to participate for financial reasons.
q_2_7_fuente: Norma para Estudios Clínicos (NEC), Chapter 9, Article 34; Chapter 9, Article 35; Chapter 7, Article 24; Chapter 37, Article 119 (item d).
q_3_1_directa: Yes. The authorization application, addressed to the NRA (AGEMED), must be accompanied by the study Protocol (Annex 1), the Investigator's Commitment (Annex 3), the accredited CEIC's Report (Annex 4), and the Site Management's Approval (Annex 5).
q_3_1_ampliada: The protocol must be a detailed document, drafted in Spanish, setting out the rationale, objectives, design, methodology, statistical analysis, description of the treatment, and the ethical and practical aspects of the study. The authorization application is submitted using the template specified in Annex 2A.
q_3_1_fuente: Norma para Estudios Clínicos (NEC), Chapter 20, Article 79 (items a-d); Chapter 5, Articles 9 and 10.
q_3_2_directa: This is not addressed by the regulations or by information available on official websites.
q_3_2_ampliada: Regulations establish that the authorization application is formally submitted to the Directorate of Medicines and Health Technology (AGEMED). However, it is not specified whether a mandatory electronic platform exists (such as a portal or digital system) or whether submission must be exclusively in physical or printed format. Documents such as the Manual para Registro Sanitario mention submission at a filing window, suggesting a paper-based process.
q_3_2_fuente: Norma para Estudios Clínicos (NEC), Chapter 20, Article 78; Manual para Registro Sanitario, 3.1.3.
q_3_3_directa: Yes. Under the prior-authorization regime, AGEMED has sixty calendar days from receipt of the application to carry out checks or raise observations. If additional information is requested, it has thirty calendar days from receipt of the last submission to grant or deny authorization.
q_3_3_ampliada: These time frames apply to studies requiring express authorization, such as the first study with a Clinical Trial Investigational Product (PEI) or the first study with a new indication. Under the abbreviated-procedure regime, if there is no express resolution within sixty calendar days, the application may be deemed approved (tacit approval).
q_3_3_fuente: Norma para Estudios Clínicos (NEC), Chapter 21, Article 83; Chapter 22, Article 85.
q_3_4_directa: Yes, costs must be covered. Although the general clinical trial regulations establish that financial matters are set out in a contract between the site and the sponsor, payment is required for certain regulatory procedures, such as the Critical Evaluation of Efficacy and Safety (Form 019) for new molecular entities.
q_3_4_ampliada: Classification as a new molecular entity before the National Pharmacological Commission (CFN) requires payment, in accordance with Resolución Ministerial No. 0265 of 2018. In addition, Good Clinical Practice (GCP) inspections carried out before, during, or after the trial are subject to the sponsor covering travel and per diem expenses, pending approval of the corresponding fee schedule.
q_3_4_fuente: Instructivo para la Evaluación Farmacológica, Table N° 1; Manual de Inspección de Buenas Prácticas Clínicas, Chapter III, c); Norma para Estudios Clínicos (NEC), Chapter 16, Article 58; Manual para Registro Sanitario, 3.2.3.
q_3_5_directa: This is not addressed by the regulations or by information available on official websites.
q_3_5_ampliada: Regulations set out detailed obligations for filing study documentation (protocol, reports, case report forms, etc.) for both the sponsor and the investigator, and require that results be communicated to the scientific community (publications). However, current regulations do not establish an obligation to register the clinical trial in a national or international public registry before it begins.
q_3_5_fuente: Norma para Estudios Clínicos (NEC), Chapter 17; Chapter 18.
q_3_6_directa: Not specified in official regulations.
q_3_6_ampliada: Although Bolivian regulations adopt international ethical and regulatory principles such as the Declaration of Helsinki and ICH Good Clinical Practice (GCP) standards, and AGEMED is a member of the Pan American Network for Drug Regulatory Harmonization (PANDRH, known regionally as the PARF Network), no formal mechanism is described for expedited recognition or validation of approvals from foreign regulatory or ethics authorities. AGEMED authorization and a prior opinion from an accredited CEIC are mandatory, local requirements. Nonetheless, AGEMED may take into account evaluations or approvals from other agencies when reviewing a protocol or product, particularly where these come from a regional or international reference authority (for example, ICH or PAHO member countries). This recognition is technical rather than legal in nature: it supports the dossier but does not replace the national review process.
q_3_6_fuente: Norma para Estudios Clínicos (NEC), Chapter 13, Article 49; Norma para Estudios Clínicos (NEC), Chapter 20, Article 77. Manual para Registro Sanitario, 1.5.
q_3_7_directa: The sequential process first requires classification of the Clinical Trial Investigational Product (if applicable), followed by a favorable opinion from the CEIC, institutional approval, and finally administrative authorization from the NRA (AGEMED).
q_3_7_ampliada:
The steps are as follows:

New Molecular Entity Classification before the National Pharmacological Commission (CFN): For investigational products that constitute new molecular entities, the sponsor must submit a specific efficacy and safety dossier (using Form 019) for evaluation and classification by the CFN, a technical advisory body of AGEMED. This process is a prerequisite for the clinical trial authorization application and involves payment of a specific fee.

IP Classification: If the product is new, the sponsor must request classification as a Clinical Trial Investigational Product (PEI) before the National Pharmacological Commission/AGEMED.

Ethical Review: The CEIC evaluates the protocol, informed consent, the risk-benefit balance, and insurance/compensation arrangements, issuing the CEIC Report (Annex 4).

PI Commitment: The Principal Investigator (PI) signs the Investigator's Commitment (Annex 3).

Institutional Approval: The site's management (hospital or administration) certifies its approval of the contract and the conduct of the study (Annex 5).

Application and Submission: The sponsor (or legal representative) submits the Clinical Study Application (Annex 2A) together with the Protocol and the signed supporting documents (PI Commitment, CEIC Report, Site Approval) to AGEMED.

Regulatory Review: AGEMED carries out the administrative and regulatory evaluation (subject to 60- or 30-day time frames, depending on the regime).

NRA Authorization: AGEMED issues express authorization, which may include authorization to import the IP.

Study Start: The investigator may begin recruitment and treatment.
q_3_7_fuente: Norma para Estudios Clínicos (NEC), Chapter 34, Article 111; Chapter 20, Articles 77 and 79; Chapter 4, Article 5; Chapter 28, Article 98.
q_4_1_directa: Yes. Investigational medicines must be manufactured, handled, and stored in accordance with Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) standards. The label must allow for the accurate identification of the product in accordance with the national clinical trial regulation. AGEMED verifies that the label template complies with current regulatory provisions.
q_4_1_ampliada: The Norma para Estudios Clínicos (NEC) sets out, in Articles 53 and 54, the specific labeling requirements for investigational products. The label must include the protocol code, the number of units and pharmaceutical form, the route of administration, the batch number, the expiry date, any special storage conditions, and the wording "Sample for clinical research use." The name and address of the manufacturing entity and of the Technical Director must also be included, except in double-blind studies, where this information is kept in a separate document. AGEMED verifies compliance with these provisions as part of the study authorization.
q_4_1_fuente: Norma para Estudios Clínicos (NEC), Chapter 14, Articles 53 and 54.
q_4_2_directa: Yes. The sponsor is required to guarantee that, when supplying the medicine to be investigated, Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) standards have been complied with.
q_4_2_ampliada: The sponsor is responsible for the manufacture and proper quality of samples in accordance with GMP standards. If samples are imported, the sponsor must certify their quality through appropriate verifications and controls. Documentation evidencing the identity, purity, and dosage of investigational products must also be kept on file.
q_4_2_fuente: Norma para Estudios Clínicos (NEC), Chapter 10, Article 42 (item f); Chapter 14, Article 52.
q_4_3_directa: No. The import of medicines and devices intended for clinical trials is subject to specific customs and health controls. A Customs Clearance Authorization Certificate (CDA) must be obtained from AGEMED, requiring submission of Form 011 and other technical requirements.
q_4_3_ampliada: Bolivian regulations do not provide for automatic granting of import authorization together with clinical trial authorization. The sponsor must independently obtain a Customs Clearance Authorization Certificate (CDA) from AGEMED, submitting Form 011 together with the required technical documentation. This procedure is subject to strict customs and health controls. The sponsor is required to keep a record of products imported for the study. However, the NEC provides, in Article 98, that this authorization may be granted jointly with the clinical trial authorization, with the same period of validity.
q_4_3_fuente: Manual de Inspección de Buenas Prácticas Clínicas; Formularios para Ensayos Clínicos. Norma para Estudios Clínicos (NEC), Chapter 28, Article 98.
q_5_1_directa: Yes. The investigator and the sponsor must report any suspected Serious Adverse Reaction (causing death, life-threatening, or requiring hospitalization) to AGEMED within a strict 24-hour time frame. The official pharmacovigilance forms used are FORM 020 for adverse drug reactions and FORM 030 for Events Supposedly Attributable to Vaccination or Immunization (ESAVI) in vaccines.
q_5_1_ampliada: Bolivia's safety reporting system establishes specific time frames: suspected serious adverse reactions must be reported to AGEMED within 24 hours of becoming known. The standardized forms of Bolivia's pharmacovigilance system are used for this purpose: FORM 020, for reporting adverse drug reactions, and FORM 030, specific to Events Supposedly Attributable to Vaccination or Immunization (ESAVI). The sponsor is also required to report any safety information suggesting a significant risk to human subjects, including relevant preclinical findings.
q_5_1_fuente: Norma para Estudios Clínicos (NEC), Chapter 12, Article 48 (item h); Chapter 15, Article 57; Formularios para Ensayos Clínicos; Circular MS/AGEMED/CR/100/2020.
q_5_2_directa: Yes. If the study lasts longer than one year, the sponsor must submit an annual progress report to the Directorate of Medicines and Health Technology (AGEMED). In addition, the Principal Investigator must submit a report every six months if the study lasts longer than 12 months.
q_5_2_ampliada: These periodic reports are essential for follow-up and oversight by the NRA. Progress reports must be kept on file. In addition, the sponsor is responsible for preparing the study's final or partial reports and communicating them to AGEMED.
q_5_2_fuente: Norma para Estudios Clínicos (NEC), Chapter 27, Article 97; Chapter 12, Article 48 (item i).
q_5_3_directa: Yes, periodic reports must be submitted. The investigator must submit a report every six months for studies lasting longer than 12 months, and the sponsor must send an annual report to AGEMED if the study lasts longer than one year.
q_5_3_ampliada: These progress reports (partial or interim) allow the NRA and the CEIC to follow up on the clinical study from its start until the final report is received. If the research does not reach completion, the sponsor must submit a report including the data obtained up to the point of suspension and the reasons for it.
q_5_3_fuente: Norma para Estudios Clínicos (NEC), Chapter 12, Article 48 (item i); Chapter 27, Article 97; Chapter 37, Article 119 (item f).
q_5_4_directa: Yes. Any substantial modification to a previously authorized protocol requires documented evaluation and approval from the Clinical Research Ethics Committee (CEIC) as well as authorization from AGEMED before it may be implemented. Increasing the number of sites also requires AGEMED authorization.
q_5_4_ampliada: Protocol amendments are classified according to their impact on participant safety and the scientific integrity of the study. Substantial modifications — defined as those involving an increased risk to participating subjects or a significant change in the study design — require full CEIC evaluation and formal AGEMED authorization before they may be implemented. To request authorization for an amendment, the template specified in Annex 2B is used, duly justifying the proposed modification. Non-substantial modifications must likewise be notified to the relevant authorities.
q_5_4_fuente: Norma para Estudios Clínicos (NEC), Chapter 25, Articles 91 and 92; Chapter 25, Article 94.
q_5_5_directa: Yes. Continued administration of study products after the trial has ended, while the medicine is not yet authorized for those conditions of use, is governed by the rules established for compassionate use.
q_5_5_ampliada: Compassionate use is defined as the use, in individual patients and outside the context of a clinical study, of clinical trial investigational products, or of pharmaceutical products for indications or conditions of use other than those authorized, when the physician considers it essential under their sole responsibility. This requires the patient's written informed consent, a justifying clinical report, and AGEMED authorization for each specific case.
q_5_5_fuente: Norma para Estudios Clínicos (NEC), Chapter 29, Article 99; Chapter 19, Articles 74 and 75.
q_6_1_directa: No, there is no specific personal data protection regulation.
q_6_1_ampliada: Clinical trial regulations require that the confidentiality of records that could identify subjects be protected, respecting privacy and confidentiality rules in accordance with the relevant legislative requirements. All parties involved (sponsor, investigator) are required to maintain the strictest confidentiality so as not to violate the personal or family privacy of participating subjects. However, no specific framework law on personal data protection exists beyond these general requirements.
q_6_1_fuente: Manual de Inspección de Buenas Prácticas Clínicas, GCP Principles; Norma para Estudios Clínicos (NEC), Chapter 7, Article 30; Chapter 12, Article 48 (item g).
q_6_2_directa: Yes. The Manual para Registro Sanitario de Vacunas (Resolución Ministerial N° 0512) exists, regulating procedures and requirements for vaccines, including clinical aspects, listing, relisting, and batch release. FORM 030 (the "Green Card") is also used to report Events Supposedly Attributable to Vaccination or Immunization (ESAVI).
q_6_2_ampliada: Vaccines are included as special medicines subject to the Ley del Medicamento and the Norma para Estudios Clínicos. While a "Manual para Registro Sanitario de Vacunas" exists, there is no specific regulation or guideline for conducting clinical trials with vaccines beyond the general application of the Norma para Estudios Clínicos.
q_6_2_fuente: Manual para Registro Sanitario de Vacunas (RM N° 0512), Chapters I and II; Norma para Estudios Clínicos (NEC), Chapter 1, Article 1; Ley del Medicamento N° 1737, Article 2.
q_6_3_directa: Not specified in official regulations.
q_6_3_ampliada: Regulations focus on the requirement that the laboratory have validated procedures for the collection, processing, handling, and transport of samples, and that staff receive specific training. There is no dedicated regulatory framework governing the collection, use (e.g., biobanks), or transfer (import/export) of biological samples for research.
q_6_3_fuente: Manual de Inspección de Buenas Prácticas Clínicas, Chapter V, 2.i); Manual de Inspección de Buenas Prácticas Clínicas, ANNEX 1.
q_6_4_directa: Yes, specific regulations or guidelines exist for Herbal Products (Annex 10 of the NEC), Medical Devices (Manual de Inspección de Buenas Prácticas Clínicas), and Resolución Administrativa N° 006, which approves requirements for clinical trials with mechanical ventilators. In addition, artisanal traditional natural products are governed by Resolución Administrativa Regulatoria N° 30/2025, which approves the Basic List of Medicinal Plants for Traditional Use – 2nd Edition (102 species and 2 products of other origin), within the framework of Ley N° 459 de Medicina Tradicional Ancestral Boliviana.
q_6_4_ampliada: The Norma para Estudios Clínicos includes a "Guide for Preparing a Clinical Trial Protocol for Herbal Products." The Manual de Inspección de Buenas Prácticas Clínicas applies to both medicines and medical devices. In addition, Resolución Administrativa N° 006 of February 2021 sets out the requirements and the four stages of clinical trials with mechanical ventilators (functional methods/testing, preclinical animal study, Phase I clinical study, Phase II clinical study). While the Ley del Medicamento N° 1737 includes medical devices within its scope, detailed regulatory development, such as the Norma para Estudios Clínicos, is primarily focused on medicines. The regulation of clinical trials with medical devices relies on the application of these general principles and on specific regulations issued for certain types of devices (e.g., Resolución Administrativa N° 006/2021 for mechanical ventilators), rather than on a body of regulation dedicated exclusively to them.
q_6_4_fuente: Norma para Estudios Clínicos (NEC), ANNEX 10; Manual de Inspección de Buenas Prácticas Clínicas, SCOPE; Resolución Administrativa N° 006, Art. FIRST; Resolución Administrativa N° 006, ANNEX 1; I Guía para la Evaluación de Tecnologías Sanitarias - ETESA; Resolución Administrativa Regulatoria N° 30/2025, Arts. FIRST and SECOND; Ley N° 459 de Medicina Tradicional Ancestral Boliviana, Art. 28.

q_1_1_directa: The National Regulatory Authority (NRA) for drug clinical trials in Brazil is the Agência Nacional de Vigilância Sanitária (National Health Surveillance Agency, ANVISA), responsible for their oversight, approval, and inspection.
q_1_1_ampliada: ANVISA is an independent administrative agency linked to the Ministry of Health. Its institutional purpose, defined in Article 6 of Lei nº 9.782/1999, is to promote the protection of public health through the sanitary control of products and services, including medicines. Article 7 of the same law sets out its powers: establishing standards, granting product registrations, and authorizing the operation of pharmaceutical companies. Its authority over clinical trials derives from its mandate to oversee drug development prior to registration.
q_1_1_fuente: Lei nº 9.782, de 26 de janeiro de 1999, Art. 6 and Art. 7.
q_1_2_directa: The main regulations governing research ethics are Lei nº 14.874/2024 and its implementing regulation, Decreto nº 12.651/2025. During the transition period, the standards of the Conselho Nacional de Saúde (National Health Council, CNS), such as Resolução CNS nº 466/2012, remain in force insofar as they do not contradict the new framework.
q_1_2_ampliada: Decreto nº 12.651/2025 implemented Lei nº 14.874/2024 and established the new National Research Ethics System. This system is made up of the National Research Ethics Authority (the new central authority, Inaep) and the CEPs. Article 39 of the decree sets out a key transitional rule: until the new authority publishes its own standards, CNS standards (including Res. 466/2012) remain in force to the extent they do not contradict the new law and decree. Sponsors must therefore comply with the principles and structures of the new legislation while continuing to follow the operational procedures (for example, the use of Plataforma Brasil) of the previous system, until these are replaced.
q_1_2_fuente: Lei nº 14.874, de 28 de maio de 2024. Decreto nº 12.651, de 7 de outubro de 2025, Art. 1, 3, and 39. Resolução CNS nº 466, de 12 de dezembro de 2012.
q_1_3_directa: The main regulation governing ANVISA's authorization of drug clinical trials is Resolução da Diretoria Colegiada - RDC nº 945, de 29 de novembro de 2024.
q_1_3_ampliada: RDC nº 945/2024 sets out the guidelines and procedures for conducting clinical trials in Brazil for drug registration purposes. This resolution modernizes the regulatory framework and aligns it with international ICH guidelines and with the new Lei nº 14.874/2024. It defines the submission process for the Dossiê de Desenvolvimento Clínico de Medicamento (Drug Clinical Development Dossier, DDCM) and the Dossiê Específico de Ensaio Clínico (Clinical Trial-Specific Dossier, DEEC), the review time frames, the safety requirements, and the sponsor's obligations. This regulation revokes and replaces RDC nº 9/2015, the previous regulatory framework.
q_1_3_fuente: Resolução da Diretoria Colegiada - RDC nº 945, de 29 de novembro de 2024, Art. 1.
q_1_4_directa: Yes, prior ethical approval is required before a clinical trial may begin. In multicenter studies, this approval is issued by a single CEP — preferably the one linked to the coordinating site — and is valid for all participating sites, without the need for additional ethical review by local CEPs.
q_1_4_ampliada:
All research involving human subjects must undergo prior ethical review by the CEPs, in accordance with Lei nº 14.874 and Resolução da Diretoria Colegiada - RDC nº 945, de 29 de novembro de 2024. A clinical trial may only begin after obtaining approval from both the CEP and ANVISA.

In multicenter studies, Despacho Inaep Nº 3, de 29 de maio de 2026 establishes the single ethical opinion regime: a single CEP — preferably the one linked to the coordinating site — conducts the ethical review and issues the opinion, which is fully valid and effective for all sites participating in the approved protocol. The CEPs of participating sites do not carry out a new ethical review on the merits; their residual role consists of receiving complaints from participants, reporting serious adverse events occurring locally, forwarding that information to the CEP responsible for the single opinion, and monitoring compliance with the approved protocol at their institution.

The participating institution retains its autonomy to decide whether to join the study by issuing an institutional Letter of Agreement, but that decision is administrative/institutional in nature and does not involve a re-evaluation of the protocol's ethical merits. A refusal to agree based on disagreement with the ethical merits of an already-approved protocol constitutes a legal defect due to overreach of authority.
q_1_4_fuente: Lei nº 14.874, de 28 de maio de 2024, Art. 14, § 7; Resolução da Diretoria Colegiada - RDC nº 945, de 29 de novembro de 2024; Decreto nº 12.651, de 7 de outubro de 2025, Art. 27; Despacho Inaep Nº 3, de 29 de maio de 2026, Sections I, II, III, and IV.
q_1_5_directa: No. Applications may be submitted in parallel to the regulatory authority (ANVISA) and the ethics committee (CEP).
q_1_5_ampliada: RDC nº 945/2024 establishes that submissions to the ethics body (CEP/CONEP) and to the regulatory body (ANVISA) are independent and may occur simultaneously. However, the clinical trial may only begin after obtaining approval from both entities.
q_1_5_fuente: Resolução da Diretoria Colegiada - RDC nº 945, de 29 de novembro de 2024, Art. 8, § 1 and § 2.
q_1_6_directa: Yes, an accreditation and certification system exists for Research Ethics Committees (CEPs). The Instância Nacional de Ética em Pesquisa (National Research Ethics Authority, Inaep) is the body responsible for this function; while the new structure is being consolidated, CONEP continues to transitionally exercise the functions of registering, auditing, and accrediting CEPs.
q_1_6_ampliada:
Lei nº 14.874 establishes that the Instância Nacional de Ética em Pesquisa (Inaep) certifies CEPs according to the level of risk of the projects they are authorized to review (low, moderate, or high). For accreditation, institutional committees must demonstrate adequate infrastructure, continuous operation, and multidisciplinary composition including representatives of research participants. While the new institutional structure is being consolidated, Decreto nº 12.651/2025 provides that CONEP retains the authority to register, audit, and accredit CEPs.

Inaep also issues binding regulatory guidance aimed at standardizing how CEPs operate throughout the system (Sinep). Despacho Inaep Nº 3, de 29 de maio de 2026, for example, establishes governance guidelines for the single ethical opinion regime in multicenter research, with precise instructions on the decision-making authority of the coordinating CEP and the residual role of local CEPs. CEPs that fail to comply with these guidelines may be subject to administrative and disciplinary measures by Inaep.
q_1_6_fuente: Lei nº 14.874, de 28 de maio de 2024, Art. 8 and 9; Resolução CNS nº 466, de 12 de dezembro de 2012, Item IX.6; Decreto nº 12.651, de 7 de outubro de 2025; Despacho Inaep Nº 3, de 29 de maio de 2026, Section VI.
q_1_7_directa: Yes, a centralized, public registry of Research Ethics Committees (CEPs) exists in the country. By regulatory mandate, committees must also keep publicly available a list of their members and their respective professional qualifications.
q_1_7_ampliada: Brazil's ethics system uses Plataforma Brasil as the unified national database for documenting the network of CEPs and processing protocols for research involving human subjects. Lei nº 14.874 assigns the central authority the function of registering, auditing, and, where appropriate, revoking the accreditation of or suspending institutional committees. This oversight through public registries and digital tools provides transparency, promotes social oversight, and confirms that committees operate in accordance with the law and GCP guidelines.
q_1_7_fuente: Resolução CNS nº 466, de 12 de dezembro de 2012; Lei nº 14.874, de 28 de maio de 2024, Art. 9.
q_1_8_directa: Yes. ANVISA is responsible for approving DDCMs (Dossiê de Desenvolvimento Clínico de Medicamento / Drug Clinical Development Dossier) for medicines intended for registration. Phase IV trials and non-interventional clinical research are excluded and only require ethical approval.
q_1_8_ampliada: ANVISA's scope of application is defined in RDC nº 945/2024. Article 2 specifies that the regulation applies to clinical trials conducted for registration purposes. Article 3 excludes Phase IV trials and non-interventional research, which only require approval from the ethics system. Trials with advanced therapy products (DDCTA) are governed by RDC nº 506/2021.
q_1_8_fuente: Resolução da Diretoria Colegiada - RDC nº 945, de 29 de novembro de 2024, Art. 2 and Art. 3. Resolução da Diretoria Colegiada - RDC nº 506, de 27 de maio de 2021.
q_2_1_directa: Yes, the regulation defines the sponsor as a natural or legal person, whether public or private, that supports the research through financing, infrastructure, human resources, or institutional support for the initiation and management of the study.
q_2_1_ampliada: The regulation, grounded in Lei nº 14.874 and RDC nº 945, clarifies that the sponsor's responsibility for the integrity and quality of the trial data cannot be delegated, even if it subcontracts functions. A key point clarified by Decreto nº 12.651 is that funding agencies, funding associations, and support foundations are not considered sponsors for purposes of assigning legal liability for the conduct of the trial, since they act solely as financial support providers.
q_2_1_fuente: Lei nº 14.874, de 28 de maio de 2024, Art. 2, item XXXI. Decreto nº 12.651, de 7 de outubro de 2025, Art. 36.
q_2_2_directa: It is not a requirement for the sponsor to have a legal domicile in Brazil, but if it has no presence in the country, it must delegate representation before the health authority to a locally established Contract Research Organization (CRO/ORPC).
q_2_2_ampliada: RDC nº 945 provides that submissions of primary filings such as the DDCM may be made by a CRO — legally known in Brazil as a Clinical Research Representative Organization (Organização Representativa de Pesquisa Clínica, ORPC) — only when the primary sponsor has no parent company or branch in Brazilian territory. In that case, the CRO assumes, together with the foreign sponsor, the obligations and follow-up of the trial before ANVISA, ensuring responsible legal representation at the national level.
q_2_2_fuente: Resolução da Diretoria Colegiada - RDC nº 945, de 29 de novembro de 2024, Art. 24, § 3.
q_2_3_directa: Yes, the sponsor must comply with Good Clinical Practice (GCP) requirements. It must implement and maintain a Quality Assurance and Quality Control (QA/QC) system supported by standard operating procedures and risk-based management.
q_2_3_ampliada: National regulations and the adoption of the ICH E6(R2) guideline require the sponsor to ensure that the study is designed, conducted, monitored, and reported in a manner that preserves data integrity and participant well-being. The sponsor is responsible for operations, for entering into formal agreements, for providing insurance, for supplying investigational products under GMP conditions, and for allowing direct access for institutional audits and official inspections by ANVISA and the Ethics System. Its quality system must cover all stages of clinical data processing.
q_2_3_fuente: Lei nº 14.874, de 28 de maio de 2024, Art. 26 (Sponsor Responsibilities); Resolução da Diretoria Colegiada - RDC nº 945, de 29 de novembro de 2024, Art. 13 and 14 (GCP Obligations); Guia de Boas Práticas Clínicas ICH E6(R2) - Versão em Português, Section 5.
q_2_4_directa: Yes, the transfer of any trial activity or function to a CRO or Clinical Research Representative Organization (ORPC) must be specified and documented in writing through contracts signed by both parties.
q_2_4_ampliada: Under Lei nº 14.874 and RDC nº 945, even if the sponsor transfers operational duties for regulatory submissions or monitoring to a locally registered Brazilian CRO, it retains ultimate, non-delegable responsibility for the quality and integrity of the research data. The subcontracted CRO, in turn, must implement its own Quality Assurance (QA/QC) systems aligned with international guidelines to ensure the trial's auditability.
q_2_4_fuente: Resolução da Diretoria Colegiada - RDC nº 945, de 29 de novembro de 2024, Art. 19 (Transfer of Functions and Ultimate Responsibility). Lei nº 14.874, de 28 de maio de 2024, Art. 26, item V (Management Responsibility).
q_2_5_directa: Yes. Clinical trial sites must be legally constituted organizations with adequate facilities for conducting the protocol. The sponsor is responsible for selecting institutions that guarantee safety and compliance with current regulations.
q_2_5_ampliada: Regulations require the clinical trial site to be licensed and to have physical infrastructure, equipment, instruments, and human resources adequate for the protocol and the participant population. In accordance with the adoption of the ICH E6(R2) guideline in RDC nº 945, the sponsor must select implementing institutions by evaluating the site's qualifications for conducting and overseeing the study. In addition, written agreements ensuring direct access to source data must be formalized. The site is also required to allow monitoring, audits, and regulatory inspections by ANVISA and the CEP/CONEP System.
q_2_5_fuente: Resolução da Diretoria Colegiada - RDC nº 945, de 29 de novembro de 2024, Art. 18; Lei nº 14.874, de 28 de maio de 2024, Art. 26.
q_2_6_directa: Yes. The investigator must have and demonstrate the technical qualifications, education, and experience necessary to take responsibility for properly conducting the research. The sponsor has a legal obligation to verify and document these competencies before the study begins.
q_2_6_ampliada: It is the investigator's responsibility to conduct the clinical trial in accordance with the agreed protocol, Good Clinical Practice (GCP), and the country's regulatory and ethical requirements. The Research Ethics Committee (CEP) and ANVISA assess the investigator's qualifications based on their up-to-date curriculum vitae (CV) and other professional documentation submitted by the sponsor. The principal investigator must sign a statement of responsibility committing to oversee the trial, report adverse events within the established time frames, and ensure comprehensive care for participants. Their technical responsibility for protecting the rights, safety, and well-being of participants enrolled at their site cannot be delegated.
q_2_6_fuente: Lei nº 14.874, de 28 de maio de 2024, Art. 12, 27; Resolução da Diretoria Colegiada - RDC nº 945, de 29 de novembro de 2024, Art. 15.
q_2_7_directa: Yes. The sponsor is responsible for providing comprehensive healthcare and financial compensation to participants who suffer harm, injury, or complications arising from their participation in the study. It must also provide insurance or indemnification for the investigator and the institution against claims arising from the trial.
q_2_7_ampliada: Lei nº 14.874 establishes as a fundamental, non-waivable right of the participant the right to receive compensation and immediate, complete healthcare in response to any adverse event related to the research. RDC nº 945 reinforces that the sponsor bears all costs of procedures, diagnostics, and hospitalizations to address such harm. As for participation, national legislation prohibits granting payment or financial advantages as an incentive to enroll. It does, however, permit and require reimbursement of basic logistical expenses, such as transportation and meals, for both the participant and their legal representative during trial visits.
q_2_7_fuente: Lei nº 14.874, de 28 de maio de 2024, Art. 23. Resolução da Diretoria Colegiada - RDC nº 945, de 29 de novembro de 2024, Art. 9. Resolução CNS nº 466, de 12 de dezembro de 2012, Items II.21, IV.3.g, and V.7.
q_3_1_directa: Yes. The initial submission to the regulatory authority (ANVISA) consists of the Drug Clinical Development Dossier (DDCM). This primary filing must be accompanied by at least one Clinical Trial-Specific Dossier (DEEC).
q_3_1_ampliada: The regulation details the documentation required for the regulatory submission. The DDCM must contain fundamental components such as the Investigational Drug Development Plan (PDME), the Investigator's Brochure (IB), and the Investigational Medicinal Product Dossier (DPI/IMPD) containing quality data. Each DEEC submitted as an independent filing must include the Clinical Trial Submission Form (FAEC), the complete clinical protocol aligned with the ICH E6(R2) guideline, and proof of trial registration in a public database recognized by WHO or the ICMJE.
q_3_1_fuente: Resolução da Diretoria Colegiada - RDC nº 945, de 29 de novembro de 2024, Art. 28.
q_3_2_directa: Yes. Submission of the Drug Clinical Development Dossier (DDCM) and of all related filings (DEEC, secondary filings, and amendments) must be entirely electronic. This centralized process is carried out through the Solicita electronic filing system, administered by ANVISA.
q_3_2_ampliada: The regulation specifies that electronic documentation must be in a dynamic format allowing text searches and data copying, and must contain bookmarks and hyperlinks to facilitate reviewer navigation. Although the main official documentation must be submitted in Portuguese, ANVISA accepts technical annexes, such as the Investigator's Brochure, in English or Spanish, and reserves the right to require a free or certified translation. Submission through the Solicita system is conditional on the prior generation and payment of the Guia de Recolhimento da União (Federal Payment Slip, GRU) corresponding to the applicable fees.
q_3_2_fuente: Resolução da Diretoria Colegiada - RDC nº 945, de 29 de novembro de 2024, Art. 25 (Electronic Submission Requirement and Document Format). Sistema Solicita.
q_3_3_directa: Yes. The regulatory authority (ANVISA) has an official time frame of 90 business days to evaluate and issue a ruling on primary filings (DDCM and DEEC). If no response is given within this time frame, the trial is released to begin operations in Brazil, provided it already has the corresponding ethical approval.
q_3_3_ampliada: National legislation establishes this 90-business-day limit, after which tacit approval applies (release upon expiry of the time frame). During technical evaluation, ANVISA may issue a single technical request, which suspends the official time frame; from that point, the sponsor has 30 business days to remedy the deficiencies and submit its responses. Expedited time frames also exist for priority filings and rare diseases, under which DDCM evaluations or preliminary rulings may be reduced to intervals of between 30 and 45 days.
q_3_3_fuente: Resolução da Diretoria Colegiada - RDC nº 945, de 29 de novembro de 2024. Art. 52.
q_3_4_directa: Yes, official fees must be paid. The sponsor is responsible for paying the Taxa de Fiscalização de Vigilância Sanitária (Health Surveillance Inspection Fee, TFVS) required to submit any clinical trial application (DDCM and DEEC) to ANVISA.
q_3_4_ampliada: Under current regulations, the TFVS fee is paid through the Guia de Recolhimento da União (Federal Payment Slip, GRU), which is generated electronically in the Solicita system. Regulatory filings are entered and processed for technical review only after ANVISA receives confirmation of full payment of the fee. The fee amount is determined according to the size of the applicant company and the subject code of the filing, and varies according to the ministerial fee schedules, which are updated periodically.
q_3_4_fuente: Resolução da Diretoria Colegiada - RDC nº 857, de 21 de maio de 2024, Art. 1 and 2 (Procedures for Charging the TFVS). Portaria Interministerial nº 45, de 27 de janeiro de 2017 (Update of TFVS Amounts).
q_3_5_directa: Yes, public registration of the clinical trial is mandatory. The study must be registered in a primary registry of the WHO International Clinical Trials Registry Platform (ICTRP) network, or in another international registry recognized by the ICMJE.
q_3_5_ampliada: Brazilian regulations require the sponsor to include official proof of this public registration in the DEEC submission to ANVISA. Within the country, use of the Registro Brasileiro de Ensaios Clínicos (Brazilian Clinical Trials Registry, ReBEC) is promoted, which functions as a certified primary registry within the WHO network. When proof of registration is not available at the time the initial DEEC is submitted, the regulation allows it to be provided later, together with the Formulário de Notificação de Início de Ensaio Clínico no Brasil.
q_3_5_fuente: Resolução da Diretoria Colegiada - RDC nº 945, de 29 de novembro de 2024, Art. 28, VI, (g) and (h).
q_3_6_directa: Yes. ANVISA has a legal mechanism known as the "optimized review procedure," based on regulatory reliance practices. This mechanism uses, as an exclusive or complementary technical reference, the documentary assessments issued by a recognized Equivalent Foreign Regulatory Authority (AREE).
q_3_6_ampliada: The reliance procedure applies to both primary filings (DDCM and DEEC) and secondary filings (protocol amendments and substantial modifications to the investigational product). The high-surveillance authorities officially designated as equivalent (AREEs) by Instrução Normativa nº 338 include the EMA, FDA, Health Canada, Swissmedic, the MHRA, and Japan's PMDA. In addition, RDC nº 997/2025 organizes this mechanism by providing that applications relying on this mechanism enter a "specific review queue." Eligibility for reliance does not, by itself, presuppose prioritization of the filing: within that queue, applications are reviewed in chronological order of submission, although priority is maintained for those already qualifying under the priority categories (RDC nº 1.001/2025 or RDC nº 205).
q_3_6_fuente: RDC nº 945, de 29 de novembro de 2024, Arts. 6, 7, and 48 to 51. Instrução Normativa - IN nº 338, de 29 de novembro de 2024, Arts. 1 and 2 + Annex I. Resolução da Diretoria Colegiada - RDC nº 997, de 7 de novembro de 2025, Arts. 4 and 5.
q_3_7_directa: Drug clinical trials require approval through two concurrent pathways, the regulatory (ANVISA) and the ethical (CEP/CONEP); both are required before the study may begin.
q_3_7_ampliada:
The sequential order of steps is as follows:

Regulatory preparation (sponsor/CRO): preparation of the Clinical Development Dossier (DDCM), including the Investigational Drug Development Plan (PDME), the Investigator's Brochure (IB), and the Investigational Medicinal Product Dossier (IMPD/DPI).

Ethical preparation (principal investigator): preparation of the research protocol and the Informed Consent Form (TCLE).

Parallel submission (sponsor/PI):

Regulatory pathway: the sponsor/CRO submits the initial DDCM through the Sistema Solicita, which must contain at least one Clinical Trial-Specific Dossier (DEEC).

Ethical pathway: the Principal Investigator (PI) submits the research project to the CEP through Plataforma Brasil.

Filing of the application (sponsor): the Guia de Recolhimento da União (GRU) is generated in the Solicita system, the Taxa de Fiscalização de Vigilância Sanitária (TFVS) is paid, and the DDCM/DEEC filing is automatically registered.

Ethical review (CEP/CONEP): the CEP reviews the ethical documentation (30-business-day time frame), may request clarifications, and records the approval.

Regulatory review (ANVISA): ANVISA carries out the technical review of the DDCM/DEEC (90-business-day time frame) and may issue a technical request for additional information, which suspends the time frame.

Final authorization (ANVISA): ANVISA publishes the DDCM/DEEC approval in the Diário Oficial da União (Federal Official Gazette, DOU).

Study start: the drug clinical trial may only begin after obtaining both ethical (CEP) and regulatory (ANVISA) approval.
q_3_7_fuente: Compilation of: Resolução da Diretoria Colegiada - RDC nº 945, de 29 de novembro de 2024 (Art. 8 for parallel submission; Art. 25 for electronic filing; Art. 28 for dossier content); Lei nº 14.874, de 28 de maio de 2024 (Ethical Framework); Resolução da Diretoria Colegiada - RDC nº 857, de 21 de maio de 2024 (Fees); Sistema Solicita and Plataforma Brasil.
q_4_1_directa: Yes, the regulation establishes labeling requirements for the investigational product (IP). Labeling must comply with Instrução Normativa nº 136/2022 and reflect the product's experimental nature. It must include, in capital letters, warnings such as "USO EXCLUSIVO EM PESQUISA CLÍNICA" [FOR CLINICAL RESEARCH USE ONLY].
q_4_1_ampliada: Primary and secondary labeling must include the name, address, and telephone number of the sponsor, the CRO, or the principal investigator, to allow rapid contact in emergencies. It must also include the pharmaceutical form, route of administration, batch code, and clinical trial reference number. Storage instructions and the period of use (expiry date) are essential traceability elements. Although the regulation allows other languages to be included on the label, the text information must be written in Portuguese. Finally, in blinded studies, labeling must be coded to protect blinding while also providing mechanisms for rapid identification in a medical emergency.
q_4_1_fuente: Instrução Normativa - IN nº 136, de 30 de março de 2022, Arts. 2, 3, and 4 + Annex I. Resolução da Diretoria Colegiada - RDC nº 945, de 29 de novembro de 2024, Arts. 37, 38, and 39.
q_4_2_directa: Yes, formal proof of compliance with Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) is required. This must be included and documented as part of the Investigational Medicinal Product Dossier (DPI/IMPD) when submitting the clinical trial to the authority.
q_4_2_ampliada: The sponsor must provide ANVISA with a formal statement that both the investigational product and the placebo are manufactured in accordance with the GMP standards of RDC nº 658. If the product already holds an official good manufacturing practice certificate or an equivalent international document, it must be attached to the initial DDCM. In addition to documentary review, ANVISA may conduct on-site manufacturing inspections to verify process controls, excipient quality, and packaging materials. As a member of the PIC/S scheme, Brazil aligns these certification and audit standards with harmonized international practices.
q_4_2_fuente: Resolução da Diretoria Colegiada - RDC nº 945, de 29 de novembro de 2024, Art. 28, V. Resolução da Diretoria Colegiada - RDC nº 658, de 30 de março de 2022. Instrução Normativa - IN nº 136, de 30 de março de 2022.
q_4_3_directa: Yes, the regulation allows the import of the investigational product to be arranged in advance. However, its distribution to clinical sites and its administration to participants are prohibited until the trial's final approval has been obtained.
q_4_3_ampliada: The regulatory framework allows ANVISA to issue an Import Document (DI) within 30 business days of the filing's submission, authorizing the physical entry of supplies into the country before the final technical ruling. To take advantage of this provision, the sponsor must attach a declaration of commitment assuming responsibility and financial risk for this advance import. The imported product must remain blocked and held in an area under the sponsor's logistical control, and may only be released and distributed to the pharmacies of research sites after the DDCM approval is officially published in the Diário Oficial da União. If ANVISA rejects the study, the sponsor must notify the export destination or the audited destruction of the products within a maximum of 60 business days.
q_4_3_fuente: Resolução da Diretoria Colegiada - RDC nº 945, de 29 de novembro de 2024, Art. 82 and Art. 83.
q_5_1_directa: Yes, regulations stipulate centralized electronic channels and strict time frames for reporting safety events. The sponsor must report Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reactions (SUSARs) to the health authority exclusively through the official VigiMed digital system.
q_5_1_ampliada: National legislation requires investigators to inform the sponsor of all Serious Adverse Events (SAEs) at their site within a maximum of 24 hours. The sponsor must then assess causality and report fatal or life-threatening SUSARs to ANVISA within a limit of seven calendar days. If the unexpected event does not pose an immediate risk of death, the reporting time frame is extended to fifteen calendar days. On the ethical pathway, investigators must record SAEs on a consolidated basis with the CEP/CONEP System through the reporting function of Plataforma Brasil. These reports allow the Investigator's Brochure to be updated and the trial's risk-benefit balance to be reassessed.
q_5_1_fuente: Resolução da Diretoria Colegiada - RDC nº 945, de 29 de novembro de 2024, Art. 71, § 1 and § 2 (SUSAR Reporting Time Frames) and Art. 72. Sistema VigiMed.
q_5_2_directa: Yes, submission of Development Safety Update Reports (DSURs) is required. These pharmacovigilance documents must be submitted annually to ANVISA and continued until the product's clinical development in the country is complete.
q_5_2_ampliada: The sponsor must submit DSURs through the Solicita electronic system, as a secondary filing linked to the main record (DDCM). The deadline for this submission is a maximum of 60 calendar days from the anniversary of the DDCM's initial approval date, or according to the global international development calendar. The format and technical content of these reports must follow the ICH E2F Harmonised Tripartite Guideline. Through this document, the sponsor consolidates the product's global safety profile and assesses trends in new adverse reactions and changes in the toxicological profile. Any safety-related change considered non-substantial is grouped together and reported to the authority within this same annual report.
q_5_2_fuente: Resolução da Diretoria Colegiada - RDC nº 945, de 29 de novembro de 2024. ICH E2F Guideline: Development Safety Update Report.
q_5_3_directa: Yes, the sponsor must submit periodic reports on the study's operational progress. Specifically, it must submit a periodic progress report, known as the annual clinical trial protocol monitoring report.
q_5_3_ampliada: The regulation establishes that this periodic report must be submitted to ANVISA electronically, as a secondary filing linked to the Clinical Trial-Specific Dossier (DEEC) record. The follow-up document must be generated and filed on the portal within 60 calendar days after the first anniversary of the trial's start date in Brazil. Its content must present tabulated information regarding the Brazilian sites actively participating in the research. The minimum data required includes local and global recruitment status, a record of protocol deviations, and a count of serious adverse events per participant. This allows the regulatory agency to track performance and clinical compliance throughout the trial in the country.
q_5_3_fuente: Resolução da Diretoria Colegiada - RDC nº 945, de 29 de novembro de 2024, Art. 67 and 68.
q_5_4_directa: Yes, the regulation establishes that only amendments categorized as "substantial" require formal submission and prior authorization. Minor, administrative changes may be implemented routinely and reported together in subsequent annual reports.
q_5_4_ampliada: An amendment is classified as substantial when it introduces changes that may affect the safety and the physical or mental integrity of participants. Operational changes that compromise the robustness and statistical reliability of the research data also reach that status. On the regulatory pathway, the sponsor submits the substantial amendment to ANVISA in a change-control document, linked as a secondary filing to the primary DEEC. On the ethics side, national legislation provides that any deviation altering the risk-benefit relationship must be evaluated and ruled on by the CEP before it takes effect at clinical visits. The only exception allowing a modification to be applied without this prior approval is an acute medical emergency, when the action is indispensable to eliminate an imminent danger to the study participant.
q_5_4_fuente: Lei nº 14.874, de 28 de maio de 2024, Art. 2, item XVIII (Definition of Substantial Amendment) and Art. 17 (Ethical Review Requirement for Substantial Amendments). Resolução da Diretoria Colegiada - RDC nº 945, de 29 de novembro de 2024, Art. 6, item XXIII (Definition of Amendment).
q_5_5_directa: Yes, Brazilian legislation imposes obligations on the sponsor regarding post-trial access to its investigational products. It requires a plan to be structured, before the trial begins, to guarantee the continued supply of the beneficial intervention once the protocol concludes.
q_5_5_ampliada: Under the new Ethics Law, the sponsor and the principal investigator must jointly submit and justify a post-trial supply plan to the relevant Ethics Committee. This free, continued provision of the experimental product is considered a fundamental right and must be implemented once it is confirmed to be the best available treatment, with a favorable risk-benefit ratio. The aim is to protect participants so that their treatment regimens are not interrupted for financial reasons once the study concludes. However, the regulation provides for exceptions under which sponsor-funded supply may be suspended temporarily or permanently. Such interruptions are permitted, upon justified grounds submitted to the committee, if an equivalent therapeutic alternative guaranteed under the public health system (SUS) becomes available, or if more than five years have passed since the medicine became commercially available in the country.
q_5_5_fuente: Lei nº 14.874, de 28 de maio de 2024, Chapter VI, Art. 37-39 (Post-Trial Access Regulation). Resolução CNS nº 466, de 12 de dezembro de 2012, Item III.2.n.
q_6_1_directa: Yes. The Lei Geral de Proteção de Dados (General Data Protection Law, LGPD, Lei nº 13.709) is the binding national regulation governing the processing of information in clinical trials. It acts as a subsidiary framework to health legislation, aiming to preserve volunteers' anonymity.
q_6_1_ampliada: The LGPD establishes the principles of minimization, adequacy, and transparency required for any data processing carried out for scientific purposes. Under this framework, the sponsor assumes the non-delegable role of "data controller," responsible for ensuring that records are collected and protected under anonymization standards. The law classifies biomedical data, medical records, and genetic profiles as "sensitive personal data." Although express, separate consent is generally required for this type of information, the law allows it to be dispensed with only when research conducted by an accredited body makes it indispensable. Finally, any breach or leak affecting participants' privacy must be documented and reported to the Autoridade Nacional de Proteção de Dados (National Data Protection Authority, ANPD) and to the data subject within three business days of becoming known.
q_6_1_fuente: Lei nº 13.709, de 14 de agosto de 2018 (LGPD). Lei nº 14.874, de 28 de maio de 2024, Art. 40, item VI and Art. 52 (Explicit Reference to the Application of the LGPD to Guarantee Privacy and Confidentiality).
q_6_2_directa: Yes, regulations address vaccine clinical trials through special guidelines oriented toward public health. Although they operate under ANVISA's general regulatory framework, recent 2024 and 2025 regulations establish prioritized ethical approval pathways for these developments.
q_6_2_ampliada: Studies on new investigational vaccine formulations are governed by RDC nº 945. ANVISA has processed these technologies as filings of high public interest, particularly following global health emergencies. Decreto nº 12.651 institutionalizes this priority treatment in ethical review: its Article 29 establishes that research of strategic interest to the Sistema Único de Saúde (Unified Health System, SUS), including vaccines of interest to the National Immunization Program, receives priority in ethical review. In such cases, the CEP must issue its ruling within a maximum of fifteen business days of receiving the request, extendable for justified technical complexity.
q_6_2_fuente: Resolução da Diretoria Colegiada - RDC nº 945, de 29 de novembro de 2024. Decreto nº 12.651, de 7 de outubro de 2025, Art. 29.
q_6_3_directa: Yes, Brazil regulates the handling of samples through a set of resolutions and administrative orders (portarias). Regulations from the Ministry of Health and the National Health Council establish the requirements for the collection, import, and ethical handling of biorepositories and biobanks.
q_6_3_ampliada: To move and share stored samples, legislation requires registration and signature of a Termo de Transferência de Material Biológico (Material Transfer Agreement, TTMB), pre-approved by the CEP system. Transport of this material, whether cross-border or local, is governed by RDC nº 504, which requires precise labeling according to global infectious-risk categories (Categories A, B, or minimal risk). When sample collection is oriented toward human genetics, Resolução CNS nº 340 establishes specific ethical standards: it requires informed consent to clearly explain the objectives of the genomic analysis to avoid information asymmetries. In addition, upon relevant clinical or hereditary findings, the principal investigator assumes responsibility for providing access to free genetic counseling for the individual assessed.
q_6_3_fuente: Resolução do Conselho Nacional de Saúde - CNS nº 441, de 12 de maio de 2011 (Storage of Biological Material), Arts. 3, 4, 5, and 6. Portaria do Ministério da Saúde - MS nº 2.201, de 14 de setembro de 2011 (Guidelines for Biobanks and Biorepositories), Arts. 5, 6, 8, 11, and 13. Resolução da Diretoria Colegiada - RDC nº 504, de 27 de maio de 2021 (Transport of Biological Material), Arts. 7, 8, 12, and 18 + Annex I. Resolução do Conselho Nacional de Saúde - CNS nº 340, de 8 de julho de 2004 (Research in Human Genetics), Arts. 4, 5, 7, and 9.
q_6_4_directa: Yes, the regulatory framework has specific pathways to expedite particular clinical situations. Expedited regulations exist for trials of orphan drugs, advanced cell therapies, and pediatric or strategic developments.
q_6_4_ampliada: RDC nº 1.001/2025 (in force since January 15, 2026, which revoked the previous RDC nº 204/2017) establishes the priority classification of applications, including prior agreement for clinical trials, and covers innovative medicines for the pediatric population and research into neglected, emerging or re-emerging diseases, and public health emergencies. RDC nº 205 condenses technical review time frames and requires ANVISA to issue a ruling within a 30-day limit for protocols introducing therapies for ultra-rare diseases. Trials involving in vivo or ex vivo manipulation of tissues, genes, and advanced cell therapy products are subject to the rulings set out in RDC nº 506. Finally, RDC nº 997/2025 organizes a specific review queue for filings relying on the regulatory reliance mechanism; within that queue, filings are reviewed in chronological order of submission, and priority is maintained for those already qualifying under the priority categories of RDC nº 1.001/2025 or RDC nº 205.
q_6_4_fuente: Resolução da Diretoria Colegiada - RDC nº 1.001, de 11 de dezembro de 2025 (Priority Classification; revokes RDC nº 204/2017). Resolução da Diretoria Colegiada - RDC nº 205, de 28 de dezembro de 2017 (Procedure for Rare Diseases). Resolução da Diretoria Colegiada - RDC nº 506, de 27 de maio de 2021 (Regulation of Advanced Therapy Products). Resolução da Diretoria Colegiada - RDC nº 997, de 7 de novembro de 2025.

q_1_1_directa: The National Regulatory Authority (NRA) for clinical trials is the Instituto de Salud Pública de Chile (Chilean Public Health Institute, ISP), which has the authority to provisionally authorize the use of medicines.
q_1_1_ampliada: The ISP is the entity responsible for the sanitary control of pharmaceutical products and medical devices throughout the national territory, and is responsible for granting special authorization for the provisional use of these products in scientific research involving human subjects. The ISP is also empowered to oversee compliance with research protocols and Good Clinical Practice (GCP).
q_1_1_fuente: Ley N° 20.724, Article 96; Decreto Supremo N° 114, de 2010, del Ministerio de Salud., Article 7; Ley N° 20.850, Article 111 A, 111 D.
q_1_2_directa: The regulations governing health research include Ley N° 20.120 (on scientific research involving human subjects and their genome), Decreto N° 114 (implementing regulation of Ley N° 20.120), and Ley N° 20.584 (on patients' rights and duties). In addition, Resolución Exenta N° 173 of 2024, which approves the "General Considerations Guide for Clinical Studies" (Guía de consideraciones generales para estudios clínicos), must be taken into account. This regulation aligns Chile with the international ICH E8(R1) guideline.
q_1_2_ampliada: These laws establish the fundamental framework for research, limiting freedom of research to respect for the essential rights and freedoms arising from human nature. Ley N° 20.584 guarantees the right to give or withhold consent to undergo any procedure or treatment related to healthcare, including the choice of whether to take part in any type of biomedical scientific research.
q_1_2_fuente: Ley N° 20.120, sobre la investigación científica en el ser humano, su genoma, y prohíbe la clonación humana., Article 1, 2; Decreto Supremo N° 114, de 2010, del Ministerio de Salud., Article 1, 2; Ley 20.584, Article 14, 21; Resolución Exenta N° 173, de 2024, del ISP.
q_1_3_directa: Authorization is governed by Ley N° 20.724 (Código Sanitario [Sanitary Code], Book IV), Decreto Supremo N° 3 of 2010 (Pharmaceutical Products Regulation), and Ley N° 20.850, which introduced specific regulations on special authorization for the provisional use of pharmaceutical products and medical devices for research.
q_1_3_ampliada: Ley 20.850 introduced Title V into Book Four of the Código Sanitario, creating the special authorization for provisional use for research purposes, granted by the ISP for pharmaceutical products and medical devices. This authorization is required even if the product already holds sanitary registration, where it is being given a use other than the one registered.
q_1_3_fuente: Ley N° 20.724, Article 99; Decreto Supremo N° 3, de 2011, del Ministerio de Salud., Article 21, 23; Ley N° 20.850, Article 111 A.
q_1_4_directa: Yes, review and a favorable opinion from an accredited Scientific Ethics Committee (CEC) is mandatory.
q_1_4_ampliada: A favorable CEC opinion is an essential precondition for scientific research and must precede the application for provisional authorization of the pharmaceutical product. The CEC's role is to protect the rights, safety, and well-being of research subjects.
q_1_4_fuente: Ley N° 20.120, sobre la investigación científica en el ser humano, su genoma, y prohíbe la clonación humana., Article 10; Decreto Supremo N° 114, de 2010, del Ministerio de Salud., Article 7, 10.
q_1_5_directa: Yes, the CEC must approve the protocol before the application for provisional use of a pharmaceutical product is submitted to the Instituto de Salud Pública (ISP).
q_1_5_ampliada: To apply for special authorization for the provisional use of pharmaceutical products or medical devices for research purposes, the applicant must submit the research protocol with the prior approval required under Article 10 of Ley N° 20.120. Without this favorable opinion, the research protocol cannot be carried out for unregistered medicines or for new uses of registered medicines.
q_1_5_fuente: Ley N° 20.724, Article 99; Decreto Supremo N° 3, de 2011, del Ministerio de Salud., Article 23; Ley N° 20.850, Article 111 A.
q_1_6_directa: Yes. The health authority responsible for granting accreditation to Scientific Ethics Committees (CECs) is the Secretaría Regional Ministerial de Salud (Regional Ministerial Secretariat of Health, SEREMI de Salud).
q_1_6_ampliada: The regulation establishes that all scientific research involving human subjects may only be conducted if it has a favorable opinion from a Scientific Ethics Committee accredited by the Health Authority. These committees are collegiate bodies responsible for protecting the rights, safety, and well-being of research subjects, and their accreditation is an indispensable requirement for their valid operation. The Ministerio de Salud (Ministry of Health, MINSAL) defines the guidelines, technical standards, and guides for this accreditation and oversight process, but its application and the accreditation ruling fall directly to the SEREMI de Salud corresponding to the region where the committee operates.
q_1_6_fuente: Decreto Supremo N° 114, de 2010, del Ministerio de Salud, Article 10 and Article 16.
q_1_7_directa: Yes. The regulation establishes the creation of a public, national registry system for accredited Scientific Ethics Committees (CECs).
q_1_7_ampliada: The Ministry of Health, through its Ministerial Bioethics Office and with the advice of the Comisión Ministerial de Ética de la Investigación en Salud (Ministerial Commission on Health Research Ethics, CMEIS), decided to carry out an accreditation process that includes establishing a public registry system for Scientific Ethics Committees (CEI/CEC), applicable to committees constituted at both public institutions and private entities. To implement this, the Ministry of Health issued specific procedures aimed at establishing this national accreditation registry.
q_1_7_fuente: Norma Técnica N° 0151 (Resolución Exenta N° 403 de 2013 del Ministerio de Salud), Standard 1; and Circular B1/2015 del Ministerio de Salud.
q_1_8_directa: Yes. All scientific research involving human subjects that uses a pharmaceutical product or medical device must be authorized by the Instituto de Salud Pública (ISP). This applies both to products without sanitary registration in the country and to registered products that will be used for a research purpose other than the one authorized (e.g., a new indication, dose, or population).
q_1_8_ampliada: Ley 20.850 introduced into the Código Sanitario the obligation to obtain "special authorization for provisional use for research purposes" from the ISP. This authorization is the central regulatory control mechanism for clinical trials with products. The regulation is clear that even a product already marketed in Chile requires this special authorization if the clinical trial proposes a use outside the conditions of its current sanitary registration.
q_2_1_directa: Yes. The sponsor is the individual, institution, company, or organization with a domicile and legal representative in Chile that takes the initiative to conduct, manage, and/or fund biomedical research, assuming full responsibility for it. The legal definition also includes anyone who, without directly funding the research, takes concrete action to secure funding for it.
q_2_1_ampliada: The full definition in Decreto 114 establishes that the sponsor assumes the legal responsibilities of the research. The regulation also extends this role to entities that actively manage the procurement of funds, even if they are not the direct source of those funds. This ensures there is always a legally responsible entity in the country for the conduct of the study and the protection of subjects.
q_2_1_fuente: Decreto Supremo N° 114, de 2010, del Ministerio de Salud., Article 8 (item b); Decreto Supremo N° 30, de 2012, N° 3 A), N° 10.
q_2_2_directa: Yes, it is an explicit requirement that the sponsor of biomedical research have a domicile and legal representative in Chile.
q_2_2_ampliada: This requirement ensures that the sponsor is accountable under the current legal system. The definition of sponsor clearly establishes this condition.
