q_2_2_fuente: Decreto Supremo N° 114, de 2010, del Ministerio de Salud., Article 8 (item b); Decreto Supremo N° 30, de 2012, N° 3 A), N° 10.
q_2_3_directa: Yes. The sponsor must have a domicile and legal representative in Chile and must adopt the necessary safeguards through insurance and guarantees expressly stated in the protocol to protect against adverse events that cause harm to individuals.
q_2_3_ampliada: The sponsor is responsible for selecting qualified investigators with professional qualifications appropriate to the complexity of the study. The protocol must include a description of these necessary safeguards.
q_2_3_fuente: Decreto Supremo N° 114, de 2010, del Ministerio de Salud., Article 25; Decreto Supremo N° 30, de 2012, N° 10.
q_2_4_directa: Yes. The Contract Research Organization (OIC; CRO) is a natural or legal person engaged as an intermediary by the sponsor to carry out one or more of its clinical trial-related duties and functions.
q_2_4_ampliada: The CRO carries out tasks on behalf of the sponsor. Authorization for the research at the site takes effect once the terms have been agreed between the sponsor (and its intermediary, where applicable) and the investigators.
q_2_4_fuente: Decreto Supremo N° 114, de 2010, del Ministerio de Salud., Article 8 (item b.1); Decreto Supremo N° 30, de 2012, N° 3 B), N° 4.
q_2_5_directa: Yes. Sites where clinical research is conducted must have authorization from the health authority (ISP or SEREMI de Salud), their respective accreditation, and the express approval of the institution's director.
q_2_5_ampliada: Regulations establish that every site where research on pharmaceutical products and medical devices in human subjects is conducted must be accredited by the Instituto de Salud Pública (ISP), in accordance with the corresponding standards, requirements, and procedures. The establishment and operation of these clinical research sites are authorized by the Secretaría Regional Ministerial (SEREMI) de Salud and the ISP, with the latter responsible for overseeing compliance with Good Clinical Practice and current regulations at their facilities.
q_2_5_fuente: Ley N° 20.850, Article 111 D; Decreto Supremo N° 114, de 2010, del Ministerio de Salud., Article 10 bis.
q_2_6_directa: Yes. The research must be conducted by qualified professionals, selected by the sponsor based on their qualifications and experience.
q_2_6_ampliada: The sponsor has an obligation to select qualified investigators with adequate academic training, experience, and training to take responsibility for the study. The investigator must know and comply with Good Clinical Practice guidelines and maintain a list of qualified persons to whom significant study tasks are delegated.
q_2_6_fuente: Decreto Supremo N° 114, de 2010, del Ministerio de Salud. Article 25; Resolución Exenta N° 460, de 2015, del ISP, Item 3.1.
q_2_7_directa: Yes. It is the sponsor's responsibility to adopt the necessary safeguards, which must be set out in the protocol, through applicable insurance, guarantees, or other financial mechanisms to cover harm to individuals that may arise from adverse events, whether foreseeable or not.
q_2_7_ampliada: The sponsor, either directly or through its intermediary, must ensure that any applicable insurance and guarantees are expressly stated in the research protocol.
q_2_7_fuente: Decreto Supremo N° 114, de 2010, del Ministerio de Salud., Article 25; Decreto Supremo N° 30, de 2012, N° 10.
q_3_1_directa: Yes. Applications for the provisional use of a pharmaceutical product submitted to the ISP must be accompanied by the protocol approved by the ethics committee, the informed consent template, and an official certificate of Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) compliance from the producing country.
q_3_1_ampliada: The application for special authorization for provisional use (Ley 20.850) requires the research protocol with prior ethical approval, the informed consent template, the insurance policy, and any other supporting documentation required under the regulation.
q_3_1_fuente: Decreto Supremo N° 3, de 2011, del Ministerio de Salud., Article 23; Ley N° 20.850, Article 111 A, 111 F.
q_3_2_directa: Yes. There are two separate processes depending on the purpose of the application: (a) authorization of the clinical trial protocol, submitted to the Instituto de Salud Pública (ISP) together with the favorable opinion of the accredited Scientific Ethics Committee (CEC), in accordance with Resolución Exenta N° 5161/2016 of the ISP; and (b) authorization for the import and use of the investigational pharmaceutical product, requested — once the study authorization has been obtained — through the Customs Destination Certificate (CDA) and the Use and Disposal Authorization (UyD) at the Single Window for Foreign Trade, via the GICONA platform.
q_3_2_ampliada: Authorization of the clinical trial protocol is governed by Resolución Exenta N° 5161/2016 of the ISP and requires, among other supporting documents, the favorable opinion of an accredited CEC, the protocol, the investigator's brochure, product certifications, and the informed consent form. Only once the Resolución Exenta authorizing the study has been obtained can the applicant request the CDA and the Use and Disposal Authorization (UyD) for the imported product through the GICONA web platform. The import process requires attaching customs documentation, information on the destination warehouse, and transport conditions.
q_3_2_fuente: Resolución Exenta N° 5161, de 2016, del ISP; Instructivo al usuario para importaciones y exportaciones asociadas a Estudios Clínicos.
q_3_3_directa: Yes. The maximum legal time frame for the entire administrative authorization procedure is six (6) months, in accordance with Article 27 of Ley N° 19.880 on the Basis of Administrative Procedures, except in cases of fortuitous event or force majeure. Within that legal time frame there are partial deadlines: the Scientific Ethics Committee (CEC) must issue its opinion within 45 days (extendable by 20); the Institution Director's authorization must be issued within 20 business days of the CEC's and ISP's favorable evaluation; and the ISP has a maximum of 15 business days to authorize the Use and Disposal (UyD) of the imported product (Safety Period). The ISP also applies internal operating guidelines and performance targets that, in practice, shorten these time frames.
q_3_3_ampliada: The import process requires the ISP to set a "Safety Period" for the purpose of carrying out a documentary review, during which (a maximum of 15 business days) the goods may not be used in patients or distributed.
q_3_3_fuente: Ley N° 19.880 sobre Bases de los Procedimientos Administrativos, Article 27; Decreto Supremo N° 114, de 2010, del Ministerio de Salud, Article 10 bis, Article 18 (item 2); Instructivo al usuario para importaciones y exportaciones asociadas a Estudios Clínicos.
q_3_4_directa: Yes, procedures before the Instituto de Salud Pública (ISP), such as applications for sanitary registration (or provisional research authorization) and the evaluation of flow diagrams, are subject to payment of the corresponding fee.
q_3_4_ampliada: The sanitary registration application is submitted to the ISP after payment of the corresponding fee, and the same applies to the evaluation of flow diagrams and other procedures. UyD import procedures through GICONA also involve a payment step. Fees are updated on this website (https://www.ispch.gob.cl/productos-y-servicios/prestaciones/).
q_3_4_fuente: Decreto Supremo N° 3, de 2011, del Ministerio de Salud., Article 43, 92; Instructivo al usuario para importaciones y exportaciones asociadas a Estudios Clínicos.
q_3_5_directa: Yes, the Instituto de Salud Pública must keep a public registry of all scientific research involving human subjects with pharmaceutical products or medical devices authorized to be conducted in the country.
q_3_5_ampliada: This public registry must contain the information required by the regulation and is subject to the provisions of Ley N° 20.285 on Access to Public Information.
q_3_5_fuente: Ley N° 20.850, Article 111 A, 111 E.
q_3_6_directa: There is no formal, universal mechanism for recognizing foreign ethical or regulatory approvals for clinical trials that would exempt an applicant from the local process. However, the ISP may accept Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) accreditations from foreign manufacturing plants if the standards applied are declared equivalent by a resolution of the Ministry of Health.
q_3_6_ampliada: For provisional authorization, the law requires the submission of an official certificate of GMP compliance issued by the competent authority of the producing country.
q_3_6_fuente: Decreto Supremo N° 3, de 2011, del Ministerio de Salud., Article 23, 193; Decreto Supremo N° 114, de 2010, del Ministerio de Salud., Article 10; Decreto Supremo N° 30, de 2012, N° 4.
q_3_7_directa: The regulatory sequence prioritizes ethical approval, followed by authorization of product use by the NRA (ISP), and finally, the institution's authorization to conduct the study.
q_3_7_ampliada:
Sponsor (S): Develops the protocol, includes insurance and guarantees, and selects qualified investigators.

Sponsor/Investigator (I): Obtain the review and favorable opinion of the accredited Scientific Ethics Committee (CEC) (45 + 20-day time frame).

Sponsor/I: Submit the application for special authorization for provisional use of the pharmaceutical product/medical device to the ISP, attaching the approved protocol, informed consent, insurance policy, and GMP certificate.

ISP: Issues the Resolución Exenta authorizing the Clinical Study (provisional authorization).

Institution Director (ID): Grants express authorization to conduct the study on its premises (20-business-day time frame from the CEC's and ISP's favorable evaluation).

Sponsor/Importer: Processes the Customs Destination Certificate (CDA) with the SEREMI.

Sponsor/Importer: Requests Use and Disposal (UyD) authorization from the ISP (via GICONA).

ISP: Evaluates the imported product during the "Safety Period" (max. 15 business days) and authorizes Use and Disposal.

Investigator: Begins the study only once the CEC's dated, written approval and the ISP's authorization for the receipt and use of the product have been obtained.
q_3_7_fuente: Decreto Supremo N° 114, de 2010, del Ministerio de Salud., Article 10 bis, 18 (item 2), 25; Decreto Supremo N° 3, de 2011, del Ministerio de Salud., Article 23, 99; Ley N° 20.850, Article 111 A; Instructivo al usuario para importaciones y exportaciones asociadas a Estudios Clínicos.
q_4_1_directa: Yes. The pharmaceutical product's secondary packaging must be labeled in Spanish, with clear information and no advertising or promotional wording.
q_4_1_ampliada: Although the specific Good Clinical Practice (GCP) framework does not address the labeling of the investigational product in detail, Decreto 3 establishes that, generally, the labeling of pharmaceutical specialties must indicate, among other information, the specialty's name, pharmaceutical form, the name and address of the holder/manufacturer, the expiry date, and the ISP registration number.
q_4_1_fuente: Decreto Supremo N° 3, de 2011, del Ministerio de Salud., Article 74, 77.
q_4_2_directa: Yes, this is mandatory. Investigational pharmaceutical products must be manufactured, handled, and stored in accordance with Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) principles and guidelines.
q_4_2_ampliada: For the application for provisional use before the ISP, an official certificate issued by the competent authority of the producing country certifying GMP compliance must be attached. The ISP is empowered to verify GMP compliance at the manufacturing laboratory.
q_4_2_fuente: Decreto Supremo N° 3, de 2011, del Ministerio de Salud., Article 23, 29 (item 10.a.4), 175, 193.
q_4_3_directa: No. Trial approval (Resolución Exenta) is necessary, but import requires a Customs Destination Certificate (CDA), and final use is conditional on the Use and Disposal Authorization (UyD) issued by the ISP.
q_4_3_ampliada: Once the product clears customs, it is held under the consignee's responsibility and may not be used, consumed, sold, or disposed of in any way without the ISP's approval granting the UyD. The ISP may set a "safety period" to carry out sanitary controls before authorizing the UyD, which has a maximum time frame of 15 business days.
q_4_3_fuente: Decreto Supremo N° 3, de 2011, del Ministerio de Salud., Article 98, 99; Instructivo al usuario para importaciones y exportaciones asociadas a Estudios Clínicos.
q_5_1_directa: Yes. The sponsor or the CRO must report national Related, Unexpected Serious Adverse Events (EASRI) to the ISP through the GICONA platform. The deadline is 15 calendar days from becoming aware of the event, or 7 calendar days if the event causes death or is life-threatening to the subject.
q_5_1_ampliada: National Serious, Unexpected Adverse Drug Reactions (RAMSI) involving medicines that hold sanitary registration (comparators/concomitant medications) must be reported separately to the Pharmacovigilance Sub-department at cenimef@ispch.cl, within a maximum of 15 calendar days. International EASRI must be reported to estudiosclinicos@ispch.cl on a bimonthly basis.
q_5_1_fuente: Instructivo de Notificación de Eventos Adversos Serios Relacionados e Inesperados (EASRI), Reacciones Adversas al Medicamento Serias e Inesperadas (RAMSI) y de Reportes Periódicos de Seguridad (DSUR) en Ensayos Clínicos.; Resolución Exenta N° 441, de 2012, del ISP, item 1.5; Ley N° 20.850, Article 111 B.
q_5_2_directa: Yes, annual submission of Development Safety Update Reports (DSURs) is required.
q_5_2_ampliada: DSURs must be submitted annually from the date of authorization of the import/manufacture and use of the investigational product, and also at the end of the clinical trial. This report must include a list of national and international serious, related, and unexpected adverse events, and the sponsor's conclusion on the product's safety profile.
q_5_2_fuente: Instructivo de Notificación de Eventos Adversos Serios Relacionados e Inesperados (EASRI), Reacciones Adversas al Medicamento Serias e Inesperadas (RAMSI) y de Reportes Periódicos de Seguridad (DSUR) en Ensayos Clínicos.
q_5_3_directa: Yes. The principal investigator must periodically inform the Scientific Ethics Committee (CEC) and the ISP of the study's progress, at a frequency of at least once a year.
q_5_3_ampliada: The frequency of reports is set by the CEC according to each protocol. Minor protocol deviations, together with critical/very serious and major/serious deviations (previously reported via GICONA), must be included in the clinical trial's annual report.
q_5_3_fuente: Instructivo Notificación de Desviaciones de Ensayos Clínicos.
q_5_4_directa: Yes. Modifications or amendments to the protocol that affect the initial authorization must be reported and formally submitted to the Instituto de Salud Pública (ISP). Protocol deviations considered critical or serious must also be reported to the ISP promptly through the GICONA platform.
q_5_4_ampliada: Intentional amendments to the study plan must be justified, approved, and signed by the study director and kept together with the study plan. If a modification is necessary to eliminate an immediate hazard to the subject, it may be applied immediately, but must be reported to the CEC as soon as possible.
q_5_4_fuente: Ley N° 20.120, sobre la investigación científica en el ser humano, su genoma, y prohíbe la clonación humana., Article 11; Decreto Supremo N° 114, de 2010, del Ministerio de Salud., Article 14; Instructivo Notificación de Desviaciones de Ensayos Clínicos.; Principios de Buenas Prácticas de Laboratorio.
q_5_5_directa: Yes, there is an explicit legal obligation established in the Código Sanitario. Patients participating in clinical trials are entitled to continued, free-of-charge treatment once the study has concluded.
q_5_5_ampliada: The patient participating in a clinical trial has the right to have the holder of the special provisional-use authorization or, subsequently, the holder of the product's sanitary registration, provide continued treatment at no cost to the patient. This obligation remains in place for as long as the treatment's therapeutic benefit persists, in accordance with the relevant research protocol. This obligation applies to the holder of the sanitary registration, even if it was not the holder of the original provisional authorization.
q_5_5_fuente: Ley N° 20.850, Article 17; Ley N° 20.850, Article 111 C.
q_6_1_directa: Yes. The regime currently in force for personal data protection applicable to clinical trials is governed by Ley N° 19.628 on the Protection of Privacy. Ley N° 21.719, published on December 13, 2024, comprehensively reforms this framework and takes full effect on December 1, 2026, introducing a new Personal Data Protection Agency, strengthened data subject rights, and a significantly stricter penalty regime.
q_6_1_ampliada:
Information contained in medical records and human genome data are considered sensitive data, the processing of which requires the express consent of the data subject. Genome data that could allow individuals to be identified must be encrypted for storage and transmission, in accordance with Ley N° 20.120 and its implementing regulation. Ley N° 20.850 amended Ley N° 20.584 to authorize the Instituto de Salud Pública (ISP) to access medical records in the exercise of its regulatory powers.

As of now, Ley N° 19.628 is in force, which recognizes health-related data as sensitive data and establishes general requirements for consent, quality, and security. Ley N° 21.719, published on December 13, 2024, comprehensively amends this framework and takes full effect on December 1, 2026, aligning Chile with international standards such as the European GDPR.

From that date, the following obligations, among others, will be fully enforceable: appointment of a Data Protection Officer (DPO) where applicable, maintenance of a record of processing activities, privacy impact assessments for high-risk processing, and notification of security incidents to the new Personal Data Protection Agency within the legal time frames. For research involving health and genome data, this new regime is especially relevant, as it will strengthen requirements regarding consent, lawful basis, and technical security measures.
q_6_1_fuente: Ley N° 20.120, sobre la investigación científica en el ser humano, su genoma, y prohíbe la clonación humana., Article 13; Ley N° 19.628, Article 2, 10; Ley 20.584, Article 13; Ley N° 20.850, Article 35; Ley N° 21.719, Article 2 (items f, g) and transitional provisions on entry into force.
q_6_2_directa: Yes. The Instituto de Salud Pública de Chile (ISP) has the technical guideline "Lineamientos y Orientación para la realización de Estudios Clínicos con Productos Biológicos" [Guidelines and Guidance for Conducting Clinical Studies with Biological Products], applicable to vaccine clinical trials. Resolución Exenta N° 173 of 2024 also approves the "General Considerations Guide for Clinical Studies," based on ICH E8(R1), which applies broadly to clinical studies in Chile, including those involving vaccines.
q_6_2_ampliada: The ISP's technical guideline for clinical studies with biological products sets out specific guidelines for the design, conduct, and reporting of clinical trials with vaccines and other biological products. Resolución Exenta N° 173/2024 complements this framework with internationally accepted principles on study design, identification of critical quality factors, safety surveillance, and reporting. Once the trial is complete and sanitary registration obtained, all biological products (including vaccines) are subject to the mandatory batch-control procedure administered by the ISP: the time frame for approving or rejecting a batch or sub-batch is 40 business days for vaccines and 20 business days for other biological products, under Decreto Supremo N° 3 of 2011.
q_6_2_fuente: Resolución Exenta N° 173, de 2024, del ISP; Guía Técnica del ISP — Lineamientos y Orientación para la realización de Estudios Clínicos con Productos Biológicos; Decreto Supremo N° 3, de 2011, del Ministerio de Salud., Article 54 G, 183, 185, 186.
q_6_3_directa: Yes. Ley N° 20.120 and its implementing regulation (Decreto Supremo N° 114, de 2010) regulate research involving human material, including biological profiles and the genome. This data qualifies as sensitive under the currently applicable Ley N° 19.628 and will retain that classification under Ley N° 21.719 once it takes effect on December 1, 2026.
q_6_3_ampliada:
Research involving human material and the processing of genome data are governed primarily by Ley N° 20.120 and its implementing regulation (Decreto Supremo N° 114, de 2010), which require express, free, informed, personal, written consent from subjects. Genome data that could allow identification must be encrypted for storage and transmission, and the preservation of biological samples or material for research, diagnostic, or treatment purposes requires sufficient security and confidentiality measures to safeguard their proper use.

On personal data protection, health-related and biological-profile data are considered sensitive. Until December 1, 2026, Ley N° 19.628 remains in force, which permits processing by public bodies when carried out to fulfill legal functions within their remit. From that date, Ley N° 21.719 takes full effect, retaining the sensitive-data classification for health, biometric, genetic, and biological-profile data, and introducing strengthened requirements on consent, lawful basis, and technical security measures.
q_6_3_fuente: Ley N° 20.120, sobre la investigación científica en el ser humano, su genoma, y prohíbe la clonación humana., Article 9, 13; Decreto Supremo N° 114, de 2010, del Ministerio de Salud.; Ley N° 19.628, Article 2 (item g), Article 10; Ley N° 21.719, Article 2 (items f, g).
q_6_4_directa: Yes, various specific regulations govern different types of clinical studies. These include: bioequivalence studies for generic medicines, governed by Norma Técnica N° 131 (Decreto N° 27/2012 of MINSAL) and Norma Técnica N° 136 (Decreto N° 500/2012 of MINSAL); studies with biological and biosimilar products, regulated by the ISP's Guía Técnica de Lineamientos y Orientación para la realización de Estudios Clínicos con Productos Biológicos and by Norma Técnica N° 170 (Decreto N° 945/2014 of MINSAL); and specific rules for research in vulnerable populations, such as minors and adults who are physically or mentally incapable of giving consent.
q_6_4_ampliada: For bioequivalence (generic) studies, Norma Técnica N° 131 defines the technical criteria for establishing therapeutic equivalence, and Norma Técnica N° 136 sets out the list of active ingredients subject to this requirement. These standards are complemented by the ISP's technical guides (G-Biof 01 for comparative bioavailability, G-Biof 02 for biowaivers, G-VMBA 01 for bioanalytical method validation) and by ISP Technical Notes (N° 5, 6, 7, 9, 10). For studies with biosimilars and biotechnological products, in addition to the ISP's Guía Técnica on Clinical Studies with Biological Products, Norma Técnica N° 170 on the sanitary registration of biotechnological products derived from recombinant DNA techniques applies. For research in vulnerable populations: in the case of adults unable to consent, the condition preventing consent must be a necessary characteristic of the group under study, the study must involve a potential direct benefit and minimal risks, and, in addition to the favorable opinion of the accredited CEC, authorization from the Secretaría Regional Ministerial de Salud (SEREMI) is required. In the case of minors, their refusal to participate or continue in the research must be respected.
q_6_4_fuente: Decreto N° 27, de 2012, del Ministerio de Salud (Norma Técnica N° 131); Decreto N° 500, de 2012, del Ministerio de Salud (Norma Técnica N° 136); Decreto N° 945, de 2014, del Ministerio de Salud (Norma Técnica N° 170); Guía Técnica del ISP — Lineamientos y Orientación para la realización de Estudios Clínicos con Productos Biológicos; Decreto Supremo N° 114, de 2010, del Ministerio de Salud, Article 11; Ley 20.584, Article 28; Ley 21.331, Article 25 N° 4.

q_1_1_directa: The National Regulatory Authority (NRA) for clinical trials is the Instituto Nacional de Vigilancia de Medicamentos y Alimentos (National Food and Drug Surveillance Institute, INVIMA).
q_1_1_ampliada: INVIMA, specifically through its Directorate of Medicines and Biological Products, is the entity responsible for evaluating and approving research protocols involving medicines conducted in Colombia. No clinical research project involving medicines and human subjects may begin without INVIMA's prior approval or clearance.
q_1_1_fuente: Resolución 2378 de 2008, Article 5; Guía para la presentación de protocolos de investigación (ASS-RSA-GU030), Section 3.1; Guía para la evaluación y seguimiento de protocolos de investigación (ASS-RSA-GU039), Section 3.1.
q_1_2_directa: The main regulation establishing scientific, technical, and administrative standards for health research is Resolución 8430 de 1993.
q_1_2_ampliada: This resolution establishes the requirements for conducting health research, including the classification of research according to risk (no risk, minimal risk, and greater-than-minimal risk), the requirements for informed consent, and the obligation to have a Research Ethics Committee. Studies must comply with the scientific and ethical principles set out in this regulation.
q_1_2_fuente: Resolución 8430 de 1993, Title I, Article 1; Guía para la evaluación y seguimiento de protocolos de investigación (ASS-RSA-GU039), Section 3.4; Guía para la presentación de protocolos de investigación (ASS-RSA-GU030), Section 7.
q_1_3_directa: The main regulations governing the specific authorization of clinical trials involving medicines and human subjects are Resolución 2378 de 2008, which adopts Good Clinical Practice (GCP), and Resolución 3823 de 1997.
q_1_3_ampliada: Resolución 2378 de 2008 is fundamental, as it adopts Good Clinical Practice on a mandatory basis for institutions conducting research involving medicines and human subjects, and establishes the obligation to register and obtain approval for every project before INVIMA. Resolución 3823 de 1997, for its part, establishes that drug research projects will be evaluated by INVIMA. Resolución 8430/1993 provides the general ethical foundation, while Resolución 2378/2008 sets out the specific technical and operational GCP requirements for drug clinical trials.
q_1_3_fuente: Guía para la presentación de protocolos de investigación (ASS-RSA-GU030), Section 3.1 and 7; Guía para la evaluación y seguimiento de protocolos de investigación (ASS-RSA-GU039), Section 3.1 and 3.4; Resolución 2378 de 2008, Article 1 and 4; Resolución 3823 de 1997, Article 6.
q_1_4_directa: Yes, evaluation and approval by a Research Ethics Committee (CEI) is required for all research involving human subjects.
q_1_4_ampliada: The research institution must have an Institutional Ethics Committee, or, if it does not have one, the project must be approved by a CEI from another institution holding a Good Clinical Practice compliance certificate issued by INVIMA. The CEI is responsible for ensuring the protection of participants' rights, safety, and well-being.
q_1_4_fuente: Resolución 2378 de 2008, Article 7; Resolución 8430 de 1993, Article 2.
q_1_5_directa: Yes, approval by the Research Ethics Committee must be obtained before the new clinical study is submitted to INVIMA.
q_1_5_ampliada: To comply with this requirement, the sponsor must ensure that the CEI evaluates the study first and completes the Formato de presentación y evaluación de protocolos de investigación ASS-RSA-FM055, which must be attached together with the approval letter when the application is submitted through INVIMA's Protocolos en Línea (Online Protocols) platform. The information in INVIMA's administrative act will be referenced exactly as it appears in the Ethics Committee's approval letter.
q_1_5_fuente: Guía para la presentación de protocolos de investigación (ASS-RSA-GU030), Section 3.1; Guía para la evaluación y seguimiento de protocolos de investigación (ASS-RSA-GU039), Section 3.1.
q_1_6_directa: In Colombia, there is no independent or standalone accreditation system for Research Ethics Committees (CEIs). The evaluation and authorization of CEIs is carried out by INVIMA as part of the Good Clinical Practice (GCP) certification process granted to research institutions. Every CEI must therefore be affiliated with the GCP certification of a Research Center in order to evaluate clinical trials in the country.
q_1_6_ampliada: The GCP certificate issued by INVIMA covers the entire research system of the Health Service Provider Institution (IPS), requiring regulatory assessors to verify strict compliance with the CEI's responsibilities, composition, and operating procedures. If an institution does not have its own institutional committee, the regulation allows projects to be evaluated by an external CEI, provided it is affiliated with another institution holding valid GCP certification issued by INVIMA. Any change or replacement of the ethics committee authorized at a site requires a formal procedure to amend the GCP certification resolution, through documentary review and a possible verification visit for new conditions. During inspections, committees are assessed to ensure they have standardized procedural manuals, decision-making independence, a minimum of five members, and an appropriate multidisciplinary composition. In this way, the licensing, oversight, and control of the CEI operate strictly under the general regulatory framework for institutional certification in clinical research.
q_1_6_fuente: Resolución 2378 de 2008, Articles 3 and 7, and Technical Annex (Tables 1-3); Guía para la presentación de protocolos de investigación (ASS-RSA-GU030), Item 3.
q_1_7_directa: Yes, a public registry of Research Ethics Committees (CEIs) exists in Colombia, maintained and published by INVIMA. Although these committees are not certified on a standalone basis, the regulatory authority keeps an official, public list of the CEIs affiliated with and authorized under institutional Good Clinical Practice (GCP) certification.
q_1_7_ampliada: In compliance with the transparency and public information access policies set out in Ley 1712 de 2014, INVIMA maintains open databases and registries for public consultation. Through its official web portal, specifically in the Clinical Research areas for medicines and medical devices, the health authority continuously makes these resources available. These include the public list of ethics committees affiliated with GCP-certified institutions, which details the bodies authorized at the national level. The Institute also periodically publishes ongoing oversight documents, such as the "Registro de estado de comités de ética y centros de investigación con visita de IVC" [Status Registry of Ethics Committees and Research Sites Subject to Inspection, Surveillance, and Control (IVC) Visits]. These openly accessible registries are essential to Colombia's regulatory ecosystem in ensuring the fitness and traceability of the research system.
q_1_7_fuente: Resolución 2378 de 2008, Article 3 and Technical Annex; Ley 1712 de 2014, Article 3; Guía para los Comités de Ética en Investigación (ASS-RSA-GU040).
q_1_8_directa: Yes. All clinical research protocols involving medicines and human subjects that are interventional in nature, covering Phases I, II, III, and IV, must be authorized in advance by INVIMA.
q_1_8_ampliada: Colombian regulations, specifically Resolución 2378 de 2008 and Resolución 3823 de 1997, unambiguously establish that no interventional clinical drug research project may begin without INVIMA's explicit approval. The authority's guidelines, such as ASS-RSA-GU030, clarify that this obligation applies to all studies from Phase I through Phase IV that involve a pharmacological intervention. By contrast, purely observational Phase IV studies (where the medicine is prescribed in the usual manner) do not require prior approval in the same sense, but must still be submitted to INVIMA for its awareness and follow-up, as detailed in the Guía para la evaluación y seguimiento de protocolos de investigación (ASS-RSA-GU039). This distinction between interventional and observational studies determines the applicable regulatory procedure.
q_1_8_fuente: Resolución 2378 de 2008, Article 5; Resolución 3823 de 1997, Article 6; Guía para la presentación de protocolos de investigación (ASS-RSA-GU030), Section 3.1; Guía para la evaluación y seguimiento de protocolos de investigación (ASS-RSA-GU039), Section 3.2.
q_2_1_directa: The sponsor is defined as the individual, company, institution, or organization responsible for initiating, managing/controlling, and/or financing a clinical study.
q_2_1_ampliada: This role may be carried out by a corporation or agency external to the institution or by the investigator or hospital institution. Its obligations go far beyond simple financing and include: ensuring the protection and safety of participants through a monitoring system, ensuring data quality and quality control, obtaining and documenting INVIMA's approval of the investigational product, and ensuring control over the distribution, handling, and return of the investigational product.
q_2_1_fuente: Guía para la presentación de protocolos de investigación (ASS-RSA-GU030), Definitions; Guía para el diligenciamiento de los formatos de reporte de eventos adversos en protocolos de investigación (ASS-RSA-GU057), Section 3; Instructivo Manejo de la Herramienta en Línea eReporting Industria (ASS-RSA-IN050), Section 3; Resolución 2378 de 2008, Chapter I; Circular Externa 1000-043-20, Table 18.
q_2_2_directa: No. The regulation requires the sponsor or the Contract Research Organization (CRO) to submit a letter or power of attorney including the information of the legal representative or proxy, such as name, ID number, email, address, and telephone number.
q_2_2_ampliada: Although the documentation requires the address and contact information of the legal representative or proxy of the sponsoring company or CRO in the country, current regulations do not expressly require the sponsor's legal entity to be legally domiciled in Colombia. However, submission of the application through INVIMA's Oficina Virtual (Virtual Office) does require entering the proxy's address and the sponsor's contact information in Colombia for notification and correspondence purposes.
q_2_2_fuente: Guía para la presentación de protocolos de investigación (ASS-RSA-GU030), Section 4; Guía para la presentación y evaluación de informes de seguridad anual en investigación clínica (ASS-RSA-GU056), Section 1.
q_2_3_directa: No. Colombian regulations do not establish an accreditation system or a prior registration for an entity to act as a sponsor. Instead, a sponsor's fitness and capacity are demonstrated during the protocol submission process, through its ability to meet all substantive obligations.
q_2_3_ampliada: The capacity to act as a sponsor is implicit in demonstrating that the necessary resources and systems are in place to meet the requirements of current regulations. This includes the financial capacity to take out the required insurance policy, the technical capacity to manage the quality of the investigational product (GMP), and the organizational capacity to implement adequate monitoring and a pharmacovigilance system. The sponsor is responsible for initiating, controlling, and/or financing the clinical study and has responsibilities that include: ensuring the study is conducted in accordance with the protocol and GCP; ensuring data quality and reliability; documenting agreements with the investigator/institution in writing; and ensuring that study staff know and properly handle the investigational product through training and written instructions. It must have available safety and efficacy data from prior clinical or preclinical studies to support administration in humans.
q_2_3_fuente: Guía para la presentación de protocolos de investigación (ASS-RSA-GU030), Section 3.1; Guía para la evaluación y seguimiento de protocolos de investigación (ASS-RSA-GU039), Section 3.1; Resolución 2378 de 2008, Table 18, Table 19; Circular Externa 1000-043-20, Table 18.
q_2_4_directa: Yes. When a Contract Research Organization (OIC or CRO) is used, it acts as an organization engaged by the sponsor to carry out one or more of the sponsor's duties and functions related to the study. The CRO has responsibilities in submitting documentation and reporting adverse events.
q_2_4_ampliada: If the sponsor delegates functions to a CRO, it must submit a power of attorney or an equivalent legal document explicitly authorizing the CRO to act on its behalf before INVIMA. It should be noted that this document is a requirement for the submission of the application. In such cases, the CRO may submit the supporting documentation for the protocol evaluation. In addition, where applicable, the CRO's name or corporate name must be recorded on the Protocol Evaluation Form. For adverse event reporting, the sponsor or the CRO must send INVIMA the national serious adverse event report and the international reports.
q_2_4_fuente: Guía para la presentación de protocolos de investigación (ASS-RSA-GU030), Section 2, Definitions; Guía para la evaluación y seguimiento de protocolos de investigación (ASS-RSA-GU039), Scope; Guía para el diligenciamiento de los formatos de reporte de eventos adversos en protocolos de investigación (ASS-RSA-GU057), Section 1 and 4.
q_2_5_directa: Yes. Entities must operate as Health Service Provider Institutions (IPS), duly registered in the Sistema Único de Habilitación (Single Licensing System). The site must also hold valid Good Clinical Practice (GCP) Certification granted by INVIMA. This certification must expressly cover the health services and medical specialties needed to safely conduct the proposed clinical research protocol.
q_2_5_ampliada: INVIMA has exclusive authority to verify that provider institutions planning to conduct clinical studies meet all technical, scientific, and administrative GCP requirements. For selection and approval, the site must demonstrate suitable physical infrastructure, including medical consulting rooms for clinical assessment, a pharmaceutical area or service with strict temperature control for the investigational medicine, a licensed clinical laboratory, and proven capacity to respond to medical emergencies. If the IPS does not have a clinical laboratory or a research ethics committee within its own facilities, the regulation allows external support through duly formalized and approved networks or contracts. It is therefore the sponsor's responsibility to rigorously verify that selected institutions maintain and keep up to date the conditions under which INVIMA issued their initial GCP certification. Failure to meet these infrastructure or licensing standards makes it impossible to conduct clinical research at the site, so any structural change must be reported and evaluated through a new-site procedure before the health authority.
q_2_5_fuente: Resolución 2378 de 2008, Articles 3 and 4 (Paragraph 2), and Technical Annex, Chapter II; Guía para la presentación de las enmiendas, nuevos centros, nuevos investigadores y consentimientos informados de protocolos de investigación (ASS-RSA-GU031), Item 4.
q_2_6_directa: Yes. Suitable academic training, experience, Good Clinical Practice training, and knowledge of current ethical and legal regulations are required.
q_2_6_ampliada: To serve as Principal Investigator, the professional must demonstrate at least three years of certified clinical experience in managing the condition under study, along with a minimum of two years of demonstrable experience in research and scientific output. As for regulatory training, national and international GCP certificates no older than three years must be submitted, along with courses of at least eight hours' duration. Where the principal investigator does not fully meet the required clinical experience or training, the regulation allows for a qualified sub-investigator or secondary investigator to be presented to provide clinical support and fill those gaps. The investigator must also sign a letter committing to comply with national regulations, the Declaration of Helsinki, and the CIOMS Guidelines, and to properly manage and report events of public health interest. Finally, it is an essential requirement that the principal investigator not be a member of the Ethics Committee evaluating the protocol, to avoid conflicts of interest, and they must guarantee sufficient, exclusive time dedication, to be assessed by that committee.
q_2_6_fuente: Resolución 2378 de 2008, Technical Annex, Table 5 (Investigator Competence); Resolución 8430 de 1993, Article 6, item f.
q_2_7_directa: Yes. It is required to submit an insurance policy, contractual or extra-contractual, covering adverse events associated with and attributable to the investigational product. Medical care must also be guaranteed, together with any legally applicable compensation for harm caused by the research.
q_2_7_ampliada: The research protocol must guarantee that medical care will be provided to subjects in the event of an adverse event related to the study medicine, and must specify the mechanism for care while insurance coverage is being accessed. The Informed Consent Form (ICF) must explain coverage for adverse event care and the availability of an insurance policy in the event of compensation or indemnification. If the insurance does not fully cover the harm, the trial sponsor, the principal investigator, and the head of the institution will be jointly and severally liable.
q_2_7_fuente: Guía para la presentación de protocolos de investigación (ASS-RSA-GU030), Section 4.1; Guía para la evaluación y seguimiento de protocolos de investigación (ASS-RSA-GU039), Section 3.4; Resolución 8430 de 1993, Article 13 and 15; Resolución 2378 de 2008, Institutional Evaluation Technical Sheet.
q_3_1_directa: Yes. The initial submission must include the documentation uploaded to the Protocolos en Línea platform, essentially the Formato Lista de Verificación (ASS-RSA-FM046), the Formato de Evaluación por el CEI (ASS-RSA-FM055), the research Protocol (in Spanish and English), the CEI approval letter, the contractual or extra-contractual insurance policy, the Investigator's Brochure (Spanish and English), and the Informed Consent Forms.
q_3_1_ampliada: The research Protocol must be complete, including the scientific rationale, objectives (general and specific), methodology (study design, sample size, inclusion/exclusion criteria, description of the intervention), analysis plan, patient information sheet, and bibliographic references. Supporting documentation for sites and investigators is also required, together with the manufacturer's Good Manufacturing Practice certificate for the investigational product (apostilled, legalized, and officially translated), stability studies, and certificates of analysis for the investigational product. For imports, the Formato de presentación y evaluación de nuevas solicitudes de importación de suministros (ASS-RSA-FM052) must be attached.
q_3_1_fuente: Guía para la presentación de protocolos de investigación (ASS-RSA-GU030), Section 4.1.
q_3_2_directa: Yes. Submission takes place through INVIMA's Protocolos en Línea platform, accessible from the Institute's website, requiring prior registration. The filing of the intent to initiate the procedure is done entirely online through INVIMA's Oficina Virtual, with no need for physical submission of documents.
q_3_2_ampliada:
The user must first register in the online procedures section of INVIMA's website, selecting the "Requiere Ingresar Protocolos de Investigación" option. Once on the "Protocolos en Línea" platform, the user selects "Nuevo formulario" and completes a 9-part form, uploading the documentation in navigable PDF format.

Completing all 9 parts generates a successful registration slip with the intent number. To file the application, the user accesses INVIMA's "Oficina Virtual," selects "Atención al Ciudadano" → "Enviar una nueva solicitud" → "Investigación Clínica," and digitally attaches: a cover letter, a letter or power of attorney with the legal representative's or proxy's information, the successful registration slip, the original proof of payment, and the intent number.

Under item 7 of Guía ASS-RSA-GU030 (version 6, effective December 22, 2025), no physical or magnetic-media documentation needs to be attached when using the "Protocolos en Línea" platform. Once the application is submitted, the system assigns a tracking ID number, which is sent to the registered email address.
q_3_2_fuente: Guía para la presentación de protocolos de investigación (ASS-RSA-GU030), Section 3.2, Section 5; Guía para la evaluación y seguimiento de protocolos de investigación (ASS-RSA-GU039), Section 3.1; Guía para la presentación de protocolos de investigación (ASS-RSA-GU030), Section 4.1.
q_3_3_directa: Yes. INVIMA's Clinical Research Group has a maximum time frame of two (2) months to give the applicant an initial response (a request for information or an approval resolution).
q_3_3_ampliada: If INVIMA requires additional information to complete the process, it will issue a single request for information (Auto). Under item 6 of Guía ASS-RSA-GU030 (version 6 of December 22, 2025), the applicant has one (1) month to respond, counted from the fifth (5th) business day following dispatch of the communication, extendable by one (1) additional month upon request, in accordance with Article 17 of the Código de Procedimiento Administrativo y de lo Contencioso Administrativo (Code of Administrative Procedure and Administrative Litigation, CPACA). The response must be limited to remedying the deficiencies identified by the Institute and is not a legal opportunity to submit new requests or additions to the initial application. Once the response is filed, INVIMA issues its final ruling of approval or denial.
q_3_3_fuente: Guía para la evaluación y seguimiento de protocolos de investigación (ASS-RSA-GU039), Section 3.4; Guía para la presentación de protocolos de investigación (ASS-RSA-GU030), Section 6.
q_3_4_directa: Yes, proof of payment of the applicable fee must be attached when filing the intent to initiate the procedure. The original proof of payment, together with the successful registration slip, is uploaded digitally to INVIMA's Oficina Virtual when the application is filed.
q_3_4_ampliada: Payment of the corresponding fee is an indispensable requirement for the assignment of a filing number to the clinical research protocol. Fee code 4070 applies to the initial evaluation procedure for protocols involving investigational products/medicines. Current fees are published in the Fees section of INVIMA's website and are updated periodically by resolution (the most recent update is Resolución 2024057944 of December 18, 2024, partially amended by Resolución 2025029573 of July 18, 2025). Proof of payment is attached digitally as part of the filing in the Oficina Virtual.
q_3_4_fuente: Guía para la presentación de protocolos de investigación (ASS-RSA-GU030), Section 3.2, Section 4.
q_3_5_directa: No. Regulations require that observational Phase IV studies state their identification code in a public clinical trial registry when submitted to INVIMA's correspondence office. For other types of studies, review of the regulations shows no evidence of a national registry of this kind.
q_3_5_ampliada: For observational Phase IV studies, the sponsor must attach a summary of the design, objectives, outcomes, analysis plan, and the identification code in a public clinical trial registry. More generally, Resolución 2378 de 2008 treats registration of the project in a public or private clinical trials network as a critical evaluation criterion.
q_3_5_fuente: Guía para la evaluación y seguimiento de protocolos de investigación (ASS-RSA-GU039), Section 3.2; Resolución 2378 de 2008, Chapter IV, Section 5.
q_3_6_directa: Not specified in official regulations.
q_3_6_ampliada: INVIMA structures its evaluation process on the basis of current national resolutions (Resolución 8430 de 1993 and Resolución 2378 de 2008). While the regime incorporates the international E2B standard for adverse event reporting and requires the manufacturer's Good Manufacturing Practice certificate to be apostilled and legalized, there is no formal mechanism in the regulations for recognizing protocol approvals, ethical reviews, or site accreditations carried out by foreign regulatory authorities that would replace or expedite the national approval process.
q_3_6_fuente: Not established in the regulations reviewed.
q_3_7_directa: The general sequential process involves planning, ethical approval, regulatory submission, INVIMA approval, and finally, authorization to begin subject recruitment.
q_3_7_ampliada:
Planning and Documentation: The sponsor prepares the protocol, the investigator's brochure, and all supporting documentation (preclinical studies, stability studies, GMP certificates, insurance policy, informed consent forms, etc.).

Ethical Evaluation and Approval (CEI): The protocol must be evaluated and approved by the Research Ethics Committee(s) (CEI) affiliated with the Research Center's GCP certification. The CEI issues the approval letter and completes Formato ASS-RSA-FM055.

Online Submission (INVIMA): The sponsor/CRO logs into INVIMA's "Protocolos en Línea" platform, registers, completes the 9-part form, and uploads all required documentation in navigable PDF format, including the CEI approval and Formato ASS-RSA-FM055.

Virtual Filing and Payment: Once the successful registration slip is generated, the user accesses INVIMA's Oficina Virtual, selects "Atención al Ciudadano" → "Enviar una nueva solicitud" → "Investigación Clínica," and digitally attaches the cover letter, the letter or power of attorney with the legal representative's or proxy's information, the successful registration slip, the original proof of payment of the applicable fee, and the intent number. Under item 7 of Guía ASS-RSA-GU030 (version 6 of December 22, 2025), no physical or magnetic-media documentation is required.

Regulatory Evaluation (INVIMA): The Clinical Research Group evaluates the protocol. If additional information is required (Auto), the applicant has one (1) month to respond, counted from the fifth business day following dispatch of the communication, extendable by one (1) additional month.

Final Approval: INVIMA communicates its final ruling (approval or denial) through an administrative act.

Study Start: The investigator and the institution may only begin the clinical study once they have the CEI's dated, written approval and INVIMA's approval.
q_3_7_fuente: Guía para la presentación de protocolos de investigación (ASS-RSA-GU030), Section 3.1, 3.2, 4.1, and 6; Guía para la evaluación y seguimiento de protocolos de investigación (ASS-RSA-GU039), Section 3.4; Resolución 2378 de 2008, Article 5 and 7, Table 8.
q_4_1_directa: Yes. Labeling of the Investigational Product (IP), including placebo or comparator, must be in Spanish and include the following information: study code, product name/code and strength, pharmaceutical form and route of administration, batch number, shelf life and storage conditions, participant identification code (where applicable), sponsor's name and address, and the statements "Medicine for clinical study use only" and "Keep out of reach of children."
q_4_1_ampliada: If the pharmaceutical form (such as blister packs or ampoules) does not allow all the information to be included on the primary packaging, it must appear on the secondary packaging. However, the primary packaging must at least contain the study code, the product name/code and strength, the batch number, the shelf life, the pharmaceutical form, the route of administration, and the sponsor's name. Labels must not contain false or misleading information, nor indicate that the medicine is safe or effective for the purposes of the research.
q_4_1_fuente: Guía de medicamentos y suministros de investigación clínica (ASS-RSA-GU045), Section 5.3.
q_4_2_directa: Yes, a Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) compliance certificate from the investigational product's manufacturer is required, duly apostilled, legalized, and officially translated into Spanish.
q_4_2_ampliada: The sponsor is responsible for demonstrating that the manufacturing process for all medicines to be used in the protocol (including placebo and comparator) is of appropriate quality (GMP). Manufacture of the investigational product (IP) must be carried out in accordance with GMP principles and guidelines, which are essential to ensure that participating subjects are not exposed to risk and that quality, efficacy, and safety do not affect the results of the clinical study.
q_4_2_fuente: Guía para la presentación de protocolos de investigación (ASS-RSA-GU030), Section 4.1; Guía de medicamentos y suministros de investigación clínica (ASS-RSA-GU045), Section 5.1.
q_4_3_directa: Yes, the import of medicines and supplies required to start the clinical study is authorized through an administrative act issued by the Directorate of Medicines and Biological Products as part of the initial protocol evaluation process.
q_4_3_ampliada: If additional medicines or supplies need to be imported after the initial approval, a new application must be filed with the Directorate of Medicines and Biological Products. Using INVIMA's ruling, the import license must be requested through the Ventanilla Única de Comercio Exterior (Single Window for Foreign Trade, VUCE) (Directorate of Sanitary Operations), which is responsible for issuing the ruling authorizing or denying import of these products.
q_4_3_fuente: Guía de medicamentos y suministros de investigación clínica (ASS-RSA-GU045), Section 5.6.1; Guía para la Presentación de Nuevas solicitudes de Importación de Suministros y Exportación de Muestras Biológicas para protocolos de Investigación (ASS-RSA-GU036).
q_5_1_directa: Yes. Investigators must report all national Serious Adverse Events (SAEs) to the Sponsor/CRO and to the CEI within no more than twenty-four (24) hours of becoming aware of them. The Sponsor/CRO, in turn, must report the national SAE assessed as related, or requested by INVIMA, to INVIMA's Sub-directorate of Medicines and Biological Products within no more than seven (7) business days from the first report received from the investigator.
q_5_1_ampliada: National SAEs are reported through an online form available on INVIMA's website (or, alternatively, by filing Formato ASS-RSA-FM100 on magnetic media). Expected International Serious Adverse Events must be reported by the Sponsor/CRO to INVIMA and to the CEIs annually through the Investigator's Brochure (or sooner if the protocol's duration is less than one year). For Unexpected International Serious Adverse Events related to the investigational molecule (SUSARs), the sponsor must send a bimonthly report (every two months) to INVIMA within the first five (5) business days of the following two-month period, using the Formato Base de Datos de Eventos Adversos Serios Internacionales (ASS-RSA-FM091) on magnetic media in Excel format.
q_5_1_fuente: Guía para el diligenciamiento de los formatos de reporte de eventos adversos en protocolos de investigación (ASS-RSA-GU057), Section 1, 4, and 5; Resolución No. 2011020764 del 10 de junio de 2011, Articles Three and Five.
q_5_2_directa: Yes, annual safety reports for clinical research protocols must be submitted. This annual safety report is known as the Development Safety Update Report (DSUR), per the international standard.
q_5_2_ampliada: The sponsor is responsible for completing and submitting the "Formato de Presentación y Evaluación del Informe de Seguridad Anual en Investigación Clínica" (ASS-RSA-FM089). This report may be submitted covering several clinical trials with the same sponsor and investigational molecule, and must be submitted on magnetic media (CD) with the corresponding filing before INVIMA. The report must include the global safety assessment, the benefit/risk assessment, and the DSUR conclusions, indicating whether it remains viable to continue the research.
q_5_2_fuente: Guía para la presentación y evaluación de informes de seguridad anual en investigación clínica (ASS-RSA-GU056), Objective and Guidelines.
q_5_3_directa: Yes, the investigator must submit written summaries of the study's status to the CEI at least once a year. An Annual Report must also be submitted to INVIMA.
q_5_3_ampliada: The CEI must establish, in writing, the procedures for following the progress of studies from approval through completion, including an annual review based on the number of subjects recruited, the latest project version, summaries of adverse events, and unanticipated problems. For INVIMA, the Formato Informe Anual de Proyectos de Investigación (ASS-RSA-FM063) must be completed in accordance with the Guía para el Diligenciamiento del Formato Anual de Proyectos de Investigación (ASS-RSA-GU041).
q_5_3_fuente: Guía para la evaluación y seguimiento de protocolos de investigación (ASS-RSA-GU039), Section 4.1; Resolución 2378 de 2008, Table 3, Table 16; Circular Externa 1000-043-20, Table 3.
q_5_4_directa: Yes. Prior CEI approval is required to prevent changes — amendments — to the project from being implemented without notice. INVIMA recently announced that it will accept amendments that include extension periods, provided the study's objectives, evaluation criteria, or participant inclusion criteria are not modified.
q_5_4_ampliada: Protocol modifications that could affect the safety of study subjects or change the interpretation of scientific evidence (a Relevant Amendment) require approval. Extending a study is considered a new research protocol if it modifies the objectives, evaluation criteria, or inclusion criteria; however, recent circulars allow extensions to be processed as amendments if they do not touch on those sensitive points. If a change to the project is needed, the investigator must agree on it with the sponsor and request new amendment approval from the CEI.
q_5_4_fuente: Circular Externa 3000-0512-2024; Resolución 2378 de 2008, Definitions, Table 3; Guía para la presentación de protocolos de investigación (ASS-RSA-GU030), Definitions; Guía para la evaluación y seguimiento de protocolos de investigación (ASS-RSA-GU039), Definitions; Resolución 2378 de 2008, Table 9.
q_5_5_directa: Not specified in official regulations.
q_5_5_ampliada: Current regulations expressly govern compensation and medical care for subjects harmed directly by the research, as well as participants' freedom to withdraw consent without prejudice to their care and treatment. However, neither Resolución 8430 de 1993 nor Resolución 2378 de 2008, nor INVIMA's operational guidelines, contain an express obligation requiring the sponsor to guarantee post-trial access to the investigational medicine.
q_5_5_fuente: Not established in the regulations reviewed.
q_6_1_directa: Yes. The applicable law is the Ley Estatutaria 1581 de 2012, which sets out general provisions for the protection of personal data, partially regulated by Decreto 1377 de 2013 and by Decreto 1081 de 2015.
q_6_1_ampliada:
The processing of personal data requires the prior, informed authorization of the data subject. However, authorization is not required in cases of medical or health emergencies, or for the processing of information authorized by law for historical, statistical, or scientific purposes. Even under these exceptions, data controllers must guarantee the security of the information to prevent its adulteration, loss, unauthorized consultation, use, or fraudulent access.

Ley 1581 de 2012 is partially regulated by Decreto 1377 de 2013 (definitions and procedures for personal data processing) and by Decreto 1081 de 2015 (which regulates, among other matters, the National Database Registry administered by the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio). Oversight and enforcement to ensure the lawfulness of data processing fall to the SIC's Delegatura para la Protección de Datos Personales (Personal Data Protection Delegation).

Update note: as of this review (June 2026), Proyecto de Ley Estatutaria 214 de 2025, consolidated with Proyecto de Ley 247 de 2025, is before the House of Representatives, seeking to modernize Ley 1581 de 2012 (new rights such as data portability and the right to object to automated decisions, penalties of up to 10,000 SMLMV [current monthly legal minimum wages] or 5% of the offender's revenue, and a special regime for children and adolescents). The reform has not been approved, and Ley 1581 de 2012 remains fully in force.
q_6_1_fuente: Ley 1581 de 2012, Articles 8, 9, and 10; Decreto 1377 de 2013; Decreto 1081 de 2015.
q_6_2_directa: Not specified in official regulations for vaccine clinical trials as such. Safety reporting guidelines recognize vaccines as a therapeutic class.
q_6_2_ampliada: Colombia's regulatory framework is structured around clinical trials involving medicines and human subjects in general, and INVIMA classifies vaccines as a "therapeutic class" for safety reporting purposes. The WHO AEFI tool (the WHO's causality assessment tool for events related to vaccines) is used to report adverse events in vaccine studies. There is no guideline or resolution in Colombia specifically and exclusively dedicated to regulating vaccine clinical trials.
q_6_2_fuente: Guía para la presentación y evaluación de informes de seguridad anual en investigación clínica (ASS-RSA-GU056), Section 2; Instructivo Manejo de la Herramienta en Línea eReporting Industria (ASS-RSA-IN050), References.
q_6_3_directa: Yes, Resolución 2640 de 2005 establishes requirements and procedures for the use of unclaimed bodies for research purposes, and regulates the transport and handling of anatomical components and biological samples.
q_6_3_ampliada: Institutions conducting research must meet specific requirements to obtain authorization to use unclaimed bodies, including submission of the research protocol and Ethics Committee approval. In addition, in the broader field of clinical research, Resolución 8430 de 1993 regulates research involving biological material, and INVIMA requires written procedures for the handling of biological samples, as well as the application form for the export of biological samples (ASS-RSA-FM053).
q_6_3_fuente: Resolución 2640 de 2005, Articles 21, 22, and 25; Guía para la evaluación y seguimiento de protocolos de investigación (ASS-RSA-GU039), Section 3.2; Guía de medicamentos y suministros de investigación clínica (ASS-RSA-GU045), Section 5.6.2; Resolución 2378 de 2008, Table 15.
q_6_4_directa: Yes, Resolución 8430 de 1993 establishes specific ethical and safety requirements for research involving minors or persons with disabilities, women of childbearing age, pregnant women, women in labor, postpartum, or breastfeeding, and newborns, as well as subordinate groups (such as students or hospital workers).
q_6_4_ampliada: For example, research involving minors or persons with disabilities must be preceded by studies in adults and immature animals (with exceptions), and requires certification from a neurologist, psychiatrist, or psychologist regarding the subject's capacity to understand, in addition to informed consent from their legal representative. The same resolution details special considerations for research into new prophylactic, diagnostic, therapeutic, and rehabilitation resources, and for research involving biosafety, such as the handling of pathogenic microorganisms or recombinant nucleic acids.
q_6_4_fuente: Resolución 8430 de 1993, Chapters III, IV, and V of Title II, Title III, and IV.

q_1_1_directa: The National Regulatory Authority (NRA) for biomedical research, which includes clinical trials, is the Consejo Nacional de Investigación en Salud (National Health Research Council, CONIS).
q_1_1_ampliada: CONIS is a body attached to the Ministry of Health with maximum administrative autonomy and instrumental legal personality, established to ensure compliance with the bioethical and scientific principles governing research. CONIS provides leadership for the development of bioethics and, among its functions, regulates, oversees, and monitors biomedical research in order to protect people's life, health, and dignity.
q_1_1_fuente: Ley Reguladora de Investigación Biomédica (Ley N° 9234), Article 34, 35; Reglamento Orgánico del CONIS (Decreto Ejecutivo No. 40884-S).
q_1_2_directa: The main regulation is Ley N° 9234, the "Ley Reguladora de Investigación Biomédica" [Biomedical Research Regulation Act], and its implementing regulation, Decreto Ejecutivo N° 39061-S, together with its amendments (Decreto N° 39533-S and N° 44033-S). This regulatory framework safeguards participants' life, health, interests, well-being, and dignity.
q_1_2_ampliada: Ley N° 9234 establishes that all research must be governed by the principles of respect for dignity, beneficence, non-maleficence, autonomy, and distributive justice. Its application is detailed in Decreto Ejecutivo N° 39061-S, the "Reglamento a la Ley Reguladora de Investigación Biomédica," which operationalizes the submission, authorization, and follow-up procedures. Subsequent reforms such as Decreto N° 39533-S and Decreto N° 44033-S have updated the documentary requirements and import procedures. The applicable regulations must comply with human rights standards, including the Universal Declaration of Human Rights and the Inter-American Convention.
q_1_2_fuente: Ley Reguladora de Investigación Biomédica (Ley N° 9234), Articles 1, 4; Reglamento a la Ley Reguladora de Investigación Biomédica (Decreto N° 39061-S), Articles 1, 2; Decreto N° 44033-S.
q_1_3_directa: Clinical trial authorization is governed primarily by Ley N° 9234 and Reglamento N° 39061-S, which require prior written approval from the Comité Ético Científico (Scientific Ethics Committee, CEC) and registration with CONIS.
q_1_3_ampliada: The Regulation details the documentary requirements (Initial Submission Package) that must be presented to the CEC to obtain approval. In addition, the requirements for the import of Investigational Products (IP) must be met, which require the research to be duly authorized and registered with CONIS.
q_1_3_fuente: Ley Reguladora de Investigación Biomédica (Ley N° 9234), Article 55; Reglamento a la Ley Reguladora de Investigación Biomédica (Decreto N° 39061-S), Articles 44, 53, 55.
q_1_4_directa: Yes. All research involving human subjects must, before it begins, have the written approval of a duly accredited CEC.
q_1_4_ampliada: CEC approval is an indispensable condition, and the Law prohibits any authority, public or private, from authorizing research without it. The CEC is obligated to ensure that participants' life, health, well-being, and human dignity are respected, and must review, approve, or reject projects.
q_1_4_fuente: Ley Reguladora de Investigación Biomédica (Ley N° 9234), Articles 55, 48.
q_1_5_directa: Yes, CEC approval is a prior, necessary requirement for registering the study with CONIS and for processing the import authorization for the Investigational Product (IP).
q_1_5_ampliada: In order for CONIS (the NRA) to process the application for authorization to release health products of interest for clinical research from customs, the application will not be processed unless it is endorsed by the CEC (Research Protocol Approval Letter). In addition, the CEC is required to provide the research information to CONIS to update the National Registry when it approves the research and before it begins.
q_1_5_fuente: Ley Reguladora de Investigación Biomédica (Ley N° 9234), Article 48; Reglamento a la Ley Reguladora de Investigación Biomédica (Decreto N° 39061-S), Article 55.
q_1_6_directa: Yes, CONIS is responsible for accreditation and must maintain a national registry of all registered CECs.
q_1_6_ampliada: CEC accreditation is valid for three years. To be accredited, CECs must meet requirements such as being multidisciplinary and having a minimum of five members, including at least one scientific expert and one person representing community interests. CONIS may temporarily or permanently suspend a CEC's accreditation if it is found not to be complying with the law.
q_1_6_fuente: Ley Reguladora de Investigación Biomédica (Ley N° 9234), Articles 43, 47; Reglamento a la Ley Reguladora de Investigación Biomédica (Decreto N° 39061-S), Article 25.
q_1_7_directa: Yes. Ley N° 9234 requires CONIS to implement an information system, accessible at all times, with up-to-date databases including the registry of Scientific Ethics Committees (CECs). An official public registry of accredited CECs is currently available on CONIS's website.
q_1_7_ampliada: CONIS must keep a national registry of all registered CECs and their accreditation status. This registry is public and accessible online through CONIS's official portal (conis.ministeriodesalud.go.cr). The law provides that CONIS must implement a biomedical research information system, accessible at all times, with up-to-date databases including information on CECs, accredited investigators, and approved and rejected research.
q_1_7_fuente: Ley Reguladora de Investigación Biomédica (Ley N° 9234), Article 43, items b), q), and t).
q_1_8_directa: Yes. All research involving human subjects must be registered with CONIS's national registry before it begins, and research requiring the import of health products of interest may only be conducted once the research has been duly approved by the CEC and registered with CONIS.
q_1_8_ampliada: CONIS implements a biomedical research information system, accessible at all times, with up-to-date databases on approved and rejected research. The CEC must provide the information for this registry. The Law also establishes a fee for registering a biomedical research project, demonstrating that formal registration with CONIS is mandatory for sponsored research.
q_1_8_fuente: Ley Reguladora de Investigación Biomédica (Ley N° 9234), Articles 43, 60; Reglamento a la Ley Reguladora de Investigación Biomédica (Decreto N° 39061-S), Article 55.
q_2_1_directa: Yes. The sponsor is defined as the individual, company, entity, or organization — public or private, national or foreign — that takes responsibility for initiating, managing, financing, and publishing the results of research, and that also assumes coverage of costs and compensation.
q_2_1_ampliada: The regulation also sets out the sponsor's main obligations, such as securing financing, selecting the investigator, and taking responsibility for short- and long-term adverse events resulting from the research.
q_2_1_fuente: Ley Reguladora de Investigación Biomédica (Ley N° 9234), Articles 2, 53, 58.
q_2_2_directa: Yes. Ley N° 9234 (Art. 58) requires the research contract to be signed by the "sponsor's representative." In addition, for research conducted within the Caja Costarricense de Seguro Social (Costa Rican Social Security Fund, CCSS), the CCSS's Biomedical Research Regulation expressly requires foreign-domiciled companies to submit legal powers of attorney for their National Representative or Proxy.
q_2_2_ampliada: Article 58 of Ley N° 9234 requires the contract signed between the parties to include the sponsor's representative. To conduct research within the CCSS (the country's main hospital network), the CCSS's Biomedical Research Regulation (Art. 29, item c.2) requires foreign-domiciled companies to submit "legal powers of attorney with sufficient authority ... authorizing the National Representative or Proxy to represent the foreign company." In addition, since civil liability insurance policies must be enforceable within the country, the sponsoring entity or insurer needs the legal capacity to answer before Costa Rican jurisdictions.
q_2_2_fuente: Ley Reguladora de Investigación Biomédica (Ley N° 9234), Articles 31, 58; Reglamento de Investigación Biomédica de la CCSS, Article 29.
q_2_3_directa: Yes. The sponsor must ensure the quality, integrity, accuracy, reliability, and consistency of electronic data, and guarantee financing and the manufacture of the IP under Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP).
q_2_3_ampliada: It is also the sponsor's obligation to take out civil liability insurance, notify the CEC and CONIS of any suspension of the research, document the financial aspects in an agreement with the investigator, and ensure the timely delivery of the IP while keeping records of its shipment and disposal.
q_2_3_fuente: Ley Reguladora de Investigación Biomédica (Ley N° 9234), Articles 31, 53.
q_2_4_directa: Yes. The sponsor may transfer tasks to a CRO (OIC), but retains ultimate responsibility for the quality and integrity of the data. CROs must be accredited by CONIS.
q_2_4_ampliada: The functions transferred to the CRO must be specified in writing. For accreditation, the CRO must hold a valid Sanitary Operating Permit, provide a description of its infrastructure, and ensure that its staff in Costa Rica, or with access to the information, have documented Good Clinical Practice (GCP) training, renewed every three years. The CRO must also comply with Ley N° 8968 on the Protection of Personal Data. Both the sponsor and the CRO are jointly and severally liable for harm caused by the transferred tasks.
q_2_4_fuente: Ley Reguladora de Investigación Biomédica (Ley N° 9234), Articles 53, 54; Reglamento a la Ley Reguladora de Investigación Biomédica (Decreto N° 39061-S), Articles 3, 28.
q_2_5_directa: Yes. The sponsor is obligated to properly select the entity where the research will be conducted. Every research site or facility where clinical activities are carried out, or where biological samples or investigational products are stored or dispensed, must hold the Sanitary Operating Permit or the corresponding sanitary license issued by the Ministry of Health. The investigator must also have adequate facilities available to conduct the study.
q_2_5_ampliada: Ley N° 9234 (Art. 53) requires the sponsor to properly select the entity where the research will be conducted, while the principal investigator must guarantee that adequate facilities are available to carry it out appropriately. Reglamento N° 39061-S (Arts. 3 and 28) sets out that research sites, including places where clinical activities are conducted and where biological material or investigational products are stored, held, or dispensed, must hold a valid Sanitary Operating Permit and sanitary license consistent with their category of establishment. To submit the project for approval, it is essential to present to the Scientific Ethics Committee (CEC) a detailed description of the site and the current licensing certificates for the facilities and laboratories. In addition, every public or private institution where such research is conducted must establish its own institutional regulations governing research, consistent with the law.
q_2_5_fuente: Ley Reguladora de Investigación Biomédica (Ley N° 9234), Articles 51 and 53; Reglamento a la Ley Reguladora de Investigación Biomédica (Decreto N° 39061-S), Articles 3, 6, 28, 44, and 46.
q_2_6_directa: Yes. The sponsor is obligated to properly select the investigator and their team. Investigators must be duly accredited by CONIS, which sets requirements for professional experience, prior participation in interventional research, and current Good Clinical Practice (GCP) training.
q_2_6_ampliada: Ley N° 9234 (Art. 53) requires the sponsor to properly select the investigator, their team, and the entity where the research will be conducted. Reglamento N° 39061-S (Art. 26) sets out the specific requirements for accrediting the Principal Investigator in interventional studies: they must be a member of the relevant professional association, have at least five years of certified professional practice, have demonstrably participated in at least two prior interventional research studies, and hold documented Good Clinical Practice (GCP) training renewed at least every three years through a program approved by CONIS. CONIS maintains a public Registry of Investigators where accreditation status can be verified.
q_2_6_fuente: Ley Reguladora de Investigación Biomédica (Ley N° 9234), Article 53; Reglamento a la Ley Reguladora de Investigación Biomédica (Decreto N° 39061-S), Articles 26, 58.
q_2_7_directa: Yes. Clinical research must have civil liability insurance enforceable within the country. The sponsor is required to cover the costs of treatment for study-related injuries.
q_2_7_ampliada: The policy must provide coverage from the start of the research and for a minimum of two years after the participant's involvement ends. The study contract must include a clause under which the sponsor accepts responsibility for short- and long-term adverse events resulting from the research. The participant or their heirs must be informed of the procedure for accessing the insurance benefits.
q_2_7_fuente: Ley Reguladora de Investigación Biomédica (Ley N° 9234), Articles 31, 58, 53; Decreto Ejecutivo N° 39533-S, Article 48.
q_3_1_directa: Yes. The essential content for CONIS's initial authorization is divided into two regulatory stages: 1) Project Registration (which requires the Registration Form and payment of the Fee) and 2) Sanitary Authorization for the Import of the Investigational Product (IP).
q_3_1_ampliada: For Registration and Fee Payment (mandatory before the study begins): The investigator must submit the Hoja inscripción de protocolo de investigación biomédica (CONIS-FORM-34) form, detailing the key administrative information, the CEC approval code, and the contract reference. This registration is essential because the principal investigator must pay CONIS a fee equal to 3% of the research's total budget. To do so, the CONIS submission requires a copy of the contract signed between sponsor and investigator (to verify the budget) and proof of the bank deposit or fee exemption agreement. For Import (where applicable): If the study requires the import of Investigational Products (IP), the application for sanitary authorization to release the products from customs must be submitted to CONIS, including the list and quantities of the IP to be imported.
q_3_1_fuente: Ley Reguladora de Investigación Biomédica (Ley N° 9234), Article 60; Reglamento a la Ley Reguladora de Investigación Biomédica (Decreto N° 39061-S), Articles 44, 55; Hoja inscripción de protocolo de investigación biomédica (CONIS-FORM-34).
q_3_2_directa: Yes. Initial documentation is submitted to the CEC in whatever format it requires (physical or digital). For procedures before CONIS, documentation may be submitted physically at its office or electronically as a PDF with a certified digital signature under Ley 8454. The Ventanilla Única de Comercio Exterior (Single Window for Foreign Trade, VUCE) is used specifically for sanitary authorization of the IP's import and customs release.
q_3_2_ampliada: Submission to the CEC depends on each committee's internal rules and may be physical or digital.
