For registration with CONIS, the CONIS-FORM-34 form must reach CONIS's Biomedical Research Technical Unit (UTIB) at least eight business days before the research begins (or 36 hours in emergencies). Accreditations and correspondence to CONIS may be submitted physically or electronically as a PDF with a certified digital signature. The VUCE electronic mechanism is used specifically by CONIS to issue sanitary authorization for the IP's import and customs release, using the instruments published by CONIS.
q_3_2_fuente: Reglamento a la Ley Reguladora de Investigación Biomédica (Decreto N° 39061-S), Articles 44, 58; Hoja inscripción de protocolo de investigación biomédica (CONIS-FORM-34), Notes.
q_3_3_directa: Yes. The CEC must issue its ruling (approval, rejection, or renewal) within one calendar month, counted from the business day following submission of the complete application.
q_3_3_ampliada: For CONIS's authorization to release the Investigational Product (IP) from customs, review of the documentation has a time frame of five calendar days. If the documentation is incomplete, CONIS issues a single request for correction, granting ten business days to remedy the deficiency. The time frame for registration with CONIS, once approved by the CEC, requires the documentation to reach the UTIB at least eight business days before the study begins.
q_3_3_fuente: Reglamento a la Ley Reguladora de Investigación Biomédica (Decreto N° 39061-S), Articles 42, 55.
q_3_4_directa: Yes. To register a biomedical research project, the principal investigator must pay CONIS a fee equal to three percent (3%) of the research's total budget.
q_3_4_ampliada: This fee is calculated on the study's total budget and must be deposited into CONIS's collection account when requesting registration of the approved project. Exempt from this payment are studies considered to be of public interest or a health priority by the Executive Branch, and independent, unsponsored research without commercial purposes (i.e., not sponsored by pharmaceutical multinationals or for-profit manufacturers/distributors).
q_3_4_fuente: Ley Reguladora de Investigación Biomédica (Ley N° 9234), Article 60, 61; Reglamento a la Ley Reguladora de Investigación Biomédica (Decreto N° 39061-S), Articles 49, 50.
q_3_5_directa: Yes. CONIS is responsible for maintaining a national registry of all biomedical research conducted in the country, and this registry must be publicly accessible.
q_3_5_ampliada: CONIS must implement an information system, accessible at all times, with up-to-date databases on approved and rejected research. The CEC, when approving a study, is required to provide the information to update this registry before the research begins.
q_3_5_fuente: Ley Reguladora de Investigación Biomédica (Ley N° 9234), Articles 43, 48.
q_3_6_directa: Not specified in official regulations. There is no explicit recognition mechanism that replaces the local approval process.
q_3_6_ampliada: Although there is no formal reciprocal recognition mechanism exempting a study from the local approval process for clinical trials in Costa Rica, the initial submission package for all experimental, clinical, or interventional research must include certification that the protocol was approved by a duly accredited Scientific Ethics Committee (CEC) in the country of origin, particularly for multicenter studies. A copy of the approval letter issued by recognized national or international regulatory agencies, such as the FDA, EMA, or other equivalents, must also be included. This recognition is limited to the documentation submitted and does not replace or suspend the obligation to comply with current national regulations, which include final review and approval by the local CEC and registration with CONIS.
q_3_6_fuente: Reglamento a la Ley Reguladora de Investigación Biomédica (Decreto N° 39061-S), Article 44.
q_3_7_directa: The order includes signing the contract and insurance policy, ethical approval (CEC), registration and payment of the fee (CONIS), and sanitary import authorization (CONIS).
q_3_7_ampliada:
Contracting and Insurance: The sponsor, the principal investigator, and the institution sign a contract that must include a clause on the sponsor's liability for adverse events. The sponsor must provide civil liability insurance enforceable in Costa Rica.

Submission to the CEC: The investigator submits the Initial Submission Package to the CEC of their choice.

Ethical Approval: The CEC issues its approval or rejection within a maximum of one calendar month.

National Registration (CONIS): The principal investigator pays the 3% fee and submits the protocol registration application (CONIS-FORM-34) to CONIS's UTIB at least eight business days before the study begins. The CEC must notify CONIS to update the national registry.

Sanitary Authorization (Import): If an IP is required, the investigator/importer submits the customs release application to CONIS, endorsed by the CEC, which CONIS will review within five calendar days.
q_3_7_fuente: Ley Reguladora de Investigación Biomédica (Ley N° 9234), Articles 31, 58, 60; Reglamento a la Ley Reguladora de Investigación Biomédica (Decreto N° 39061-S), Articles 42, 44, 55; Hoja inscripción de protocolo de investigación biomédica (CONIS-FORM-34).
q_4_1_directa: Yes. Labeling must be in Spanish, and the investigational product must visibly bear the statement "Producto en Investigación - Uso restringido a personal autorizado" [Investigational Product - Restricted to authorized personnel] or equivalent wording.
q_4_1_ampliada: The sponsor must ensure that the IP is properly coded and labeled to protect blinding. Supplementary labels (e.g., barcodes, participant numbers) are permitted, provided they do not conceal the essential information on the original label. If the expiry date is extended, the investigator must request duly documented permission from CONIS to modify the label.
q_4_1_fuente: Ley Reguladora de Investigación Biomédica (Ley N° 9234), Article 53; Reglamento a la Ley Reguladora de Investigación Biomédica (Decreto N° 39061-S), Article 56.
q_4_2_directa: Yes. The sponsor must certify that the Investigational Products (IP), including comparators and placebo, are manufactured in accordance with applicable Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP).
q_4_2_ampliada: For import, one of the requirements is to submit the GMP Certificate for the establishments manufacturing the IP, issued by the regulatory authority of the manufacturing country. If the product is manufactured or packaged in its final form in Costa Rica, the local establishment must hold a valid registration and guarantee compliance with the applicable GMP aspects.
q_4_2_fuente: Ley Reguladora de Investigación Biomédica (Ley N° 9234), Article 53; Reglamento a la Ley Reguladora de Investigación Biomédica (Decreto N° 39061-S), Articles 56, 55.
q_4_3_directa: No. CEC approval and registration of the study with CONIS are prior, necessary conditions, but import requires a separate sanitary customs-release authorization issued by CONIS.
q_4_3_ampliada: The investigator or importer submits the formal customs-release application to CONIS, which must be endorsed by the CEC. CONIS reviews the documentation within five calendar days and issues sanitary authorization for unregistered medicines when they are intended exclusively for clinical research purposes, using the electronic Single Window for Foreign Trade mechanism.
q_4_3_fuente: Reglamento a la Ley Reguladora de Investigación Biomédica (Decreto N° 39061-S), Articles 55, 58.
q_5_1_directa: Yes. The principal investigator must report Serious Adverse Events (SAEs) — unexpected or clinically significant ones — to the CEC within no more than 24 hours of becoming aware of them.
q_5_1_ampliada: The CEC is the primary safety reporting channel for clinical trials. The investigator must also report related non-serious adverse events to the CEC on a monthly basis, and unrelated non-serious adverse events in the quarterly report. For post-marketing studies, the pharmaceutical industry must report suspected serious or unexpected adverse reactions to the CNFV within a maximum of 24 hours, using the adapted CIOMS form.
q_5_1_fuente: Reglamento a la Ley Reguladora de Investigación Biomédica (Decreto N° 39061-S), Articles 26, 44; Decreto 35244, Article 12; Reglamento de Buenas Prácticas de Farmacovigilancia (Decreto N° 39417-S), Article 8.1.
q_5_2_directa: Yes, the principal investigator is required to submit periodic and final reports to the CEC. For marketed products, Periodic Safety Reports (IPS) must be submitted on a schedule that may be annual (from the third year onward) or every 5 years (from the sixth year onward).
q_5_2_ampliada: The CEC is obligated to follow up on project execution through the reports periodically submitted by the investigator. Submission of IPS reports is mandatory for innovative medicines, biologics, and those required to demonstrate therapeutic equivalence. The time frame for submitting IPS reports is 70 calendar days for 6- or 12-month intervals, and 90 calendar days for intervals longer than 12 months, counted from the Data Lock Point (DLP).
q_5_2_fuente: Ley Reguladora de Investigación Biomédica (Ley N° 9234), Article 48; Reglamento a la Ley Reguladora de Investigación Biomédica (Decreto N° 39061-S), Article 44; Reglamento de Buenas Prácticas de Farmacovigilancia (Decreto N° 39417-S), Article 12.8.
q_5_3_directa: Yes. The principal investigator must submit periodic reports on the progress of the research. In addition, Site Management Organizations (OAC) and CROs (OIC) are required to submit quarterly and annual reports on their activities to the CEC for its records.
q_5_3_ampliada: Responsibility for following up on project execution rests with the CEC, which does so through the investigator's periodic reports. These quarterly and annual OAC/CRO reports must include the agreement signed with the sponsor, as well as any amendments to that agreement, within a maximum of eight business days.
q_5_3_fuente: Ley Reguladora de Investigación Biomédica (Ley N° 9234), Article 48.
q_5_4_directa: Yes. The CEC must review, approve, or reject all amendments to the original protocol, the informed consent, and the informed assent. The investigator must submit these amendments to the CEC before the changes are implemented.
q_5_4_ampliada: If the changes involve a modification to the risk-benefit relationship, participants must be notified and an addendum to the consent is required. CONIS must be notified of any amendment made after protocol approval, including an increase in the number of participants (with the corresponding fee payment) or any other change to the informed consent or assent.
q_5_4_fuente: Ley Reguladora de Investigación Biomédica (Ley N° 9234), Articles 48, 51, 15; Hoja inscripción de protocolo de investigación biomédica (CONIS-FORM-34).
q_5_5_directa: Yes. Participants have the right to receive, free of charge, the preventive, therapeutic, and diagnostic treatments generated by the study, if they are shown to benefit their health, for as long as they need them.
q_5_5_ampliada: The sponsor may only discontinue this access if the medicine ceases to be effective, if its development is discontinued, if the investigator certifies that it is not essential to the participant's health (and alternatives exist), or if the patient does not consent to continuing treatment. Extended-access or compassionate-use programs are subject to CEC approval and to the same liability requirements as the original research.
q_5_5_fuente: Ley Reguladora de Investigación Biomédica (Ley N° 9234), Article 53; Reglamento a la Ley Reguladora de Investigación Biomédica (Decreto N° 39061-S), Articles 3, 62.
q_6_1_directa: Yes. The applicable law is Ley N° 8968, the "Ley de Protección de la Persona frente al Tratamiento de sus Datos Personales" [Law on the Protection of Individuals with Regard to the Processing of Their Personal Data].
q_6_1_ampliada: This law prohibits the processing of sensitive data (such as health-related data), except for exceptions such as the need for medical prevention or diagnosis. CROs must comply with this law, and the sponsor must ensure the integrity, accuracy, reliability, consistency, and confidentiality of all information handled. The Agencia de Protección de Datos de los Habitantes (Data Protection Agency, Prodhab) is the body with maximum administrative autonomy responsible for overseeing compliance with this regulation.
q_6_1_fuente: Ley de Protección de la Persona frente al Tratamiento de sus Datos Personales (Ley N° 8968), Articles 2, 9, 15; Reglamento a la Ley Reguladora de Investigación Biomédica (Decreto N° 39061-S), Article 28; Reglamento de Buenas Prácticas de Farmacovigilancia (Decreto N° 39417-S), Article 12.7.
q_6_2_directa: Yes. The Regulation implementing Ley N° 9234 sets out specific requirements for vaccines and medicines in the submission package, including presentation of the Investigational New Drug (IND) exemption or its equivalent, a Good Manufacturing Practice certificate, and strict Spanish-language labeling requirements.
q_6_2_ampliada: The Regulation implementing the Ley Reguladora de Investigación Biomédica (Decreto N° 39061-S, Art. 44) establishes that, for vaccines and medicines, the IND (Investigational New Drug) or an equivalent document issued by the FDA, EMA, or another recognized agency must be submitted. A Good Manufacturing Practice certificate for the manufacturing establishment, issued by the regulatory authority of the manufacturing country, is also required. In addition, the Spanish-language label must include the pharmaceutical form, route of administration, batch number, expiry date, dosage, storage conditions, and participant details. These biological products are also subject to mandatory submission of Periodic Safety Reports (IPS).
q_6_2_fuente: Reglamento a la Ley Reguladora de Investigación Biomédica (Decreto N° 39061-S), Article 44, items h), r), and s); Reglamento de Buenas Prácticas de Farmacovigilancia (Decreto N° 39417-S), Article 12.8.
q_6_3_directa: Yes, the use and transfer of biological samples are regulated by Chapter III of Ley N° 9234 and Reglamento N° 39061-S.
q_6_3_ampliada: The regulation specifies that transferring any biological sample outside the country requires a Material Transfer Agreement (ATMB) signed by the legal authorities and investigators of both institutions. Informed consent must specifically authorize the collection, transfer, and future uses of the samples. Samples will only be retained for as long as necessary for the purposes that justified their collection, unless explicit consent is given for other uses.
q_6_3_fuente: Ley Reguladora de Investigación Biomédica (Ley N° 9234), Articles 19, 21, 22; Reglamento a la Ley Reguladora de Investigación Biomédica (Decreto N° 39061-S), Article 11.
q_6_4_directa: Yes. Reglamento N° 39061-S includes specific requirements for: research with Biomedical Equipment and Material (EMB), the use of placebo, and vulnerable groups such as minors, indigenous communities, and persons with mental disorders.
q_6_4_ampliada: For EMB, the principal investigator is required to be a professional appropriate to the product, and the protocol must include the equipment's expected useful life and the potential impact of its failure. For research involving patients with moderate or severe mental disorders, the participant's refusal to take part must be sufficient grounds for excluding them from participation, and the participant's autonomy must be respected, even with the legal equality guarantor present.
q_6_4_fuente: Ley Reguladora de Investigación Biomédica (Ley N° 9234), Articles 63, 66; Reglamento a la Ley Reguladora de Investigación Biomédica (Decreto N° 39061-S), Articles 52, 64, 72, 73, 68, 69.

q_1_1_directa: The National Regulatory Authority (NRA) for clinical trials is the Centro para el Control Estatal de Medicamentos, Equipos y Dispositivos Médicos (State Center for the Control of Medicines, Equipment and Medical Devices, CECMED), under the Ministry of Public Health.
q_1_1_ampliada: CECMED's mission is to promote and protect public health through an effective, transparent system of regulation, oversight, and sanitary surveillance that ensures medicines, equipment and medical devices, services, and other health products are safe, effective, and of good quality. One of its functions is to authorize clinical trials and other biomedical research in humans involving health products and procedures, and to issue the corresponding certifications and rulings.
q_1_1_fuente: RESOLUCIÓN No. 435 (MINSAP, 2017) (Article 2, Article 6, Article 9); RESOLUCIÓN No. 14/18 (CENCEC, 2018) (Article 1, Article 9).
q_1_2_directa: Health research is governed by Ley No. 165, the "Ley de la Salud Pública" [Public Health Act] of 2023 (in force since January 2026), and its implementing regulation, in the chapter on Science and Innovation. Clinical trials must comply with Good Clinical Practice (GCP) requirements, and Cuba has accordingly adopted the harmonized ICH E6(R2) Good Clinical Practice guideline.
q_1_2_ampliada: Ley 165 establishes that the Ministry of Public Health (MINSAP) regulates and controls health research. Clinical trials must ensure their rigor and transparency by complying with Good Clinical Practice standards, which seek to guarantee the protection of subjects' rights, safety, and well-being, as well as the credibility of the data.
q_1_2_fuente: Ley No. 165 (Ley de la Salud Pública), Article 183; Decreto 133/2025 (Reglamentario de la Ley 165 de la Salud Pública), Article 176; Lineamiento armonizado ICH E6(R2) - Buena Práctica Clínica; RESOLUCIÓN No. 435 (MINSAP, 2017), Article 14.
q_1_3_directa: The main clinical trial regulations follow a clear hierarchy: Ley No. 165 on Public Health is the general framework, RESOLUCIÓN No. 435/17 of MINSAP is the specific implementing regulation, and RESOLUCIÓN No. 14/18 of CENCEC is the implementation procedure. The GCP standards (Res. 165/2000) and the Ethics Committee standards (Res. 40/2014) are cross-cutting quality and ethics standards.
q_1_3_ampliada: The legal structure of clinical research in Cuba is organized in a pyramidal fashion, starting with Ley 165 on Public Health, which establishes MINSAP's non-delegable oversight role. To directly regulate research involving human subjects, MINSAP's Resolución 435/2017 serves as the framework regulation defining institutional responsibilities and approval requirements. To operationalize this regulation, CENCEC issued Resolución 14/2018, which details the practical procedures, time frames, and forms applicable to every sponsor. CECMED's Regulación 21-08 sets out the specific requirements for authorizing and modifying clinical trials. MINSAP's Resolución 40/2014 regulates the establishment and operation of Research Ethics Committees. The entire research cycle must comply with the scientific quality guidelines set by the Regulatory Authority and the bioethical standards established for Research Ethics Committees.
q_1_3_fuente: Ley No. 165 (Ley de la Salud Pública), Article 183; RESOLUCIÓN No. 435 (MINSAP, 2017), First, Article 2; RESOLUCIÓN No. 14/18 (CENCEC, 2018), First, Article 1; REGULACIÓN 21-08 CECMED; RESOLUCIÓN No. 40 (MINSAP, 2014).
q_1_4_directa: Yes, every clinical trial, regardless of the intervention, must have the approval of a Research Ethics Committee (CEI) at each participating institution before it may be conducted.
q_1_4_ampliada: The CEI is an independent body responsible for ensuring the protection of the rights, safety, and well-being of the human subjects involved, as well as for reviewing and approving the protocol and the informed consent materials. The CEI must issue an approval ruling before the research may be conducted.
q_1_4_fuente: Ley No. 165 (Ley de la Salud Pública), Article 183. RESOLUCIÓN No. 435 (MINSAP, 2017) (Article 5, Article 15); RESOLUCIÓN No. 14/18 (CENCEC, 2018) (Annex 1 - Research Ethics Committee Approval, Annex 2 - Second).
q_1_5_directa: Yes, Research Ethics Committee (CEI) approval does precede submission to the regulatory authority. Submission of the CEI's approval ruling is a mandatory requirement and must be attached to the clinical trial authorization application submitted to CECMED.
q_1_5_ampliada: The regulation establishes that CEI approval is a requirement for conducting the trial, but does not define its exact place in the national approval sequence. However, Article 20 of Resolución 14/18 indicates that the "Initial Control Form" is sent to CENCEC in the month the protocol is submitted to the CEI. Since this form is part of the file CENCEC evaluates for MINSAP's approval, it can be inferred that ethical review must begin at least in parallel. In addition, regulations for medical devices do require CEI endorsement letters as part of the initial application. Sponsors should therefore treat submission to the CEI as an early, critical step in the overall timeline.
q_1_5_fuente: RESOLUCIÓN No. 435 (MINSAP, 2017) (Article 6, Article 15); RESOLUCIÓN No. 14/18 (CENCEC, 2018) (Annex 2).
q_1_6_directa: The country has a mandatory evaluation and registration system for institutional Research Ethics Committees. Each committee is strictly required to be listed in the National Registry of Research Ethics Committees. The body that oversees CEI operations is the National Commission on Research Ethics, through ministerial regulations.
q_1_6_ampliada: The technical operation of Ethics Committees in Cuba is standardized and rigorously supervised at the national level. Institutions are required by regulation to comply with the guidelines of MINSAP's Resolución 40/2014, and must hold the corresponding registration code in the National Registry of Research Ethics Committees. The enactment of Ley 165 on Public Health has recently strengthened this system of ethical control and oversight. Together with Resolución 145/2025, the new legal framework establishes and regulates the National Commission on Medical Ethics as the highest cross-cutting governing body in this area. Accordingly, for a local CEI to be accredited to evaluate protocols, it must demonstrate its fitness through a formal founding resolution and strict adherence to standardized operating procedures.
q_1_6_fuente: Ley No. 165 (Ley de la Salud Pública), Article 13; Resolución 145/2025 "Procedimiento para la constitución y funcionamiento de la Comisión Nacional de Ética Médica". RESOLUCIÓN No. 435 (MINSAP, 2017) (Fourth); RESOLUCIÓN No. 14/18 (CENCEC, 2018) (Article 6, Annex 2).
q_1_7_directa: Current health regulations do not provide for a centralized, publicly accessible registry dedicated to Research Ethics Committees. While committees are subject to an internal national control registry, their organizational data does not constitute a list open to the general public. The level of public transparency rests instead with the platform for registering the clinical trials themselves.
q_1_7_ampliada: In Cuba's regulatory ecosystem, the principle of transparency in clinical research is primarily embodied by the Registro Público Cubano de Ensayos Clínicos (Cuban Public Registry of Clinical Trials, RPCEC). This primary registry is intended for the mandatory disclosure of protocol information and results to the international community. Regarding CEIs, the Ministry of Public Health exercises oversight through the National Commission on Medical Ethics and the internal National Registry of such committees. However, this database is used for regulatory, methodological, and institutional purposes and is not publicly accessible. Sponsors and authorities therefore have full access to a CEI's credentials and procedures when submitting studies, but the law does not require their publication on a freely accessible public portal.
q_1_7_fuente: Resolución 145/2025 "Procedimiento para la constitución y funcionamiento de la Comisión Nacional de Ética Médica". RESOLUCIÓN No. 165 (MINSAP, 2000), Items 3.2.1, 3.4. RESOLUCIÓN No. 14/18 (CENCEC, 2018), Article 25.
q_1_8_directa: Yes, current regulations mandate that all research involving human subjects have the express authorization of the National Regulatory Authority (NRA) before it begins. No clinical research, regardless of its origin or phase, may enroll participants without the Ministry of Public Health's feasibility and relevance approval and the NRA's authorization.
q_1_8_ampliada: Cuban legislation clearly establishes that the Ministry of Public Health holds the non-delegable legal authority to regulate and control all health research. Specifically, the Reglamento de los Ensayos Clínicos [Clinical Trial Regulation] defines and subjects to state control any inquiry involving human subjects aimed at verifying the clinical effects of an investigational product. It is therefore an unavoidable legal requirement to obtain the approval of MINSAP's Management Council before any study begins within the health network. In parallel, the protocol must meet the rigorous technical, analytical, and safety parameters validated by the National Drug Regulatory Authority (CECMED). This two-tier evaluation ensures that every product or device under trial is methodologically justified before patient recruitment proceeds.
q_1_8_fuente: Ley No. 165 (Ley de la Salud Pública), Article 183; RESOLUCIÓN No. 435 (MINSAP, 2017) (Article 1, Article 6); RESOLUCIÓN No. 14/18 (CENCEC, 2018) (Article 9).
q_2_1_directa: Yes. The "Promotor" (sponsor) is the individual, company, institution, or organization responsible for the initiation, management, and/or financing of a clinical trial.
q_2_1_ampliada: The sponsor is the party responsible for establishing and maintaining the quality assurance and quality control systems throughout the clinical trial. Its involvement may include financing assumed by the implementing healthcare institutions, particularly if the clinical trial proposal is submitted outside the regular calls for proposals.
q_2_1_fuente: RESOLUCIÓN No. 435 (MINSAP, 2017) (Article 5, Article 7); RESOLUCIÓN No. 14/18 (CENCEC, 2018) (Annex 1 - Sponsor, Quality Assurance).
q_2_2_directa: The regulation does not specify a need for foreign sponsors to have a local legal representative. However, the mandatory engagement of CENCEC to conduct the trial functionally fulfills this role, acting as the Cuba-domiciled legal entity responsible for the study.
q_2_2_ampliada: Unlike other jurisdictions that require a foreign sponsor to appoint a local legal representative, the Cuban framework establishes a broader requirement: mandatory engagement of CENCEC to conduct and manage the trial. In practice, CENCEC becomes the contractual and legal counterpart of the foreign sponsor within Cuba, assuming operational responsibility before the National Health System. This eliminates the need for the sponsor to establish its own legal entity in the country, but makes negotiating the services contract with CENCEC a fundamental strategic step. Cuban sponsors, by contrast, contract directly with the Regulatory Authority, CECMED, and may choose to engage CENCEC to conduct the proposed clinical trial.
q_2_2_fuente: RESOLUCIÓN No. 435 (MINSAP, 2017) (Article 3, Article 20); RESOLUCIÓN No. 14/18 (CENCEC, 2018) (Article 2).
q_2_3_directa: Yes. The sponsor must establish and maintain the trial's quality assurance and quality control systems, use qualified medical staff for advice, and obtain the investigator's/institution's commitment to conduct the trial in accordance with GCP. It must also appoint suitably qualified monitors, carry out systematic audits, and manage the proper supply of the investigational product.
q_2_3_ampliada: The sponsor must establish and maintain quality assurance and quality control systems, developing written standard operating procedures. Before the trial begins, it must ensure that the clinical and non-clinical information supports the proposed trial, providing an up-to-date Investigator's Brochure. It is the sponsor's obligation to appoint suitably qualified monitors, carry out systematic audits, and manage the proper supply and handling of the investigational product. It must also document the trial's financial aspects through a contract between the parties, and ensure sufficient preclinical data exist to support administering the product to humans. In the event of any serious or persistent non-compliance by sites or investigators, the sponsor must intervene immediately and suspend or withdraw the offending site's participation.
q_2_4_directa: Yes. If the sponsor transfers functions to a Contract Research Organization (CRO), this transfer must be specified in writing, and the sponsor must ensure that the CRO has quality assurance and quality control in place for the clinical trial.
q_2_4_ampliada: Transferring functions to the CRO does not exempt the sponsor from ultimate responsibility. Agreements between the sponsor, the CRO, and the investigator/institution must allow the sponsor and regulatory authorities to monitor, audit, and inspect the trial. In Cuba, CRO functions are assigned to the Centro Nacional Coordinador de Ensayos Clínicos (National Coordinating Center for Clinical Trials, CENCEC).
q_2_4_fuente: RESOLUCIÓN No. 14/18 (CENCEC, 2018) (Annex 1 - Contract Research Organization, 6.2, 6.1.2).
q_2_5_directa: Yes, research sites or units must belong to the network of institutions of the National Health System, which is entirely public and accessible. They must also reliably demonstrate that they have the infrastructure, equipment, and technological capacity required by the protocol.
q_2_5_ampliada: Every proposed hospital or site must first submit a formal institutional endorsement accepting the conduct of the study and guaranteeing its technical feasibility. The regulation requires the site to prepare its facilities and support services (such as pharmacy and laboratories) to comply with Good Clinical Practice (GCP) guidelines. The study monitor is responsible for continuously verifying on-site that the site's capabilities remain adequate for the duration of the research. The local Ethics Committee also assesses the suitability and safety of the facilities where participants will be treated.
q_2_5_fuente: RESOLUCIÓN No. 435 (MINSAP, 2017) (Article 4); RESOLUCIÓN No. 14/18 (CENCEC, 2018) (Annex 1 - 6.6.1, 6.18.4, Annex 2 - Fourth).
q_2_6_directa: Yes, the regulation requires that the selection of the principal investigator and their collaborators be rigorously based on their technical and moral qualifications. They must have the education, specialized training, and demonstrable clinical experience needed to take on the ethical and scientific conduct of the study. The sponsor and the ethics committee are responsible for evaluating these credentials before the study begins.
q_2_6_ampliada: The sponsor has direct, non-delegable responsibility for selecting each principal investigator and the participating institutions. This selection is based on the candidate's academic credentials, resources, and professional track record. The investigator is required to demonstrate a real potential to recruit the required number of subjects within the planned time frame, based on the site's retrospective morbidity data. Before formalizing any contractual agreement, the sponsor must provide the full protocol and the Investigator's Brochure so the candidate can assess the study's scientific and operational feasibility. The selected investigator must sign a written commitment to comply with Good Clinical Practice, follow the data reporting procedures, and allow free access for monitoring and audits at the research site.
q_2_7_directa: Yes. The sponsor must insure or indemnify (legal and financial coverage) the investigator/institution against claims, and the sponsor's procedures must cover the costs of treating trial subjects in the event of harm arising from the trial, in accordance with current regulatory requirements.
q_2_7_ampliada: This obligation excludes harm arising from negligence and/or malpractice by the investigator/institution. Any compensation received by trial subjects must comply with current regulatory requirements as to method and form.
q_3_1_directa: Yes. The clinical trial proposal is submitted through information forms via CENCEC. For formal approval, the sponsor must submit the Model Description of Clinical Trial Characteristics and Declaration of Required Resources (Annex No. 3) and the Report on the Feasibility and Relevance of the Clinical Trial (Annex No. 4).
q_3_1_ampliada:
These forms contain detailed information such as: title, product, indication, phase, sample size, expected start date, list of clinical sites, and a summary of the financial resources to be provided by both the sponsor and MINSAP. The feasibility report must include the sponsor's assessment of the study's relevance to the Health System.

For the evaluation and subsequent authorization issued by the NRA, the following must be submitted: the clinical trial authorization application form, the institution's Research Ethics Committee approval ruling, MINSAP's endorsement, and the dossier compiled according to the investigational product's stage of development, its degree of novelty, and the type of product, organized in blocks of information generally divided into four parts: Part I: Administrative Information; Part II: Chemical-Pharmaceutical and Biological Information; Part III: Non-Clinical Information (Pharmacology and Toxicology); and Part IV: Clinical Information (Results of prior studies and the current protocol).
q_3_1_fuente: RESOLUCIÓN No. 435 (MINSAP, 2017) (Article 8); RESOLUCIÓN No. 14/18 (CENCEC, 2018) (Article 12, Annexes 3 and 4).
q_3_2_directa: Clinical trial authorization applications are submitted to CECMED's Department for the Receipt and Pre-Evaluation of Filings, directly by the sponsor or by the contract research organization (CENCEC). The information may be submitted in print, in digital format, or uploaded to the cloud repository set up for filings at the website: https://nc.cecmed.cu.
q_3_2_ampliada: CECMED is the authority that receives and evaluates the clinical trial authorization application. The sponsor or CENCEC, in its role as contract research organization, files the documentation through one of three available channels: printed submission, digital files, or upload to the institutional cloud repository enabled at https://nc.cecmed.cu. Prior to this stage, the proposed healthcare units must have sent CENCEC their endorsement accepting the trial, and the feasibility evaluation results must have been submitted to MINSAP's Management Council for its agreement.
q_3_2_fuente: RESOLUCIÓN No. 435 (MINSAP, 2017) (Article 8, Article 9); RESOLUCIÓN No. 14/18 (CENCEC, 2018) (Article 13, Article 17).
q_3_3_directa: Under current CECMED regulations, clinical trial authorization applications receive a response within no more than 90 days of the filing being submitted. If inconsistencies are found during the file's evaluation or additional information is required, the sponsor is asked for a completion submission, for which it has up to 120 days to respond. Once the response is received, the NRA has up to 75 days, counted from submission of the completion, to issue its decision.
q_3_3_ampliada: If the initial documentation is rejected (not accepted), the sponsor has five business days to correct and resubmit the deficiencies to CENCEC. The sponsor must also submit its initial information within no more than ten business days of the call for proposals being launched.
q_3_3_fuente: RESOLUCIÓN No. 435 (MINSAP, 2017) (Article 9); RESOLUCIÓN No. 14/18 (CENCEC, 2018) (Article 12, Article 15, Article 16).
q_3_4_directa: Yes, the fees set out in the NRA's list of services must be paid. CECMED's official price list for Scientific-Technical Services and the applicable fees are published on CECMED's website (Fee Schedule).
q_3_4_ampliada: CECMED publishes a Fee Schedule with the official price list for the Scientific-Technical Services applicable to its regulatory procedures, including clinical trial evaluation. The list is publicly accessible through CECMED's portal. Cuba's clinical trial model includes the "commercialization of scientific-technical services" by CENCEC, governed by a separate services contract for conducting, monitoring, and operationally coordinating the trial within the National Health System. Sponsors must therefore budget for two components: CECMED's regulatory fees and CENCEC's contractual fees.
q_3_4_fuente: RESOLUCIÓN No. 435 (MINSAP, 2017) (Article 20, Article 23, Third); RESOLUCIÓN No. 14/18 (CENCEC, 2018).
q_3_5_directa: Yes, this is mandatory. Every clinical trial must be registered in CENCEC's Cuban Public Registry of Clinical Trials before the first participant is enrolled.
q_3_5_ampliada: The Cuban Public Registry of Clinical Trials is a WHO primary registry and is governed by WHO guidelines. The sponsor must complete the application (forms in Spanish and English) within no more than seven business days of the process starting. Failure to meet this deadline results in cancellation of the application and may lead to a halt in patient enrollment in the trial.
q_3_5_fuente: RESOLUCIÓN No. 435 (MINSAP, 2017) (Article 16); RESOLUCIÓN No. 14/18 (CENCEC, 2018) (Article 25, Article 26, Article 77).
q_3_6_directa: Yes. CECMED's Resolución 78/2023 establishes the practice of regulatory reliance in Cuba, whereby CECMED takes into account the decisions of another regulatory authority or international body when making its own regulatory decisions, while retaining independence and responsibility for the decisions it makes.
q_3_6_ampliada: CECMED's Resolución 78/2023 approves and brings into force, for all regulatory functions, the practice of regulatory reliance. CECMED applies this principle to the decisions and processes of Regional Reference National Regulatory Authorities certified by the Pan American Health Organization, Authorities listed by WHO, and any National Regulatory Authorities with which bilateral agreements establishing this exist. Vaccines and other WHO-prequalified medical products are recognized by CECMED, and expedited approval procedures apply to them. This framework does not exempt products from national evaluation: CECMED retains independence and responsibility for its decisions, but it allows evaluations to be accelerated and simplified when a prior ruling already exists from a recognized regulatory authority.
q_3_6_fuente: Resolución 78/2023 CECMED, Resolving Clauses First and Second; RESOLUCIÓN No. 435 (MINSAP, 2017), Article 2, Article 6, Article 14.
q_3_7_directa: The process begins with MINSAP's Call for Proposals, followed by Submission of Documentation to CENCEC, Feasibility Evaluation, Higher-Level Approval (MINSAP), Ethical Approval (CEI), Public Registration, and, finally, Execution/Patient Enrollment.
q_3_7_ampliada:
The authorization flow is summarized in the following documented steps:

Annual Call for Proposals: MINSAP, through the Directorate of Science and Technological Innovation, issues two calls for proposals per year to evaluate submissions.

Proposal Submission (Sponsor): The sponsor sends CENCEC the information forms, including the Resource Description Model and the Feasibility and Relevance Report (Annexes 3 and 4), within no more than ten business days of the call for proposals.

Institutional Endorsement (Healthcare Unit): Healthcare institutions submit their endorsement accepting the trial to CENCEC (Annex 5).

Documentary Review (CENCEC): CENCEC reviews the submitted information and communicates its outcome (accepted/not accepted) within up to ten business days. If not accepted, the sponsor has five business days to make corrections.

Feasibility Evaluation: CENCEC processes the information and submits it to the Directorate of Science and Technological Innovation for feasibility evaluation.

Higher-Level Approval (MINSAP): The results are submitted to MINSAP's Management Council, whose decision is communicated to the sponsor within no more than 7 business days.

Contracting: For foreign sponsors, CENCEC formalizes the work contracts with the healthcare institutions.

Ethical Approval (CEI): The protocol must be approved by the Research Ethics Committee of each participating institution.

Public Registration: The trial must be registered in CENCEC's Cuban Public Registry of Clinical Trials before the first participant is enrolled.

CECMED Authorization and Start Certificate: Once MINSAP's approval, the CEI's ruling, and the technical documentation — including the clinical protocol and the Investigator's Brochure — are in hand, the authorization application is submitted to CECMED, which evaluates all the information and issues its decision through the Clinical Trial Start Certificate.

Start of Execution and Inspection: With the Start Certificate, patient enrollment may begin. Based on a risk-based approach, the clinical trial is inspected by CECMED to verify adherence to the protocol and compliance with Good Clinical Practice.
q_3_7_fuente: RESOLUCIÓN No. 435 (MINSAP, 2017) (Articles 6, 7, 8, 9, 15, 16); RESOLUCIÓN No. 14/18 (CENCEC, 2018) (Articles 12, 13, 15, 26, 58).
q_4_1_directa: Yes. The investigational product must be labeled on the primary packaging, in indelible ink and in Spanish, identifying at least the sponsor, the trial, and the product, along with batch, expiry, dosage, and storage information. The label must also include the statements "Prohibida su venta" [Sale prohibited] and "Producto para uso exclusivo en investigación" [Product for research use only].
q_4_1_ampliada: The minimum information the label must contain is: identification of the sponsor, the clinical trial, and the investigational product, the expiry date, the protocol code, the product code, the batch number, the number of units, the pharmaceutical form, the route and dose of administration, and storage conditions. When the primary packaging does not have enough space, this information is printed on secondary packaging. The use of Spanish and indelible ink is intended to ensure traceability and the product's permanent legibility throughout the clinical handling chain, and the mandatory statements prevent any diversion into commercial channels. In blinded trials, the investigational product's coding system must include a mechanism allowing rapid identification in a medical emergency, without undetectably breaking the blind. The sponsor must also inform all parties involved (monitors, investigators, pharmacists) of the appropriate storage temperatures, reconstitution, and infusion procedures.
q_4_1_fuente: RESOLUCIÓN No. 14/18 (CENCEC, 2018) (Annex 1 - 6.13.1, 6.13.5).
q_4_2_directa: Yes. Legal provisions and regulations establish that experimental medical products used in clinical trials must comply with Good Manufacturing Practice requirements. This is set out in Annex 07, "Good Manufacturing Practice for Investigational Pharmaceutical Products," part of Regulación 16-2012, "Guidelines on Good Manufacturing Practice for Pharmaceutical Products," issued under CECMED's Resolución 156/2012.
q_4_2_ampliada: Compliance with GMP is essential to ensure the IP has characteristics appropriate to the product's stage of development. The sponsor must keep records of batch samples and analyses, ensuring sufficient quantities of the IP are retained to reconfirm specifications if necessary.
q_4_2_fuente: Regulación 16-2012 CECMED, Annex 07; Resolución CECMED 156/2012; RESOLUCIÓN No. 14/18 (CENCEC, 2018), Annex 1, items 6.13.1 and 6.14.5.
q_4_3_directa: Clinical trial authorization does not automatically grant permission to import the investigational product. The application to import the investigational product, comparator, and/or supplementary supplies for use in a clinical trial must be submitted to CECMED in accordance with the applicable regulations (Resolución No. 131/2015, "Regulation for the Sanitary Control of Imports of Medicines for Human Use").
q_4_3_ampliada: The national legal system, led by Ley 165 on Public Health, separates evaluation of the clinical design from foreign trade operations. The Ministry of Public Health directly and restrictively controls the import of medicines and other substances to safeguard national sanitary security. In practice, this process is governed by the Regulation for the Sanitary Control of Imports issued by CECMED. This provision stipulates that, before the product is shipped to Cuban territory, the importer must formally request documentary authorization for the clinical batch. During this customs procedure, the authorities verify that the product has prior research endorsement and meets the required storage conditions. If the foreign sponsor lacks this specific document, the General Customs Office of the Republic will block clearance and release to hospitals.
q_4_3_fuente: Resolución 131/2015 CECMED; RESOLUCIÓN No. 165 (MINSAP, 2000), Item 6.14.1; Ley No. 165 (Ley de la Salud Pública), Article 277.
q_5_1_directa: Yes. The sponsor must report Serious Adverse Events (SAEs) and Serious Unexpected Adverse Reactions (RASI) to CECMED. Although the general resolutions only require "prompt" notification, specific CECMED technical guidelines set out the exact time frames and procedures.
q_5_1_ampliada: Responsibility for pharmacovigilance in Cuba rests with CECMED, which is therefore the regulatory authority to which clinical trial adverse events must be reported. CECMED's Regulación 45-2007 establishes that the adverse event report must be submitted to CECMED as soon as possible and no later than 7 calendar days if the adverse event is fatal or life-threatening to the subject; otherwise, the reporting time frame is 15 days. The regulation also describes the information the submitted documentation must contain. The report form must be completed by the responsible investigator or principal investigator, and submitting it to CECMED is the sponsor's responsibility.
q_5_1_fuente: REGULACION No. 45-2007 CECMED; RESOLUCIÓN No. 14/18 (CENCEC, 2018), Annex 1, Definitions, Execution, items 6.16.2 and 6.17.1.
q_5_2_directa: Yes, the sponsor must submit all periodic reports and safety updates to the regulatory authorities, as required under current regulatory requirements.
q_5_2_ampliada: The annual and interim reports required by the CEI and the regulatory authorities are considered essential documents that must be kept on file by the sponsor and at the institution. In addition to these reports, the sponsor has an ongoing obligation to assess the safety of the investigational product.
q_5_2_fuente: RESOLUCIÓN No. 14/18 (CENCEC, 2018) (Annex 1 - 6.17.2, Trial Execution, 6.16.1).
q_5_3_directa: Yes, the sponsor is responsible for submitting to CENCEC, on a quarterly basis, the information required for national oversight of trials. In addition, implementing healthcare institutions must send CENCEC information on the status of ongoing trials at the close of each month.
q_5_3_ampliada: The monthly information submitted by institutions is provided using the Periodic Clinical Trial Control Form (Annex No. 7). If implementing institutions fail to submit the information to CENCEC within the established time frame, CENCEC will order the trial halted until the update is received.
q_5_3_fuente: RESOLUCIÓN No. 435 (MINSAP, 2017) (Article 11, Article 12); RESOLUCIÓN No. 14/18 (CENCEC, 2018) (Article 23, Article 22).
q_5_4_directa: Yes. Regulación 21-08, "Requirements for Authorizing and Modifying Clinical Trials," classifies amendments or modifications as minor or major. Any modification to the protocol, the Case Report Form (CRD), or the Informed Consent (CI) template requires CEI approval, as well as approval/authorization/notification of the modifications by the regulatory authority (CECMED).
q_5_4_ampliada: A request to modify the ruling issued by the Directorate of Science and Technological Innovation must be submitted to CENCEC for reconciliation. A modification involving the addition of new clinical sites must be evaluated for feasibility and requires the new healthcare unit's acceptance endorsement.
q_5_4_fuente: REGULACIÓN 21-08 CECMED; RESOLUCIÓN No. 435 (MINSAP, 2017), Article 10; RESOLUCIÓN No. 14/18 (CENCEC, 2018), Annex 1 - Trial Execution, Article 19.
q_5_5_directa: Yes, the principal investigator has an obligation to arrange for the research subject to continue treatment and care after the study ends, seeking to avoid side effects arising from discontinuing the intervention.
q_5_5_ampliada: Post-trial access to the intervention must be considered from the design stage of the research, based on the subject's safety and well-being. The informed consent the participant signs before the study must detail the continuing medical treatment they will have access to. All of this must be reflected in the documents ruled on by the Research Ethics Committee. For situations where medical necessity arises outside the protocol's context, CECMED approved Regulación 63-2012, which allows the exceptional use of investigational products under a compassionate-use regime. This mechanism requires an approving ruling from the Ethics Committee and demonstration of a positive risk-benefit balance derived from the study's earlier phases.
q_5_5_fuente: REGULACION No. 63-2012. RESOLUCIÓN No. 14/18 (CENCEC, 2018) (Annex 1 - 6.8.2, Trial Termination).
q_6_1_directa: Not specified in official regulations.
q_6_1_ampliada: Although Good Clinical Practice requires that subjects' rights, integrity, and confidentiality be protected, and requires security systems for handling automated data to prevent unauthorized access, no specific Cuban personal data protection law applicable to research is named.
q_6_1_fuente: RESOLUCIÓN No. 14/18 (CENCEC, 2018) (Annex 1 - RESOLUCIÓN No. 165 (MINSAP, 2000), 6.5.3).
q_6_2_directa: Yes. Regulación 21-08, "Requirements for Authorizing and Modifying Clinical Trials," in its Annex 4, "General Considerations for the Clinical Evaluation of Vaccines," sets out the requirements for vaccine clinical trials.
q_6_2_ampliada: The general regulatory framework applies to pharmaceutical and biotechnological products and "any other health technology," and includes biologics and vaccines as a specific product classification. In addition to this general framework, CECMED's Regulación 21-08 devotes its Annex 4 to general considerations for the clinical evaluation of vaccines, setting out the specific technical requirements for this type of trial.
q_6_2_fuente: REGULACIÓN 21-08 CECMED, Annex 4; RESOLUCIÓN No. 435 (MINSAP, 2017), Article 1; RESOLUCIÓN No. 14/18 (CENCEC, 2018), Annex 6.
q_6_3_directa: Yes, the handling and movement of bodily samples in clinical research are governed by bioethical and sanitary rules in the country. The new Ley 165 on Public Health establishes the core protective framework regarding consent and handling in the donation of biological cellular material. In addition, when research requires moving such samples internationally, specific high-biosafety and customs-control resolutions apply, overseen by the State.
q_6_3_ampliada: The handling of bodily extractions and remains is today grounded in the bioethical safeguards enshrined in the modern Ley 165 on Public Health. This legislation governs the donation, safekeeping, and clinical or research use of organs, fluids, tissues, and cells, requiring explicit consent in all cases. At the same time, the Good Clinical Practice framework requires principal investigators to rigorously record the exact location and identifying codes of all stored biological fluids intended for retrospective analysis. It is essential to note that, when a study design requires exporting or importing such samples, the Regulation for the Control of Cross-Border Movement of Biological Material (Resolución 07/2008) applies. This statute imposes an expedited procedure managed before the national health authority (BRPS), which validates the purpose of the research and certifies the microbiological safeguarding of the transfer. Under these operational guidelines, the international transit of genomic information or human tissue is prohibited without prior tracking and state authorization.
q_6_3_fuente: Ley No. 165 (Ley de la Salud Pública), Article 147; Resolución No. 07/2008 (BRPS), Articles 4, 8. RESOLUCIÓN No. 14/18 (CENCEC, 2018), Annex 1.
q_6_4_directa: Yes. CECMED has established specific regulations: Resolución 54/2020 and Regulación M 75-20, on Emergency Use Authorization of investigational medicines and biological products for human use; and Regulación 18-2007, on the requirements for bioavailability and bioequivalence studies.
q_6_4_ampliada: Cuba's regulatory landscape includes supplementary guidelines for specific situations. For public health emergencies declared by the competent authorities, CECMED's Resolución 54/2020 and Regulación M 75-20 enable differentiated Emergency Use Authorization procedures for medicines, biological products, medical devices, and other health technologies, as well as for investigational products. Meanwhile, CECMED's Regulación 18-2007 sets out the requirements for bioavailability and bioequivalence studies, an indispensable condition for supporting therapeutic equivalence in certain developments. Through these specific regulatory instruments, the authority maintains stable, differentiated standards for highly complex interventions or health emergencies.
q_6_4_fuente: Resolución CECMED 54/2020; Regulación M 75-20 CECMED; Regulación 18-2007 CECMED; RESOLUCIÓN No. 435 (MINSAP, 2017), Article 23.

q_1_1_directa: The National Regulatory Authority (NRA) for clinical trials is the Agencia Nacional de Regulación, Control y Vigilancia Sanitaria (National Agency for Health Regulation, Control and Surveillance, ARCSA), the entity responsible for granting authorization.
q_1_1_ampliada: ARCSA, which has administrative, technical, operational, and financial autonomy, is responsible for the control and oversight of clinical trials. Although ARCSA grants regulatory authorization, ethical approval — granted by a Comité de Ética de Investigación en Seres Humanos (Research Ethics Committee for Human Subjects, CEISH) — is an indispensable requirement prior to authorization.
q_1_1_fuente: Reglamento para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos (Acuerdo Ministerial Nro. 00069-2024) (Art. 3, Art. 4, Art. 6, Art. 79); Decreto Ejecutivo 1290 (Art. 10, item 8); Reglamento sustitutivo del Reglamento Para la Aprobación y Seguimiento de Comités de Ética (CEISH y CEAS) (Art. 4, Art. 7, Art. 8, Art. 9); Reglamento para la aprobación, desarrollo, vigilancia y control de investigaciones observacionales y estudios de intervención en seres humanos (Art. 8); Reglamento General a la Ley Orgánica de Protección de Datos Personales (Art. 79).
q_1_2_directa: The main regulations include the Constitución de la República del Ecuador, the Ley Orgánica de Salud (Organic Health Law, LOS), and international ethical standards such as the Declaration of Helsinki and the CIOMS International Ethical Guidelines.
q_1_2_ampliada: The Ley Orgánica de Salud establishes the Ministry of Public Health's responsibility to participate in health science and technology research and development, under bioethical principles and safeguarding human rights (LOS, Art. 32). It also guarantees that every person has the right not to be subjected to tests, clinical trials, or research without their prior knowledge and written consent (LOS, Art. 7).
q_1_2_fuente: Reglamento para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos (Acuerdo Ministerial Nro. 00069-2024) (Art. 6); Ley Orgánica de Salud (Art. 7); Ley Orgánica para la atención integral de Cáncer (Arts. 35, 36 and Amending Provision); Reglamento sustitutivo del Reglamento Para la Aprobación y Seguimiento de Comités de Ética (CEISH y CEAS); Reglamento para la aprobación, desarrollo, vigilancia y control de investigaciones observacionales y estudios de intervención en seres humanos.
q_1_3_directa: The key regulation governing the authorization, conduct, and control of clinical trials with medicines and processed natural products for human use is the Reglamento para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos (Acuerdo Ministerial Nro. 00069-2024).
q_1_3_ampliada: This Regulation applies to clinical trials using products without sanitary registration in Ecuador, as well as to trials of already-registered products studying a new therapeutic indication, new route of administration, new strength, new pharmaceutical form, new dosage regimen, new combinations, bioavailability and bioequivalence, or any post-registration change requiring clinical data. This Regulation repeals the previous regulation, the "Reglamento para la Aprobación, Desarrollo, Vigilancia y Control de los ensayos clínicos," issued through Acuerdo Ministerial Nro. 0075 of May 19, 2017.
q_1_3_fuente: Reglamento para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos (Acuerdo Ministerial Nro. 00069-2024) (Recitals, Art. 2, Sole Repealing Provision).
q_1_4_directa: Yes, approval from a Comité de Ética de Investigación en Seres Humanos (CEISH) approved by the Ministry of Public Health (MSP) is an indispensable requirement before ARCSA can subsequently authorize the conduct of the clinical trial.
q_1_4_ampliada: CEISHs are responsible for evaluating the ethical, methodological, and legal aspects of research, in order to safeguard participants' dignity, rights, integrity, safety, and well-being. CEISH approval must be requested in advance by the principal investigator.
q_1_4_fuente: Reglamento para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos (Acuerdo Ministerial Nro. 00069-2024) (Art. 3, Art. 8); Reglamento sustitutivo del Reglamento Para la Aprobación y Seguimiento de Comités de Ética (CEISH y CEAS) (Art. 4).
q_1_5_directa: Yes, the CEISH's clinical trial approval letter is a mandatory requirement the sponsor must submit to ARCSA when requesting authorization.
q_1_5_ampliada: To apply for clinical trial authorization (described in Article 2, items 1 and 2 of the Clinical Trial Regulation), CEISH approval is one of the listed documentary requirements. It is important to understand the division of responsibilities in the evaluation. While ARCSA verifies that the CEISH approval letter, the protocol, and the informed consent have been submitted as indispensable elements of the dossier, the regulation states that substantive evaluation of the ethical and methodological content of these documents is the exclusive competence of the CEISH. This means ARCSA does not conduct a second substantive review of these aspects, instead relying on the prior evaluation of the MSP-accredited ethics committee. The quality and rigor of the CEISH's review are therefore decisive for the trial's integrity and eventual authorization.
q_1_5_fuente: Reglamento para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos (Acuerdo Ministerial Nro. 00069-2024) (Art. 10.3, Art. 10.4, Art. 10.5, Art. 10.15).
q_1_6_directa: Approval and oversight of CEISHs fall to the Ministry of Public Health (MSP). The MSP's Coordinación General de Sostenibilidad del Sistema y Recursos approves these committees, while the Dirección Nacional de Investigación en Salud monitors approved CEISHs.
q_1_6_ampliada: Under Acuerdo Ministerial No. 0005-2022, if the CEISH meets the requirements set out in the regulation, the MSP's Coordinación General de Sostenibilidad del Sistema y Recursos approves the committee, valid for five (5) years. Requirements for CEISH approval include the committee's multidisciplinary composition, an approved set of internal bylaws establishing its operation, and standardized operating procedures for the ethical evaluation of research.
q_1_6_fuente: Reglamento sustitutivo del Reglamento Para la Aprobación y Seguimiento de Comités de Ética (CEISH y CEAS), Art. 4; Acuerdo Ministerial No. 00005-2022.
q_1_7_directa: Yes, an official, freely searchable public registry exists listing all research ethics committees approved by the Ministry of Public Health. This registry is updated quarterly by the Dirección Nacional de Investigación en Salud.
q_1_7_ampliada: Ethics committees must obtain an operating authorization from the MSP to operate legally. The updated list of approved CEISHs is publicly available on the "Registro público de Comités de Ética de Investigación en Seres Humanos (CEISH) - MSP" [Public Registry of Research Ethics Committees for Human Subjects], an institutional dashboard managed by the MSP's Dirección Nacional de Investigación en Salud.
q_1_7_fuente: Reglamento sustitutivo del Reglamento Para la Aprobación y Seguimiento de Comités de Ética (CEISH y CEAS); Registro público de Comités de Ética de Investigación en Seres Humanos (CEISH) - MSP.
q_1_8_directa: Yes, all clinical trials covered by the Reglamento para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos con Medicamentos y Productos Naturales Procesados de Uso Medicinal de Uso Humano (Acuerdo Ministerial Nro. 0069-2024), as well as medical devices, must be authorized by ARCSA before being conducted in the country, including trials with unregistered products and those seeking new indications or significant modifications to already-registered products.
q_1_8_ampliada: The clinical trials that must be authorized are those described in Article 2, items 1 and 2. However, clinical trials with already-registered products, conducted under normal medical practice or post-marketing conditions (Article 2, item 3), only require a registration request to ARCSA and are not subject to evaluation and follow-up by that Agency.
q_1_8_fuente: Reglamento para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos (Acuerdo Ministerial Nro. 00069-2024) (Art. 2, Art. 4, Art. 8, Art. 10, Art. 11, Art. 12).
q_2_1_directa: Yes. The sponsor is defined as the individual, company, institution, or organization with legal representation in Ecuador, responsible for the organization, initiation, conduct, management, financing, and/or completion of the clinical trial.
q_2_1_ampliada: Under Article 3 of Acuerdo Ministerial 00069-2024, the sponsor bears full responsibility for the trial. If foreign, it must have a legal representative domiciled in the country or delegate its obligations to a Contract Research Organization (OIC/CRO) legally established in Ecuador.
q_2_1_fuente: Reglamento para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos (Acuerdo Ministerial Nro. 00069-2024), Art. 3.
q_2_2_directa: Yes. If the sponsor is foreign and has no presence in Ecuador, it must have a legal representative domiciled in the country and registered in the corresponding public registries, unless it delegates all its functions and obligations to a Contract Research Organization (OIC/CRO).
q_2_2_ampliada: If a CRO is delegated this role, it must be legally domiciled in the country, and the delegation must be recorded in a legalized contract or agreement. Foreign CROs must have a branch in Ecuador or maintain a contract with a CRO registered in the local National Registry.
q_2_2_fuente: Reglamento para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos (Acuerdo Ministerial Nro. 00069-2024) (Art. 10.2, Art. 91, Art. 104).
q_2_3_directa: Yes. The sponsor must establish and maintain a quality assurance and quality control system across all stages of data handling, have standard operating procedures (SOPs) in place, and have qualified staff for the trial's design, oversight, data management, and statistical analysis.
q_2_3_ampliada: The sponsor must guarantee the integrity, accuracy, reliability, and consistency of the data. It is responsible for filing all documentation and data obtained in the country for a minimum of fifteen (15) years after the study concludes, and must report protocol deviations and violations to ARCSA.
q_2_3_fuente: Reglamento para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos (Acuerdo Ministerial Nro. 00069-2024) (Art. 92, Art. 95, Art. 100).
q_2_4_directa: Yes. When the sponsor delegates tasks to a CRO, the CRO must be legally domiciled in the country, and the delegation must be formalized through a written agreement specifying the obligations and tasks transferred.
q_2_4_ampliada: The CRO must have a branch in Ecuador or a contract with a local CRO, be registered in ARCSA's National Registry of Contract Research Organizations, and have technical staff trained in Good Clinical Practice (GCP). Despite the delegation, ultimate responsibility for the conduct of the protocol and the clinical trial as a whole remains with the sponsor.
q_2_4_fuente: Reglamento para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos (Acuerdo Ministerial Nro. 00069-2024) (Art. 10.2, Art. 104, Art. 106, Art. 108).
q_2_5_directa: Yes. Clinical Research Sites (CIC) must be registered in ARCSA's National Registry of CICs, renewable every two years. Once the specific regulation is in place, CICs will also need to obtain an operating permit issued by the Agencia de Aseguramiento de la Calidad de Servicios de Salud y Medicina Prepagada (Healthcare and Prepaid Medicine Quality Assurance Agency, ACESS).
q_2_5_ampliada: CICs may be public or private. They must demonstrate suitable infrastructure, equipment, and competent staff. ARCSA carries out periodic inspections to verify compliance with Good Clinical Practice (GCP).
q_2_5_fuente: Reglamento para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos (Acuerdo Ministerial Nro. 00069-2024), Art. 112, 115.
q_2_6_directa: Yes. The principal investigator must be a healthcare professional with a graduate-level degree in the relevant field, hold valid licenses from the competent authorities, and demonstrate clinical trial experience and certified training in Good Clinical Practice (GCP) and research ethics.
q_2_6_ampliada: The investigator is responsible for conducting the study according to the protocol and protecting participants' integrity. They must have ethics training, ensure care for adverse events, and hold qualifications relevant to the area of the clinical research being conducted.
q_2_6_fuente: Reglamento para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos (Acuerdo Ministerial Nro. 00069-2024), Art. 115, 116.
q_2_7_directa: Yes. The sponsor must include, in its submission to ARCSA, a copy of an insurance policy issued by an institution legally registered in the country, covering the liability of all parties involved and providing for financial compensation and treatment for participants in the event of harm caused by the clinical trial. Coverage must extend for at least one year after the study ends.
q_2_7_ampliada: If the insurance policy proves insufficient, the sponsor is directly liable for the costs of any harm to participants' health, as well as financial losses arising from the clinical trial. The informed consent document must specify the policy's coverage and the contact information of the person responsible in the event of any incident. The sponsor must also ensure that the investigational product and trial-related procedures are provided to participants free of charge.
q_2_7_fuente: Reglamento para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos (Acuerdo Ministerial Nro. 00069-2024), Art. 56, 64, 98.
q_3_1_directa: Yes. The essential content for clinical trial authorization includes the formal application, the CEISH approval letter, the research Protocol, the CEISH-approved Informed Consent document, the Investigator's Brochure (IB), the manufacturer's Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) Certification, and a copy of the insurance policy.
q_3_1_ampliada: The application must also include information on the investigational product's quality, the draft labeling, a detailed list of medicines and supplies (Annex I), the clinical laboratory's quality management system certificate, the investigators' curricula vitae, the contracts/agreements with the CIC and the investigator, and the Case Report Form (CRD). If functions are delegated to a CRO, the legalized contract or agreement must be included.
q_3_1_fuente: Reglamento para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos (Acuerdo Ministerial Nro. 00069-2024) (Art. 10).
q_3_2_directa: Yes. Submission is digital, through the Quipux platform (or gob.ec), and requires a mandatory electronic signature on all official documents.
q_3_2_ampliada: Applications for clinical trial authorization are submitted digitally, through the Quipux document platform or via the institutional email address ARCSA designates for this purpose.
q_3_2_fuente: Reglamento para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos (Acuerdo Ministerial Nro. 00069-2024) (Art. 13).
q_3_3_directa: Yes. ARCSA issues its evaluation report within up to sixty (60) days, counted from verification that the application and the submitted documentation meet all requirements.
q_3_3_ampliada: If ARCSA requests modifications, the sponsor has ninety (90) days to respond, and may request an additional ninety (90) calendar days in justified cases. If the initial documentation is incomplete, the applicant has thirty (30) days (extendable by an additional 30 calendar days) to remedy the deficiencies before the application is archived.
q_3_3_fuente: Reglamento para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos (Acuerdo Ministerial Nro. 00069-2024) (Art. 14, Art. 15).
q_3_4_directa: Yes, good-practice certification or renewal processes, as well as other regulatory procedures, are subject to payment of the fees established under current regulations.
q_3_4_ampliada: The implementing regulation of the Ley Orgánica de Salud establishes that the Ministry of Public Health will set the fee for sanitary registration and re-registration, and for services rendered. The fees in effect for 2025 can be consulted at the corresponding link.
q_3_4_fuente: Normativa Técnica Sanitaria (ARCSA-DE-2022-008-AKRG) (Art. 5); Reglamento a la Ley Orgánica de Salud (Art. 9).
q_3_5_directa: Yes, the clinical trial must be registered before the first participant is enrolled, in a registry feeding into the World Health Organization's (WHO) International Clinical Trials Registry Platform (ICTRP) or in a registry approved by the International Committee of Medical Journal Editors (ICMJE).
q_3_5_ampliada: The sponsor must notify ARCSA of the registered clinical trial's identification code within ten (10) days of registration, and this code must be included in the informed consent documents. In addition, the research results must be included in the clinical trial registry within one (1) year of its completion.
q_3_5_fuente: Reglamento para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos (Acuerdo Ministerial Nro. 00069-2024) (Art. 87, Art. 89).
q_3_6_directa: Yes, ARCSA may evaluate guidelines or reports from other "high sanitary surveillance agencies" that have authorized clinical trials in which Ecuador participates. This is defined in Resolución ARCSA-DE-2023-025-AKRG, which lists the recognized bodies (PAHO/WHO Regional Reference Authorities, WHO Stringent Regulatory Authorities, South Korea's MFDS, and the EMA).
q_3_6_ampliada: Ecuador's regulatory authority may take into account and give significant weight to evaluations from another trusted authority or institution when making its own decision. On the ethics side, for multicenter studies, the local CEISH requires the investigator to submit the ethics committee approval from the country where the sponsor is based.
q_3_6_fuente: Reglamento para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos (Acuerdo Ministerial Nro. 00069-2024) (Art. 3, Art. 7); Reglamento Comités Ética Investigación Seres Humanos (Art. 8.m), Resolución ARCSA-DE-2023-025-AKRG.
q_3_7_directa: The process is sequential and requires prior ethical approval (CEISH), followed by regulatory authorization (ARCSA), and concludes with public registration and the start-of-trial notification.
q_3_7_ampliada:
The sequence of key steps is as follows:

Sponsor/Investigator: The sponsor selects the investigator (meeting the required qualifications) and the Clinical Research Site (CIC) (with adequate infrastructure and staff).

Principal Investigator: Obtains and signs the institutional letter of interest for conducting the trial, signed by the legal representative of the health facility.

Principal Investigator/Sponsor: Submits the protocol and related documentation for review and obtains CEISH Approval.

Sponsor/Legal Representative: Prepares the complete documentation (including the CEISH Approval Letter and the insurance policy) and applies to ARCSA for Authorization.

ARCSA: Verifies formal requirements and, if necessary, requests corrections (30 days, extendable to 60 days in total).

ARCSA: Begins the regulatory evaluation and issues the evaluation report (up to 60 days), and may request modifications.

ARCSA: Grants (or denies) clinical trial Authorization.

Sponsor/Legal Representative: Applies to ARCSA for Import Authorization of the investigational product (IP) and biological samples (a step separate from trial authorization).

Sponsor/Legal Representative: Registers the trial on an international platform (ICTRP/ICMJE) and notifies ARCSA of the code within ten (10) days.

Sponsor/Legal Representative: Notifies ARCSA and the CEISH of the Trial Start (the first act of selecting a participant) within fourteen (14) days of that start.
q_3_7_fuente: Reglamento para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos (Acuerdo Ministerial Nro. 00069-2024) (Art. 10, Art. 14, Art. 15, Art. 37, Art. 57, Art. 87, Art. 115, Art. 116, Art. 183).
q_4_1_directa: Yes. Labeling on the primary packaging must be in Spanish, in indelible ink, and indicate at least: sponsor, clinical trial, investigational product, expiry date, protocol code, product code, batch number, number of units, pharmaceutical form, route and dose of administration, storage conditions, and the statements "Prohibida su venta" [Sale prohibited] and "producto para uso exclusivo en investigación" [product for research use only].
q_4_1_ampliada: If the primary packaging is too small, the information must be printed on secondary packaging. The sponsor must submit the draft labeling for the investigational product and comparators as a requirement for trial authorization.
q_4_1_fuente: Reglamento para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos (Acuerdo Ministerial Nro. 00069-2024) (Art. 10.8, Art. 73, Annex 2).
q_4_2_directa: Yes, submission of the Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) Certification, or its equivalent, for the investigational medicine's manufacturing plant is mandatory.
q_4_2_ampliada: This certification must be issued by the National Regulatory Authority (NRA) of the manufacturing country. If the country-of-origin NRA does not issue such a certificate, a document confirming that the IP was manufactured under GMP will be accepted, such as an inspection report for the manufacturing plant. ARCSA also has the authority to certify GMP compliance for the IP's manufacture.
q_4_2_fuente: Reglamento para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos (Acuerdo Ministerial Nro. 00069-2024) (Art. 5.h, Art. 10.9, Art. 72).
q_4_3_directa: No, ARCSA's clinical trial authorization does not include authorization for the import and/or use of the investigational product. Import of the IP will be authorized by ARCSA after trial authorization and will be subject to Good Manufacturing Practice standards for investigational products and any other rules ARCSA sets for this purpose.
q_4_3_ampliada: ARCSA authorizes the import and export of the IP, comparator, and complementary products for research purposes only, and this import must comply with Good Manufacturing Practice standards for investigational products. The sponsor is responsible for ensuring the proper transport and distribution of the IP to research sites.
q_4_3_fuente: Reglamento para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos (Acuerdo Ministerial Nro. 00069-2024) (Art. 5.g, Art. 69, Art. 70).
q_5_1_directa: Yes. The principal investigator must report Serious Adverse Events (EAG/EAS) to the sponsor within no more than twenty-four (24) hours of becoming aware of them. The sponsor must report fatal or life-threatening Serious Unexpected Adverse Reactions (RAGI/RASI) to ARCSA and to investigators within seven (7) days, followed by a complete report within an additional eight (8) days.
q_5_1_ampliada: Non-fatal, non-life-threatening RASIs must be reported by the sponsor to ARCSA and to investigators within fifteen (15) days of becoming aware of them. The principal investigator must also report EAS/RAGI to the CEISH within the time frame set by the applicable regulation. Any information of immediate importance, such as findings of teratogenicity or carcinogenicity in animals, must be reported to ARCSA and investigators within ten (10) days.
q_5_1_fuente: Reglamento para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos (Acuerdo Ministerial Nro. 00069-2024) (Art. 82, Art. 84); Reglamento sustitutivo del Reglamento Para la Aprobación y Seguimiento de Comités de Ética (CEISH y CEAS) (Art. 105, Art. 106 A).
q_5_2_directa: Yes, the sponsor is required to submit an annual Development Safety Update Report (DSUR) to ARCSA.
q_5_2_ampliada: The DSUR's main purpose is to provide a detailed annual review of the safety information collected, with its structure and content following the ICH E2F guideline.
q_5_2_fuente: Reglamento para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos (Acuerdo Ministerial Nro. 00069-2024) (Art. 3, Art. 84); Reglamento sustitutivo del Reglamento Para la Aprobación y Seguimiento de Comités de Ética (CEISH y CEAS) (Art. 106 A).
q_5_3_directa: Yes, the sponsor must submit a semi-annual clinical trial progress report to ARCSA, which must first be prepared by the principal investigator.
q_5_3_ampliada: The semi-annual report must detail the number of people invited to participate, participants enrolled and withdrawn (with justification), serious adverse events occurring at the site, and protocol deviations and violations with their respective corrective measures. Upon completion of the study, the sponsor must send ARCSA and the Dirección Nacional de Investigación en Salud a report of results and conclusions within one (1) year of completion.
q_5_3_fuente: Reglamento para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos (Acuerdo Ministerial Nro. 00069-2024) (Art. 38, Art. 83, Art. 84, Art. 92, Art. 97, Art. 120, Art. 121); Reglamento sustitutivo del Reglamento Para la Aprobación y Seguimiento de Comités de Ética (CEISH y CEAS) (Art. 106, Art. 107, Art. 108).
q_5_4_directa: Yes. Substantial amendments (changes to the design, population, procedures, or investigational product) require prior CEISH approval and ARCSA authorization before they may be implemented.
q_5_4_ampliada: If an amendment is implemented to reduce an imminent risk to participants, it does not require prior approval, but must be reported to the CEISH and ARCSA within seven (7) days of implementation. Administrative amendments do not require approval or authorization, but must be reported to both authorities for their records within fifteen (15) days of implementation.
q_5_4_fuente: Reglamento para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos (Acuerdo Ministerial Nro. 00069-2024) (Art. 3, Arts. 22-29, Art. 116.f); Reglamento sustitutivo del Reglamento Para la Aprobación y Seguimiento de Comités de Ética (CEISH y CEAS) (Arts. 70-77).
q_5_5_directa: Yes, the sponsor or its legal representative is obligated to guarantee post-trial access (free provision of the investigational product) to the participant after the study or their participation ends, even if the product does not have sanitary registration in Ecuador.
q_5_5_ampliada: Post-trial access must meet certain conditions, including that the potential benefit to the participant must justify the potential risks of the treatment. The conditions and terms of this post-trial access must be specified in the informed consent document, where applicable.
q_5_5_fuente: Reglamento para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos (Acuerdo Ministerial Nro. 00069-2024) (Art. 64, Art. 80, Art. 81).
