q_6_1_directa: Yes. The Ley Orgánica de Protección de Datos Personales (LOPDP) is the applicable regulation, governing the processing of personal data on any medium.
q_6_1_ampliada: Health-related data is considered a special category of data. Processing health data in clinical trials requires the explicit consent of the data subject, clearly specifying its purposes. In the context of data protection, if the data controller is not established in Ecuador but processes data of residents, it must appoint a special proxy residing in the country with sufficient authority.
q_6_1_fuente: Reglamento para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos (Acuerdo Ministerial Nro. 00069-2024) (Art. 45.c, Art. 58, Final Provision, Art. 116.i); Ley Orgánica de Protección de Datos Personales (Art. 7, Art. 25, Art. 26, Art. 30, Art. 31, Art. 32); Reglamento General a la Ley Orgánica de Protección de Datos Personales (Art. 3).
q_6_2_directa: No regulation specifically and exclusively dedicated to vaccine clinical trials was found. However, vaccines are included in the definition of "Medicine" under the Reglamento para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos.
q_6_2_ampliada: Vaccine clinical trials are therefore governed by the same provisions of the Reglamento para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos (Acuerdo Ministerial Nro. 00069-2024), including the requirements for approval, authorization, product management, and safety reporting. The Ley Orgánica de Salud mentions that biological products imported by the State for the Expanded Program on Immunization do not require sanitary registration, but must have registration from the country of origin and proof of quality.
q_6_2_fuente: Reglamento para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos (Acuerdo Ministerial Nro. 00069-2024) (Art. 3); Ley Orgánica de Salud (Art. 55).
q_6_3_directa: Yes. The handling of biological samples for research is governed by the Reglamento para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos and supplemented by the Ministry of Public Health's Good Clinical Laboratory Practice Guide (BPLC).
q_6_3_ampliada: The BPLC Guide establishes operational standards for the collection, labeling, handling, transport, storage, and filing of specimens, including the need for Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs). In addition, the Ley Orgánica de Donación y Trasplante prohibits obtaining organs and/or tissue from persons with psychiatric or mental disorders involving cognitive impairment (unless their legal representative authorizes it), or from the bodies of pregnant women.
q_6_3_fuente: Reglamento para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos (Acuerdo Ministerial Nro. 00069-2024) (Art. 57); Guía de Buenas Prácticas de Laboratorio Clínico (BPLC) (Chapters 7, 9); Ley Orgánica de Donación y Trasplante de Órganos, Tejidos y Células (Art. 16).
q_6_4_directa: Yes, specific regulations exist for public health emergency situations, along with references to forthcoming regulation of clinical trials involving vulnerable populations and medical devices.
q_6_4_ampliada: Chapter XVII of the Clinical Trial Regulation is devoted to declared public health emergency situations, requiring CEISH approval and ARCSA authorization. The Ministry of Public Health must issue specific regulations for clinical trials with medical devices (within 12 months of the Regulation's publication) and for clinical trials involving pregnant or breastfeeding women and minors. The Ley Orgánica de Donación y Trasplante also requires authorization from the National Health Authority for research involving tissue engineering.
q_6_4_fuente: Reglamento para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos (Acuerdo Ministerial Nro. 00069-2024) (Chapter XVII, Second Provision, Seventh Transitional Provision, Tenth Transitional Provision); Ley Orgánica de Donación y Trasplante de Órganos, Tejidos y Células (Art. 54).

q_1_1_directa: The National Regulatory Authority (NRA) for clinical trials is the Superintendencia de Regulación Sanitaria (Superintendency of Health Regulation, SRS), which replaces and succeeds, in all its functions, the former Dirección Nacional de Medicamentos (National Directorate of Medicines, DNM), now dissolved.
q_1_1_ampliada: El Salvador's regulatory framework, in force since August 7, 2024, establishes that the SRS is the sole competent authority for authorizing clinical trials. The process, however, is sequential: the sponsor must first submit the application to the Comité Nacional de Ética de la Investigación en Salud (National Health Research Ethics Committee, CNEIS) and, once its favorable opinion is obtained, the CNEIS forwards the file to the SRS for technical evaluation and final authorization. Both rulings are therefore required: CNEIS approval and SRS authorization.
q_1_1_fuente: Ley de la Superintendencia de Regulación Sanitaria (Decreto Legislativo No. 891); Guía para la Autorización del Proyecto de Investigación del Ensayo Clínico, Enmiendas, Notificaciones e Informes.
q_1_2_directa: Health research is governed primarily by the Constitución de la República, the Ley de la Superintendencia de Regulación Sanitaria, the Ley de Medicamentos, the Ley de Deberes y Derechos de los Pacientes y Prestadores de Servicios de Salud, the Ley para la Protección de Datos Personales, and the Código de Salud. These are complemented by international guidelines adopted by the country, such as those of the International Council for Harmonisation (ICH) and the International Medical Device Regulators Forum (IMDRF).
q_1_2_ampliada:
El Salvador's legal framework is grounded in the Ley de la Superintendencia de Regulación Sanitaria, the entity that centralizes regulation, and in the substantive provisions in force under the Ley de Medicamentos (Arts. 2, 29, 66, 74(b), and 85). The country has formally adopted guidelines adapting the ICH E6(R3) Good Clinical Practice Guideline; for medical devices, the ISO 14155 standard and various IMDRF guidelines apply.

Also mandatory are the Ley de Deberes y Derechos de los Pacientes (Articles 5, 9, 16, 17, and 18), which governs informed consent, and the Código de Salud (Articles 7 and 41). On privacy, all clinical research must comply with the Ley para la Protección de Datos Personales and the principles of the Declaration of Helsinki.
q_1_2_fuente: Constitución de la República de El Salvador, Articles 68 and 69; Ley de la Superintendencia de Regulación Sanitaria (Decreto Legislativo No. 891); Ley de Medicamentos (Decreto Legislativo No. 1008), Articles 2, 29, 66, 74(b), and 85; Ley de Deberes y Derechos de los Pacientes y Prestadores de Servicios de Salud (Decreto Legislativo No. 307), Articles 5, 9, 15, 16, 17, and 18; Ley para la Protección de Datos Personales (Decreto Legislativo No. 144, 2024), Articles 1 and 39; Código de Salud (Decreto Legislativo No. 955), Articles 7 and 41; Instructivo para la Autorización, Modificación y Registro de Protocolos de Investigación Clínica, Section 5.
q_1_3_directa: Clinical trial authorization is governed by the Ley de la Superintendencia de Regulación Sanitaria, the Ley de Medicamentos, and the "Guía para la Autorización del Proyecto de Investigación del Ensayo Clínico, Enmiendas, Notificaciones e Informes." The technical and operational procedure is governed by the "Instructivo para la Autorización, Modificación y Registro de Protocolos de Investigación Clínica" and the "Instructivo del Usuario para el Sometimiento de los trámites de Ensayos Clínicos en la Plataforma SRS - CNEIS-ES."
q_1_3_ampliada:
The Ley de la Superintendencia de Regulación Sanitaria grants the SRS the exclusive authority to authorize interventional health research projects, in accordance with Article 29 of the Ley de Medicamentos, which requires prior authorization for all experimentation. The documentary procedure is detailed in the official authorization Guide and in the "Instructivo para la Autorización, Modificación y Registro de Protocolos de Investigación Clínica," which set out the chemical, medical, biomedical, and ethical evaluation requirements.

Procedures are managed through the unified electronic platform SRS-CNEIS-ES; its operation, profile creation, and submission workflows are governed by its own user manual. These guidelines formalize the country's national adoption of ICH standards and the ISO 14155 standard. Substantial amendments and maintenance of the protocol's public registry are governed by these same instruments.
q_1_3_fuente: Ley de la Superintendencia de Regulación Sanitaria (Decreto Legislativo No. 891), Articles 3, 6, 22, and 25; Ley de Medicamentos (Decreto Legislativo No. 1008), Article 29; Instructivo para la Autorización, Modificación y Registro de Protocolos de Investigación Clínica, Section 6; Instructivo del Usuario para el Sometimiento de los trámites de Ensayos Clínicos en la Plataforma SRS - CNEIS-ES, Section 7; Guía para la Autorización del Proyecto de Investigación del Ensayo Clínico, Enmiendas, Notificaciones e Informes, Section 6.
q_1_4_directa: Yes, written approval or a favorable opinion from El Salvador's Comité Nacional de Ética de la Investigación en Salud (CNEIS-ES) is a mandatory requirement. Without this ethical endorsement, projects cannot be authorized to be conducted in the country.
q_1_4_ampliada:
El Salvador's regulatory framework requires all clinical research to have ethics committee approval before it begins. The CNEIS-ES is the body responsible for receiving and ethically evaluating the protocol, substantial amendments, informed consent forms, and any participant recruitment materials.

For the SRS to process a clinical trial's technical authorization, the sponsor must include the "Ethics Research Committee Approval Certificate" among the general technical requirements of the file. Subsequent modifications or substantial amendments also require re-evaluation and approval by the committee.
q_1_4_fuente: Guía para la Autorización del Proyecto de Investigación del Ensayo Clínico, Enmiendas, Notificaciones e Informes, Section 6.4; Instructivo del Usuario para el Sometimiento de los trámites de Ensayos Clínicos en la Plataforma SRS - CNEIS-ES, Section 3 and 7.1; Instructivo para la Autorización, Modificación y Registro de Protocolos de Investigación Clínica, Section 6.
q_1_5_directa: Yes, ethical approval is a requirement prior to final regulatory authorization. Filing for both entities is done centrally and electronically through the shared SRS-CNEIS-ES platform, but the technical file evaluated by the SRS must include the approval certificate issued by the ethics committee.
q_1_5_ampliada:
Although document management is centralized in a single electronic window, authorization still depends on ethical evaluation. On the SRS-CNEIS-ES Platform, the sponsor or investigator uploads the CNEIS-ES-exclusive requirements in step 2 of the unified form, the shared requirements in step 3, and the SRS-exclusive requirements in step 4.

The CNEIS-ES receives and ethically evaluates the application, focusing on participants' rights, safety, and well-being. The SRS's Clinical Trials Unit (UEC) carries out the regulatory technical evaluation and requires, among the general technical requirements, the official ethics committee approval certificate. Although document submission is consolidated on a single platform, the SRS does not issue its authorization ruling without formal proof of prior ethical approval.
q_1_5_fuente: Instructivo del Usuario para el Sometimiento de los trámites de Ensayos Clínicos en la Plataforma SRS - CNEIS-ES, Section 4 and 7.1; Guía para la Autorización del Proyecto de Investigación del Ensayo Clínico, Enmiendas, Notificaciones e Informes, Section 6.4.
q_1_6_directa: Yes, the CNEIS is the governing body responsible for registering and accrediting local or institutional Research Ethics Committees (CEIs) in the country.
q_1_6_ampliada: The CNEIS verifies that all local committees operating in El Salvador function in accordance with national regulations and international ethical standards. Health or academic institutions must apply to the CNEIS to register their committees and demonstrate compliance with the established requirements.
q_1_6_fuente: Manual de Funcionamiento del Comité Nacional de Ética de la Investigación en Salud (CNEIS).
q_1_7_directa: Current regulations do not provide for a publicly accessible registry of Research Ethics Committees. The CNEIS maintains a centralized, internal registry, in which all authorized local committees must register annually.
q_1_7_ampliada:
Current regulations establish that local ethics committees, constituted at academic institutions or healthcare facilities, must formally register with the CNEIS. To obtain registration, applicant entities submit documentation demonstrating their fitness: their founding record, operating bylaws, and members' curricula vitae.

Registration is mandatory and must be renewed at each local committee renewal period. This mechanism gives the CNEIS institutional control over the country's ethical review bodies, but current guidelines do not require the list to be published on publicly accessible platforms.
q_1_7_fuente: Manual de Funcionamiento del Comité Nacional de Ética de la Investigación en Salud (CNEIS), Items 9 and 21.
q_1_8_directa: Yes, the regulation defines the scope of studies subject to prior authorization. Phase I, II, and III clinical trials, pilot or feasibility studies with medicines, biologics, vaccines, and medical devices, and pharmacokinetic, bioavailability, and bioequivalence studies all require SRS authorization before being conducted.
q_1_8_ampliada:
The SRS requires prior submission and evaluation of all interventional research in human subjects aimed at obtaining or updating sanitary registration. This covers Phase I, II, and III clinical trials, or pilot and pivotal stages, involving pharmaceutical products, advanced biotechnology therapies, vaccines, and medical devices.

This scope also includes products already registered with the SRS when the study evaluates a new therapeutic indication, a new dosage regimen, a new pharmaceutical form, or a strength higher than the one registered. Pharmacokinetic, bioavailability, and bioequivalence studies are also subject to prior authorization and must comply with the ICH E6 Good Clinical Practice guidelines.
q_1_8_fuente: Instructivo para la Autorización, Modificación y Registro de Protocolos de Investigación Clínica, Section 2; Instructivo del Usuario para el Sometimiento de los trámites de Ensayos Clínicos en la Plataforma SRS - CNEIS-ES, Section 2; Instructivo para Elaborar el Contenido del Protocolo para Ensayos Clínicos, Section 2.
q_2_1_directa: Yes, Salvadoran regulations define the sponsor as the person, company, institution, or organization that takes responsibility for the initiation, management, and financing arrangements of a clinical trial. The regulation provides that a project may have one or several sponsors, all bearing the same legal and operational responsibilities.
q_2_1_ampliada:
The regulatory framework formally recognizes the sponsor's role and assigns it overall responsibility for the conduct of the clinical research. Where several sponsors are involved, the regulation requires them to document their respective obligations and tasks in an agreement; if the agreement does not specify who is responsible for a given task, regulatory responsibility falls jointly and severally on all of them.

The sponsor is also primarily responsible for managing the authorization procedures and document submission before the SRS and the ethics committee, through the unified digital platform. Its non-delegable obligations include submitting joint declarations of financial capacity and signing formal contracts with the principal investigators.
q_2_1_fuente: Instructivo del Usuario para el Sometimiento de los trámites de Ensayos Clínicos en la Plataforma SRS - CNEIS-ES, Section 4; Guía para la Autorización del Proyecto de Investigación del Ensayo Clínico, Enmiendas, Notificaciones e Informes, Section 6.4.
q_2_2_directa: Yes, the regulation requires the sponsor to have a legal representative residing in El Salvador. This must be a natural or legal person acting on behalf of the foreign sponsor, holding a valid power of attorney granting the authority to take regulatory actions and decisions before the country's authorities.
q_2_2_ampliada:
To submit a research project to the SRS, official guidelines require the identification, contact, and address details of the sponsor's representative or proxy in El Salvador. This legal representative is the point of contact responsible for managing procedures before the SRS and the CNEIS-ES through the shared digital platform; their residence in national territory and valid power of attorney allow the foreign sponsor to be held accountable for the acts, decisions, and regulatory aspects arising from the trial's conduct.

The technical regulation also establishes that, if the submission is made through an authorized person, the signature on the document granting that authorization must be notarized, in accordance with the Ley de Procedimientos Administrativos. Without formal accreditation of this legally domiciled representative, the system denies progress of the initial authorization application.
q_2_2_fuente: Instructivo del Usuario para el Sometimiento de los trámites de Ensayos Clínicos en la Plataforma SRS - CNEIS-ES, Section 4 and 7; Guía para la Autorización del Proyecto de Investigación del Ensayo Clínico, Enmiendas, Notificaciones e Informes, Section 6.1.1.2; Ley de Procedimientos Administrativos, Article 5.
q_2_3_directa: Yes, the regulation sets out technical, ethical, and legal requirements for the sponsor to operate in El Salvador. It is responsible for ensuring investigational products are manufactured under Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) and for maintaining ongoing safety oversight of the trial; it must also provide verifiable financial guarantees and sign formal contracts with investigators.
q_2_3_ampliada:
El Salvador's regulatory framework holds the sponsor responsible for the ongoing evaluation of clinical safety: it must prepare periodic reports and report Serious Unexpected Adverse Events (EASI) to the SRS and the ethics committee. For supply management, it must provide the manufacturer's GMP certificates and stability studies applicable to the climatic zone, and ensure the products are safely packaged.

It also takes on legal obligations: submitting a formal joint declaration of its financial capacity to ensure the trial's completion, and obtaining an insurance policy with national coverage. Finally, it must provide the investigator with an up-to-date Investigator's Brochure and document the delegation of responsibilities through contracts based on PAHO/WHO models.
q_2_3_fuente: Instructivo para la Notificación de Eventos Adversos Durante la Investigación Clínica, Section 6.1.1; Instructivo para la Autorización, Modificación y Registro de Protocolos de Investigación Clínica, Section 6.1 and 6.2; Guía para la Autorización del Proyecto de Investigación del Ensayo Clínico, Enmiendas, Notificaciones e Informes, Section 6.4 and 7.1.
q_2_4_directa: Yes, the regulation allows the sponsor to delegate operational functions to a Contract Research Organization (CRO), provided its involvement and the scope of the delegation are declared in the official application forms submitted to the health authority. Ultimate responsibility for data quality and integrity, however, always rests with the sponsor, in accordance with Good Clinical Practice standards.
q_2_4_ampliada:
The SRS's regulatory system requires that, if the sponsor operates through a CRO, this relationship be documented in the "Declaración de inventario de suministros para el desarrollo del ensayo clínico." Any transfer of management or monitoring tasks is subject to the standards of the "Lineamientos para las Buenas Prácticas Clínicas" officially adopted in the country.

The regulation assigns the CRO specific operational roles: it may receive immediate Serious Adverse Event (SAE) notifications from the principal investigator and appear as the primary reference contact on the investigational product's official labeling. Even when it carries out critical processes and acts as the operational point of contact, the sponsor retains ultimate regulatory responsibility before the national authority and is legally liable for any protocol deviation or technical failure in the study.
q_2_4_fuente: Guía para la Autorización del Proyecto de Investigación del Ensayo Clínico, Enmiendas, Notificaciones e Informes, Section 6.2; Instructivo para la Notificación de Eventos Adversos Durante la Investigación Clínica, Section 6.1.2; Instructivo de Etiquetado para Productos Farmacéuticos y Dispositivos Médicos como Producto de Investigación, Section 6.1; Lineamientos para las Buenas Prácticas Clínicas en Establecimientos en los que se Realizan Investigaciones o Ensayos Clínicos (ICH E6).
q_2_5_directa: Yes, specific requirements exist for research sites; the main one is holding valid registration and authorization with the SRS. During the digital application, only sites already validated and incorporated into the system can be selected on the SRS-CNEIS-ES platform.
q_2_5_ampliada:
The regulation requires sponsors and investigators to verify that health institutions or research sites meet the standards for conducting clinical trials. Operationally, the "Instructivo del Usuario para el Sometimiento de los trámites de Ensayos Clínicos" establishes a system-level control: the applicant may only select sites pre-authorized in the system, and if a site is not on the list, its formal incorporation must be requested before the protocol is uploaded.

The digital file requires the establishment's operating license in the case of private organizations, a letter of recognition or institutional authorization signed by the site's management or legal representative, and, for associated sites, a contract setting out the parties' responsibilities.
q_2_5_fuente: Instructivo del Usuario para el Sometimiento de los trámites de Ensayos Clínicos en la Plataforma SRS - CNEIS-ES, Section 7.1; Guía para la Autorización del Proyecto de Investigación del Ensayo Clínico, Enmiendas, Notificaciones e Informes, Section 6.1.1.5 and 6.4.
q_2_6_directa: Yes. The principal investigator and key staff must demonstrate academic and technical fitness to conduct clinical trials, evidenced by valid practicing licenses and Good Clinical Practice (GCP) certification.
q_2_6_ampliada: The SRS and the ethics committee evaluate investigators' competencies as a condition for data quality and participant safety. When submitting the procedure on the SRS-CNEIS-ES platform, the national or international medical license of the investigators involved must be attached, along with a document certifying GCP training for investigators, sub-investigators, coordinators, and staff handling the dispensing and storage of the investigational product. The principal investigator must also disclose their current workload (clinical work, teaching, writing articles, and running other trials simultaneously), as a condition of the study's feasibility. Investigators also sign a statement of commitment to the Declaration of Helsinki and the applicable regulations.
q_2_6_fuente: Instructivo del Usuario para el Sometimiento de los trámites de Ensayos Clínicos en la Plataforma SRS - CNEIS-ES, Section 7.1; Guía para la Autorización del Proyecto de Investigación del Ensayo Clínico, Enmiendas, Notificaciones e Informes, Section 6.1.1.10 and 6.4.
q_2_7_directa: Yes, the regulation establishes insurance and compensation requirements for research participants. The sponsor must obtain and submit a medical coverage and civil liability insurance policy effective within Salvadoran territory, and both the protocol and the informed consent document must detail the compensation and medical treatment arrangements for participants who suffer harm or injury from the clinical intervention.
q_2_7_ampliada:
The SRS requires the insurance policy or proof of its purchase to be uploaded to the "Requisitos SRS/CNEIS-ES" module of the digital platform during the initial application. The policy must remain valid throughout the study, and its coverage limit and validity are reported annually through the "Formulario para Presentación de Informe Periódico de Avance."

At the documentary level, the protocol must include a section on "Ancillary Care After the Clinical Trial," with the fiduciary provisions for compensating those who suffer harm. The informed consent process, for its part, must explain in writing to volunteers the existence of compensation or medical treatment for trial-related injuries, as well as any possible additional expenses.
q_2_7_fuente: Guía de Buenas Prácticas Clínicas (BPC) (Section 5.8); Guía para la Autorización del Proyecto de Investigación del Ensayo Clínico, Enmiendas, Notificaciones e Informes.
q_3_1_directa: Yes, the regulation defines the essential content of the initial authorization file, submitted through the unified SRS-CNEIS-ES digital platform. Three main official forms are required (the evaluation application, the supply inventory declaration, and the project registration form), plus the general technical, ethical, and manufacturing quality requirements applicable depending on whether the investigational product is a pharmaceutical or a medical device.
q_3_1_ampliada:
The initial authorization process requires documentation structured across different modules of the electronic platform. Requirements shared by the ethics committee and the regulatory authority include the original protocol, the up-to-date Investigator's Brochure, informed consents, and contracts between the parties. The research team's suitability is verified through medical licenses, curricula vitae, and current Good Clinical Practice (GCP) certificates.

For the SRS's exclusive technical evaluation, the file must include the ethics committee's prior approval certificate, formal declarations of financial capacity, and the insurance policy with national coverage. Regarding supply quality, the primary and secondary packaging artwork, Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) certificates, and stability studies or sterility certificates (depending on the nature of the intervention) are attached, together with proof of fee payment.
q_3_1_fuente: Instructivo del Usuario para el Sometimiento de los trámites de Ensayos Clínicos en la Plataforma SRS - CNEIS-ES, Section 7.1; Guía para la Autorización del Proyecto de Investigación del Ensayo Clínico, Enmiendas, Notificaciones e Informes, Section 6.1 and 6.4.
q_3_2_directa: Yes, the submission process is regulated and was updated at the end of 2025. Filing for clinical trial authorization is managed electronically and centrally through the unified SRS-CNEIS-ES platform, and the technical and ethical file documents must be uploaded in fully legible PDF or Word format.
q_3_2_ampliada:
El Salvador's operational framework moved from a dual physical and magnetic-media (CD/USB) system to a fully digital one with the new 2025 guidelines. To begin the authorization process, the sponsor or investigator accesses the online services on the SRS's website and logs into the SRS-CNEIS-ES platform.

The system organizes submission into consolidated steps: the ethics committee's exclusive requirements are uploaded in step 2, shared requirements in step 3, and the SRS's own requirements in step 4, all within the same environment. All documents (protocol, informed consents, licenses) must be legible and submitted in PDF or Word format. Receipt, the CNEIS-ES's ethical evaluation, and the Clinical Trials Unit's technical ruling are thereby processed in an integrated manner.
q_3_2_fuente: Instructivo del Usuario para el Sometimiento de los trámites de Ensayos Clínicos en la Plataforma SRS - CNEIS-ES, Sections 4, 7, and 7.1.
q_3_3_directa: Yes, the technical regulation sets official regulatory time frames for evaluating clinical trials. The time frame for the SRS's final response is 20 business days; if the project is submitted in the context of a public health emergency, this is reduced to a maximum of 5 calendar days.
q_3_3_ampliada:
Once the file is submitted through the digital platform, the Clinical Trials Unit (UEC) has a maximum of 20 business days to evaluate the requirements and issue its ruling, on the basis of which the Intendencia de Registros e Inscripciones grants or denies authorization for the research.

If the evaluation reveals inconsistencies or additional requirements, the authority issues formal observations, and the sponsor or investigator has 10 business days to remedy them, in accordance with the Ley de Procedimientos Administrativos. The legal framework also provides for exceptional circumstances in which clinical trial procedures are prioritized and expedited due to public health necessity.
q_3_3_fuente: Instructivo para la Autorización, Modificación y Registro de Protocolos de Investigación Clínica, Section 6 and 6.10; Ley de Procedimientos Administrativos.
q_3_4_directa: Yes, payment of fees is a mandatory requirement for the trial's technical evaluation. Payment is made in accordance with the Ley Especial de Precios por Servicios de la Dirección Nacional de Medicamentos, which the SRS continues to apply.
q_3_4_ampliada:
Every clinical research project submitted for evaluation must have its fee paid before the authority begins the technical review. On the unified SRS-CNEIS-ES digital platform, the "Requisitos CNEIS-ES" and "Requisitos SRS" steps require uploading proof of fee payment or the corresponding payment order; the system validates and reflects the payment within 24 hours of it being made.

In both physical and electronic files, including the "duly paid fee" is classified as a non-remediable general technical requirement for authorizing the study or its substantial amendments. The fee process is governed by the inherited fee schedule currently in effect for health regulatory services.
q_3_4_fuente: Instructivo para la Autorización, Modificación y Registro de Protocolos de Investigación Clínica, Section 5 and 6; Instructivo del Usuario para el Sometimiento de los trámites de Ensayos Clínicos en la Plataforma SRS - CNEIS-ES, Section 7 and 7.1; Guía para la Autorización del Proyecto de Investigación del Ensayo Clínico, Enmiendas, Notificaciones e Informes, Section 6.4.
q_3_5_directa: Yes, public registration of clinical trials is a regulatory requirement, in line with WHO Good Clinical Practice. The SRS authorization procedure includes registering the protocol, using the form required from the moment the file is submitted.
q_3_5_ampliada:
To begin the authorization process, the sponsor or investigator must attach the "Formato de Registro de Proyectos de Investigación Clínica," completed in Word format, on the SRS-CNEIS-ES digital platform. The document compiles the study's public information: title, phase, design, number of participants, current status, and scientific contact email.

Using this data, the SRS publishes and updates monthly, on its website, the official list of approved, suspended, completed, or denied protocols, together with audit results. Keeping the registry information up to date throughout the trial's conduct is the sponsor's responsibility.
q_3_5_fuente: Instructivo para la Autorización, Modificación y Registro de Protocolos de Investigación Clínica, Section 6.6 and 6.8; Instructivo del Usuario para el Sometimiento de los trámites de Ensayos Clínicos en la Plataforma SRS - CNEIS-ES, Section 7.1; Guía para la Autorización del Proyecto de Investigación del Ensayo Clínico, Enmiendas, Notificaciones e Informes, Section 6.3.
q_3_6_directa: Yes, the current regulatory framework applies formal regulatory reliance mechanisms for recognizing prior evaluations. The SRS may officially recognize decisions, reports, and certificates issued by peer agencies classified as reference authorities by international bodies.
q_3_6_ampliada:
The SRS established an official regulatory reliance policy applicable both to clinical trial evaluation and to Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) certificates. The sponsor may select the "Reliance" application type when completing the general information on the SRS-CNEIS-ES platform.

The Salvadoran authority recognizes the endorsement of agencies certified at Level IV by the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) and those classified as WHO Listed Authorities (WLA). It specifically recognizes the scrutiny of the health authorities of the United States, Canada, Australia, Switzerland, Japan, South Korea, Singapore, the United Kingdom, Spain, France, Portugal, the European Medicines Agency (EMA), and Latin American countries with high sanitary surveillance (Argentina, Colombia, Brazil, Cuba, Chile, and Mexico). To use this scheme, the regulated party must include in its file the prior trial authorization issued by the reference authority and a summary of the evaluation.
q_3_6_fuente: Instructivo para la Autorización, Modificación y Registro de Protocolos de Investigación Clínica, Section 2 and 6.9; Instructivo para Elaborar el Contenido del Protocolo para Ensayos Clínicos, Section 2; Guía para la Autorización del Proyecto de Investigación del Ensayo Clínico, Enmiendas, Notificaciones e Informes, Section 6.1.1.1 and 6.4.
q_3_7_directa: The sequential order is built into the unified SRS-CNEIS-ES digital platform. The sponsor or principal investigator creates the online application and completes four document-upload steps grouping the ethical and technical requirements. Once the application is submitted, the ethics committee carries out its evaluation; on that same unified workflow, the SRS's Clinical Trials Unit issues its technical ruling, and the Intendencia de Registros e Inscripciones grants the final authorization.
q_3_7_ampliada:
The process begins when the user logs into the SRS-CNEIS-ES platform and completes Step 1 with general information and the selection of a pre-authorized research site. In Step 2, the CNEIS-ES-exclusive requirements are uploaded (such as proof of payment and medical licenses); in Step 3, the shared requirements (original protocol, Investigator's Brochure, insurance policies, and contracts); and in Step 4, the SRS-exclusive requirements, which include the inventory and registration forms and the product's manufacturing certificates.

Once the unified application is submitted, the CNEIS-ES conducts the ethical review and issues its approval, which is a condition for the process to continue. The Clinical Trials Unit (UEC) evaluates the technical, chemical, medical, and biomedical components within a maximum of 20 business days and issues its ruling, on the basis of which the Intendencia de Registros e Inscripciones decides on authorizing or denying the trial's conduct.
q_3_7_fuente: Instructivo del Usuario para el Sometimiento de los trámites de Ensayos Clínicos en la Plataforma SRS - CNEIS-ES, Section 7.1; Instructivo para la Autorización, Modificación y Registro de Protocolos de Investigación Clínica, Section 6; Guía para la Autorización del Proyecto de Investigación del Ensayo Clínico, Enmiendas, Notificaciones e Informes, Section 5.
q_4_1_directa: Yes, the regulation sets out labeling requirements aimed at identification, traceability, and the safe use of the investigational product. Labeling must include the sponsor's and investigator's contact information, the pharmaceutical form, the trial's reference code, the batch number, the expiry date, and the special statement "For clinical trial use only."
q_4_1_ampliada:
The SRS requires the primary and secondary packaging artwork to be submitted with the initial application to verify regulatory compliance. The official labeling instruction states that, in addition to basic information, the participant's or treatment's identification number and storage instructions must be included. When the primary packaging has limited space, the complete information appears on the outer secondary packaging, but the primary packaging retains the minimum data: batch, expiry date, and route of administration.

In blinded trial designs, the labeling of the placebo and comparator must have a visual and descriptive format identical to that of the investigational product so as not to compromise blinding. If the product's shelf life is extended, relabeling is carried out under Good Manufacturing Practice, without hiding the original information.
q_4_1_fuente: Instructivo de Etiquetado para Productos Farmacéuticos y Dispositivos Médicos como Producto de Investigación, Section 6.1, 6.2, and 6.3; Instructivo de Criterios de Evaluación de Ensayos Clínicos para la Elaboración de Dictamen Técnico, Section 7.1; Guía para la Autorización del Proyecto de Investigación del Ensayo Clínico, Enmiendas, Notificaciones e Informes, Section 6.1.1 and 6.4.
q_4_2_directa: Yes, submitting proof of Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) compliance is a mandatory technical requirement. The sponsor must guarantee that all investigational products, whether pharmaceuticals or medical devices, are manufactured under controlled quality standards backed by official certifications.
q_4_2_ampliada:
Salvadoran regulation classifies GMP verification into three scenarios, depending on the country-of-origin agency. If the manufacturer's regulatory authority issues GMP certificates for investigational product lines, that document must be submitted in full (Case A). If the agency does not issue such certificates but does conduct audits, an official declaration of conformity is accepted (Case B); and if neither option is available, a declaration from an independent accredited body is required (Case C).

For biotechnological products, vaccines, and medical devices, the file must be supplemented with evidence of sterility testing, manufacturing process validation, and batch-to-batch quality controls. The preclinical stage of these interventions is also required to demonstrate Good Laboratory Practice (GLP) compliance through the Investigator's Brochure.
q_4_2_fuente: Instructivo de criterios de evaluación de ensayos clínicos para la elaboración de dictamen técnico, Section 7.1; Instructivo para la Autorización, Modificación y Registro de Protocolos de Investigación Clínica, Section 6.1 and 7.1; Guía para la Autorización del Proyecto de Investigación del Ensayo Clínico, Enmiendas, Notificaciones e Informes, Section 7.1 and 7.2.
q_4_3_directa: A favorable clinical trial ruling is the prerequisite for processing the import of products. Bringing in the supplies also requires a specific customs and regulatory procedure, supported by the "Formato de Declaración de Inventario de Suministros," previously validated by the competent authority.
q_4_3_ampliada:
The import process is linked to clinical trial authorization but requires its own operational steps. During the initial submission, the sponsor presents the inventory declaration consistent with the protocol design, including quantities and surplus. Once the SRS issues its favorable ruling, the Clinical Trials Unit stamps this inventory and issues an official "noted" resolution.

With that approved documentation, the regulated party processes the special import permit before the Unidad de Importaciones y Exportaciones (Import/Export Unit, UIE). For subsequent periodic imports, the updated form must be resubmitted to the UEC, which must issue a new validation before proceeding to customs.
q_4_3_fuente: Instructivo para la Validación del Inventario de Suministros para la Ejecución del Ensayo Clínico, Section 6.1, 6.2, and 6.3; Instructivo del Usuario para el Sometimiento de los trámites de Ensayos Clínicos en la Plataforma SRS - CNEIS-ES, Section 7; Guía para la Autorización del Proyecto de Investigación del Ensayo Clínico, Enmiendas, Notificaciones e Informes, Section 6.2.
q_5_1_directa: Yes, requirements, channels, and time frames are established for reporting adverse events. Initial notification of national Serious Unexpected Adverse Events (EASI) that cause death or are life-threatening must be submitted to the SRS within 7 calendar days of becoming aware of them, and within 15 calendar days for other serious events. Reports are submitted using the official form sent to the Clinical Trials Unit's institutional email address.
q_5_1_ampliada:
The reporting flow first makes the principal investigator responsible, who must immediately report any Serious Adverse Event (SAE) to the sponsor (or the CRO) and to the ethics committee. The sponsor, in turn, formally reports EASI and Serious Unexpected Adverse Drug Reactions (RAMSI) to the SRS using the "Formulario de notificación de eventos adversos en ensayos clínicos." After the initial notification, it must submit a follow-up report within the following 8 calendar days, an obligation that repeats until the event is definitively resolved.

For EASI and serious unexpected device-related adverse effects occurring internationally, the mechanism changes: the sponsor does not report each event within 7 or 15 days, but instead consolidates them and reports them to the SRS in a summary format on a bimonthly basis.
q_5_1_fuente: Instructivo para la Notificación de Eventos Adversos Durante la Investigación Clínica, Section 6.1.1, 6.1.2, and 6.3; Guía para la Autorización del Proyecto de Investigación del Ensayo Clínico, Enmiendas, Notificaciones e Informes, Section 9.7 and 10.
q_5_2_directa: Yes, this is a regulatory requirement. The sponsor is required to submit periodic safety reports on an annual basis, counted from the date the investigational product's import and use were authorized, and at the end of the clinical trial.
q_5_2_ampliada:
The SRS requires ongoing safety evaluation of the trial in progress. The sponsor submits the information using the "Formulario para presentación de informe periódico de seguridad" (aligned with the Development Safety Update Report, DSUR), submitted through the Post-Authorization Procedures module of the shared SRS-CNEIS-ES platform.

The document consolidates the updated safety profile and includes a summary of adverse events (expected and unexpected), flow diagrams, and Data Safety Monitoring Committee reports. Through these annual reports, the national authority continuously assesses the risk-benefit relationship of the intervention in the Salvadoran population.
q_5_2_fuente: Instructivo para la Notificación de Eventos Adversos Durante la Investigación Clínica, Section 6.1.1; Guía para la Autorización del Proyecto de Investigación del Ensayo Clínico, Enmiendas, Notificaciones e Informes, Section 9.2 and 9.6; Instructivo del Usuario para el Sometimiento de los trámites de Ensayos Clínicos en la Plataforma SRS - CNEIS-ES, Section 7.3.
q_5_3_directa: Yes, the regulation requires periodic progress reports to be submitted to the authorities. These are submitted together using the "Formulario para Presentación de Informe Periódico de Avance," following the frequency set in the trial's original authorization ruling.
q_5_3_ampliada:
Through the SRS-CNEIS-ES platform's single window, the sponsor or principal investigator submits the trial's progress reports. The official form requires documenting progress in participant recruitment, the number of participants who completed the study, the project's current status, and justification for any early termination or temporary suspension.

The same periodic report must also validate the status of the insurance policy covering the trial, including its coverage expiration date, so that participant protection is not interrupted during the study's conduct.
q_5_3_fuente: Guía para la Autorización del Proyecto de Investigación del Ensayo Clínico, Enmiendas, Notificaciones e Informes, Section 9.3 and 9.6; Instructivo del Usuario para el Sometimiento de los trámites de Ensayos Clínicos en la Plataforma SRS - CNEIS-ES, Section 7.3.
q_5_4_directa: Yes, the regulation distinguishes between types of modifications. Every substantial protocol amendment must be authorized by the SRS and approved by the ethics committee before it may be implemented, while non-substantial amendments need only be reported.
q_5_4_ampliada:
The 2025 technical regulation defines a "substantial amendment" as a modification with a significant impact on participants' safety or physical or mental integrity, on the trial's scientific value, or on the investigational product's quality and safety. Major changes such as replacing the principal investigator, updating technical documents (consents), or changing the sponsor are requested through the "Formulario de Trámites Post Autorización" on the SRS-CNEIS-ES platform, together with payment of the corresponding fee.

The only exception allowing a change to be implemented without prior authorization is the need to eliminate an immediate danger to study participants. Outside that emergency exception, unauthorized implementation constitutes a serious violation.
q_5_4_fuente: Instructivo para la Autorización, Modificación y Registro de Protocolos de Investigación Clínica, Section 6.5 and 8.1; Instructivo del Usuario para el Sometimiento de los trámites de Ensayos Clínicos en la Plataforma SRS - CNEIS-ES, Section 4 and 7.3; Instructivo para Elaborar el Contenido del Protocolo para Ensayos Clínicos, Section 6.3.
q_5_5_directa: Yes, documentary obligations exist regarding post-trial care in El Salvador. The regulation requires the protocol to include a specific section titled "Ancillary Care After the Clinical Trial," setting out the planned arrangements for caring for participants once the study ends.
q_5_5_ampliada:
The regulatory framework requires clarity about what will happen to the patient once their participation in the study ends. Through the "Instructivo para Elaborar el Contenido del Protocolo para Ensayos Clínicos," the SRS establishes that the sponsor must detail the arrangements, if any, for complementary and post-trial medical care. The regulation also requires documenting the fiduciary measures for financial compensation or medical treatment for participants who suffer injury or harm as a result of their participation.

All information on post-study care, possible additional expenses, and the consequences of the research ending must be presented in an understandable way in the informed consent document, so the volunteer knows in advance whether they will have continued access to treatment and under what conditions.
q_5_5_fuente: Instructivo para Elaborar el Contenido del Protocolo para Ensayos Clínicos, Section 6.1.8; Instructivo de Criterios de Evaluación de Ensayos Clínicos para la Elaboración de Dictamen Técnico, Section 7.3.
q_6_1_directa: Yes, El Salvador has a mandatory public-order law in force, the Ley para la Protección de Datos Personales. This law classifies information relating to physical and mental health as "sensitive personal data" and requires the data subject's express, unequivocal, and preferably written consent to process such data in research.
q_6_1_ampliada:
The Ley para la Protección de Datos Personales establishes a legal framework applicable to all data controllers, including clinical trial sponsors and investigators. It enshrines the right to informational self-determination and grants participants the ARCO-POL rights over their health data: access, rectification, cancellation, objection, portability, erasure, and restriction.

For processing sensitive data, the investigator and the health facility must guarantee confidentiality under professional secrecy and collect information only through free, specific, individualized informed consent. The law also imposes data-minimization principles, technological security measures, and rules for the international transfer of medical information to third countries. Failure to comply with these safeguards empowers the state Cybersecurity Agency to apply sanctions and fines proportional to the violation, which may be classified as very serious.
q_6_1_fuente: Ley para la Protección de Datos Personales (Decreto Legislativo No. 144, 2024), Articles 1, 4, 5, 26, 37, 39, 44, and 50.
q_6_2_directa: Yes, a specific technical regulation exists for this type of biological product. The SRS issued the "Instructivo para Elaborar el Manual del Investigador en Ensayos Clínicos con Vacunas como Producto en Investigación," applicable to Phase I, II, and III studies, which requires documenting viral safety, manufacturing processes, and immunological correlates before administration in humans.
q_6_2_ampliada:
El Salvador's regulatory framework requires vaccine clinical trials to meet preclinical characterization and manufacturing standards. Through the guideline issued in 2025, the SRS requires sponsors to detail in the Investigator's Brochure the manufacturing process, the control and history of cell lines (master and working cell banks), and testing for the inactivation or removal of adventitious agents. Prior toxicity studies, biodistribution data in animal models, and verification of batch-to-batch consistency are also required.

For the clinical stage, the regulation requires justifying the antigen design, predefining statistical analysis populations, and submitting a pharmacovigilance plan that monitors and mitigates any immune-mediated adverse reactions.
q_6_2_fuente: Instructivo para Elaborar el Manual del Investigador en Ensayos Clínicos con Vacunas como Producto en Investigación, Section 2, 6.1.4, and 6.1.4.1.
q_6_3_directa: Yes, El Salvador's regulatory framework sets out guidelines for the handling, storage, and final disposal of biological samples in clinical research. Regulations require protocols and informed consent forms to detail specimen collection plans and their final destination, especially if they will be used for genetic analysis or future complementary studies.
q_6_3_ampliada:
The SRS incorporated requirements on biological samples into its recent technical regulations. Under the "Instructivo para la Autorización, Modificación y Registro de Protocolos de Investigación Clínica," both the regulatory authority and the participant must be informed of exactly how samples taken during the trial will be handled, and their final destination once the study ends must be legally declared.

At the document design level, the "Instructivo para Elaborar el Contenido del Protocolo para Ensayos Clínicos" requires the sponsor to include a specific annex on "Biological Specimens," covering the collection plan, laboratory evaluation, and temporary or long-term storage conditions. This traceability supports the protection of participants' rights, genetic confidentiality, and compliance with ICH Good Clinical Practice.
q_6_3_fuente: Instructivo para la Autorización, Modificación y Registro de Protocolos de Investigación Clínica, Section 6.3; Instructivo para Elaborar el Contenido del Protocolo para Ensayos Clínicos, Section 6.1.9.
q_6_4_directa: Yes, recently published technical instructions exist for specific situations and interventions, with differentiated regulations for the design of the Investigator's Brochure in clinical trials involving medical devices, biotechnological products, and antivenoms or immunoglobulins of animal origin. Specific guidelines have also been implemented for authorizing and monitoring clinical trials during exceptional circumstances or health emergencies.
q_6_4_ampliada:
The SRS has diversified its regulatory structure to address the particularities of different medical technologies. For biotechnological products and antivenoms, the 2025 guidelines require demonstrating genetic stability, characterizing antigen purification, and controlling risks of infectious agents or zoonoses. For medical devices, the evaluation aligns with the ISO 14155 standard and requires ex vivo performance testing and mechanical risk management plans.

The Salvadoran system also provides a framework for "Emergency Use Authorization," which allows for expedited clinical trial evaluation (within 5 calendar days) in the face of imminent public health risks. This mechanism is complemented by an alert-monitoring guideline that classifies the risks of these circumstances and establishes crisis management committees to continuously assess approved protocols.
q_6_4_fuente: Instructivo para elaborar el Manual del Investigador en Ensayos Clínicos para Productos Biotecnológicos en Investigación; Instructivo para elaborar el Manual del Investigador en Ensayos Clínicos con Dispositivos Médicos como Producto en Investigación; Instructivo para Elaborar el Manual del Investigador para Ensayos Clínicos con Antivenenos/ Inmunoglobulinas de Animales Inmunizados en Investigación; Lineamiento para la Obtención de Autorizaciones en Circunstancias Excepcionales, Section 5; Instructivo de Monitoreo y Detección de Alertas ante Riesgos Asociados a Circunstancias Excepcionales de la Unidad de Ensayos Clínicos, Section 2 and 9.

q_1_1_directa: The National Regulatory Authority (NRA) for clinical trials is the Departamento de Regulación y Control de Productos Farmacéuticos y Afines (Department for the Regulation and Control of Pharmaceutical and Related Products, DRCPFA), of the Ministry of Public Health and Social Welfare.
q_1_1_ampliada: Clinical research may only begin once the protocol has been authorized by the Department, which acts as the regulatory authority and also maintains the national clinical trial registry and database. This authorization is granted after the protocol passes a two-stage evaluation, one part of which involves the Research Ethics Committee.
q_1_1_fuente: Normativa para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos en Humanos (Acuerdo Ministerial 206-2021), Article 4.110, Article 5, Introduction.
q_1_2_directa: The main regulations governing health research are the Normativa para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos en Humanos (Acuerdo Ministerial 206-2021), the specific, prevailing regulation on this subject, and the Código de Salud (Decreto del Congreso 90-97), which establishes the country's general public health framework.
q_1_2_ampliada: Guatemala's legal framework for clinical research operates on different levels of specificity. The Código de Salud (Decreto 90-97) establishes, in Article 165, the Ministry of Health's general duty to control and oversee pharmaceutical products. On that basis, Acuerdo Ministerial 206-2021 was enacted to regulate all aspects of clinical trials involving human subjects. This specific regulation details the requirements, procedures, and ethical principles, and aligns them with international standards such as the Declaration of Helsinki and Good Clinical Practice (GCP). AM 206-2021 is therefore the governing document that must be consulted for any clinical trial.
q_1_2_fuente: Normativa para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos en Humanos (Acuerdo Ministerial 206-2021), Article 2, Introduction; Código de Salud (Decreto del Congreso 90-97), Article 165.
q_1_3_directa: The main regulation specifically governing authorization is the Normativa para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos en Humanos (Acuerdo Ministerial 206-2021), whose purpose is to establish the requirements and ethical principles for conducting clinical trials in human subjects in the country.
q_1_3_ampliada: Acuerdo Ministerial 206-2021 is the regulation that sets out in detail all the requirements and ethical principles for authorizing and conducting clinical trials in Guatemala. While earlier regulations such as the Reglamento para el Control Sanitario de los Medicamentos y Productos Afines (Acuerdo Gubernativo 712-99) mention, in Article 93, the need for authorization of research protocols, AM 206-2021 updates and details that process and constitutes the directly applicable, prevailing regulation.
q_1_3_fuente: Normativa para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos en Humanos (Acuerdo Ministerial 206-2021), Article 1; Reglamento para el Control Sanitario de los Medicamentos y Productos Afines (Acuerdo Gubernativo 712-99), Article 93.
q_1_4_directa: Yes, review and approval of the research protocol and the informed consent template by an authorized Research Ethics Committee (CEI) is required.
q_1_4_ampliada: The regulation establishes that every clinical trial involving human subjects must pass a two-stage evaluation, one part of which is approval by an Independent or institutional Ethics Committee. The CEI is essential, as its responsibility is to help safeguard the dignity, rights, safety, and well-being of all research participants.
q_1_4_fuente: Normativa para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos en Humanos (Acuerdo Ministerial 206-2021), Article 5, Article 37, Article 42.4, Introduction.
q_1_5_directa: Yes, CEI approval must precede submission of the documentation to the Department for its evaluation and subsequent authorization.
q_1_5_ampliada: The documentation submitted to the NRA for clinical trial authorization must include the report approving the research protocol and the informed consent template, issued by the Research Ethics Committee registered with the Department. The CEI must therefore have approved the conduct of the clinical trial before the sponsor or investigator submits it to the Department.
q_1_5_fuente: Normativa para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos en Humanos (Acuerdo Ministerial 206-2021), Article 37.8, Article 42, Article 42.4.
q_1_6_directa: Yes, Guatemala has a mandatory accreditation system for Research Ethics Committees (CEIs). This accreditation is granted by the DRCPFA and is valid for a maximum of two years, after which it must be renewed. Every clinical trial must be evaluated and approved by a CEI duly accredited by the health authority.
q_1_6_ampliada: The CEI accreditation process consists of two main stages: evaluation of the submitted documentation and an on-site inspection by the DRCPFA to verify the committee's resources. Documentary requirements include submission of the internal bylaws, standard operating procedures, and sworn declarations of no conflict of interest from its members. In addition, the committee must have a minimum of seven members, ensuring a multidisciplinary composition that includes at least one non-scientific member and one member unaffiliated with the institution. CEIs established under an institution's authority must have their director's explicit guarantee that the necessary resources will be provided for its operation. If any non-compliance is found during the evaluation or inspection, the DRCPFA issues recommendations that the CEI must address within fifteen days to obtain accreditation.
q_1_6_fuente: Normativa para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos en Humanos (Acuerdo Ministerial 206-2021), Articles 30, 31, 32, 33, and 35.
q_1_7_directa: Yes, an official public registry exists of Research Ethics Committees (CEIs) accredited and authorized to operate in Guatemala. This registry is managed by the DRCPFA through its institutional web portal. The list is maintained and updated periodically to reflect each committee's current legal status.
q_1_7_ampliada: Once a CEI successfully completes the accreditation or re-accreditation process before the DRCPFA, it receives a registration code and is added to the country's official list of accredited committees. This list is publicly accessible through the Ministry of Public Health and Social Welfare's (MSPAS) Medicines query website, where it is published and regularly updated. Maintaining this public registry is essential for the transparency of Guatemala's regulatory system. The regulation requires every clinical trial to be reviewed and approved exclusively by a CEI that is duly registered and holds current accreditation.
q_1_7_fuente: Normativa para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos en Humanos (Acuerdo Ministerial 206-2021), Articles 30, 42.3, and 51.
q_1_8_directa: Yes. Authorization is mandatory for clinical trials and drug utilization studies, whether involving new or existing molecules, to guarantee their validity and compliance with all regulatory requirements. This includes compliance with fundamental ethical principles, such as respect for persons, beneficence, and justice.
q_1_8_ampliada: Clinical research may only begin once the research protocol has been authorized by the Department of the Ministry of Public Health and Social Welfare.
q_1_8_fuente: Normativa para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos en Humanos (Acuerdo Ministerial 206-2021), Article 5; Reglamento para el Control Sanitario de los Medicamentos y Productos Afines (Acuerdo Gubernativo 712-99), Article 93.
q_2_1_directa: Guatemalan regulations do not provide an explicit definition of the term "sponsor" in their text. However, it is functionally defined as the individual or legal person that assumes ultimate responsibility for the initiation, management, financing, and quality of a clinical trial.
q_2_1_ampliada: Unlike other regulations, Acuerdo Ministerial 206-2021 does not include a glossary of terms. However, it defines the sponsor's role through the responsibilities it assigns. The sponsor is the entity that signs the trial authorization application together with the principal investigator; it is responsible for selecting qualified investigators and sites; it must take out an insurance policy to protect participants (Article 87.3.14); it is responsible for the manufacture of the investigational product under GMP standards (Article 105.2.4); it bears ultimate responsibility for the quality and integrity of the trial data, even if it delegates tasks to a CRO, and it assumes safety-reporting responsibilities before the regulatory authority (Article 118).
q_2_1_fuente: Normativa para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos en Humanos (Acuerdo Ministerial 206-2021), Article 42.1, Article 87.3.3, Article 87.3.14, Article 105.2.4, Article 118.
q_2_2_directa: Yes, if the sponsor is not legally established in the country, it must have a Contract Research Organization (CRO) or a Site Management Organization (SMO) to take on the regulatory and legal aspects in Guatemala.
q_2_2_ampliada: Sponsors not legally established in Guatemala must submit a certification issued by the regulatory authority of their home country demonstrating that they are registered, and this certification must be updated annually. They must also have a CRO or SMO to handle the regulatory and legal requirements.
q_2_2_fuente: Normativa para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos en Humanos (Acuerdo Ministerial 206-2021), Article 87.2.10; F-EC-a-15, Documentos que Acompañan la Solicitud No. 13.
q_2_3_directa: Yes. The sponsor must register with the Department, submitting legal documentation (public deed and trade license), proof of active professional association membership (where applicable), and an institutional profile demonstrating its operational capacity and ethical compliance.
q_2_3_ampliada: Registration requirements include a copy of the company's public deed of incorporation, the trade license, current legal representation, and an institutional profile (brochure) detailing objectives, organizational chart, site and investigator selection procedures, and a training plan. The sponsor is required to process authorization for a drug wholesaler (droguería) to import and handle the investigational product, or submit a storage contract with an authorized drug wholesaler, or a sworn statement of the mechanism it will use.
q_2_3_fuente: Normativa para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos en Humanos (Acuerdo Ministerial 206-2021), Article 87.2.8, Article 87.2.9; F-EC-a-15, Documentos que Acompañan la Solicitud.
q_2_4_directa: Yes. When the sponsor transfers functions to a CRO, the CRO must be registered with the Department, implement a quality assurance system, and must not include research sites or centers within its own physical facilities.
q_2_4_ampliada: When a sponsor delegates tasks, this must be formalized in writing. The CRO assumes responsibility for the transferred functions and must be legally established in Guatemala (public deed, trade license, etc.) and registered with the DRCPFA. It must submit a sworn statement that it operates in accordance with current regulations and Good Clinical Practice. To prevent conflicts of interest, the CRO is prohibited from housing clinical research sites or centers within its own facilities. The CRO must also ensure proper storage of investigational products, either through its own facilities meeting drug wholesaler requirements or through a contract with an authorized drug wholesaler.
q_2_4_fuente: Normativa para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos en Humanos (Acuerdo Ministerial 206-2021), Articles 94, 95, and 96.
q_2_5_directa: Yes, Guatemalan regulations establish requirements for selecting and registering clinical research sites or centers. Every site must register with the DRCPFA and hold a valid health establishment license issued by the DRACES. They must also undergo an on-site inspection to verify their technical suitability and infrastructure.
q_2_5_ampliada: For a site to be authorized to conduct clinical trials, it must meet specific technical-sanitary requirements covering staff, facilities, equipment, and standard operating procedures. The site must have qualified medical and nursing staff, and facilities with properly separated areas for administration, confidential records, medicine storage, treatment, and sample processing. Essential medical equipment is mandatory, such as internationally endorsed cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) equipment and monitoring systems for high-risk studies. In addition, the clinical unit must demonstrate prior experience caring for patients similar to the subjects to be enrolled under the proposed protocol. Private clinics may only serve as research sites if the trial involves outpatient treatments that do not carry a significant additional risk for the condition being treated.
q_2_5_fuente: Normativa para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos en Humanos (Acuerdo Ministerial 206-2021), Article 42.2, Article 87.3.3, Article 91, Article 97, Article 98, Article 100, Article 100.2.
q_2_6_directa: Yes. The principal investigator must be a healthcare professional duly registered with their professional association and with the DRCPFA, with demonstrated research experience and current Good Clinical Practice (GCP) certification issued by a recognized entity in the country.
q_2_6_ampliada: To act as principal investigator, the professional must have the scientific training and clinical experience necessary to safeguard subjects' safety and assess their response to the product under study. Accreditation before the health authority requires submitting a curriculum vitae updated annually, proof of a specialty or subspecialty registered in the country, proof of active professional association membership, and the corresponding GCP certification. The investigator must formally commit to complying with the approved protocol and ethical regulations, taking on non-delegable responsibility for the trial's conduct. If a study's principal investigator is not a physician, the regulation requires a licensed physician to be included on the team as sub-investigator. These requirements ensure that medical decisions made during the clinical trial always rest with competent, authorized personnel.
q_2_6_fuente: Normativa para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos en Humanos (Acuerdo Ministerial 206-2021), Articles 88, 88.1, and 88.2.
q_2_7_directa: Yes. The sponsor must provide research subjects with insurance covering medical care for adverse reactions and/or procedures related to the clinical research.
q_2_7_ampliada: The valid insurance policy obtained by the sponsor is an essential document for the authorization application. The Research Ethics Committee is responsible for evaluating the scope of the compensation to be offered to subjects for their participation, and must request a copy of the insurance to provide for compensation and treatment in the event of injury or death attributable to the trial. The Informed Consent must indicate the emergency facility that will handle emergencies arising from the clinical trial.
q_2_7_fuente: Normativa para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos en Humanos (Acuerdo Ministerial 206-2021), Article 18.15, Article 37.6, Article 37.7, Article 42.17, Article 87.3.14.
q_3_1_directa: Yes. The essential submission must include the Application Form (F-EC-a-01), CEI approval, the research protocol, the Investigator's Brochure, the insurance policy, proof of payment, the no-conflict-of-interest declaration, the principal investigator's CV, and the health institution's authorization and commitment letters, among others.
q_3_1_ampliada: The clinical trial authorization application is a complete dossier that must be submitted to the DRCPFA. In addition to key documents such as the application form (F-EC-a-01) signed by the investigator and the sponsor, the CEI's favorable ruling, the protocol in Spanish, and the Investigator's Brochure, the application must include: the valid insurance policy for participants; proof of payment of the evaluation fee; a sworn no-conflict-of-interest declaration; the updated curriculum vitae of the principal investigator and sub-investigators; a copy of the contract between the sponsor, the site, and the investigator; an authorization letter from the management of the health institution where the trial will be conducted; and current DRCPFA registration certificates for the sponsor (or its CRO), the principal investigator, and the research site.
q_3_1_fuente: Normativa para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos en Humanos (Acuerdo Ministerial 206-2021), Article 42.
q_3_2_directa: Yes. Although legislation promotes digitalization, current practice requires certain key documents to be submitted in physical format, such as the application form and proof of payment.
q_3_2_ampliada: Decreto 05-2021, the Ley de Simplificación de Trámites Administrativos, mandates that state entities implement technologies for remote procedures. In line with this, Acuerdo Ministerial 206-2021 (Article 143) provides for the use of an electronic portal for communications. However, the same regulation clarifies that this will be implemented "when available" and explicitly requires physical submission of documents such as Form F-EC-a-01 and proof of payment. This creates an implementation gap.
q_3_2_fuente: Normativa para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos en Humanos (Acuerdo Ministerial 206-2021), Article 42, Article 143; Ley de Simplificación de Trámites Administrativos (Decreto 05-2021), Article 25.
q_3_3_directa: Yes. The DRCPFA has a maximum of thirty (30) business days for the substantive review and authorization of a clinical trial. However, this time frame is suspended if clarifications are requested, resuming once the sponsor responds.
q_3_3_ampliada: The process begins with the Department validating the application within five (5) calendar days. If the application is deficient, the applicant has ten (10) calendar days to correct it. If additional clarifications are needed during the review, the applicant has fifteen (15) business days to respond, and final authorization will be issued within fifteen (15) business days of receiving the requested information.
q_3_3_fuente: Normativa para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos en Humanos (Acuerdo Ministerial 206-2021), Article 44.1, Article 44.2, Article 47.
q_3_4_directa: Yes, payment of a fee is required for evaluating a clinical trial, based on the cost-recovery principle.
q_3_4_ampliada: Payment of the processing fee is an indispensable requirement for the authorization application. This fee must be deposited into the bank account of the DRCPFA's FONDO PRIVATIVO DEP. REG. CONT. If the trial is conducted at multiple sites or centers, the fee must be paid for each of them.
q_3_4_fuente: Normativa para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos en Humanos (Acuerdo Ministerial 206-2021), Article 42.1.9, Article 132.
q_3_5_directa: Yes, the Department maintains a database or registry of clinical trials accessible to the public on its website.
q_3_5_ampliada: Once the authorization process is complete, the Department must make the following information public: the research protocol title, protocol number, study phase, sponsor, Research Ethics Committees involved, and the trial's status (authorized or not authorized). The clinical trials database is freely available to the public at no cost.
q_3_5_fuente: Normativa para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos en Humanos (Acuerdo Ministerial 206-2021), Article 4.110, Article 51, Article 144.
q_3_6_directa: No, the regulation does not establish a formal recognition procedure or expedited pathway for the initial authorization of a clinical trial based on prior approval by a foreign regulatory authority. Each application is evaluated independently by the DRCPFA and the local CEI.
q_3_6_ampliada: The process for authorizing a clinical trial in Guatemala is sovereign and independent. There are no mutual recognition, accreditation, or reliance mechanisms that would allow the DRCPFA's and CEI's local evaluation to be expedited or replaced, even if the trial has already been approved by Level IV Regulatory Authorities (per the PAHO/WHO classification). However, the regulation does indicate that information and decisions from these authorities are taken into account in other contexts. For example, when suspending or canceling a trial for safety reasons, the Department will consider information from these agencies. In addition, supporting documentation for the investigational product, such as the GMP certificate, must come from competent authorities in the country of origin. This reflects respect for those agencies' standards, though not a delegation of the authorization decision.
q_3_6_fuente: Normativa para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos en Humanos (Acuerdo Ministerial 206-2021).
q_3_7_directa: The process is sequential, beginning with the registration of the parties involved and concluding with NRA authorization after ethical approval.
q_3_7_ampliada:
The sequence of key steps to be completed by the parties involved is as follows:

Registration of Regulatory Parties (Prior to or Concurrent with Submission): The sponsor (or its CRO/SMO representative), the principal investigator, sub-investigators, and the research site or center must register with the Department. The sponsor must also register the drug wholesaler (droguería) that will handle the Investigational Product (IP).

Preparation and Ethical Approval: The sponsor/investigator prepares the protocol and essential documents (Informed Consent, Investigator's Brochure) and submits them to the Research Ethics Committee (CEI). The CEI evaluates the study and issues its approval (favorable ruling), which must precede submission to the NRA.

Institutional Commitments: An authorization letter must be obtained from the management or administrative authority of the health institution where the trial will be conducted, along with a commitment letter to address study-related serious adverse events.

Documentation Gathering: The sponsor or investigator must obtain the trial's insurance policy, complete the Application Form (F-EC-a-01), and obtain proof of payment of the processing fees.

Submission to the NRA: The sponsor/investigator submits the complete documentation to the Department.

Application Validation: The Department verifies that the application meets all requirements within five (5) calendar days. If there are deficiencies, the applicant has ten (10) calendar days to correct them.

Final Authorization: The Department examines the technical documentation and, if appropriate, issues the clinical trial authorization within no more than thirty (30) business days of receiving the complete documentation, notifying all parties involved.
q_3_7_fuente: Normativa para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos en Humanos (Acuerdo Ministerial 206-2021), Article 42, Article 44, Article 47, Article 87.2.9, Article 91, Article 98.
q_4_1_directa: Yes. Labeling of the Investigational Product (IP) must include, among other information, the route of administration, batch number, expiry date, storage conditions, and the statements "Muestra para investigación clínica" [Sample for clinical research] and "Prohibida su venta" [Sale prohibited].
q_4_1_ampliada: The label must contain the product name, strength, route of administration, batch, expiry date, storage conditions, and the statements "Sample for clinical research" and "Sale prohibited." Under Article 115 of AM 206-2021, Guatemalan regulations do not permit relabeling of investigational products once they are in the country. This restriction means that all label information must be final from the point of manufacture, and that activities such as extending shelf life through new local labeling cannot be carried out. This requires precise logistical and inventory planning by the sponsor to avoid the product expiring during the trial.
q_4_1_fuente: Normativa para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos en Humanos (Acuerdo Ministerial 206-2021), Article 114.1, Article 115.
q_4_2_directa: Yes, the sponsor must ensure investigational products are manufactured under applicable Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) procedures and must submit the GMP Certificate.
q_4_2_ampliada: The GMP Certificate and the summary product release documents must be duly apostilled or consularized. If they are in a language other than Spanish, they must be translated by a sworn translator authorized in Guatemala. If the medicine comes from a third country with marketing authorization, that country's current GMP Certificate must also be submitted.
q_4_2_fuente: Normativa para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos en Humanos (Acuerdo Ministerial 206-2021), Article 105.2.4, Article 105.2.6.
q_4_3_directa: Yes, the sponsor must process authorization for a drug wholesaler (droguería) for the import, storage, and distribution of the clinical trial's products as part of the authorization application process.
q_4_3_ampliada: The sponsor must submit to the Department, at the time of the trial's approval application, a list of the complementary pharmaceutical and related products that need to be imported. If the sponsor does not have its own drug wholesaler, it must submit a storage contract with an authorized drug wholesaler to ensure the IP is properly handled.
q_4_3_fuente: Normativa para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos en Humanos (Acuerdo Ministerial 206-2021), Article 87.2.9, Article 111.
q_5_1_directa: Yes. The investigator must immediately (within 24 hours) report Serious Adverse Events (SAEs) to the sponsor. The sponsor is then responsible for reporting Suspected Serious Unexpected Adverse Reactions (RASI or SUSARs) to the Department and the CEI within strict time frames: a maximum of seven (7) calendar days for those that are life-threatening or result in death, and a maximum of fifteen (15) calendar days for others.
q_5_1_ampliada: Non-fatal, non-life-threatening SUSARs must be reported no later than seven (7) days after the sponsor becomes aware of them. Reports of suspected adverse reactions occurring outside Guatemala are made using the CIOMS form, communicated in English with a Spanish summary, while those occurring in Guatemala must be in Spanish.
q_5_1_fuente: Normativa para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos en Humanos (Acuerdo Ministerial 206-2021), Article 91.2.18, Article 116.1, Article 116.6, Article 118.4, Article 118.7, Article 118.8.
q_5_2_directa: Yes, sponsors are required to prepare and submit a periodic report assessing the safety of the investigational medicine.
q_5_2_ampliada: This periodic safety report must be submitted to the Department, the competent authorities, and the Research Ethics Committees involved, annually until the end of the clinical trial.
