This report must take into account all available safety information and does not replace the process for requesting modifications to trial documents.
q_5_2_fuente: Normativa para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos en Humanos (Acuerdo Ministerial 206-2021), Article 119.
q_5_3_directa: Yes, the investigator, sponsor, CRO, or SMO is required to submit progress reports for each research site or center to the Department on a semi-annual basis.
q_5_3_ampliada: In addition to the semi-annual progress reports, the principal investigator is required to regularly inform the Research Ethics Committee of the trial's progress. At the end of the clinical trial, the sponsor must submit the immediate final report for each site within a maximum of ninety (90) calendar days, and the national final report within a maximum of sixty (60) calendar days.
q_5_3_fuente: Normativa para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos en Humanos (Acuerdo Ministerial 206-2021), Article 82, Article 83.1, Article 91.2.20.
q_5_4_directa: Yes. Any substantial modification to a clinical trial's authorized conditions requires the prior favorable ruling of the Research Ethics Committee and authorization from the Department.
q_5_4_ampliada: A substantial amendment is defined as any written change that could have a significant impact on subjects' safety or integrity, the study's scientific value, its conduct or management, or the product's quality/safety profile. The only exception is when the modification is necessary to eliminate an immediate danger to subjects' health, in which case the investigator must inform the CEI as soon as possible.
q_5_4_fuente: Normativa para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos en Humanos (Acuerdo Ministerial 206-2021), Article 52, Article 74.1, Article 91.2.13.
q_5_5_directa: Yes, once the clinical trial ends, continued administration of the products used must be governed by the rules established for compassionate use.
q_5_5_ampliada: The sponsor is responsible for supplying the investigational product free of charge to subjects once their participation ends, if discontinuing treatment would endanger their safety and no other medicine option exists in the country, or if continued treatment is essential. A Compassionate Use Protocol must be used for this purpose, which requires medical justification and authorization from the Department.
q_5_5_fuente: Normativa para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos en Humanos (Acuerdo Ministerial 206-2021), Article 64, Article 65, Article 103.2.
q_6_1_directa: Guatemala does not have a general personal data protection law. However, the protection of clinical trial participants' information is governed by the duty of confidentiality set out in the Código de Salud, the Ley de Acceso a la Información Pública, and the ethical principles of Acuerdo Ministerial 206-2021.
q_6_1_ampliada: Scattered legal obligations exist to protect the confidentiality of research participants. The Código de Salud (Decreto 90-97) recognizes the right to confidentiality of medical information. The Ley de Acceso a la Información Pública (Decreto 57-2008) classifies personal and sensitive data as confidential information requiring express consent for its use or transfer. Acuerdo Ministerial 206-2021 requires informed consent to detail how data will be protected, and regulates the handling of data and biological samples.
q_6_1_fuente: Ley de Acceso a la Información Pública (Decreto 57-2008), Articles 9, 30; Código de Salud (Decreto del Congreso 90-97); Normativa para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos en Humanos (Acuerdo Ministerial 206-2021).
q_6_2_directa: No specific regulation or guideline sets out additional or different requirements for authorizing and conducting vaccine clinical trials. These studies are governed by the general provisions of Acuerdo Ministerial 206-2021.
q_6_2_ampliada: Vaccine clinical trials must follow the same authorization and conduct process as any other investigational product. However, it is strategically important to note that vaccines, as biological products, are subject to additional technical regulations that, while not directly affecting the trial's conduct, are relevant to the eventual post-research sanitary registration application.
q_6_2_fuente: Normativa para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos en Humanos (Acuerdo Ministerial 206-2021); Norma Técnica 67 versión 6-2023; Norma Técnica 77 versión 08-2023.
q_6_3_directa: Yes, Chapter XV of the Normativa para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos en Humanos (Acuerdo Ministerial 206-2021) sets out specific provisions on human biological samples.
q_6_3_ampliada: Collection must be evaluated by the CEI and the Department. The subject must give informed consent, be notified of the location, duration, and purposes of storage, and has the right to withdraw consent. Shipping biological samples out of the country must follow International Air Transport Association (IATA) Guidelines, and the process must be documented and reported to the Department monthly. Commercialization of these samples is prohibited.
q_6_3_fuente: Normativa para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos en Humanos (Acuerdo Ministerial 206-2021), Article 46.7, Chapter XV (Articles 122-130), Article 126.
q_6_4_directa: Yes, the regulation addresses rules for clinical trials involving incapacitated subjects (including minors), culturally distinct communities, studies with psychotropic drugs, and procedures during public health emergencies.
q_6_4_ampliada: For psychotropic drugs, the sponsor/investigator must submit quarterly reports to the Department in the form of a sworn declaration, detailing enrolled patients and the medicine used, under penalty of the trial's cancellation. For minors, they must have received information adapted to their age and mental maturity. During a public health emergency, protocol modifications may be implemented without prior CEI and Department approval to minimize immediate risks, but must be reported afterward.
q_6_4_fuente: Normativa para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos en Humanos (Acuerdo Ministerial 206-2021), Article 21 (sub-items), Article 23, Article 67, Article 68.

q_1_1_directa: The National Regulatory Authority (NRA) for clinical trials is the Agencia de Regulación Sanitaria (Health Regulatory Agency, ARSA).
q_1_1_ampliada: ARSA is the government body with the explicit legal mandate to authorize, regulate, oversee, and, where necessary, suspend or terminate clinical trials within national territory. It is responsible for developing, updating, and enforcing the regulatory framework governing products, services, and establishments of health interest, having taken over the powers previously held by the Secretaría de Salud (Ministry of Health) in this area.
q_1_1_fuente: Decreto PCM-032-2017 (Ley de la Agencia de Regulación Sanitaria), Article 3; Acuerdo No. 0256-ARSA-2025 (Disposiciones para la Regulación y Control Sanitario de los Ensayos Clínicos con seres humanos en fase I, II, III, IV y sus cuotas de recuperación) (Recitals).
q_1_2_directa: The fundamental regulation establishing the general framework for scientific research involving human subjects is the Código de Salud, approved through Decreto NÚMERO 65-91.
q_1_2_ampliada: The Código de Salud, in its Title on "Scientific Research," stipulates that all research involving human subjects must be conducted by specialized professionals and at establishments with adequate infrastructure, equipment, and materials. Crucially, it establishes that this activity must be governed by special regulations approved by the health authority (formerly the Secretaría de Salud, now ARSA), laying the legal foundation for the specific regulations currently in force on clinical trials.
q_1_2_fuente: Decreto NÚMERO 65-91 (Código de Salud), Article 175; Acuerdo No. 0256-ARSA-2025 (Disposiciones para la Regulación y Control Sanitario de los Ensayos Clínicos con seres humanos en fase I, II, III, IV y sus cuotas de recuperación) (Recitals).
q_1_3_directa: The main regulation currently in force is Acuerdo No. 0256-ARSA-2025, which provides unified regulation of Phase I, II, III, and IV clinical trials involving both pharmaceutical products and medical devices. Complementarily, Acuerdo-0631-ARSA-2023 regulates general sanitary aspects of medical devices not specific to clinical trials.
q_1_3_ampliada: The regulation in force since February 27, 2026 establishes the unified legal framework for conducting clinical trials with human subjects in all phases, covering both pharmaceutical products and medical devices. It replaces the previous regime and incorporates ICH Good Clinical Practice standards, the CIOMS guidelines, and the Declaration of Helsinki. The special pharmacovigilance regulations for reporting adverse events with pharmaceutical products, and the technovigilance regulations for medical devices, apply as complementary regulations.
q_1_3_fuente: Acuerdo No. 0256-ARSA-2025 (Disposiciones para la Regulación y Control Sanitario de los Ensayos Clínicos con seres humanos en fase I, II, III, IV y sus cuotas de recuperación), Articles 1 and 2; Acuerdo No. 194-ARSA-2025 (Reglamento Especial para la Farmacovigilancia), TITLE II, CHAPTER IX; Acuerdo No. 0185-ARSA-2025 – Reglamento de Tecnovigilancia, TITLE IV, CHAPTER III.
q_1_4_directa: Yes, obtaining approval from a Comité Ético Científico (Scientific Ethics Committee, CEC) duly registered with ARSA is an indispensable, mandatory requirement.
q_1_4_ampliada: Current regulations make regulatory authorization contingent on prior ethical approval. For trials involving both pharmaceutical products and medical devices, the protocol and other essential study documents (informed consent, Investigator's Brochure, insurance policy, ancillary tools) must have a prior ruling from a Scientific Ethics Committee duly registered and authorized by ARSA in the Scientific Ethics Committee Registry (RCEC). Without this prior ethical approval, ARSA will not accept the trial's sanitary authorization application.
q_1_4_fuente: Acuerdo No. 0256-ARSA-2025 (Disposiciones para la Regulación y Control Sanitario de los Ensayos Clínicos con seres humanos en fase I, II, III, IV y sus cuotas de recuperación), Articles 3, 23, and 24.
q_1_5_directa: Yes, the trial's essential documentation must be approved by the CEC before being submitted for ARSA authorization.
q_1_5_ampliada: The clinical trial authorization application must attach the most recent version of the research Protocol, the Investigator's Brochure, and the Informed Consent, all already approved by the CEC. In addition, for medical devices, ARSA will only authorize the import of the investigational product once the protocol has been approved by the Scientific Ethics Committee.
q_1_5_fuente: Acuerdo No. 0256-ARSA-2025 (Disposiciones para la Regulación y Control Sanitario de los Ensayos Clínicos con seres humanos en fase I, II, III, IV y sus cuotas de recuperación), Articles 45 and 46.
q_1_6_directa: Yes. Official recognition of Scientific Ethics Committees (CECs) operates through a mandatory registration system administered by ARSA. Every committee must register and be authorized in the RCEC for its rulings to be valid. The regulation does not use the term "accreditation," but this state registry serves that function by certifying committees' competence and fitness.
q_1_6_ampliada: Acuerdo No. 0256-ARSA-2025 establishes the procedure for a CEC to lawfully operate in the country by registering with the RCEC. The application is submitted using the form available on ARSA's official website (www.arsa.gob.hn) and includes a sworn statement, articles of incorporation (for independent committees) or a document from the relevant governing authority (for government or university committees), internal bylaws, individual documentation for each member (identification, CV, professional license where applicable), and authorization of the minutes book. The committee must have a minimum of five members. ARSA issues its decision within 30 business days. Registration is valid for five years and must be renewed five months before expiry (or up to six months late). The authority retains the power to revoke registration for violating internal bylaws, altering minutes or reports, or failing to comply with ethical principles; in such cases, members of the revoked CEC may not join another CEC for at least two years. Registration of foreign CECs is also permitted, provided they meet the same requirements and hold current registration issued by their country's national regulatory authority.
q_1_6_fuente: Acuerdo No. 0256-ARSA-2025 (Disposiciones para la Regulación y Control Sanitario de los Ensayos Clínicos con seres humanos en fase I, II, III, IV y sus cuotas de recuperación), Articles 27, 28, 31, and 32.
q_1_7_directa: Yes. Acuerdo No. 0256-ARSA-2025 expressly establishes that ARSA must maintain, on its website, a registry with information on Scientific Ethics Committees (CECs) authorized to review the clinical trials within their remit. ARSA must also publish, on its website, the clinical trials authorized, denied, canceled, suspended, or withdrawn, in a publicly accessible database.
q_1_7_ampliada: Unlike the previous regime, the new regulatory framework expressly establishes the public nature of the registry. Article 6, item 13 of Acuerdo No. 0256-ARSA-2025 provides that ARSA must maintain a registry of authorized CECs on its website, turning the RCEC into a publicly searchable online registry. Article 67 also establishes that ARSA must record, in a publicly accessible database on its website, the clinical trials that are authorized, denied, and suspended. This public availability allows investigators, sponsors, and the public to verify committees' current status and the state of ongoing clinical trials.
q_1_7_fuente: Acuerdo No. 0256-ARSA-2025 (Disposiciones para la Regulación y Control Sanitario de los Ensayos Clínicos con seres humanos en fase I, II, III, IV y sus cuotas de recuperación), Article 6, item 13; Article 67.
q_1_8_directa: Yes. Prior ARSA authorization is required for Clinical Trials with Human Subjects or their Biological Samples in Phases I, II, III, and IV (for pharmaceutical products) and for clinical trials with medical devices.
q_1_8_ampliada: The scope of application of the current sanitary regulation explicitly covers all phases of clinical development for both pharmaceutical products and medical devices. This prior-authorization requirement is grounded in the broader principle of the Código de Salud, which establishes that all research involving human participants must be subject to special regulations approved by the health authority.
q_1_8_fuente: Acuerdo No. 0256-ARSA-2025 (Disposiciones para la Regulación y Control Sanitario de los Ensayos Clínicos con seres humanos en fase I, II, III, IV y sus cuotas de recuperación), Articles 1, 2, and 3; Decreto NÚMERO 65-91 (Código de Salud), Article 175.
q_2_1_directa: Yes. The regulation defines the sponsor as an individual, company, institution, or organization with legal representation in the country, responsible for the organization, initiation, conduct, management, financing, and completion of the clinical trial.
q_2_1_ampliada: The current definition incorporates two elements: the full range of responsibilities the sponsor assumes for the trial, and the requirement to have legal representation in Honduras. This second condition is part of the very definition of the role, meaning no sponsor may operate in the country without first appointing a legal proxy or establishing a legal entity domiciled in Honduras.
q_2_1_fuente: Acuerdo No. 0256-ARSA-2025 (Disposiciones para la Regulación y Control Sanitario de los Ensayos Clínicos con seres humanos en fase I, II, III, IV y sus cuotas de recuperación), Article 4 (Definitions).
q_2_2_directa: Yes. Current regulations expressly require the sponsor to have legal representation in Honduras. The authorization documentation requires submitting a special or general power of attorney for the sponsor's legal representative domiciled in the country, for trials involving both pharmaceutical products and medical devices.
q_2_2_ampliada: Unlike the previous regime, where the requirement was inferred from regulatory practice, it is now established expressly at two levels. At the definitional level, the sponsor is characterized as a person or entity "with legal representation in the country." At the documentary level, the authorization provisions require the application to be accompanied by a special or general power of attorney for the sponsor's legal representative domiciled in the country. In practice, a foreign sponsor can meet this requirement by appointing a local legal proxy, engaging a Contract Research Organization (CRO) with legal representation in Honduras, or establishing a subsidiary entity domiciled in the country. Without meeting this requirement, ARSA will not accept the application.
q_2_2_fuente: Acuerdo No. 0256-ARSA-2025 (Disposiciones para la Regulación y Control Sanitario de los Ensayos Clínicos con seres humanos en fase I, II, III, IV y sus cuotas de recuperación), Article 4 (Definitions); Article 45, item 3; Article 46, item 3.
q_2_3_directa: Yes. The sponsor must have legal representation in Honduras, implement quality assurance and quality control systems, submit a letter accepting the trial, sign a confidentiality agreement with the principal investigator, take out an insurance policy for participants, and archive the trial's documentation for at least ten years.
q_2_3_ampliada: Current regulations detail the sponsor's responsibilities. It must implement quality assurance and quality control systems with standard operating procedures, select a suitable investigator and site, document the study's financial information in a written agreement, provide products and procedures to participants free of charge, take out an insurance policy, and archive all documentation for a minimum of ten years. It must submit the semi-annual per-site report to ARSA and the final report within one year of completion, reporting any protocol deviation or violation that poses a risk. The sponsor may transfer tasks to a CRO, but retains ultimate responsibility for data quality and integrity.
q_2_3_fuente: Acuerdo No. 0256-ARSA-2025 (Disposiciones para la Regulación y Control Sanitario de los Ensayos Clínicos con seres humanos en fase I, II, III, IV y sus cuotas de recuperación), Articles 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, and 19.
q_2_4_directa: Yes. Obligations the sponsor transfers to a Contract Research Organization (CRO) must be specified in a written agreement. The CRO must have standard operating procedures and technical staff trained in Good Clinical Practice with demonstrated experience for the delegated functions.
q_2_4_ampliada: Every transfer of obligations from the sponsor to the CRO must be recorded in a written agreement; any task not expressly transferred remains the sponsor's responsibility. The CRO must have standard operating procedures for all phases of the trial and technical staff trained in GCP. Ultimate responsibility for data quality and integrity always rests with the sponsor.
q_2_4_fuente: Acuerdo No. 0256-ARSA-2025 (Disposiciones para la Regulación y Control Sanitario de los Ensayos Clínicos con seres humanos en fase I, II, III, IV y sus cuotas de recuperación), Articles 15, 21, and 22.
q_2_5_directa: Yes. Research sites must hold a Sanitary License issued by ARSA, following an inspection verifying Good Clinical Practice compliance. At hospitals or healthcare facilities, the license is granted exclusively for the areas where the authorized trials will be conducted. Warehouses used for storing and distributing investigational products require a separate sanitary license.
q_2_5_ampliada: The sanitary license application for research sites is submitted through an online form (www.arsa.gob.hn) with a sworn statement, articles of incorporation, the medical or technical director's license, a site map and layout of areas, photographs, and proof of fee payment. The license may be valid for 2, 4, or 6 years, with tiered fees. Renewal must be submitted five months before expiry. Modifications (change of name, director, location, legal representative, or transfer) require prior authorization. Warehouses storing investigational products need a separate license that cannot exceed the main establishment's validity period. ARSA conducts periodic GCP inspections both at the site and at outsourced providers (hospitals, clinical laboratories, warehouses, and imaging centers).
q_2_5_fuente: Decreto NÚMERO 65-91 (Código de Salud), Article 175; Acuerdo No. 0256-ARSA-2025 (Disposiciones para la Regulación y Control Sanitario de los Ensayos Clínicos con seres humanos en fase I, II, III, IV y sus cuotas de recuperación), Articles 34, 37, 42, and 43.
q_2_6_directa: Yes. The principal investigator must be a healthcare professional duly licensed with their professional association, with experience and training in Good Clinical Practice. The regulation assigns them specific responsibilities regarding the study's conduct, participant safety, and document filing.
q_2_6_ampliada: Current regulations devote an entire chapter to the principal investigator. Their responsibilities include: conducting the trial in accordance with the approved protocol, obtaining in advance the institutional letter of interest signed by the health facility's legal representative, having CEC approval and ARSA authorization before starting, managing substantial amendments, allowing audits and inspections, ensuring adequate medical care in the event of adverse events, keeping physical and digital documents for ten years from the study's closure, and providing the sponsor with the semi-annual progress report. The investigator may delegate activities but retains ultimate responsibility, and must protect participants' identity and personal data. The regulation also classifies the following as breaches of responsible research conduct: (i) distortion of information, data, or results; (ii) falsification of materials, processes, or data; and (iii) plagiarism. In the event of early termination or suspension of the trial, the investigator must inform participants, the sponsor, the CEC, and ARSA.
q_2_6_fuente: Decreto NÚMERO 65-91 (Código de Salud), Article 175; Acuerdo No. 0256-ARSA-2025 (Disposiciones para la Regulación y Control Sanitario de los Ensayos Clínicos con seres humanos en fase I, II, III, IV y sus cuotas de recuperación), Articles 7, 8, 10, 12, and 13.
q_2_7_directa: Yes. The regulation establishes two central sponsor obligations: taking out an insurance policy for participants with an authorized company, covering harm arising from the study; and guaranteeing free medical care and treatment for any harm resulting from participation.
q_2_7_ampliada: The current regulatory framework substantially changes the previous regime and establishes participant protection at several levels. Taking out an insurance policy is an express sponsor obligation; the policy must be issued to the research site, contracted with an authorized company, and cover harm arising from the study's procedures and interventions. Submitting it is a documentary requirement of the authorization dossier for trials involving both medical devices and pharmaceutical products, and the Scientific Ethics Committee must evaluate it as part of its review. In addition, the principal investigator and the sponsor must provide free, timely, and equitable medical care and treatment for any physical, psychological, or other harm resulting from participation. The informed consent document must include an explanation of the policy's coverage and the contact information of the person responsible in the event of an incident.
q_2_7_fuente: Acuerdo No. 0256-ARSA-2025 (Disposiciones para la Regulación y Control Sanitario de los Ensayos Clínicos con seres humanos en fase I, II, III, IV y sus cuotas de recuperación), Article 18, item 4; 24; 45, item 14; 46, item 18; 55, item 7; 61 and 62.
q_3_1_directa: Yes. The essential content includes the official application form (online at www.arsa.gob.hn), a sworn statement, the CEC-approved protocol and Investigator's Brochure in Spanish, the informed consent form, the CEC's ruling, the sponsor's acceptance letter, the confidentiality agreement, the research team's curricula vitae with GCP certification, the insurance policy, and proof of payment.
q_3_1_ampliada: The dossier must contain the research protocol with a table of contents, summary, objectives, rationale, methodological design, participant selection criteria, intervention, evaluation variables, timeline, and ethical aspects. It is accompanied by the Investigator's Brochure, informed consent documentation, CEC-approved ancillary tools (surveys, diaries, scales), the investigational product's GMP certificate, the site's sanitary license, and the insurance policy. For trials with medical devices, proof of the study's registration in a registry affiliated with the International Clinical Trials Registry Platform (ICTRP) is additionally required.
q_3_1_fuente: Acuerdo No. 0256-ARSA-2025 (Disposiciones para la Regulación y Control Sanitario de los Ensayos Clínicos con seres humanos en fase I, II, III, IV y sus cuotas de recuperación), Articles 45 and 46.
q_3_2_directa: Yes. The application begins with the official form available online on ARSA's website (www.arsa.gob.hn), together with a sworn statement and supporting documentation. All documentation must be submitted in Spanish.
q_3_2_ampliada: The process combines online form submission with delivery of supporting documentation. The entire dossier must be in Spanish; documents prepared in another language require a certified Spanish translation, consistent with the original document. Documentation may also be submitted on electronic media (USB or CD).
q_3_2_fuente: Acuerdo No. 0256-ARSA-2025 (Disposiciones para la Regulación y Control Sanitario de los Ensayos Clínicos con seres humanos en fase I, II, III, IV y sus cuotas de recuperación), Articles 45, 46, and 100.
q_3_3_directa: Yes. Resolution time frames are selectable by the applicant: 15, 30, 60, or 120 business days, with tiered fees depending on the time frame chosen. These apply to all phases (I, II, III, and IV), for trials with both pharmaceutical products and medical devices.
q_3_3_ampliada: Time frames are counted in business days from the day after a complete application meeting all technical and legal requirements is submitted. If ARSA requires corrections, the time frame restarts from the day after the requirement is met. If the case warrants an inspection, it is carried out within the same time frame. If, after submitting the application, the applicant wishes to shorten the time frame, they may request the change by paying the corresponding fee difference.
q_3_3_fuente: Acuerdo No. 0256-ARSA-2025 (Disposiciones para la Regulación y Control Sanitario de los Ensayos Clínicos con seres humanos en fase I, II, III, IV y sus cuotas de recuperación), Articles 43, 45, 46, and 101.
q_3_4_directa: Yes. Cost-recovery fees must be paid for services rendered, calculated as fractions of the average minimum wage (SMP). Proof of payment is a mandatory submission requirement for initial authorization, renewals, amendments, and product imports.
q_3_4_ampliada: The fee varies depending on the requested resolution time frame (15, 30, 60, or 120 business days): the shorter the time frame, the higher the fee. For non-governmental trials, initial authorization fees range from 1 SMP (Phase IV at 120 days) to 5 SMP (Phase I at 15 days). Government or university committees pay a reduced, flat fee of 1/40 SMP. Fees are also charged for authorization renewal (1/2 SMP), amendments (1/16 SMP), research site licenses (1/4 to 3 SMP depending on validity period and time frame), storage warehouses, and special authorizations for importing and exporting products and biological samples.
q_3_4_fuente: Acuerdo No. 0256-ARSA-2025 (Disposiciones para la Regulación y Control Sanitario de los Ensayos Clínicos con seres humanos en fase I, II, III, IV y sus cuotas de recuperación), Articles 45, 46, 47, 49, 86, 87, and 88.
q_3_5_directa: Yes. Clinical trials must be registered before the first participant is enrolled, in a registry affiliated with WHO's International Clinical Trials Registry Platform (ICTRP), or in a registry approved by the International Committee of Medical Journal Editors (ICMJE).
q_3_5_ampliada: ARSA must require the sponsor to register the trial and must maintain, in a publicly accessible database on its website, the clinical trials that are authorized, denied, canceled, suspended, or withdrawn. For trials with medical devices, proof of registration in an ICTRP-affiliated database is a mandatory documentary requirement of the authorization dossier. The informed consent document must include the trial's ICTRP registration details.
q_3_5_fuente: Acuerdo No. 0256-ARSA-2025 (Disposiciones para la Regulación y Control Sanitario de los Ensayos Clínicos con seres humanos en fase I, II, III, IV y sus cuotas de recuperación), Article 6, item 14; Article 45, item 24; Article 55, item 12; Articles 66 and 67.
q_3_6_directa: Yes. ARSA recognizes relevant decisions, reports, and notifications related to clinical trials from stringent National Regulatory Authorities such as the EMA, FDA, MHRA (United Kingdom), Health Canada, TGA (Australia), and PMDA (Japan), and from others demonstrating maturity level 3 or 4 on WHO's Global Benchmarking Tool (GBT).
q_3_6_ampliada: This recognition is used as supporting evidence in the evaluation of trials to be conducted at authorized research sites within national territory, without prejudice to ARSA also drawing on other international regulations and frameworks (the Declaration of Helsinki, the Belmont Report, the CIOMS guidelines, ICH Good Clinical Practice, and IMDRF guidelines for medical devices). In the event of conflict between applicable documents or frameworks, ARSA applies the stricter one to guarantee the protection of participants' health and rights.
q_3_6_fuente: Acuerdo No. 0256-ARSA-2025 (Disposiciones para la Regulación y Control Sanitario de los Ensayos Clínicos con seres humanos en fase I, II, III, IV y sus cuotas de recuperación), Articles 95 and 99.
q_3_7_directa: The sequential order begins with prior registration of the trial on an ICTRP/ICMJE platform and ethical approval by the CEC, followed by regulatory submission to ARSA, site verification and a Good Clinical Practice inspection, and concludes with the trial's sanitary authorization and special authorization to import the investigational product.
q_3_7_ampliada:
The process is structured in the following mandatory steps:

Registration of the Scientific Ethics Committee (CEC): the CEC must be previously registered and authorized by ARSA in the RCEC.

Prior ethical approval: the sponsor or investigator submits the protocol, Investigator's Brochure, informed consent, insurance policy, and ancillary tools to the CEC for its approval.

Research site authorization: the site must hold a current Sanitary License issued by ARSA following an inspection verifying Good Clinical Practice compliance, and must guarantee the infrastructure and response capacity needed for medical care.

Trial registration: the sponsor must register the study in a registry affiliated with WHO's International Clinical Trials Registry Platform (ICTRP) or approved by the ICMJE.

Documentation preparation: the sponsor or the CRO provides the acceptance letter, the confidentiality agreement with the principal investigator, the research team's CVs, the Good Manufacturing Practice certifications, and the insurance policy.

Regulatory submission: the sponsor submits to ARSA, through the online form (www.arsa.gob.hn), the formal application with a sworn statement, all documentation approved by the CEC, and proof of payment of the fee corresponding to the chosen resolution time frame.

Evaluation and inspection: ARSA carries out the critical evaluation and, where appropriate, a site inspection to verify Good Clinical Practice.

Execution authorization: ARSA grants authorization valid for two years, renewable.

Import authorization: once the trial is approved, special authorization is granted to import the investigational product.
q_3_7_fuente: Acuerdo No. 0256-ARSA-2025 (Disposiciones para la Regulación y Control Sanitario de los Ensayos Clínicos con seres humanos en fase I, II, III, IV y sus cuotas de recuperación), Articles 3, 6, 27, 34, 45, 46, 47, 66, and 86.
q_4_1_directa: Yes. Labeling must be in Spanish and printed on the primary packaging in indelible ink. It must include the mandatory warnings "Exclusivamente para uso en ensayo clínico" [For clinical trial use only], "Manténgase fuera del alcance de los niños" [Keep out of reach of children], "Prohibida su venta" [Sale prohibited], and "producto para uso exclusivo en investigación" [product for research use only], and must not contain false or misleading claims about the product's safety or efficacy.
q_4_1_ampliada: The regulation distinguishes between pharmaceutical products and medical devices. For pharmaceutical products, labeling must identify the sponsor, manufacturer, country of origin, pharmaceutical form, route of administration, batch, expiry date, storage conditions, trial identification code, protocol number, site and investigator, and instructions for use. For medical devices, it must also include the device's name and reference code, manufacturing date, model or serial number, and sterilization method where applicable. If the original labeling is in another language, a Spanish translation must be submitted. The cover letter must consolidate all the study's identifying information and the contact details of the site and the principal investigator.
q_4_1_fuente: Acuerdo No. 0256-ARSA-2025 (Disposiciones para la Regulación y Control Sanitario de los Ensayos Clínicos con seres humanos en fase I, II, III, IV y sus cuotas de recuperación), Articles 89, 90, 91, and 92.
q_4_2_directa: Yes. A Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) Compliance Certificate is required for both investigational pharmaceutical products and medical devices, including placebo and comparator where applicable.
q_4_2_ampliada: The sponsor must guarantee that investigational products are manufactured in accordance with Good Manufacturing Practice, submitting the certificate issued by the National Regulatory Authority of the manufacturing country. When that authority does not issue such a certificate, a document certifying that the product was manufactured under GMP is accepted as an alternative, such as the plant inspection report. For medical devices, an ISO 13485 Certificate is additionally required.
q_4_2_fuente: Acuerdo No. 0256-ARSA-2025 (Disposiciones para la Regulación y Control Sanitario de los Ensayos Clínicos con seres humanos en fase I, II, III, IV y sus cuotas de recuperación), Article 45, items 20 and 21; Article 46, item 14; Article 82.
q_4_3_directa: No, trial approval does not automatically include import authorization. Investigational products, whether pharmaceutical or medical devices, must obtain a separate special import authorization from ARSA, after the clinical trial has been authorized.
q_4_3_ampliada: Special import authorization is requested through the online form (www.arsa.gob.hn), accompanied by a sworn statement, a pro forma invoice or product description, a descriptive table in ARSA format, supporting documentation justifying the import, and proof of payment. The resolution time frame is selectable (5, 10, 15, or 20 business days), with tiered fees ranging from 1/16 to 1 SMP for non-governmental committees. Exporting biological samples and investigational products also requires special authorization through specific procedures. Controlled pharmaceutical products or regulated chemical substances are additionally subject to the regulations applicable to those categories.
q_4_3_fuente: Acuerdo No. 0256-ARSA-2025 (Disposiciones para la Regulación y Control Sanitario de los Ensayos Clínicos con seres humanos en fase I, II, III, IV y sus cuotas de recuperación), Article 3; Articles 86, 87, and 88.
q_5_1_directa: Yes. In the event of a serious adverse event, the principal investigator must inform the sponsor within no more than 24 hours of becoming aware of it. The sponsor must report fatal serious unexpected adverse reactions to ARSA and the CEC within 7 days, non-fatal ones within 15 days, and other relevant safety findings within 10 days.
q_5_1_ampliada: Reporting covers events occurring both in Honduras and in other countries. The investigator must report to the CEC serious adverse events at the site, serious unexpected adverse reactions occurring at any of the study's sites, recommendations from the Independent Data Monitoring Committee (CIMD) where one exists, and any safety finding received from the sponsor. The sponsor's initial reports must be followed up with follow-up reports and a final report until the event is resolved or stabilized. Information from animal studies suggesting a significant risk to participants (including teratogenicity or carcinogenicity) must also be reported within 10 days of becoming known. For pharmaceutical products in general, reporting is supplemented by the procedures set out in the Reglamento Especial para la Farmacovigilancia.
q_5_1_fuente: Acuerdo No. 0256-ARSA-2025 (Disposiciones para la Regulación y Control Sanitario de los Ensayos Clínicos con seres humanos en fase I, II, III, IV y sus cuotas de recuperación), Articles 64 and 65; Acuerdo No. 194-ARSA-2025 (Reglamento Especial para la Farmacovigilancia), Chapter IX.
q_5_2_directa: Yes. The sponsor must submit a semi-annual Development Safety Update Report (DSUR) to ARSA, prepared in accordance with the ICH E2F guideline.
q_5_2_ampliada: The DSUR is submitted semi-annually by the sponsor and aims to provide an assessment of the safety information collected during the reporting period in relation to the investigational product. Its structure and content follow the ICH E2F guideline. For pharmaceutical products, detailed submission procedures (format, time frames after the data-lock point, and reporting channel) are supplemented by the provisions of the Reglamento Especial para la Farmacovigilancia.
q_5_2_fuente: Acuerdo No. 0256-ARSA-2025 (Disposiciones para la Regulación y Control Sanitario de los Ensayos Clínicos con seres humanos en fase I, II, III, IV y sus cuotas de recuperación), Article 65, item 5; Acuerdo No. 194-ARSA-2025 (Reglamento Especial para la Farmacovigilancia), Article 30, items 1 and 2.
q_5_3_directa: Yes. The principal investigator must prepare and submit semi-annual clinical trial progress reports to ARSA. The reports are submitted by the sponsor to ARSA, signed by each investigator according to their site.
q_5_3_ampliada: The semi-annual report must contain: title, protocol number, research phase, sponsor, research site; number of participants screened, enrolled, who completed the trial, and who discontinued; the number of serious adverse events and their description; and major protocol deviations along with their preventive measures. In addition, the sponsor must deliver to ARSA a final study report within no more than 6 months of the research's completion, including a summary, introduction, study design, participant characteristics, interventions, results, statistical analysis, discussion, conclusions, and references.
q_5_3_fuente: Acuerdo No. 0256-ARSA-2025 (Disposiciones para la Regulación y Control Sanitario de los Ensayos Clínicos con seres humanos en fase I, II, III, IV y sus cuotas de recuperación), Article 4 (Definition of "Semi-Annual Follow-Up Report"); Article 8, item 8; Article 18, item 8; Article 76.
q_5_4_directa: Yes. The regulation distinguishes between substantial and non-substantial amendments. Substantial amendments require prior approval from the Scientific Ethics Committee and ARSA before they may be implemented. Non-substantial amendments need only be reported to the CEC and ARSA.
q_5_4_ampliada: Substantial amendments are changes that affect participants' safety or integrity, the interpretation of the documentation or the trial's scientific value, the quality or safety profile of the investigational product, the conduct or management of the study, a change or addition of a site or principal investigator, a change of sponsor or legal representative, and the transfer of major trial-related tasks. Non-substantial amendments include minor changes such as contact information, typographical errors, and contact details. The amendment request is submitted through an online form with a sworn statement, a copy of the CEC minutes approving the amendment, justification, the protocol with the changes, a summary of changes, and proof of the cost-recovery fee (1/16 SMP for non-governmental committees).
q_5_4_fuente: Acuerdo No. 0256-ARSA-2025 (Disposiciones para la Regulación y Control Sanitario de los Ensayos Clínicos con seres humanos en fase I, II, III, IV y sus cuotas de recuperación), Articles 48 and 49.
q_5_5_directa: Yes, but conditionally. The regulation provides for post-trial access (through extension trials or compassionate use) when three cumulative conditions are met: the patient has a serious or life-threatening condition and essentially requires the product, which is not available in the country; no comparable alternative therapy exists; and the potential benefit justifies the risks.
q_5_5_ampliada: Post-trial access consists of the sponsor or its legal representative providing the investigational product to the participant free of charge, even when it does not hold sanitary registration in Honduras, after the trial's completion or once the participant's involvement ends. The sponsor must facilitate this access when the three conditions noted are met and when it considers this appropriate. This is therefore not an unconditional obligation for continued treatment, but rather a compassionate-use or extension-trial mechanism subject to restrictive medical criteria. The specific considerations for its application are detailed in the current regulation and must be disclosed to the participant during the informed consent process.
q_5_5_fuente: Acuerdo No. 0256-ARSA-2025 (Disposiciones para la Regulación y Control Sanitario de los Ensayos Clínicos con seres humanos en fase I, II, III, IV y sus cuotas de recuperación), Article 18, item 5; Article 63.
q_6_1_directa: No single personal data protection law exists in Honduras. The confidentiality of health information and clinical trial participants' data is protected by provisions scattered across multiple regulations, including the Código de Salud, the pharmacovigilance and technovigilance regulations, the specific clinical trial provisions, and the Criminal Code.
q_6_1_ampliada: Protecting participants' data relies on an integrated set of provisions. The specific clinical trial regulation establishes that every participant has the right to the protection and confidentiality of their personal data, as well as to access, rectification, and cancellation of that data. The principal investigator, the CECs, and the institution where the trial is conducted are required to protect participants' identity and personal data, both during the conduct of the research and during the publication or disclosure of results. The informed consent document must include a description of the confidentiality measures to be taken. In addition, the technovigilance and pharmacovigilance regulations establish the confidential nature of reports, the Código de Salud defines epidemiological information as confidential, and the Criminal Code classifies as a criminal offense the disclosure of secrets affecting privacy, including health data.
q_6_1_fuente: Acuerdo No. 0256-ARSA-2025 (Disposiciones para la Regulación y Control Sanitario de los Ensayos Clínicos con seres humanos en fase I, II, III, IV y sus cuotas de recuperación), Articles 5, 10, 11, and 55, item 9; Acuerdo No. 0185-ARSA-2025 – Reglamento de Tecnovigilancia, TITLE VII, Article 27; Acuerdo No. 194-ARSA-2025 (Reglamento Especial para la Farmacovigilancia), Article 34; Decreto NÚMERO 65-91 (Código de Salud), Article 181; Código Penal, ARTICLE 276, item 2.
q_6_2_directa: No separate regulation exists for vaccine clinical trials. Vaccines are considered pharmaceutical products and are governed by the general provisions for the sanitary regulation and control of Phase I, II, III, and IV clinical trials with pharmaceutical products.
q_6_2_ampliada: Vaccines, as investigational pharmaceutical products, are covered by the general clinical trial regulation. This includes sanitary authorization requirements, the dossier's documentary requirements (protocol, Investigator's Brochure, insurance policy, ICTRP registration, Good Manufacturing Practice), and adverse event reporting processes. The Pharmacovigilance Regulation additionally requires reporting suspected serious or unexpected adverse reactions from medicines and vaccines within 72 hours.
q_6_2_fuente: Acuerdo No. 0256-ARSA-2025 (Disposiciones para la Regulación y Control Sanitario de los Ensayos Clínicos con seres humanos en fase I, II, III, IV y sus cuotas de recuperación), Articles 1 and 46; Acuerdo No. 194-ARSA-2025 (Reglamento Especial para la Farmacovigilancia), Article 14, item 1.
q_6_3_directa: Yes. Current regulations include specific provisions on informed consent for the collection, storage, and future use of biological materials in research, as well as a detailed procedure for special authorization to export biological samples. ARSA has the express authority to authorize such exports.
q_6_3_ampliada: For the collection, storage, and future use of biological materials in research, the regulation requires adequate informed consent. If the future use of samples is known at the time of collection, specific consent must be obtained; if the use is unknown, broad consent must be obtained detailing who is responsible, the storage period, foreseeable conditions of use, review by a CEC, confidentiality measures, and options for withdrawing consent. Exporting biological samples requires special authorization from ARSA through an online form, with supporting documentation (a list of samples, the contract with the processing laboratory, analytical tests, and transport details) and selectable resolution time frames (5, 10, or 15 business days) with tiered fees.
q_6_3_fuente: Acuerdo No. 0256-ARSA-2025 (Disposiciones para la Regulación y Control Sanitario de los Ensayos Clínicos con seres humanos en fase I, II, III, IV y sus cuotas de recuperación), Article 6, item 15; Articles 60 and 87.
q_6_4_directa: Yes. Current regulations establish specific provisions for bioequivalence, biosimilar, and advanced therapy clinical trials (for both pharmaceutical products and medical devices), and provide for expedited evaluation and approval procedures in national emergency situations.
q_6_4_ampliada: Bioequivalence or biosimilar clinical trials of pharmaceutical products, and advanced therapy clinical trials of pharmaceutical products and medical devices, will be regulated through special regulations to be issued by ARSA for this purpose. In addition, ARSA may apply expedited evaluation and approval procedures for clinical trials in national emergency situations or when it deems appropriate, provided the protection of participants, data integrity, and compliance with the ethical and scientific principles of Good Clinical Practice are guaranteed. The specific criteria for expedited procedures will be defined through supplementary regulatory provisions.
q_6_4_fuente: Acuerdo No. 0256-ARSA-2025 (Disposiciones para la Regulación y Control Sanitario de los Ensayos Clínicos con seres humanos en fase I, II, III, IV y sus cuotas de recuperación), Articles 93 and 94.

q_1_1_directa: The National Regulatory Authority (NRA) for clinical trials is the Comisión Federal para la Protección contra Riesgos Sanitarios (Federal Commission for Protection against Sanitary Risks, COFEPRIS).
q_1_1_ampliada: COFEPRIS operates with technical, administrative, and operational autonomy to regulate, evaluate, and control health research and sanitary risks affecting the Mexican population. Within COFEPRIS, the Comisión de Autorización Sanitaria (Sanitary Authorization Commission, CAS) is responsible for issuing, extending, or revoking clinical research protocol authorizations. The CAS's work is carried out by the Dirección Ejecutiva de Autorización de Productos y Establecimientos, which oversees the Área de Coordinación de Ensayos Clínicos. This body is authorized to monitor and verify approved clinical studies to be conducted in Mexico. The entire technical review and approval process for protocol applications and amendments is centrally managed through the DIGIPRiS digital filing platform.
q_1_1_fuente: Ley General de Salud, Title Two, Chapter II, Article 17 bis and Article 17 bis 2; NOM-012-SSA3-2012, Item 4.2.
q_1_2_directa: Clinical research involving humans is fundamentally governed by the Ley General de Salud and the Reglamento de la Ley General de Salud en Materia de Investigación para la Salud. At the operational and technical level, project conduct is governed by the Norma Oficial Mexicana NOM-012-SSA3-2012.
q_1_2_ampliada: This primary framework is complemented by the Pharmacovigilance Standard (NOM-220-SSA1-2016) and the adoption of the ICH E6 Good Clinical Practice guidelines. The recent 2026 Decree introduced significant reforms to the Ley General de Salud affecting research. These reforms merged the former hospital committees into a single 'Ethics and Research Committee' and established the new mandatory regulatory framework for the application of 'Digital Health' and the use of information technologies in medical and clinical settings.
q_1_2_fuente: Ley General de Salud, Articles 41 Bis, 71 Bis to 71 Octies; Reglamento de la Ley General de Salud en Materia de Investigación para la Salud, Article 1; NOM-012-SSA3-2012, Items 0, 1, and 2; NOM-220-SSA1-2016, Instalación y operación de la farmacovigilancia, Items 1 and 2.
q_1_3_directa: The authorization process is defined by the Reglamento de la Ley General de Salud en Materia de Investigación para la Salud. At the operational level, submission and approval rules are set out in NOM-012-SSA3-2012 and in COFEPRIS's official technical guides.
q_1_3_ampliada: Any project involving the use of medicines or new materials, or seeking to modify established therapeutic indications, requires formal evaluation and authorization from the Secretaría de Salud through COFEPRIS. The process is administratively structured under procedure code COFEPRIS-04-010, which divides trial applications into different modalities depending on the nature of the product.
q_1_3_fuente: Reglamento de la Ley General de Salud en Materia de Investigación para la Salud, Article 62; NOM-012-SSA3-2012, Item 1; Formato COFEPRIS-04-010: Solicitud de Autorización de Protocolo de Investigación en Seres Humanos.
q_1_4_directa: Yes. Every experimental project must have a favorable ruling from the institutional Ethics and Research Committee, which evaluates both the ethical content and the scientific-methodological rigor of the proposed study.
q_1_4_ampliada: Historically, Mexican regulations required separate rulings from a Research Committee and an Ethics in Research Committee. However, following the reforms enacted in the 2026 Decree to the Ley General de Salud (Article 41 Bis), these functions were merged into a single collegiate body formally called the 'Ethics and Research Committee.' This committee must be made up of healthcare professionals, experts trained in bioethics, and non-scientific representatives. For protocols involving radiation or genetic engineering, a ruling from the institutional Biosafety Committee is also still required.
q_1_4_fuente: Ley General de Salud, Article 41 Bis. Reglamento de la Ley General de Salud en Materia de Investigación para la Salud, Article 14, Section VII, and Article 100; NOM-012-SSA3-2012, Item 4.4 and Section 9; Guía para la Solicitud de Protocolos de Investigación en Seres Humanos (COFEPRIS-04-010), Section XI.
q_1_5_directa: Yes, the favorable ruling issued by the Ethics and Research Committee is a mandatory, prior procedural requirement. This official approval document must be uploaded and attached to the authorization application submitted to COFEPRIS.
q_1_5_ampliada: Mexico's clinical regulations impose a sequential review scheme, in which the national regulatory agency makes the start of its technical evaluation conditional on the existence of institutional ethical validation. When entering information on the DIGIPRiS platform, the exact version and dates of the submitted protocol, Investigator's Brochure, and informed consent must match those recorded in the local committee's approval ruling. Ethical and regulatory review time frames therefore cannot run in parallel.
q_1_5_fuente: NOM-012-SSA3-2012, Item 4.4. Guía para la Solicitud de Protocolos de Investigación en Seres Humanos (COFEPRIS-04-010), Sections XI and XII.
q_1_6_directa: Yes. All institutional Ethics and Research Committees must undergo an accreditation and administrative registration process supervised and issued directly by the Comisión Nacional de Bioética (National Bioethics Commission, CONBIOÉTICA).
q_1_6_ampliada: Clinical facilities and establishments may not authorize empirical research without first holding this federal registration. CONBIOÉTICA's accreditation is officially valid for three years, after which the medical institution must process its renewal to continue evaluating protocols. The registration's alphanumeric number must be included in the COFEPRIS-04-010 application to prove the technical validity of its local ethical review.
q_1_6_fuente: Ley General de Salud, Article 41 Bis; Guía Nacional para la Integración y el Funcionamiento de los CEI, Section 3.
q_1_7_directa: Yes, a publicly available registry exists, managed and updated by CONBIOÉTICA. This official catalog lists the establishments legally endorsed to carry out ethical review tasks.
q_1_7_ampliada: As a measure to promote transparency, the federal government keeps available to the general public and industry a complete registry of all Ethics and Research Committees (CEIs) accredited in the country. This digital tool allows sponsors, investigators, and government inspectors to quickly confirm whether the committee designated in a given protocol holds an active, valid sanitary registration.
q_1_7_fuente: Lista de Registro de Comités de Ética en Investigación (CONBIOÉTICA).
q_1_8_directa: Yes. Prior COFEPRIS authorization is required for research involving medicines, biologics, biotechnology products, or new resources, under scenarios A, B, and C of the COFEPRIS-04-010 procedure. No-risk research has no longer required this authorization since the Acuerdo published in the DOF on May 4, 2026, which eliminated modality D of the procedure.
q_1_8_ampliada:
The application for authorization of a research protocol involving human subjects (procedure code COFEPRIS-04-010) covers scenarios A (medicines, biologics, and biotechnology products), B (medicines, bioequivalence studies), and C (new resources: materials, grafts, transplants, prostheses, and physical, chemical, and surgical procedures, excluding pharmacological ones).

The Acuerdo published in the DOF on May 4, 2026 eliminated modality D, "No-Risk Research," which covered observational studies, documentary research, and studies not involving intervention or intentional modification of participants' physiological, psychological, or social variables. As a result, this type of research must still comply with applicable regulations, but no longer requires COFEPRIS authorization to be conducted.
q_1_8_fuente: Reglamento de la Ley General de Salud en Materia de Investigación para la Salud, Article 62; Acuerdo por el que se actualizan los medios de presentación de los trámites COFEPRIS-04-010 y COFEPRIS-09-012 (DOF 04/05/2026), Article Four; Guía para la Solicitud de Protocolos de Investigación en Seres Humanos (COFEPRIS-04-010).
q_2_1_directa: Yes, official regulations formally define the sponsor as the individual, corporation, institution, or organization that takes responsibility for initiating, managing, and/or financing a clinical research project or protocol, whether in whole or in part.
q_2_1_ampliada: The Norma Oficial Mexicana NOM-012-SSA3-2012 and COFEPRIS's Good Clinical Practice guidelines clearly define the sponsor's concept and scope. Under these standards, and consistent with the ICH E6(R1) guideline, the sponsor always retains ultimate responsibility for the quality, data integrity, and ethical conduct of the trial. This applies regardless of whether the entity delegates certain operational functions to authorized third parties, such as Contract Research Organizations (CROs). Any transferred function must be documented in writing, and any obligation not explicitly delegated remains the sponsor's exclusive responsibility.
q_2_1_fuente: NOM-012-SSA3-2012, Item 0; Guía ICH E6(R2) para Buenas Prácticas Clínicas, Section 1.53 and Section 5.
q_2_2_directa: Yes, health legislation requires the protocol applicant and permit holder to reside in Mexico. If the sponsor is foreign, it must carry out its legal and regulatory processes through a legal representative or a Contract Research Organization (CRO) duly domiciled in national territory.
q_2_2_ampliada: The Ley General de Salud stipulates that whoever processes primary approvals, such as protocol authorization and import licenses for medical supplies, must reside in Mexico or operate through an accredited legal representative. Good Clinical Practice guidelines determine that foreign Contract Research Organizations (CROs) must have a registered domicile in the country and a valid operating notice or authorization to carry out clinical activities. The submission ecosystem on the DIGIPRiS platform reinforces this requirement, as it requires the use of the e.firma, a digital certificate issued only by Mexican tax authorities to formally constituted local entities.
q_2_2_fuente: Guía para la Solicitud de Protocolos de Investigación en Seres Humanos (COFEPRIS-04-010), Section I; Términos de Uso de DIGIPRIS; Ley de Firma Electrónica Avanzada.
q_2_3_directa: Yes, the sponsor must assume administrative, financial, and quality assurance responsibilities, formalizing them by submitting a duly completed official single-form document to COFEPRIS. It is also responsible for implementing ongoing control systems, providing supplies and safety information, and ensuring risk coverage for participants.
q_2_3_ampliada: Previously, multiple separate free-form letters were required to certify the absence of conflicts of interest and the adequacy of resources at medical units. Following the recent administrative simplification reforms enacted in 2025, these bureaucratic requirements were consolidated into a "Sponsor Single Form" that centralizes these legal declarations. Nonetheless, under Good Clinical Practice (GCP) standards, the sponsor remains obligated to set out all research roles in writing and to fund an insurance policy or coverage fund for injuries. It must also submit and execute structured audit and clinical monitoring plans throughout the research's life cycle.
q_2_3_fuente: Guía para la Solicitud de Protocolos de Investigación en Seres Humanos (COFEPRIS-04-010), Section IX; Reglamento de la Ley General de Salud en Materia de Investigación para la Salud, Articles 14, 63, and 120; NOM-012-SSA3-2012, Items 6.3.2.4, 7.2, and 7.4.5; Acuerdo por el que se establecen acciones de simplificación para trámites que se realizan ante la Comisión Federal para la Protección contra Riesgos Sanitarios.
q_2_4_directa: Yes, the sponsor may partially or fully delegate the study's operational functions to a CRO, provided each transferred activity is documented in writing through a contract. Despite this delegation, the sponsor retains ultimate legal responsibility for data integrity and the trial's qualitative conduct.
q_2_4_ampliada: The national regulatory framework and Good Clinical Practice guidelines determine that any function, duty, or responsibility not explicitly and documentarily transferred to the CRO remains, by default, under the sponsor's administrative and ethical jurisdiction. The contracted research entity must transparently disclose any potential conflict of interest, incentive, or related financial arrangement. If an internationally based CRO is used, the regulation requires this entity to have a registered tax and corporate domicile in Mexico, backed by an operating notice or sanitary authorization legitimizing its clinical research operations within national territory.
q_2_4_fuente: Guía para la Solicitud de Protocolos de Investigación en Seres Humanos (COFEPRIS-04-010), Section IX and Section III; Guía ICH E6(R2) para Buenas Prácticas Clínicas, Section 5.2.
q_2_5_directa: Yes, the sponsor is required to ensure that every recruited research site has appropriate physical infrastructure, sufficient clinical staff, an active Operating Notice with COFEPRIS, and legal access to a duly accredited Ethics and Research Committee.
q_2_5_ampliada: A site's structural evaluation requires demonstrating technical, human, and material adequacy throughout the entire life of the planned protocol. If the host site lacks its own emergency facilities, it must enter into a referral contract or agreement with an external medical unit meeting the standards of NOM-027-SSA3-2013 for managing serious complications in participants. Consistent with the recent reforms under the 2026 Decree to the Ley General de Salud, designated establishments may not operate without a ruling or the regulatory backing of the now-consolidated Ethics and Research Committee.
q_2_5_fuente: NOM-012-SSA3-2012, Section 8 and Section 10; Guía para la Solicitud de Protocolos de Investigación en Seres Humanos (COFEPRIS-04-010), Section IX; NOM-027-SSA3-2013.
q_2_6_directa: Yes, the Principal Investigator (PI) and selected associate investigators must have the academic credentials, specific training, and technical experience needed to take on the proposed trial's methodological and clinical leadership.
q_2_6_ampliada: The sponsor bears legal responsibility for verifying in advance that the profile of the entire research team aligns with international Good Clinical Practice (GCP) guidelines. At the documentary level, the regulation requires submission of official evidence legally issued in the country; this includes signed curricula vitae, proof of specialized training, and copies of professional licenses corresponding to the areas of the condition being studied. The principal investigator must demonstrate solid prior scientific output or standing, as well as certified training evidence confirming their proficiency in applying GCP standards.
q_2_6_fuente: Reglamento de la Ley General de Salud en Materia de Investigación para la Salud; NOM-012-SSA3-2012.
q_2_7_directa: Yes. Official regulations prohibit the clinical trial from beginning operations if the sponsor does not have a solid financial fund or a civil liability insurance policy protecting participants against any incident arising from the study.
q_2_7_ampliada: This indemnity and medical coverage instrument must be issued in favor of the holding establishment or the sponsor, detailing the study's name, the protocol's alphanumeric code, and the total universe of participants covered locally by the respective site. Under COFEPRIS's current regulatory simplification framework, implemented starting in 2025, the sponsor or representative must submit the definitive document evidencing insurance coverage within 15 business days of the protocol's initial authorization notice being issued. Every consent document given to participants must state that costs arising from incidents fall exclusively on the trial's budgetary provision.
q_2_7_fuente: Reglamento de la Ley General de Salud en Materia de Investigación para la Salud, Article 21, Section X; NOM-012-SSA3-2012, Item 10.6; Acuerdo por el que se establecen acciones de simplificación para trámites que se realizan ante la Comisión Federal para la Protección contra Riesgos Sanitarios.
q_3_1_directa: Yes. The COFEPRIS-04-010 procedure requires the online form, proof of legal representation, proof of payment, the Sponsor Single Form, the research protocol, the Investigator's Brochure, the Ethics and Research Committee's registration and approval ruling, the single forms for the institution's head and the principal investigator and their team, and the Good Manufacturing Practice certificate together with the investigational product's stability report.
q_3_1_ampliada:
The 2025 simplification Acuerdo replaced free-form cover letters with official single forms consolidating the declarations of the sponsor, the institution's head, and the principal investigator. The Acuerdo published in the DOF on May 4, 2026 updated the requirements of the COFEPRIS-04-010 procedure and clarified that the documents provided for in Article Five of the 2025 Acuerdo may be submitted from the time the application is filed and are not subject to ruling as a condition for granting the procedure.

The technical file must include the certificate of compliance with Good Manufacturing Practice for the investigational product, together with the stability report and results for the product and placebo. The protocol, the Investigator's Brochure, and the consent or assent forms are registered, evaluated, and ruled on under Article 41 Bis, Section II, of the Ley General de Salud. Under the sixth transitional provision of the 2026 Acuerdo, the Sponsor Single Form and the institution head's form will no longer be required once the procedure's technological improvements are implemented.
q_3_1_fuente: Ley General de Salud, Article 41 Bis, Section II; Acuerdo por el que se establecen acciones de simplificación para trámites que se realizan ante la Comisión Federal para la Protección contra Riesgos Sanitarios; Acuerdo por el que se actualizan los medios de presentación de los trámites COFEPRIS-04-010 y COFEPRIS-09-012 (DOF 04/05/2026), Articles Three and Five.
q_3_2_directa: Yes. Under the Acuerdo published in the DOF on May 4, 2026, the procedure follows a hybrid process: the application is submitted through the DIGIPRiS: Regulación en Línea platform and, when it results in an authorization, delivery is made through COFEPRIS's Centro Integral de Servicios (Comprehensive Service Center, CIS). The application is signed with an advanced electronic signature (e.firma), and, while the technological upgrades are being carried out, submission continues to be done through DIGIPRiS.
q_3_2_ampliada:
The authorized user completes the required fields on the platform and uploads the documentation in unrestricted, readable PDF format. The platform handles both protocol authorization applications (procedure code COFEPRIS-04-010) and modifications and amendments (procedure code COFEPRIS-09-012). Under the Acuerdo of May 4, 2026, the procedure operates under a hybrid scheme: submission is digital through DIGIPRiS: Regulación en Línea, and delivery of applications resulting in authorization is made through the Centro Integral de Servicios (CIS).

COFEPRIS uses the email address provided by the applicant as the official channel for issuing notices and notifications of deficiency requests or dismissal. The deficiency request is issued only once and must be addressed through the Nube Ensayos Clínicos in a single file upload; documentation uploaded after that first upload is not taken into account.
q_3_2_fuente: Acuerdo por el que se actualizan los medios de presentación de los trámites COFEPRIS-04-010 y COFEPRIS-09-012 (DOF 04/05/2026), Articles One and Two; Guía para la Solicitud de Protocolos de Investigación en Seres Humanos (COFEPRIS-04-010), Section I and Section IX; Manual del Usuario DIGIPRIS - Investigación y Ensayos Clínicos.
q_3_3_directa: Yes. Current regulations establish that COFEPRIS must complete the technical review and issue a ruling to authorize research protocols within a maximum of 30 calendar days. In cases where the sponsor relies on a foreign-decision recognition model (reliance), the agency has up to 45 calendar days.
q_3_3_ampliada: The review process timeline follows specific deadlines. During the evaluation, if the authority finds inconsistencies or requires additional information, it will issue a deficiency notice within the first 10 calendar days; after notification, the sponsor has a 5-business-day window to address the findings. If the health agency fails to respond once the statutory 30 days have elapsed, the application is deemed constructively denied and considered rejected. Alternatively, applicants may submit their files for an optional pre-ruling managed by the Unidades Habilitadas de Apoyo al Pre-dictamen (Authorized Pre-Ruling Support Units, UHAP), which have a maximum resolution time of 30 calendar days.
q_3_3_fuente: Acuerdo por el que se establecen acciones de simplificación para trámites que se realizan ante la Comisión Federal para la Protección contra Riesgos Sanitarios; Reglamento de la Ley General de Salud en Materia de Investigación para la Salud, Article 122; Guía para la Solicitud de Protocolos de Investigación en Seres Humanos (COFEPRIS-04-010) Modality D, Section "PRE DICTAMEN DE LA UHAP-INP".
q_3_4_directa: Yes, payment of federal fees is a mandatory administrative requirement. The applicant must generate and attach the original proof of payment validated by the bank in order for COFEPRIS's technical review to proceed.
q_3_4_ampliada: All procedures involving clinical protocols, from the initial evaluation application (procedure code COFEPRIS-04-010) to processing methodological amendments (procedure code COFEPRIS-09-012), carry a specific, non-refundable fee. During data entry on DIGIPRiS, the investigator or sponsor must enter the transaction's alphanumeric code, which serves as a fiscal cross-check mechanism. If the automated tracking of the payment reference detects inconsistencies between the deposit and the annual fee amount set by the Ley Federal de Derechos, the procedure will be summarily rejected. The applicable costs for these evaluations are determined and published annually by the regulatory commission itself.
q_3_4_fuente: Guía para la Solicitud de Protocolos de Investigación en Seres Humanos (COFEPRIS-04-010), Section VIII; Ley Federal de Derechos.
q_3_5_directa: Yes. Registering the protocol's general and scientific information is a mandatory directive within national territory. This mandate is executed automatically by integrating the application into the Registro Nacional de Ensayos Clínicos (National Clinical Trials Registry, RNEC v2.0) at the time the study is authorized.
q_3_5_ampliada: While completing the electronic application on the DIGIPRiS platform, the system requires the applicant to enter informational fields that the legal framework predefines as public. Once the evaluating body approves the trial's technical merits, the system automatically migrates this data to the RNEC v2.0 disclosure repository, managed by the same agency. This openly searchable database displays core attributes such as the sponsor's name, the trial's operational phases, the list of authorized hospital sites, and the primary recruitment profiles.
q_3_5_fuente: Guía para la Solicitud de Protocolos de Investigación en Seres Humanos (COFEPRIS-04-010).
q_3_6_directa: Yes. The legal framework has a simplified validation mechanism (a 'reliance' model) designed to recognize rulings previously issued by foreign high-surveillance National Regulatory Authorities. Its scope is limited exclusively to studies and interventions classified as Phase III.
q_3_6_ampliada: The interinstitutional agreement grants COFEPRIS the authority to recognize approval notices issued by leading peer agencies, namely: the European Medicines Agency (EMA), the US FDA, the UK's MHRA, and Health Canada. Organizations invoking this approval pathway benefit from an expedited review period of 45 calendar days. At the documentary level, an apostilled certification of the primary international authorization must be submitted through the portal, accompanied by its corresponding Spanish translations. However, this exception mechanism is not available for trials with adaptive designs, studies conducted under external expedited schemes, or medicines under serious safety alerts issued by the World Health Organization.
q_3_6_fuente: Acuerdo por el que se establecen los criterios para la autorización de protocolos de investigación en seres humanos que cuenten con la autorización previa por una autoridad regulatoria extranjera.
q_3_7_directa: The procedural flow follows a mandatory sequence of steps. The research team develops the protocol, obtains institutional ethical approval in advance, and then electronically submits the entire technical package to the DIGIPRiS environment for review and eventual approval by COFEPRIS.
q_3_7_ampliada: The initial phase involves the clinical design and technical compilation; here, the sponsor incorporates the Investigator's Brochure, the protocol, and the new standardized Single Forms declaring infrastructure and absence of conflicts. Next, sites must secure the study's approval from their accredited Ethics and Research Committee, and from the Biosafety Committee where warranted, in accordance with the reforms enacted under the 2026 Decree. With these favorable rulings in hand, the sponsor's legal representative submits the application on DIGIPRiS, signs it using the e.firma, and pays the applicable fees. The state's evaluation phase is limited to 30 calendar days; if deficiencies exist, a deficiency notice is triggered, which the applicant must address within 5 business days. This leads either to the protocol's authorization or to its administrative rejection.
q_3_7_fuente: NOM-012-SSA3-2012; Guía para la Solicitud de Protocolos de Investigación en Seres Humanos (COFEPRIS-04-010).
q_4_1_directa: Yes. The minimum mandatory information the investigational medicine's label must contain includes the sponsor's or primary contact's name, address, and telephone number, the pharmaceutical form, the route of administration, the batch number, the expiry date, and the statement "Exclusivamente para estudios clínicos" [For clinical study use only].
q_4_1_ampliada: Labeling of medicines for clinical use is subject to the applicable legal provisions, as established by the Norma Oficial Mexicana on Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP). The product's packaging must protect it from alteration, contamination, and damage during storage and shipping.
q_4_1_fuente: NOM-059-SSA1-2015, Buenas prácticas de fabricación de medicamentos, Regulatory Appendix C.
q_4_2_directa: Yes, submitting documentation certifying Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) compliance is mandatory. This guarantees that the investigational product and placebo maintain the identity, purity, safety, potency, and quality characteristics required for their use.
q_4_2_ampliada: This documentation is required in the "Investigational Product" section of the COFEPRIS-04-010 application. Medicines for research use in Mexico must be released in accordance with Good Clinical Practice and the sponsor's established procedures. The sponsor must keep the file with information related to the medicine's manufacture and control for at least 5 years after the product's registration is granted.
q_4_2_fuente: NOM-059-SSA1-2015, Buenas prácticas de fabricación de medicamentos, Items 1.1 and 1.2; Guía para la Solicitud de Protocolos de Investigación en Seres Humanos (COFEPRIS-04-010), Section "Producto de investigación".
q_4_3_directa: No, information on imported supplies is informational only, not an authorization, so those responsible for the study must apply for the import permit through a separate procedure before the relevant authority.
q_4_3_ampliada: The protocol application (COFEPRIS-04-010) requires a letter listing imported supplies, stating their quantity and description, with a maximum surplus of 20%. However, this information will not be cited in the authorization notice. Protocol authorization is not equivalent to an import permit.
q_4_3_fuente: Guía para la Solicitud de Protocolos de Investigación en Seres Humanos (COFEPRIS-04-010), Section XIV; Homoclave COFEPRIS-01-010-A.
q_5_1_directa: Yes. Reports to the Centro Nacional de Farmacovigilancia (National Pharmacovigilance Center, CNFV) follow a differentiated scheme: fatal events must be reported within 7 calendar days, and non-fatal serious events within 15 calendar days. Two or more similar serious cases at the same site with the same batch require immediate notification (within a maximum of 48 hours). Non-serious events must be reported when the clinical study ends.
q_5_1_ampliada: The Principal Investigator has the dual responsibility of reporting adverse events both to the National Pharmacovigilance Center and to their institution's Ethics in Research and Research Committees. Expedited reporting of individual cases is managed through global electronic platforms such as VigiFlow. The recent 2026 Decree to the Ley General de Salud reinforces that COFEPRIS permanently coordinates and reports these activities nationally through that Center. For fatal events, the 7-day time frame corresponds to an initial notification. The research team subsequently has up to 15 calendar days to deliver the complete, detailed report.
q_5_1_fuente: NOM-220-SSA1-2016, Instalación y operación de la farmacovigilancia, Item 8.1.10.1 and the associated reporting time frame tables; NOM-012-SSA3-2012; Guía para la Presentación de la Información de los Informes Técnico-Descriptivos.
q_5_2_directa: Yes, the regulation requires submission of an annual clinical safety report. The deadline for submitting this document is determined by the date on which COFEPRIS granted the study's first national authorization.
q_5_2_ampliada: Official clinical research pharmacovigilance guidelines establish that the registration holder, the sponsor, or its legal representative is obligated to submit these periodic reports. Every clinical safety report must be written in Spanish and submitted electronically through the National Pharmacovigilance Center's channels. The regulation also requires submission of a final safety report. This definitive report must be delivered when the clinical study ends normally, is canceled, or is permanently suspended, provided it included at least one research site in the country.
q_5_2_fuente: NOM-220-SSA1-2016, Instalación y operación de la farmacovigilancia, Items 7.1.5 and 8.1.10.2; Guía de Farmacovigilancia para la Investigación Clínica (G-ClinResPV); Guía de Farmacovigilancia para la Elaboración del Reporte Periódico de Seguridad (G-PharmPerSafRpt).
q_5_3_directa: Yes, the Principal Investigator (PI) must submit a Partial Technical Report to the Secretaría at least once a year to communicate the research's progress and partial results.
q_5_3_ampliada: Technical-descriptive reports are a follow-up task the PI must perform. The Partial Technical Report is submitted to COFEPRIS through a free-form letter ("Escrito Libre") at no cost, and must use the established format, including the study's status, a summary of Adverse Drug Reaction (ADR) and Adverse Event (AE) reports, and relevant information indicating the research's progress in the Results and Conclusions section.
