The PI must deliver a copy of each report to the Research and Ethics in Research Committees.
q_5_3_fuente: NOM-012-SSA3-2012, Section 7, Item 7.4; Guía para la Presentación de la Información de los Informes Técnico-Descriptivos.
q_5_4_directa: Yes. Amendments to the base documents (protocol, Investigator's Brochure, and informed consent) are processed under procedure code COFEPRIS-09-012 in its "with ruling" form, which requires prior COFEPRIS authorization. The Acuerdo published in the DOF on May 4, 2026 also created an "immediate resolution" form for certain administrative changes, in which COFEPRIS only validates payment of fees. In situations of imminent risk, safety amendments may be applied immediately and formalized afterward.
q_5_4_ampliada:
Any modification processed under procedure code COFEPRIS-09-012 can follow one of two pathways. Under the "with ruling" form, COFEPRIS evaluates the application and issues a decision following a favorable ruling from the Ethics and Research Committee; this is the pathway applicable to amendments to the protocol, the Investigator's Brochure, and the informed consent or assent. Under the "immediate resolution" form, provided for in the Acuerdo of May 4, 2026 for changes or additions to the research team, changes to the emergency-referral site, and the change or addition of an importer, COFEPRIS validates payment of fees and issues a record that takes effect as authorization and remains subject to subsequent verification.

The regulatory framework retains an exception to protect participants: in the event of severe adverse events or imminent risks, the principal investigator may implement safety changes immediately. After the event is addressed, the investigator must submit the documentary evidence and technical justifications to the Ethics and Research Committee and to the Secretaría de Salud for the record and formalization.
q_5_4_fuente: NOM-012-SSA3-2012, Item 10.3; Acuerdo por el que se actualizan los medios de presentación de los trámites COFEPRIS-04-010 y COFEPRIS-09-012 (DOF 04/05/2026), Articles Six, Seven, and Eight; Guía para el Sometimiento de Enmiendas al Protocolo de Investigación en Seres Humanos (COFEPRIS-09-012).
q_5_5_directa: Yes, the principal investigator has an obligation to arrange for the research subject to continue treatment and care after the study ends. This seeks to avoid side effects arising from discontinuing the experimental intervention.
q_5_5_ampliada: This extended provision of treatment and care must be considered from the research's budget-design stage. The informed consent the participant signs before the study must detail the continued medical treatment they will have access to. The study's budget must also provide for a policy or mechanisms to compensate the person, without prejudice to the continuity of their institutional medical care. All of this must be recorded in the documents ruled on by the Ethics in Research Committee.
q_5_5_fuente: NOM-012-SSA3-2012, Item 11.2.2; Reglamento de la Ley General de Salud en Materia de Investigación para la Salud, Article 14.
q_6_1_directa: Yes. Since 2025, the country has had two main legal frameworks for personal data protection: the Ley Federal de Protección de Datos Personales en Posesión de los Particulares (private sector) and the Ley General de Protección de Datos Personales en Posesión de Sujetos Obligados (public sector). Both govern the handling of confidential information and the clinical records of research subjects.
q_6_1_ampliada:
Since March 21, 2025, personal data protection in Mexico has been governed by two laws issued that year: the Ley Federal de Protección de Datos Personales en Posesión de los Particulares, applicable to sponsors and private entities, and the Ley General de Protección de Datos Personales en Posesión de Sujetos Obligados, applicable to public institutions; both repealed the previous 2010 and 2017 legislation.

Current legislation requires the data controller to issue a Privacy Notice to the participant and obtain their express, written consent to process sensitive personal data, such as health data. Research subjects retain, at all times, the right to exercise access, rectification, cancellation, and objection (ARCO rights) over their information. All information arising from the clinical study must be handled confidentially and with administrative, physical, and technical security measures. The 2026 Decree to the Ley General de Salud also incorporates Digital Health and Telehealth guidelines, which reinforce the obligation to safeguard the confidentiality and integrity of personal data in digital medical environments.
q_6_1_fuente: Ley Federal de Protección de Datos Personales en Posesión de los Particulares, Articles 8, 14, and 21; Ley General de Protección de Datos Personales en Posesión de Sujetos Obligados, Articles 21 and 37; NOM-004-SSA3-2012, Del expediente clínico; NOM-012-SSA3-2012, Item 5.10; Ley General de Salud, Article 71 Septies.
q_6_2_directa: Yes, the applicable Norma Oficial Mexicana subjects vaccines to pharmacovigilance guidelines for monitoring their safety issues during research and marketing. The authority centralizes all reports of effects associated with immunization products.
q_6_2_ampliada: This regulation defines the mechanisms for mandatory reporting of Events Supposedly Attributable to Vaccination or Immunization (ESAVI). The Centro Nacional de Farmacovigilancia y Tecnovigilancia has the primary function of managing all safety information on medicines and vaccines tested or distributed in the country. The sponsor and the research site are responsible for assessing and submitting the Periodic Safety Reports (RPS) required for vaccines, so that COFEPRIS can assess their risk-benefit ratio. Recent updates to the Ley General de Salud also reaffirm COFEPRIS's authority to control all biological products and vaccines within the territory.
q_6_2_fuente: NOM-220-SSA1-2016, Instalación y operación de la farmacovigilancia, Items 2, 4, and 8.1.5.
q_6_3_directa: Yes, the handling of human biological samples and material is regulated by the Ley General de Salud, its implementing regulations, and CONBIOÉTICA's ethical provisions. Their commercialization is prohibited, and express, written consent from the donor is always required.
q_6_3_ampliada: To collect, process, and store biological samples (such as tissue, cells, blood, and blood products), the research subject must give specific, independent authorization. The Ethics in Research Committee is responsible for setting time limits on the use of biological material and prohibiting its use for undisclosed purposes. The recent 2026 Decree to the Ley General de Salud significantly expands and modernizes the applicable framework. These recent reforms reinforce the principles of altruism, traceability, and non-profit in the disposition of stem cells and blood products. They also integrate the registration of these activities with the Centro Nacional de la Transfusión Sanguínea, establishing mandatory specialized biovigilance committees at all authorized establishments.
q_6_3_fuente: Ley General de Salud, Articles 314, 316, 327, 340 Bis, 341, and 342 Bis 3; Guía Nacional para la Integración y el Funcionamiento de los CEI; Reglamento de la Ley General de Salud en Materia de Trasplantes, Article 33.
q_6_4_directa: Yes, various specific regulations set out detailed rules for interchangeability (generics) and biocomparability (biosimilars) studies, as well as no-risk research. For bioequivalence tests specifically, these must be conducted by units or sites certified as Authorized Third Parties.
q_6_4_ampliada: Current regulations govern the tests used to demonstrate therapeutic equivalence and require compliance with Good Clinical Practice and adverse event monitoring at all times. There are also specific rules for submitting studies with biotechnology medicines and evaluating new non-pharmacological technical or surgical resources. Post-marketing and research surveillance has also evolved. The recent 2026 Decree to the Ley General de Salud formalizes and elevates the mandatory nature of technovigilance to the level of law. This mechanism, set out in the new Article 262 Bis, establishes systematic safety monitoring of medical devices in use through mandatory reporting of any adverse incident.
q_6_4_fuente: Norma Oficial Mexicana NOM-177-SSA1-2013; NOM-240-SSA1-2012, Instalación y operación de la tecnovigilancia; Ley General de Salud, Article 262 Bis.

q_1_1_directa: The National Regulatory Authority (NRA) for clinical trials in Nicaragua is the Autoridad Nacional de Regulación Sanitaria (National Health Regulatory Authority, ANRS), under the Ministry of Health (MINSA). The ANRS evaluates the investigational product's safety profile and issues a Technical Report whose conclusion is binding for the trial's authorization.
q_1_1_ampliada:
NTON 19001:2022 defines the ANRS as the National Regulatory Authority (NRA), responsible for the sanitary regulation of medicines and for controlling investigational products. Its involvement in a clinical trial is expressed through a Technical Report on the product's safety profile, whose conclusion is binding.

Conducting a clinical trial, however, does not depend on the ANRS alone. Nicaragua applies a dual-approval system: final authorization to begin the trial rests with the Comité Nacional de Investigación en Salud (National Health Research Committee, CONIS), which cannot issue it without first obtaining the approvals of the Research Ethics Committee (CEI) and, decisively, the ANRS's binding Technical Report. Verifying compliance with NTON 19001 is the responsibility of MINSA through the ANRS, which acts as the executing arm of sanitary surveillance and control, while CONIS holds the final decision on the study's viability.
q_1_1_fuente: Norma Técnica Obligatoria Nicaragüense NTON 19001:2022, "Medicamentos de Uso Humano. Ensayos Clínicos. Requisitos para su Autorización" (Chapter 4, item 1; Chapter 5, item 1; Chapter 13, first part; Chapter 18); Ley N°. 1068, "Ley Creadora de la Autoridad Nacional de Regulación Sanitaria (ANRS)" (Article 4).
q_1_2_directa: Health research in Nicaragua is governed hierarchically by Ley N°. 423, the Ley General de Salud, which establishes the State's obligation to promote research and creates the National Research Committee. This law is complemented by the Norma Técnica Obligatoria Nicaragüense (NTON) 19001, which details the specific requirements for conducting clinical trials and requires adherence to international ethical standards.
q_1_2_ampliada: Ley N°. 423 declares research a fundamental action of the Ministry of Health (MINSA). Article 15 establishes that MINSA must "promote scientific research in health." Article 16 of the same law requires all research involving human subjects to be governed by internationally accepted scientific and ethical principles, and mentions the existence of a "National Research Committee" (now CONIS) to promote and prioritize research topics. NTON 19001 gives effect to this mandate by explicitly establishing that clinical trials must comply with the principles of the Declaration of Helsinki, the Belmont Report, and internationally accepted Good Clinical Practice (GCP) standards.
q_1_2_fuente: Ley N°. 423, "Ley General de Salud" (Title III, Chapter I, Section I, Articles 15 and 16); Norma Técnica Obligatoria Nicaragüense NTON 19001:2022, "Medicamentos de Uso Humano. Ensayos Clínicos. Requisitos para su Autorización" (Chapter 3, item 3.1; Chapter 5, item 4).
q_1_3_directa: The Norma Técnica Obligatoria Nicaragüense (NTON) 19001, published in October 2022, is the main, specific regulation setting out the detailed requirements and procedures for authorizing drug clinical trials involving human subjects in the country.
q_1_3_ampliada: NTON 19001's purpose is to "establish the requirements and procedures for regulating drug clinical trials," and its scope covers "all drug clinical trials in human subjects conducted at authorized institutions." This regulation implements Ley N°. 292, the Ley de Medicamentos y Farmacias, whose Article 17 sets out the general mandate that "conducting drug studies and clinical trials in the country requires authorization and oversight from the Ministry of Health, for which the corresponding regulation shall be issued." Ley 292 therefore creates the legal obligation, and NTON 19001 implements it in practice.
q_1_3_fuente: Norma Técnica Obligatoria Nicaragüense NTON 19001:2022, "Medicamentos de Uso Humano. Ensayos Clínicos. Requisitos para su Autorización" (Chapter 1: Purpose; Chapter 2: Scope of Application); Ley N°. 292, "Ley de Medicamentos y Farmacias" (Title II, Article 17).
q_1_4_directa: Yes, favorable approval from a Research Ethics Committee (CEI) is an indispensable, prior requirement for CONIS to authorize any clinical trial.
q_1_4_ampliada: The regulation assigns the sponsor responsibility for "ensuring approval from the CEI authorized by CONIS" before proceeding with the trial authorization application. Chapter 5 of NTON 19001 explicitly states that CONIS's authorization to begin a trial is contingent on first having, among other things, the CEI's approval. The regulation defines the CEI as the independent body whose primary responsibility is to "ensure the protection of the rights, safety, and well-being of the human subjects involved in a study."
q_1_4_fuente: Norma Técnica Obligatoria Nicaragüense NTON 19001:2022, "Medicamentos de Uso Humano. Ensayos Clínicos. Requisitos para su Autorización" (Chapter 4, item 7; Chapter 5, item 1; Chapter 10, item 10.1, item b).
q_1_5_directa: Yes, the CEI's approval letter is a mandatory component of the documentary dossier the sponsor or investigator must submit to CONIS to request the clinical trial's authorization.
q_1_5_ampliada: Among the documents the sponsor or investigator must submit to CONIS to request clinical trial authorization is the approval letter from the CEI registered with CONIS, in cases where an independent CEI is used. CONIS's final authorization to begin conducting the trial requires the trial to first have the CEI's approval.
q_1_5_fuente: Norma Técnica Obligatoria Nicaragüense NTON 19001:2022, "Medicamentos de Uso Humano. Ensayos Clínicos. Requisitos para su Autorización" (Chapter 5, item 1 and item 2, item e).
q_1_6_directa: Yes, an accreditation and authorization system exists for Research Ethics Committees (CEIs), administered by the Ministry of Health through CONIS. Any CEI evaluating clinical trials must be duly accredited and authorized by this governing body for its rulings to have regulatory validity.
q_1_6_ampliada: Nicaraguan regulations formally establish that Research Ethics Committees (CEIs) must be accredited by the Ministry of Health to legally operate in reviewing clinical trial protocols. The implementing regulation of Ley 292 requires a prior report issued by an Ethics Committee duly accredited by the health authority. In addition, both Normativa 166 and the more recent NTON 19001:2022 reaffirm that the sponsor or principal investigator must ensure approval from a CEI that is expressly authorized and registered with CONIS. CONIS thus serves as the central body concentrating the authorization and rigorous oversight of ethics committees, whether independent or institutional, ensuring they meet the standards for ruling on research involving human subjects.
q_1_6_fuente: Norma Técnica Obligatoria Nicaragüense NTON 19001:2022, "Medicamentos de Uso Humano. Ensayos Clínicos. Requisitos para su Autorización" (Chapter 4, items 6 and 42; Chapter 5, item 2, items b and e). Texto Consolidado, Normativa-166 – Norma para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos de Medicamentos en Seres Humanos (MINSA), Chapters VI and VII.
q_1_7_directa: Nicaraguan legislation requires Research Ethics Committees (CEIs) to be registered with CONIS. However, current health regulations do not explicitly specify that this registry is public or freely searchable by the general public.
q_1_7_ampliada: Under the national regulatory framework, every independent or institutional Research Ethics Committee (CEI) involved in evaluating clinical trials must have formal registration with CONIS. Applicable technical regulations require, as part of the unavoidable documentary requirements for authorizing a trial, submission of an approval letter issued by a CEI duly "registered with CONIS." Although the Ministry of Health maintains this official register and control of accredited, authorized committees, the legal texts do not detail mechanisms for this registry to be published or openly searchable by the general public. The legislation focuses primarily on the registry's existence for compliance, regulatory, and internal oversight purposes by the health authorities.
q_1_7_fuente: Normativa-166 – Norma para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos de Medicamentos en Seres Humanos (MINSA), Chapter VII; Norma Técnica Obligatoria Nicaragüense NTON 19001:2022, "Medicamentos de Uso Humano. Ensayos Clínicos. Requisitos para su Autorización", Item 5.1.
q_1_8_directa: Yes. All drug clinical trials involving human subjects conducted within Nicaraguan territory, without exception, require prior authorization from CONIS before any study-related activity may begin.
q_1_8_ampliada: NTON 19001's scope of application is universal for "all drug clinical trials in human subjects." The regulation broadly defines "clinical trial" as any research in humans intended to verify clinical or pharmacological effects and confirm a product's safety and/or efficacy. The mandatory nature of prior authorization is underscored in Chapter 5, which categorically states: "A clinical trial may only begin once it has been authorized by CONIS."
q_1_8_fuente: Norma Técnica Obligatoria Nicaragüense NTON 19001:2022, "Medicamentos de Uso Humano. Ensayos Clínicos. Requisitos para su Autorización" (Chapter 2; Chapter 4, item 12; Chapter 5, item 1).
q_2_1_directa: Yes. The regulation defines the sponsor as an individual, group, company, institution, or organization (including academic ones) with legal representation in Nicaragua that assumes full responsibility for a clinical trial's initiation, management, and/or financing.
q_2_1_ampliada: The legal definition, found in NTON 19001's Terms and Definitions section, emphasizes the sponsor's full responsibility for the trial's entire life cycle, from conception through financing. A key element of the definition is the requirement to have "legal representation in the country," which lays the basis for the requirement of a local representative for foreign sponsors.
q_2_1_fuente: Norma Técnica Obligatoria Nicaragüense NTON 19001:2022, "Medicamentos de Uso Humano. Ensayos Clínicos. Requisitos para su Autorización" (Chapter 4, item 28).
q_2_2_directa: Yes, this is a mandatory requirement. If the sponsor is a foreign entity, it must appoint and maintain a legal representative domiciled in Nicaragua for the entire duration of the clinical trial.
q_2_2_ampliada: NTON 19001 establishes this obligation explicitly in the chapter on sponsor responsibilities, stating that "if the sponsor is foreign, it is obligated to have a legal representative in Nicaragua." The regulation defines the "sponsor's legal representative" as the person accredited to act on the sponsor's behalf when it is not established in the country. This role serves as the legal and administrative point of contact with Nicaraguan authorities.
q_2_2_fuente: Norma Técnica Obligatoria Nicaragüense NTON 19001:2022, "Medicamentos de Uso Humano. Ensayos Clínicos. Requisitos para su Autorización" (Chapter 4, item 39; Chapter 10, item 10.1, item c).
q_2_3_directa: Yes. To act as a sponsor, an entity must have legal representation in Nicaragua and take on a set of key responsibilities, including: obtaining all necessary regulatory authorizations before starting, ensuring compliance with Good Clinical Practice (GCP), securing the trial's full financing, and providing a financial guarantee (insurance policy or notarized statement) to cover potential harm to participants.
q_2_3_ampliada: The sponsor's obligations are extensively detailed in Chapter 10 of NTON 19001. The most notable include: obtaining CONIS's written authorization before starting the trial; ensuring all study information and documentation complies with GCP; ensuring the investigational medicine complies with Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP), Good Laboratory Practice (GLP), and Good Storage Practice (GSP); and having an insurance policy or, alternatively, committing through a notarized statement to cover all medical care costs and related expenses for any harm to a participant's health arising from the trial.
q_2_3_fuente: Norma Técnica Obligatoria Nicaragüense NTON 19001:2022, "Medicamentos de Uso Humano. Ensayos Clínicos. Requisitos para su Autorización" (Chapter 4, item 28; Chapter 10, item 10.1, items a, d, j, q).
q_2_4_directa: The sponsor may transfer any trial-related task or function to a Contract Research Organization (OIC/CRO), but must do so through a written agreement clearly specifying the delegated tasks. Fundamentally, ultimate responsibility for the trial data's quality and integrity always remains with the sponsor.
q_2_4_ampliada: The regulation allows delegating functions to a CRO, but imposes strict conditions. Every task transfer must be "specified in writing" before the study begins. The CRO, in turn, must implement and document in writing its own quality assurance and quality control procedures. Although the CRO takes on the operational responsibilities of the functions transferred to it, NTON 19001 is clear that ultimate responsibility cannot be delegated and rests with the sponsor.
q_2_4_fuente: Norma Técnica Obligatoria Nicaragüense NTON 19001:2022, "Medicamentos de Uso Humano. Ensayos Clínicos. Requisitos para su Autorización" (Chapter 10, item 10.2, items a, b, d).
q_2_5_directa: Yes, Nicaragua has specific requirements for selecting clinical research sites. Every public or private institution participating as a research site must be registered and expressly authorized by CONIS. The sponsor and principal investigator must also ensure the site has adequate infrastructure, the necessary equipment, and qualified staff to conduct the study in accordance with Good Clinical Practice (GCP).
q_2_5_ampliada: To serve as a research site, an establishment must meet the basic infrastructure and response-capacity requirements that guarantee study subjects' safety and well-being, tailored to the specific demands of the trial phase (I, II, or III). During the trial's authorization application, a copy of the Registry as a CONIS-authorized Research Site and approval from the authorities of the institution where the trial will be conducted must be submitted. A notarized statement certifying the availability of funding and specific physical spaces is also required, such as consulting rooms, secure archives, controlled-condition storage for investigational products, and access to emergency medical care. The sponsor is obligated to select suitable institutions with trained staff, and to ensure these quality standards are maintained throughout the clinical study's conduct. Finally, these sites are subject to sanitary licensing, as well as to ordinary and extraordinary inspections and audits by CONIS bodies and the ANRS, to verify strict regulatory compliance.
q_2_5_fuente: Normativa-166 – Norma para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos de Medicamentos en Seres Humanos (MINSA), Chapter VI, Chapter VII, and Annex VI; Norma Técnica Obligatoria Nicaragüense NTON 19001:2022, "Medicamentos de Uso Humano. Ensayos Clínicos. Requisitos para su Autorización", Items 4, 5.1, and 5.2.
q_2_6_directa: Yes, legislation requires specific criteria for investigators, with the sponsor bearing the initial responsibility for their proper selection. The principal investigator must be a qualified healthcare professional with proven experience in research and in the particular clinical area of the proposed trial. They must also demonstrate recognized professional integrity and commit to strict compliance with Good Clinical Practice (GCP).
q_2_6_ampliada: Under Nicaragua's regulatory framework, the selection of professionals responsible for a trial must guarantee their full technical and ethical competence to assess the clinical response to investigational products. To validate this fitness, submitting updated curricula vitae for the principal investigator, co-investigators, and study coordinators to CONIS is a mandatory requirement. Beyond medical qualifications, the regulations require these individuals to have recognized ethical standing and to formally take on responsibility for ensuring procedures are conducted while protecting patients' rights, safety, and well-being. The sponsor has a legal duty to confirm that the research team is duly trained and agrees to submit to the monitoring, audits, and provisions set by the health authorities and local ethics committees.
q_2_6_fuente: Norma Técnica Obligatoria Nicaragüense NTON 19001:2022, "Medicamentos de Uso Humano. Ensayos Clínicos. Requisitos para su Autorización". Items 5.1 and 10.3; Normativa-166 – Norma para la Regulación de Ensayos Clínicos de Medicamentos en Seres Humanos (MINSA), Chapters VI and VII.
q_2_7_directa: Yes. The sponsor is required to guarantee financial coverage for potential harm to participants' health. This may be met in two ways: submitting a valid insurance policy or, alternatively, signing a notarized statement committing to cover all medical care costs and other related expenses if a subject is harmed as a result of participating in the trial.
q_2_7_ampliada: Submitting the "copy of the valid insurance policy" or the notarized statement (a template for which is provided in Annex G of the regulation) is a documentary requirement for the trial's authorization. This obligation covers the guarantee of free medical treatment and compensation for financial losses arising directly from harm to health, provided such harm is not inherent to the subject's underlying condition. The regulation also provides for financial compensation for extraordinary expenses incurred by the participant to take part in the study (such as transportation, lodging, communication, and meals). These costs must be covered by the trial's budget and clearly specified in the informed consent document, so the participant is aware of them and accepts them in advance.
q_2_7_fuente: Norma Técnica Obligatoria Nicaragüense NTON 19001:2022, "Medicamentos de Uso Humano. Ensayos Clínicos. Requisitos para su Autorización" (Chapter 5, item 2, item h; Chapter 8, penultimate paragraph; Chapter 9, item 9.2, item i; Chapter 10, item 10.1, item q).
q_3_1_directa: Yes. The sponsor or principal investigator must submit to CONIS an application dossier containing eleven essential documents and/or document categories. This package includes the application form, the research protocol, the Investigator's Brochure, the CEI's approval, the insurance policy (or notarized statement), the budget, and proof of fee payment.
q_3_1_ampliada: The full content of the initial authorization submission is detailed in Chapter 5, item 2 of NTON 19001 and comprises the following elements: Authorization application form (Annex B); Copy of the Registry as a CONIS-authorized Research Site; Authorization from the highest authority of the institution where the trial will be conducted; Research Protocol (per Annex H) and Informed Consent template (in Spanish and in the original language, if applicable); Approval letter from the CEI registered with CONIS; Updated Investigator's Brochure (per Annex J); Detailed Clinical Trial Budget (per Annex I); Copy of the valid insurance policy or notarized statement; Curricula Vitae of the core research team (Principal Investigator, Co-investigators, and Coordinators); Proof of payment of the processing fee; List of investigational products and other supplies needed for the trial (per Annex K).
q_3_1_fuente: Norma Técnica Obligatoria Nicaragüense NTON 19001:2022, "Medicamentos de Uso Humano. Ensayos Clínicos. Requisitos para su Autorización" (Chapter 5, item 2, items a-k).
q_3_2_directa: Nicaraguan regulations do not establish a specific electronic platform for submitting the initial clinical trial application, requiring the file to be submitted directly to CONIS. In terms of format, official standardized forms must be used, and legal documents must be submitted in original or legalized-copy form, entirely drafted in Spanish or accompanied by an official translation.
q_3_2_ampliada: The submission process requires the sponsor or principal investigator to compile a complete technical and legal file for formal submission to CONIS. Under general provisions, any official or legal document issued abroad must be duly legalized (apostilled or consularized), ensuring full legal validity in the country. All required scientific, clinical, and administrative information must also be provided in its original language and translated into Spanish. This covers everything from the research protocol and the Investigator's Brochure to the informed consent document and insurance policies. Finally, although the study's initial authorization is managed through document submission to CONIS, the import processes for the trial's required supplies are digitized; these are processed through the Import System of the Ventanilla Única de Comercio Exterior Nacional (Single Window for Foreign Trade, VUCEN), requiring supporting documentation to be uploaded in electronic PDF format.
q_3_2_fuente: Norma Técnica Obligatoria Nicaragüense NTON 19001:2022, "Medicamentos de Uso Humano. Ensayos Clínicos. Requisitos para su Autorización", (Section 5). Normativa 063:2025 (Res. 0009/2025).
q_3_3_directa: Yes. Nicaraguan regulations do not establish an overall time frame for reviewing and authorizing a clinical trial. The only officially defined time frame is the NRA's for issuing its opinion on the product's safety, which is a maximum of 45 business days.
q_3_3_ampliada: Once CONIS receives the authorization application, it must ask the ANRS to evaluate the investigational product's safety profile. The ANRS has a "maximum time frame of 45 (forty-five) business days" to issue its binding opinion through a Technical Report. However, NTON 19001 does not define standard time frames for the other stages of the process, such as CONIS's initial review, the time for the sponsor to address observations, or the final time frame for issuing authorization once all favorable opinions are in hand. This lack of defined time frames introduces an element of uncertainty into study planning.
q_3_3_fuente: Norma Técnica Obligatoria Nicaragüense NTON 19001:2022, "Medicamentos de Uso Humano. Ensayos Clínicos. Requisitos para su Autorización" (Chapter 13, first part).
q_3_4_directa: Yes, payment of a fee for evaluating the clinical trial is a mandatory requirement. Proof of payment must be included as part of the initial application's documentation.
q_3_4_ampliada: Including "proof of payment of the processing fee" is an explicit requirement listed in NTON 19001 for initial authorization. The chapter on pharmacovigilance and other regulatory aspects reiterates that the sponsor must pay the corresponding fee into a designated bank account. The regulation provides for an exemption from this fee for clinical trials classified as "non-commercial clinical research" with a clear public health purpose.
q_3_4_fuente: Norma Técnica Obligatoria Nicaragüense NTON 19001:2022, "Medicamentos de Uso Humano. Ensayos Clínicos. Requisitos para su Autorización" (Chapter 5, item 2, item j; Chapter 14, item 14.4, items k, l, m).
q_3_5_directa: Nicaraguan regulations do not specify an obligation for the sponsor to register the clinical trial in a globally accessible public registry (such as ClinicalTrials.gov or a WHO primary registry) before it begins.
q_3_5_ampliada: Local regulation focuses on creating a national registry. NTON 19001 establishes that CONIS is responsible for maintaining a database of clinical trials authorized and conducted in the country, which must contain key study information.
q_3_5_fuente: Norma Técnica Obligatoria Nicaragüense NTON 19001:2022, "Medicamentos de Uso Humano. Ensayos Clínicos. Requisitos para su Autorización" (Chapter 10, item 10.10.1).
q_3_6_directa: Yes, Nicaragua has explicit mechanisms for recognizing evaluations carried out by other countries' National Regulatory Authorities (NRAs). This procedure is fundamentally structured around the concept of "reliance," or recognition of foreign regulatory decisions. Its purpose is to use evaluations from reference authorities to strengthen local safety and efficacy assessment, while always preserving the Nicaraguan State's independence and responsibility in decision-making.
q_3_6_ampliada: Nicaragua's regulatory framework adopts these practices through Resolución Administrativa N° 0006/2024, which sets out specific guidelines for using regulatory decisions from other jurisdictions applicable to medicines and medical devices. Specifically for clinical trials, the technical regulation establishes that it is a valid condition for requesting a study's authorization that the investigational products already have approval for human use from recognized international NRAs. Pharmacovigilance regulation also requires sponsors to update safety information based on the conclusions and evaluations published by reference National or International Regulatory Agencies. In addition, for quality control and import processes, the country recognizes and relies on good-practice, batch-release, and quality certificates issued by the competent health authorities of the products' country of origin.
q_3_6_fuente: Normativa 063:2025 (Res. 0009/2025), Definitions and General Provisions (Item 5); Norma Técnica Obligatoria Nicaragüense NTON 19001:2022, "Medicamentos de Uso Humano. Ensayos Clínicos. Requisitos para su Autorización" (Chapter 5, item 1; Chapter 13, item 13.1, item a).
q_3_7_directa: The authorization process is sequential and multi-stage, beginning with document preparation and local approvals (institution and CEI), followed by formal submission to CONIS, which in turn requests the binding safety evaluation from the ANRS before it can issue final authorization to begin the trial.
q_3_7_ampliada:
The sequential order of key steps is as follows:

Preparation Phase (Sponsor/Investigator):

Preparing the study's core documentation: Research Protocol (Annex H) and Informed Consent (Annex E), both in Spanish and in the original language where applicable.

If the sponsor is foreign, formally appointing a legal representative domiciled in Nicaragua.

Obtaining the financial guarantee: a copy of the valid insurance policy, or preparing the notarized statement covering medical expenses.

Selecting qualified investigators and research sites.

Local Approvals Phase (Institution/CEI):

The proposed research site must obtain its Registry as a CONIS-authorized Research Site (if it does not already have one).
An authorization letter must be obtained from the highest authority of the institution where the trial is planned to be conducted.

The protocol, informed consent, and other relevant documents are submitted to a Research Ethics Committee (CEI) registered with CONIS. A favorable approval letter from the CEI must be obtained.

Formal Submission Phase (CONIS):

The sponsor or principal investigator compiles the complete dossier, including all documents from the previous phases.

The processing fee is paid.

The formal application is submitted to CONIS, using Form Annex B and attaching all required documentation.

Regulatory Review Phase (ANRS and CONIS):

CONIS receives the dossier and verifies it is complete.

CONIS formally requests the ANRS to evaluate the investigational product's safety profile.

The ANRS carries out its evaluation and issues a binding Technical Report within a maximum of 45 business days.

Final Authorization Phase (CONIS):
Once CONIS has all the required prior approvals (mainly the CEI's and the ANRS's binding opinion), it proceeds to its final deliberation.

If the outcome is favorable, CONIS issues formal written authorization to begin conducting the clinical trial.
q_3_7_fuente: Norma Técnica Obligatoria Nicaragüense NTON 19001:2022, "Medicamentos de Uso Humano. Ensayos Clínicos. Requisitos para su Autorización" (Chapter 5, items 1 and 2; Chapter 10, item 10.1, item c; Chapter 13, first part).
q_4_1_directa: Yes. Labeling of the investigational product must be in Spanish, indelible, and contain essential information for its correct identification and use. It must include the protocol code, route of administration, expiry date, storage conditions, and, mandatorily, the statements "Muestra para investigación clínica" [Sample for clinical research] and "Prohibida su venta" [Sale prohibited].
q_4_1_ampliada: Medicines for clinical trials must be packaged and labeled to allow their "accurate identification." The primary packaging label must contain, at minimum: protocol code, number of units and pharmaceutical form, route of administration, manufacturer's name and address, batch number, expiry date, special storage conditions, and the two aforementioned statements. If the primary packaging's size does not allow all this information to be included, it must appear on the secondary packaging. The regulation explicitly prohibits relabeling investigational products once they have been labeled under these conditions.
q_4_1_fuente: Norma Técnica Obligatoria Nicaragüense NTON 19001:2022, "Medicamentos de Uso Humano. Ensayos Clínicos. Requisitos para su Autorización" (Chapter 13, item 13.12, items 1 and 3; Chapter 13, item 13.13).
q_4_2_directa: Yes, the sponsor must ensure the investigational medicine complies with Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP), and a duly legalized GMP Certificate from the country of origin is required if the product comes from a third country or from a manufacturer other than the sponsor.
q_4_2_ampliada: The sponsor bears direct responsibility for "ensuring the medicine used in the clinical trial complies with GMP," as well as Good Laboratory Practice (GLP) and Good Storage Practice (GSP). For the ANRS's evaluation of the product, if the medicine comes from a third country or from a manufacturer other than the sponsor, submitting the "GMP Certificate from the country of origin, which must be legalized" is mandatory. This requirement ensures the quality of the product used in the trial meets international standards.
q_4_2_fuente: Norma Técnica Obligatoria Nicaragüense NTON 19001:2022, "Medicamentos de Uso Humano. Ensayos Clínicos. Requisitos para su Autorización" (Chapter 10, item 10.1, item j; Chapter 13, item 13.4.2, item h).
q_4_3_directa: Yes. The clinical trial's authorization presupposes and validates the use of the investigational products listed in the application. As part of the initial dossier, the sponsor must submit a detailed list of all products that will need to be imported, including the investigational medicine, comparators, and any other pharmaceutical supplies.
q_4_3_ampliada: The sponsor must attach to the initial authorization application the "List of investigational products and other necessary supplies (Annex K)." This list must include all pharmaceutical products that will need to be imported, even if they are control medicines or vaccines already marketed in other countries. Although CONIS's trial authorization legitimizes the need to import these products for research purposes, clinical trial regulations do not specify whether this authorization simplifies, expedites, or replaces standard customs procedures or import permits for controlled substances. A separate import procedure before the ANRS is likely required, using the trial authorization as a fundamental supporting document.
q_4_3_fuente: Norma Técnica Obligatoria Nicaragüense NTON 19001:2022, "Medicamentos de Uso Humano. Ensayos Clínicos. Requisitos para su Autorización" (Chapter 5, item 2, item k).
q_5_1_directa: Yes. Mandatory, expedited reporting time frames exist for safety events. The investigator must report Serious Adverse Events (SAEs) to the sponsor and to the authorities within no more than 24 hours. The sponsor, in turn, must report Suspected Serious Unexpected Adverse Reactions (RASI/SUSARs) to the authorities and investigators, with a strict 7-day deadline, preferably using the Noti-FACEDRA online system.
q_5_1_ampliada: Investigator's Obligations: The investigator must report any Serious Adverse Event (SAE) they become aware of, in writing or by email, to the sponsor, the CEI, CONIS, and the ANRS within no more than 24 hours. A detailed follow-up report must be submitted afterward. Sponsor's Obligations: The sponsor is responsible for assessing the causality and expectedness of events. It must report all Suspected Serious Unexpected Adverse Reactions (RASI/SUSARs), including those occurring at other sites or in other countries with the same product, to the principal investigator in Nicaragua, the CEI, CONIS, and the ANRS. Initial notification must be made within the first 24 hours of becoming aware, with a strict deadline of no more than seven (7) days to complete the report. Reporting Mechanism: The preferred channel for reporting suspected adverse reactions to the authority is the Central American Pharmacovigilance Network's online reporting system, Noti-FACEDRA (www.notificacentroamerica.net).
q_5_1_fuente: Norma Técnica Obligatoria Nicaragüense NTON 19001:2022, "Medicamentos de Uso Humano. Ensayos Clínicos. Requisitos para su Autorización" (Chapter 14, item 14.1, items b and c; item 14.2, item 1); Resolución Administrativa N° 0009/2025, "Actualización de la Normativa 063 Farmacovigilancia y Manual de Notificación" (items 18, 38).
q_5_2_directa: Yes, this is mandatory. Sponsors must prepare and submit an annual Periodic Safety Report (IPS), equivalent to a DSUR, to CONIS, the ANRS, and the Research Ethics Committees (CEIs) involved in the study.
q_5_2_ampliada: The IPS's purpose is to provide a cumulative safety assessment of the investigational medicine. This annual report must be submitted within 90 calendar days of the product's international data-lock point. The regulation allows for submitting a simplified report if the investigational medicine already holds marketing authorization and is being used in accordance with the terms of that authorization.
q_5_2_fuente: Norma Técnica Obligatoria Nicaragüense NTON 19001:2022, "Medicamentos de Uso Humano. Ensayos Clínicos. Requisitos para su Autorización" (Chapter 14, item 14.3, items 1 and 2); Resolución Administrativa N° 0009/2025, "Actualización de la Normativa 063 Farmacovigilancia y Manual de Notificación" (item 49).
q_5_3_directa: Yes, semi-annual progress reports must be submitted to CONIS by the investigator, sponsor, CRO, or site-responsible organization.
q_5_3_ampliada: The progress report must be submitted "semi-annually by each of the sites or research centers conducting the clinical trial." This report, defined in the regulation as the "Progress Report," must contain a summary of the study's conduct, including partial results and recruitment progress (randomized, enrolled, active, withdrawn, and completed patients), as well as a summary of the serious adverse events occurring during the reporting period.
q_5_3_fuente: Norma Técnica Obligatoria Nicaragüense NTON 19001:2022, "Medicamentos de Uso Humano. Ensayos Clínicos. Requisitos para su Autorización" (Chapter 4, item 23; Chapter 11, item 11.1, item 1).
q_5_4_directa: Yes. Amendments are classified as "major" or "minor." "Major" amendments require CONIS's prior approval before implementation. To request this approval from CONIS, the amendment must already have prior approval from the CEI. "Minor" amendments need only be reported to CONIS.
q_5_4_ampliada: A "major" amendment is defined as one that has a significant impact on subjects' safety or integrity, the study's scientific value, or its conduct and management. Examples include changes to objectives, design, study population, or medicine dosage. To process an approval request for this type of amendment before CONIS, a documentary requirement is attaching the "amendment approval letter and, where applicable, the informed consent approval letter from the authorized CEI." By contrast, "minor" amendments, such as changes to monitoring or logistics staff, need only be reported to CONIS and do not require an approval response before being implemented.
q_5_4_fuente: Norma Técnica Obligatoria Nicaragüense NTON 19001:2022, "Medicamentos de Uso Humano. Ensayos Clínicos. Requisitos para su Autorización" (Chapter 5, item 6, item c; Chapter 6, items 1 and 2).
q_5_5_directa: Yes, the sponsor has two main obligations regarding post-trial access. First, it must guarantee continued treatment if discontinuing it would endanger the participant's safety. Second, it must ensure access to procedures (preventive, diagnostic, or therapeutic) that proved beneficial during the trial, if no other alternatives exist, until the medicine is commercially available.
q_5_5_ampliada: The regulation establishes the sponsor's obligation to "guarantee subjects access to the product once their participation ends in cases where discontinuing treatment would endanger their safety." More broadly, it must also "ensure subjects have access, after the clinical trial's completion, to the procedures (...) that proved beneficial, if no other adequate treatment alternative exists (...) until the medicine is commercially available." These conditions and commitments must be clearly described in the informed consent document.
q_5_5_fuente: Norma Técnica Obligatoria Nicaragüense NTON 19001:2022, "Medicamentos de Uso Humano. Ensayos Clínicos. Requisitos para su Autorización" (Chapter 10, item 10.1, item p).
q_6_1_directa: Yes. Ley N°. 787, the Ley de Protección de Datos Personales, is the applicable general legal framework. However, this same law, in Article 27, establishes an exception for scientific or medical research, exempting it from certain obligations provided the data is obtained with the express, informed consent of the data subject and used solely for the purpose for which it was requested.
q_6_1_ampliada: Ley N°. 787 establishes the right to informational self-determination and the obligation of data confidentiality. The Article 27 exception for scientific research is not absolute; it is conditional on informed consent and use strictly limited to the original purpose. This poses a challenge for secondary use of data or samples for future research. A critical factor is that the Dirección de Protección de Datos Personales, the authority created by this law, has not been formally established and is not operational. In practice, this means there is no registry of data files, nor an authority to consult on interpreting the law. The absence of this oversight authority shifts the entire burden of compliance and correct interpretation of the law onto the sponsor and the CEI. The informed consent's design therefore becomes the central instrument for ensuring compliance, and it must be extremely clear and specific about the scope of data use to avoid future legal disputes.
q_6_1_fuente: Ley N°. 787, "Ley de Protección de Datos Personales" (Chapter IV, Articles 3, 27). Norma de Ensayos Clínicos (Chapter IV, item 4).
q_6_2_directa: Yes, although no regulation specifically addresses vaccine clinical trials, the Norma Técnica Obligatoria Nicaragüense (NTON) 19011-19 on vaccine sanitary registration sets out clinical documentation requirements that are directly applicable. It requires all vaccine clinical studies to comply with WHO guidelines and Good Clinical Practice (GCP) standards.
q_6_2_ampliada: Although NTON 19011-19's main purpose is sanitary registration, its Chapter 6 details the requirements for submitting clinical study reports. It explicitly requires clinical studies to follow the WHO's "Guidelines on Clinical Evaluation of Vaccines: Regulatory Expectations," WHO Technical Report Series 1004, Annex 9, 2017 (or its current version). Chapter 5 of the same regulation also establishes that all clinical studies must comply with international GCP standards. Any vaccine clinical trial conducted in Nicaragua must therefore be designed and conducted following these international guidelines for its results to be acceptable for future sanitary registration in the country.
q_6_2_fuente: NTON 19011-19, "Medicamentos de Uso Humano. Vacunas. Requisitos de Registro Sanitario" (Chapter 5, item 5.7; Chapter 6, item 6.1.5).
q_6_3_directa: No single, specific regulation exists for the collection and use of biological samples in research. Regulation is fragmented across NTON 19001, which sets the documentation requirements in the protocol and informed consent, and Normativa 059, which establishes the technical standards for their handling and transport.
q_6_3_ampliada: The regulatory framework for biological samples must be pieced together from several sources. NTON 19001 requires the research Protocol to describe sample collection and the Informed Consent to specify their destination and possible future use, even requiring special consent for supplementary tests such as pharmacogenetics. For the technical aspects of collection, handling, and transport, the "Guía para la Toma, Identificación, Manejo, Conservación y Transporte de Muestras para Laboratorios de Salud" (Normativa 059) provides the applicable standards in the country.
q_6_3_fuente: Norma Técnica Obligatoria Nicaragüense NTON 19001:2022, "Medicamentos de Uso Humano. Ensayos Clínicos. Requisitos para su Autorización" (Annex E, item 7, items d, h; Annex H, item 11, item c); Normativa 059, "Guía para la Toma, Identificación, Manejo, Conservación y Transporte de Muestras para Laboratorios de Salud".
q_6_4_directa: Yes, Nicaraguan regulations include specific provisions for special situations and other types of clinical research. These include expedited procedures for public health events, regulations for compassionate use of medicines, and guidelines for trials with no direct benefit in healthy volunteers. Special regulations also exist for handling dangerous microorganisms and importing psychotropic substances for scientific research purposes.
q_6_4_ampliada: The regulatory framework, through CONIS, allows clinical trials to be authorized under expedited procedures in emergencies or public health events. For patients who need continued experimental treatment and have no other therapeutic alternative, CONIS may approve "compassionate use" of the medicine, requiring a justified clinical report, institutional authorization, and a specific informed consent. As for trials with no direct benefit, such as those conducted in healthy volunteers, the technical regulation requires the risk to be fully justified by a collective benefit and the procedures to be comparable to standard practice. In addition, research involving pathogenic microorganisms or dangerous parasites, as well as the use of narcotics and psychotropics for science, requires special, exclusive permits issued directly by MINSA. In all these exceptional situations, the rights, safety, and well-being of the human participants must always prevail over any other scientific interest.
q_6_4_fuente: Norma Técnica Obligatoria Nicaragüense NTON 19001:2022, "Medicamentos de Uso Humano. Ensayos Clínicos. Requisitos para su Autorización" (Chapter 6, item 5; Chapter 7, item 7.7; Chapter 8, items 8.5, 8.9).

q_1_1_directa: The National Regulatory Authority (NRA) for clinical trials is the Ministry of Health (MINSA), which oversees health research through the administrative unit Regulación de Investigación para la Salud (Health Research Regulation Unit, RegulaIPS).
q_1_1_ampliada: The Dirección General de Salud Pública, through RegulaIPS, coordinates the regulation, oversight, and strengthening of health research. While MINSA is the overall governing authority, the Dirección Nacional de Farmacia y Drogas (National Directorate of Pharmacy and Drugs, DNFD), under MINSA, has exclusive authority over the sanitary registration, control, and oversight of medicines, which includes the Investigational Product (IP) used in clinical trials.
q_1_1_fuente: Ley 84 de 14 de mayo de 2019, Article 10; Ley 84 de 14 de mayo de 2019, Article 27; Ley 419 de 1 de febrero de 2024, Article 10; Resolución N° 512 de 28 de junio de 2019, Article 2.
q_1_2_directa: The main regulation governing health research, establishing its oversight and governance, is Ley 84 de 2019.
q_1_2_ampliada: Ley 84 de 2019 regulates and promotes health research and protects participants. In addition, the Código Sanitario (Ley 66 de 1947) is a fundamental legal framework for public health, and Ley N° 81 de 2019 establishes the framework for Personal Data Protection.
q_1_2_fuente: Ley 84 de 14 de mayo de 2019; Ley 66 de 1947; Ley 81 de 26 de marzo de 2019.
q_1_3_directa: Clinical trial authorization is governed by Ley 84 de 2019 (ethical and governance framework), Resolución No. 512 de 2019 (RESEGIS registration procedure), Ley 419 de 2024 (medicines regulation), and Decreto Ejecutivo N.° 27 de 2024 (implementing Ley 419).
q_1_3_ampliada: Ley 84 de 2019 makes ethical approval mandatory, and Resolución 512 de 2019 establishes the administrative process for registering protocols. If the trial involves pharmaceutical products, Ley 419 and Decreto Ejecutivo N.° 27 de 2024 govern the handling of Investigational Products (IPs), pharmacovigilance, the clinical studies required for sanitary registration, and authorization to import the IP through an exception to sanitary registration.
q_1_3_fuente: Ley 84 de 14 de mayo de 2019, Article 37; Resolución N° 512 de 28 de junio de 2019, Article 1; Ley 419 de 1 de febrero de 2024, Article 1; Decreto Ejecutivo N.° 27 de 10 de mayo de 2024, Article 1; Decreto Ejecutivo N° 179 del 8 de junio de 2018.
q_1_4_directa: Yes, approval is mandatory. All research involving human participants must obtain ethical approval from a Research Bioethics Committee (CBI) accredited by the CNBI.
q_1_4_ampliada: Ethical approval is a fundamental requirement established in Ley 84 de 2019, and must be obtained before the study begins. For clinical trials or experimental-risk studies, approval is required from a Research Bioethics Committee (CBI) that is among those authorized by the CNBI.
q_1_4_fuente: Ley 84 de 14 de mayo de 2019, Article 37; Resolución N° 512 de 28 de junio de 2019, Article 3; Circular 003/DGS/CRIPS de 25 de septiembre de 2015.
q_1_5_directa: No. Registering the protocol with MINSA (the NRA) must occur before or concurrently with submission to the CBI. The procedure requires that, after obtaining institutional agreement, registration with MINSA/RegulaIPS be requested; only after this registration, or in parallel if the CBI allows it, does ethical review proceed.
q_1_5_ampliada: The descriptive flow guide establishes that the protocol is submitted for registration with MINSA's Health Research Regulation Unit, and only after this stage must the investigator submit the protocol to the CBI for ethical approval. Resolución 512/2019 clarifies that ethical review by the CNBI or CBI may take place in parallel with the Ministry of Health's protocol evaluation, if the CBI has arranged for this.
q_1_5_fuente: Resolución N° 512 de 28 de junio de 2019, Article 13.
q_1_6_directa: Yes, a formal accreditation system exists for Research Bioethics Committees (CBIs). This system is centrally administered by the CNBI, the governing body responsible for evaluating and certifying institutional committees. Only committees holding current accreditation are legally authorized to review, approve, and follow up on clinical trials in the country.
q_1_6_ampliada: Panama's regulatory framework grants the CNBI exclusive authority to promote, accredit, evaluate, and oversee CBIs, both public and private. Under Ley 84 de 2019 and its complementary regulations, health or academic institutions wishing to establish a committee must meet minimum criteria, such as having a multidisciplinary team, at least 25% external members, and ensuring members are trained in the field. The accreditation process involves reviewing founding documents, standard operating procedures (SOPs), and CNBI inspection visits. Accreditations are granted for defined periods and require periodic re-accreditation to avoid authorizations lapsing.
q_1_6_fuente: Ley 84 de 14 de mayo de 2019, Article 31; Decreto Ejecutivo N° 1843 de 2014.
q_1_7_directa: Yes, legislation requires a public registry of Research Bioethics Committees (CBIs) to exist. The CNBI has the legal mandate to maintain and publish the list of all duly accredited committees nationwide. This information must be available to the public and investigators through official digital platforms.
q_1_7_ampliada: Ley 84 de 2019, which regulates health research in Panama, establishes, among the CNBI's explicit functions, the obligation to publish an up-to-date list of accredited CBIs, those undergoing accreditation, and those that have been sanctioned. This measure is essential for promoting transparency and ensuring the rigor of the country's clinical research system. In practice, the CNBI, with logistical support from the Secretaría Nacional de Ciencia, Tecnología e Innovación (National Secretariat of Science, Technology and Innovation, SENACYT), keeps published on its institutional website the list of committees authorized to evaluate protocols. This allows sponsors and principal investigators to verify the legal validity of the committee to which they will submit their proposals, preventing projects from being submitted to and evaluated by entities lacking the corresponding legal authority.
q_1_7_fuente: Ley 84 de 14 de mayo de 2019, Article 31.
q_1_8_directa: Yes. All health research must be registered and have institutional approval and/or agreement. Protocols classified as high-risk, such as clinical trials, or involving medicines, require a technical evaluation and opinion from the regulatory authorities before they begin.
q_1_8_ampliada: The mandatory registration with MINSA, through the Health Research Regulation Unit, extends to all health research protocols. However, the NRA applies more rigorous evaluation for high-risk protocols, such as clinical trials, or those that could interfere with public health or the environment. In addition, if the research uses medicines or investigational products, the DNFD must issue a technical opinion and authorize their import, which, together with mandatory approval from the Research Ethics Committee (CEI), constitutes the prior regulatory authorization for the study to begin. Projects using laboratory or experimental animals must also be evaluated in advance by an animal ethics and welfare committee.
q_1_8_fuente: Ley 84 de 14 de mayo de 2019 (Article 54); Decreto Ejecutivo N.° 27 de 10 de mayo de 2024 (Articles 70, 339); Circular 003/DGS/CRIPS; Guía descriptiva del flujo de los protocolos de investigación para la salud; Resolución N° 512 de 28 de junio de 2019 (Article 19).
q_2_1_directa: Not specified in official regulations.
q_2_1_ampliada: Ley 84 de 2019 mentions the sponsor as one of the parties involved, alongside investigators and funders, and requires it to ensure that projects are planned, conducted, and their results reported in accordance with current regulations. However, none of the regulations reviewed provides an explicit, detailed legal definition of the term "sponsor" of a clinical trial.
q_2_1_fuente: Ley 84 de 14 de mayo de 2019, Article 45.
q_2_2_directa: Not specified in official regulations for the research protocol registration process.
q_2_2_ampliada: That said, Ley 84 de 2019 requires research conducted in Panama to have a responsible local counterpart with duly formalized support. In addition, for procedures before the DNFD, such as requesting a sanitary-registration exception for the Investigational Product (IP), the applicant must be represented by a lawyer and have the endorsement of a qualified local pharmacist acting as technical officer.
q_2_2_fuente: Ley 84 de 14 de mayo de 2019, Article 46; Decreto Ejecutivo N.° 27 de 10 de mayo de 2024, Article 19, item 1; Decreto Ejecutivo N.° 27 de 10 de mayo de 2024, Article 42.
q_2_3_directa: Yes. The sponsor must ensure compliance with current regulations and, when dealing with pharmaceutical products, must guarantee their quality, safety, efficacy, and rational use during the research.
q_2_3_ampliada: Decreto Ejecutivo N.° 27 de 2024, implementing Ley 419, emphasizes that cooperation with the DNFD by suppliers and legal entities, whether for post-market control or pharmacovigilance, is mandatory, and failure to comply may be considered a serious violation. For importing the IP, the applicant (which may be the sponsor or its delegate) must submit the application on the form established by the DNFD.
q_2_3_fuente: Ley 84 de 14 de mayo de 2019, Article 45; Ley 419 de 1 de febrero de 2024, Article 1; Ley 419 de 1 de febrero de 2024, Article 69.
q_2_4_directa: Not specified in official regulations.
q_2_4_ampliada: Panamanian regulations do not contain specific rules for CROs. These organizations may operate under general principles of delegation of sponsor functions, but without a specific regulatory framework establishing particular requirements, accreditation, or responsibilities.
q_2_4_fuente: No specific information was found in official regulations.
q_2_5_directa: Yes, partially. The regulation does not detail an exhaustive list of requirements for the general technical licensing of research sites, but it does mandatorily require every protocol to have an institutional "agreement or no-objection" letter before operations begin. This document certifies that the site's authorities authorize the specific study's conduct and confirm its facilities are suitable for the proposed procedures.
q_2_5_ampliada: Although Ley 84 de 2019 mentions promoting the official certification of clinical research sites among its objectives, current administrative regulation focuses on protocol-specific validation. To conduct a clinical trial at MINSA facilities, the Caja de Seguro Social, or private clinics and hospitals, the investigator must submit an official no-objection letter signed by the institution's highest authority. This document serves as a statement that the research site approves the study's feasibility and guarantees sufficient medical resources to safeguard participants. Obtaining this institutional authorization is a prior, indispensable requirement for advancing through the regulatory workflow. Without this document, it is not possible to proceed with registering the project on the government platform (RESEGIS) or with its subsequent ethical evaluation by the CBI.
q_2_5_fuente: Ley 84 de 14 de mayo de 2019, Article 29; Ley 84 de 14 de mayo de 2019, Article 49; Guía descriptiva del flujo de los protocolos de investigación para la salud.
q_2_6_directa: Yes, requirements exist to certify the technical, scientific, and ethical competence of clinical investigators and their support staff. The research team must demonstrate professional fitness through local licenses, up-to-date training in Good Clinical Practice (GCP), and knowledge of research ethics. They must also submit sworn documentation showing the absence of conflicts of interest that could compromise the results.
q_2_6_ampliada: Ley 84 de 2019 establishes the principle of research competence, providing that only professionals with the proper technical training may conduct or supervise research involving human subjects. To comply with this, CBIs are required to rigorously evaluate the profile of the principal investigator and sub-investigators before granting ethical endorsement. When formally submitting a project, an up-to-date curriculum vitae, professional fitness certificates issued by the health authorities, and formal declarations of financial interests must be submitted. It is also a strictly enforced standard that investigators demonstrate training through current Good Clinical Practice (GCP) certifications. Under general CNBI rules, this specialized research-ethics training must be formally renewed by investigators and their teams at least every three years.
q_2_6_fuente: Ley 84 de 14 de mayo de 2019, Articles 11 and 29.
q_2_7_directa: Not specified in official regulations.
q_2_7_ampliada: Although there is a practice of requiring insurance for clinical research, the regulation does not establish a specific requirement, types of coverage, minimum amounts, or detailed procedures. Protection is based on the general ethical principles of Ley 84 de 2019.
q_2_7_fuente: Ley 84 de 14 de mayo de 2019, Article 5.
q_3_1_directa: Yes. For initial registration on RESEGIS, the investigator must attach the institutional agreement or no-objection letter, the registration application (from an activated user account), the research Protocol, and the following mandatory annexes: timeline, budget, informed consent, and data collection instrument.
q_3_1_ampliada: All attached documentation must be the same version to be submitted to the CBI. For research into developing a new medicine, it is considered good practice to attach the certificate of analysis and the Investigator's Brochure. Total uploaded files must not exceed 10 MB.
q_3_1_fuente: Guía descriptiva del flujo de los protocolos de investigación para la salud; Preguntas y respuestas frecuentes de los investigadores, Questions 4 and 3.
q_3_2_directa: Yes. The process is digital and online, through the Registro y Seguimiento de los Protocolos de Investigación para la Salud (Health Research Protocol Registration and Follow-up, RESEGIS) web platform.
q_3_2_ampliada: To register, the investigator or the person handling the procedure must have an active RESEGIS account. Official documents written in a language other than Spanish must be submitted with their corresponding translation by an authorized public translator. However, Decreto 27/2024 accepts submission of clinical studies in English, provided they are accompanied by a Spanish summary of all clinical evidence.
q_3_2_fuente: Resolución N° 512 de 28 de junio de 2019, Article 1; Decreto Ejecutivo N.° 27 de 10 de mayo de 2024, Article 30; Decreto Ejecutivo N.° 27 de 10 de mayo de 2024, Article 28; Guía introductoria a la Plataforma RESEGIS.
q_3_3_directa: Yes. Registering a protocol with complete requirements takes a maximum of three (3) business days. If the protocol involves high-risk research, such as a clinical trial, the maximum time frame for evaluation by technical-regulatory bodies is thirty (30) calendar days.
q_3_3_ampliada: Resolución 512 establishes that the Dirección General de Salud Pública must ensure the process is expeditious, and for high-risk studies, the 30-calendar-day evaluation aims to verify the study does not interfere with public health or the environment. For public health emergencies, disasters, or outbreaks, the Special Review Procedure (Resolución No. 400 de 2021) establishes that approval will be resolved within no more than two (2) business days.
q_3_3_fuente: Resolución N° 512 de 28 de junio de 2019, Article 9; Preguntas y respuestas frecuentes de los investigadores, Question 5; Resolución N° 400 de 7 de junio de 2021, Article Six.
q_3_4_directa: Yes, fees must be paid. Research Bioethics Committees and the CNBI are authorized to charge for the ethical review of protocols. In addition, the DNFD sets fees for its services.
q_3_4_ampliada: Decreto 27/2024 confirms that, before the Sanitary Registration Certificate is granted, payment of the corresponding fee to the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas is required. The Colegio Nacional de Farmacéuticos also charges a fee for the endorsement required in medicine-related procedures. No official link to the current fee schedule was found.
q_3_4_fuente: Ley 84 de 14 de mayo de 2019, Article 32; Ley 419 de 1 de febrero de 2024, Article 19; Decreto Ejecutivo N.° 27 de 10 de mayo de 2024, Article 43; Decreto Ejecutivo N.° 27 de 10 de mayo de 2024, Article 44.
q_3_5_directa: Yes, this is mandatory. Resolución 512 de 2019 establishes the administrative procedure for registering and tracking research projects in RESEGIS, which is a publicly accessible platform.
q_3_5_ampliada: Ley 84 de 2019 requires MINSA to create and maintain a publicly accessible virtual platform with information on protocols and publications. After obtaining ethical approval and institutional authorization, the investigator must request that the project be marked "Active" on RESEGIS in order to begin the study.
q_3_5_fuente: Resolución N° 512 de 28 de junio de 2019, Article 1; Ley 84 de 14 de mayo de 2019, Article 8.
q_3_6_directa: Yes, regulatory reliance mechanisms exist for pharmaceutical products, based on decisions from high-standard Regulatory Authorities (WHO/PAHO). However, ethical approval must still be granted by an accredited Panamanian CBI.
q_3_6_ampliada: The DNFD will use regulatory reliance for decision-making, basing its decisions wholly or partly on those of other regulatory jurisdictions. This applies, for example, to opting for the abbreviated sanitary-registration procedure. Regarding ethics, although CBIs must operate under international ethical standards, local regulations require approval from a CBI accredited in Panama for the research to be conducted.
q_3_6_fuente: Ley 419 de 1 de febrero de 2024, Article 3, item 7; Ley 419 de 1 de febrero de 2024, Article 54; Decreto Ejecutivo N.° 27 de 10 de mayo de 2024, Article 12; Circular 003/DGS/CRIPS de 25 de septiembre de 2015.
q_3_7_directa: The sequence of steps required is: 1) Institutional Agreement, 2) Administrative Registration with MINSA (RESEGIS), 3) Ethical Approval (CBI/CNBI), 4) Activation request on RESEGIS, and 5) Import Authorization (DNFD, if applicable).
q_3_7_ampliada:
Institutional Agreement or No-Objection: The authority at the site (or bodies) where the research is proposed must give its approval, certifying the protocol's feasibility and value.

Registration with MINSA (RESEGIS): The Principal Investigator requests registration on the RESEGIS platform, attaching the Institutional Agreement, the Protocol, and the required annexes.

MINSA Administrative and Technical Evaluation: MINSA/RegulaIPS reviews the documentation (3 business days). If it is high-risk (a clinical trial), it undergoes technical evaluation (maximum 30 calendar days).

Ethical Review and Approval (CBI): The protocol is submitted for review by an accredited CBI, which may run in parallel with MINSA's review.

Project Activation on RESEGIS: The investigator must upload the Bioethics Committee's Approval and the Institutional Authorization to RESEGIS and request that the project be marked "Active."

IP Import/Use Authorization (DNFD): If the Investigational Product (IP) is needed, a Sanitary Registration Exception must be requested from the DNFD, attaching the accredited CBI's approval of the protocol/amendment. This authorization is a separate procedure and is necessary for the import.
q_3_7_fuente: Resolución N° 512 de 28 de junio de 2019; Guía descriptiva del flujo de los protocolos de investigación para la salud; Decreto Ejecutivo N.° 27 de 10 de mayo de 2024, Article 213.
q_4_1_directa: Yes. The content of primary, secondary, and tertiary packaging labels is regulated by the Health Authority and must be printed in multiple languages, provided one of them is Spanish.
q_4_1_ampliada: For medicines in general, the DNFD does not accept relabeling or overlabeling, with exceptions regulated by the Health Authority. Labels in a language other than Spanish are accepted for intra-hospital products if a Spanish translation by an authorized public translator is provided to both the DNFD and the hospital. For the Investigational Product (IP), the exception request must detail the IP to be imported.
q_4_1_fuente: Ley 419 de 1 de febrero de 2024, Article 37; Decreto Ejecutivo N.° 27 de 10 de mayo de 2024, Article 54; Decreto Ejecutivo N.° 27 de 10 de mayo de 2024, Article 128; Decreto Ejecutivo N.° 27 de 10 de mayo de 2024, Article 213, item 1.
q_4_2_directa: Yes, a Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) Certificate is required. For the sanitary-registration exception for products intended for research, a copy of the GMP Certificate must be submitted, where applicable.
q_4_2_ampliada: If a GMP certificate for the IP is not issued (for medicines or products intended for research), a Good Manufacturing Practice declaration from a qualified person may be submitted, in accordance with the requirements set by high-standard regulatory authorities. The DNFD (through Ley 419) adopts WHO guidelines on GMP.
q_4_2_fuente: Ley 419 de 1 de febrero de 2024, Article 29, item 3; Ley 419 de 1 de febrero de 2024, Article 47, item 3; Decreto Ejecutivo N.° 27 de 10 de mayo de 2024, Article 209, item 4; Decreto Ejecutivo N.° 27 de 10 de mayo de 2024, Article 213.
q_4_3_directa: No. A Sanitary Registration Exception for the medicine or product intended for research purposes must be obtained, requested from the DNFD.
q_4_3_ampliada: Following a substantiated request from the public or private entity, the DNFD may authorize the import of products for scientific research purposes, provided the research complies with the bioethics and biosafety parameters set out in national regulations. This request must be accompanied by a copy of the protocol or protocol amendment approved by the accredited CBI. Once approved, the Sanitary Registration Exception is valid for 60 business days for importing the product into the country, with no possibility of extension.
q_4_3_fuente: Ley 419 de 1 de febrero de 2024, Article 45, item 4; Decreto Ejecutivo N.° 27 de 10 de mayo de 2024, Article 213; Decreto Ejecutivo N.° 27 de 10 de mayo de 2024, Article 214.
q_5_1_directa: Yes. Reports of suspected serious adverse reactions (including SAEs) occurring in Panama must be submitted by the manufacturer/distributor to the CNFV within up to ten (10) business days of becoming aware of them. Reports of suspected non-serious adverse reactions must be submitted within up to fifteen (15) business days.
q_5_1_ampliada: Reports must be submitted using the national form or the CIOMS-I form. Manufacturers are required to use MedDRA and WHODrug coding systems for reporting suspected adverse reactions, in compliance with ICH international standards. Serious reports must initially be sent by email and then in original form. The responsible investigator also has a general obligation to immediately notify the health authority and the CBI of any finding with public health impact.
q_5_1_fuente: Ley 84 de 14 de mayo de 2019, Article 61; Decreto Ejecutivo N.° 27 de 10 de mayo de 2024, Article 326; Decreto Ejecutivo N.° 27 de 10 de mayo de 2024, Article 325; Decreto Ejecutivo N.° 27 de 10 de mayo de 2024, Article 318; Decreto Ejecutivo N.° 27 de 10 de mayo de 2024, Article 2, item 69.
q_5_2_directa: Yes. Submission of Periodic Safety Reports (IPS) or Periodic Benefit-Risk Evaluation Reports (PBRER) is required for innovative, biotechnological, biological, and interchangeable medicines.
q_5_2_ampliada: Reports are submitted according to the following frequency: every six months (the first two years on the market), annually (the following three years), and every fifth year thereafter. These reports (IPS or PBRER) must follow the structure based on the ICH E2C(R2) format and may be submitted in English, provided a Spanish translation of the Executive Summary by an authorized public interpreter is included.
q_5_2_fuente: Decreto Ejecutivo N.° 27 de 10 de mayo de 2024, Article 327; Decreto Ejecutivo N.° 27 de 10 de mayo de 2024, Article 328; Decreto Ejecutivo N.° 27 de 10 de mayo de 2024, Article 331; Decreto Ejecutivo N.° 27 de 10 de mayo de 2024, Article 2, item 75.
q_5_3_directa: Yes, periodic follow-up and electronic linking of reports and publications to RESEGIS is required, within no more than three (3) months of their publication.
q_5_3_ampliada: The RESEGIS platform allows the investigator to upload follow-up documents, such as the "Interim Summary" and the "Executive Summary with Results." Once the study is complete, the investigator must upload the Closure Note to the CBI that approved the study to request that the project be marked "Closed" on the platform.
q_5_3_fuente: Ley 84 de 14 de mayo de 2019, Article 62; Guía adición de co investigadores y seguimiento a proyecto.
q_5_4_directa: Yes. Substantial changes, such as addenda or amendments to the project, must be uploaded to RESEGIS. Changes to the registered protocol or title may only be updated after obtaining the corresponding ethical approval from the CBI, and must be requested from MINSA's coordinator.
q_5_4_ampliada: If a change is needed to the project's basic and funding information (including the bioethics committee), this may only be edited by the coordinator role at MINSA's research regulation unit, following the investigator's email communication attaching the files justifying the change. This means substantial changes are subject to both ethical approval and MINSA's administrative validation.
q_5_4_fuente: Guía adición de co investigadores y seguimiento a proyecto; Preguntas y respuestas frecuentes de los investigadores, Questions 8 and 9.
q_5_5_directa: Yes, Decreto Ejecutivo N.° 27 de 2024 regulates authorization to import medicines or products for post-trial access (Art. 342). In addition, Ley 419 de 2024 provides for Managed Entry Agreements for advanced therapies, which may include contractual provisions for continued treatment.
q_5_5_ampliada: To obtain post-trial access, the participating investigating physician must support, through a sworn statement, the expected benefit for the patient and the medicine's favorable benefit/risk balance. The application to the DNFD must include a copy of the protocol or amendment approval note at the study's completion, issued by the accredited CBI. Managed Entry Agreements are contracts applicable to advanced therapies based on health or financial outcomes.
q_5_5_fuente: Ley 419 de 1 de febrero de 2024, Article 3, item 3; Decreto Ejecutivo N.° 27 de 10 de mayo de 2024, Article 342; Decreto Ejecutivo N.° 27 de 10 de mayo de 2024, Article 342, item 2.
q_6_1_directa: Yes. The applicable law is Ley N° 81 de 2019, Sobre Protección de Datos Personales.
q_6_1_ampliada: The research regulatory framework requires MINSA to guarantee confidentiality in handling information. Under Ley 84 de 2019, misusing privileged or confidential information is a serious violation. Ley 419/Decreto 27 also requires confidentiality of the information and documentation submitted in procedures before the DNFD.
q_6_1_fuente: Gaceta Oficial N° 28743-A (Ley 81 de 26 de marzo de 2019); Ley 84 de 14 de mayo de 2019, Article 76; Ley 419 de 1 de febrero de 2024, Article 12.
q_6_2_directa: No specific regulations or guidelines for vaccine clinical trials were found in the sources, but Decreto Ejecutivo N.° 27 de 2024 regulates vaccines as biological pharmaceutical products and requires a Batch Release Certificate from the DNFD for import.
q_6_2_ampliada: Decreto 27/2024 incorporates Events Supposedly Attributable to Vaccination or Immunization (ESAVI) into the National Pharmacovigilance System, requiring coordination with the Expanded Immunization Program (PAI). Imported vaccines are subject to post-market controls to oversee their safety, efficacy, and quality.
