q_6_2_fuente: Decreto Ejecutivo N.° 27 de 10 de mayo de 2024, Article 14; Decreto Ejecutivo N.° 27 de 10 de mayo de 2024, Article 101; Decreto Ejecutivo N.° 27 de 10 de mayo de 2024, Article 260, item 3; Decreto Ejecutivo N.° 27 de 10 de mayo de 2024, Article 302.
q_6_3_directa: Yes, specific regulations exist for research involving human tissues and cells, set out in Decreto Ejecutivo N° 179 de 2018.
q_6_3_ampliada: This Decree requires research to be conducted with full respect for the human being and their rights, with CNBI evaluation and the donor's explicit informed consent. Specifically, the use of individually identifiable tissues or cells requires registration with MINSA. For umbilical cord donation, the mother is considered the donor.
q_6_3_fuente: Decreto Ejecutivo N° 179 del 8 de junio de 2018, Article 1 and Article 7; Ley 419 de 1 de febrero de 2024, Article 86.
q_6_4_directa: Yes, a Special Review Procedure exists for protocols related to public health emergencies, disasters, or disease outbreaks, established by Resolución No. 400 de 2021.
q_6_4_ampliada: The special review allows for expedited ethical approval and registration for urgent studies, with a registration resolution time frame of no more than two (2) business days. In addition, Resolución 512 de 2019 establishes that projects using laboratory animals must be evaluated by an animal ethics and welfare committee.
q_6_4_fuente: Resolución N° 400 de 7 de junio de 2021, Article One; Resolución N° 400 de 7 de junio de 2021, Article Six; Resolución N° 512 de 28 de junio de 2019, Article 19.

q_1_1_directa: The National Regulatory Authority (NRA) for clinical trials is the Dirección Nacional de Vigilancia Sanitaria (National Health Surveillance Directorate, DINAVISA), under the Ministry of Public Health and Social Welfare.
q_1_1_ampliada: DINAVISA is the implementing body that acts as the national health authority, verifying compliance with legal and regulatory provisions on health products. It is responsible for authorizing, controlling, and overseeing clinical trials within Paraguayan territory. Ley N.º 7361/2024 amended and expanded Ley N.º 6788/2021, incorporating the functions of the former Instituto Nacional de Alimentación y Nutrición (INAN) into DINAVISA, which becomes the country's sole health surveillance authority, without affecting the current framework for clinical trials.
q_1_1_fuente: Ley N.º 1119/97 de Productos para la Salud y Otros (Title I, Chapter I, Article 3.1); Ley N.º 6788/2021 (Article 5); Ley N.º 7361/2024 (Articles 3 and 5); Resolución DINAVISA N.º 238/2024 (Article 1).
q_1_2_directa: The main regulations include Ley 1119/97 de Productos para la Salud y Otros, which establishes the general framework for clinical trials, and Resolución S.G. N.º 355/2024, which updates and implements the Política Nacional de Ética en la Investigación para la Salud Paraguay 2023.
q_1_2_ampliada: Ley 1119/97 regulates prior authorization of products in the clinical research phase and establishes that all clinical trials must be authorized in advance by the national health authority, in accordance with good clinical practice. The National Ethics Policy, for its part, seeks to establish an ethical governance system capable of ensuring research meets the highest international ethical standards, including the Declaration of Helsinki and the CIOMS Guidelines.
q_1_2_fuente: Ley N.º 1119/97 de Productos para la Salud y Otros (Title II, Chapter II, Article 23 and Chapter VI, Article 30); Resolución S.G. N.º 355/2024 (Article 1, Introduction).
q_1_3_directa: The main regulation governing the specific authorization of clinical trials for medicines, vaccines, medical devices, and in vitro diagnostic products is Resolución DINAVISA N.º 238/2024, expanded by Resolución DINAVISA N.º 56/2026.
q_1_3_ampliada:
This resolution establishes the requirements for granting authorization to conduct, control, and oversee clinical trials, requiring compliance with Good Clinical Practice (GCP). It also reiterates that clinical trials must be conducted with respect for individuals' fundamental rights and the ethical principles of the Declaration of Helsinki and the CIOMS ethical guidelines.

Resolución DINAVISA N.º 56/2026 expands Resolución 238/2024 and adds two complementary requirements: (i) the Investigator's Brochure submitted with the application must comply with the ICH E6(R3) Good Clinical Practice guideline, on penalty of the authorization being rejected; and (ii) the sponsor or its legal representative in Paraguay must submit to DINAVISA, in addition to the final reports required under 238/2024, the study's global reports within no more than twelve (12) months of the trial's completion, aligned with the ICH E3 Guideline (Clinical Study Reports), on penalty of sanction.
q_1_3_fuente: Resolución DINAVISA N.º 238/2024 (Recitals, Article 1, Article 8); Resolución DINAVISA N.º 56/2026 (Articles 1, 2, and 3).
q_1_4_directa: Yes, approval from a Health Research Ethics Committee (CEIS) is required for all clinical trials before they begin.
q_1_4_ampliada: The regulation establishes that CEIS approval is mandatory to guarantee the protection of participants' rights, dignity, and well-being. For clinical trials involving medicines, vaccines, medical devices, and in vitro diagnostic products, protocols must be approved by a CEIS accredited by the Ministry of Public Health and Social Welfare (MSPBS).
q_1_4_fuente: Resolución DINAVISA N.º 238/2024 (Article 7, Article 9, Article 4.1).
q_1_5_directa: Yes, CEIS approval is a general documentary requirement for the submission to DINAVISA, and the approval document must specify the list of approved documents with their corresponding versions.
q_1_5_ampliada: DINAVISA requires the clinical trial authorization application to include a certified copy of the CEIS's approval. In fact, the informed consent and assent document submitted to the NRA must be approved and initialed by the CEIS, confirming the sequential nature of the process: ethics first, then sanitary regulation.
q_1_5_fuente: SOLICITUD DE ENSAYO CLÍNICO (FOR-DI-02) (Section 4.3, 4.6); Resolución DINAVISA N.º 238/2024 (Article 47.a.6, Article 47.a.9).
q_1_6_directa: Yes, a dual accreditation system exists for Health Research Ethics Committees (CEIS). This mechanism is split between a basic accreditation granted by the MSPBS and a supplementary accreditation issued by DINAVISA. The supplementary accreditation is mandatory for committees seeking to evaluate clinical trials involving medicines, vaccines, or medical devices.
q_1_6_ampliada: The accreditation system seeks to ensure CEIS operate under rigorous ethical standards and have the technical competence needed to evaluate complex protocols. Under regulations implemented in 2025, basic accreditation is granted by the MSPBS's Dirección General de Planificación y Evaluación (DGPE) for research in general. Subsequently, to evaluate clinical trials with products subject to sanitary surveillance, the committee must obtain DINAVISA's supplementary accreditation, valid for 24 months. To request the latter, institutions must already hold current basic accreditation. DINAVISA continuously supervises and audits these committees to verify their independence, transparency, and proper operation.
q_1_6_fuente: Resolución S.G. N° 379/2025, Articles 1 and 3; Resolución DINAVISA N° 327/2025, Articles 4, 10, and 16.
q_1_7_directa: Yes, a public, up-to-date registry exists of Health Research Ethics Committees (CEIS) duly accredited in the country. The MSPBS and DINAVISA are required by regulation to publish this information. The list allows the scientific community to verify which committees hold basic accreditation and which hold supplementary authorization.
q_1_7_ampliada: The transparency of Paraguay's ethical review system is guaranteed by legal mandates requiring the authorities to publish committee registries. Under Resolución DINAVISA N° 327/2025, the regulatory authority must maintain on its official website a database listing all CEIS holding the Supplementary Accreditation certificate. DINAVISA must also periodically communicate this updated list to the MSPBS for formal consolidation. The National Ethics Policy (Resolución S.G. N° 355/2024) also assigns the MSPBS the unavoidable responsibility of maintaining a public database on its website with information on all nationally accredited committees. This allows sponsors and contract research organizations to easily consult the committees authorized in the country.
q_1_7_fuente: Resolución DINAVISA N° 327/2025, Article 8; Resolución S.G. N.º 355/2024, Section 11.
q_1_8_directa: Yes. All clinical trials involving a product in the clinical research phase must have a prior authorization ruling from the national health authority, specifically including clinical trials for medicines, vaccines, medical devices, and in vitro diagnostic products.
q_1_8_ampliada: DINAVISA must grant prior authorization for clinical trials involving products with or without registration in Paraguay, or those registered with other national authorities, if they involve any post-registration change requiring registrable clinical data (such as a new therapeutic indication, new route of administration, or new dosage regimen). The authority to order a clinical trial's precautionary suspension when any established condition is not met rests with the national health authority.
q_1_8_fuente: Ley N.º 1119/97 de Productos para la Salud y Otros (Title II, Chapter II, Article 23.1, Chapter VI, Article 30.4); Resolución DINAVISA N.º 238/2024 (Article 3).
q_2_1_directa: Yes. The sponsor is defined as the individual, group of individuals, company, institution, or organization responsible for the initiation, management, completion, and financing of a clinical trial, and must have legal representation in the country.
q_2_1_ampliada: The definition covers any entity, including academic institutions, that takes on the study's legal and financial burden. If the sponsor is foreign, it must have a legal representative in Paraguay. The sponsor's responsibilities are broad, including quality management, maintaining records for 10 years after the trial's conclusion, and guaranteeing participants' safety and well-being.
q_2_1_fuente: Resolución DINAVISA N.º 238/2024 (Article 36, Article 7, Article 27.e).
q_2_2_directa: Yes. When the sponsor is foreign, it must submit an original document or notarized copy of proof of the delegation of functions to its legal representative in Paraguay.
q_2_2_ampliada: The legal representative is essential for channeling all communication with DINAVISA throughout the clinical trial's conduct. This requirement ensures a legally responsible party domiciled in Paraguay exists to answer to the health authority for obligations arising from the study. The sponsor must appoint this representative.
q_2_2_fuente: SOLICITUD DE ENSAYO CLÍNICO (FOR-DI-02) (Section 4.2); Resolución DINAVISA N.º 238/2024 (Article 34.a, 34.b, Article 47.a.5).
q_2_3_directa: Yes. The sponsor must guarantee the investigational product's fitness, safety, and quality, submit the CEIS's ethical approval, and take out a civil liability insurance policy.
q_2_3_ampliada: To act as sponsor, an entity must have sufficient safety and efficacy data from non-clinical and/or clinical studies to support human exposure. A sworn statement or certification that the product meets Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) requirements for investigational products is also required, along with a formal contract with the research institution and the investigator.
q_2_3_fuente: SOLICITUD DE ENSAYO CLÍNICO (FOR-DI-02) (Section 4.7, 4.8); Resolución DINAVISA N.º 238/2024 (Article 34.d, Article 41.a, 41.b, Article 47.a.10, 47.a.11).
q_2_4_directa: Yes. The sponsor may transfer tasks to a CRO, but must specify the delegated functions in writing and retain ultimate responsibility for the quality and integrity of the research data.
q_2_4_ampliada: If a CRO takes on responsibilities, it must have a legal representative in Paraguay when these responsibilities relate to a clinical trial. The CRO must implement a written quality assurance and quality control system. The sponsor must ensure the CRO fulfills all subcontracted, trial-related tasks.
q_2_4_fuente: Resolución DINAVISA N.º 238/2024 (Article 36, Article 37).
q_2_5_directa: Yes, Paraguayan regulations require research sites to hold specific technical authorization to conduct each clinical trial. Facilities must be physical and adequately equipped for the study's duration and procedural demands, operating under Good Clinical Practice (GCP) at all times. Documented institutional authorization to host the project is also required.
q_2_5_ampliada: For a research site to be licensed as a trial's official location, the sponsor must submit a specific site authorization application to DINAVISA. Under Article 21 of Resolución DINAVISA N° 238/2024, the principal investigator is responsible for ensuring the facilities have appropriate, safe resources to conduct the trial and handle the experimental products. The filed dossier must include certified copies of the express authorization issued by the health facility's highest authority and, where applicable, the local teaching and research committee. These sites are subject to periodic inspections and audits by the regulatory authority to ensure continued compliance with operational regulations.
q_2_5_fuente: Resolución DINAVISA N.º 238/2024, Article 21; Requisitos de Ensayos Clínicos, Section 3.
q_2_6_directa: Yes. The principal investigator and their team must be legally registered and licensed in the country, with demonstrable clinical fitness for the study's field and formal, up-to-date training in Good Clinical Practice (GCP) and research ethics.
q_2_6_ampliada: The regulatory framework requires the principal investigator and their team to demonstrate their technical fitness through an up-to-date curriculum vitae and notarized copies of their current professional licenses. Under Resolución DINAVISA N° 238/2024, for Phase II and III clinical trials, the principal investigator is explicitly required to hold a medical specialty degree directly corresponding to the condition under study. The entire clinical team involved must provide proof of GCP training and sign a sworn commitment statement agreeing to adhere to international ethical standards and national regulations. Finally, the principal investigator assumes full responsibility for the study's conduct and must strictly oversee any function delegated at their site.
q_2_6_fuente: Resolución DINAVISA N.º 238/2024, Articles 20 and 21; Requisitos de Ensayos Clínicos, Section 2.
q_2_7_directa: Yes. Taking out civil liability insurance for potential harm caused by the trial, issued by insurers registered in Paraguay, is mandatory, and the sponsor is required to compensate participants for any harm they suffer.
q_2_7_ampliada: The policy must be issued by insurers licensed, supervised, and overseen by the Superintendencia de Seguros, and must protect both investigators and participants. The sponsor's responsibilities include ensuring coverage of medical care, diagnosis, treatment, and hospitalization for all protocol-related costs. The insurance policy must also clearly establish the commitment to compensate participants for harm caused.
q_2_7_fuente: SOLICITUD DE ENSAYO CLÍNICO (FOR-DI-02) (Section 4.8); Resolución DINAVISA N.º 238/2024 (Article 40.a, 40.b, Article 41.k).
q_3_1_directa: Yes. The submission must include the Application Form, the research Protocol, the Investigator's Brochure, the CEIS's approval, the CEIS-initialed Informed Consent, the insurance policy, and registration in WHO's ICTRP registry.
q_3_1_ampliada: All key documentation, such as the Protocol and the Investigator's Brochure, must be submitted in Spanish and in the original language. For foreign sponsors, proof of the delegation of functions to the legal representative in Paraguay is required. A sworn statement from the sponsor on GMP compliance must also be included. Under Resolución DINAVISA N.º 56/2026 (Article 2), the Investigator's Brochure must comply with the ICH E6(R3) Good Clinical Practice guideline, including the corresponding documentary requirements; failure to comply is grounds for rejecting the clinical trial authorization application.
q_3_1_fuente: SOLICITUD DE ENSAYO CLÍNICO (FOR-DI-02) (Section 4); Resolución DINAVISA N.º 238/2024 (Article 47.a.4 to 47.a.17); Resolución DINAVISA N.º 56/2026 (Article 2).
q_3_2_directa: Yes. The authorization application, including the attached documentation, must be submitted by the sponsor in printed format to DINAVISA.
q_3_2_ampliada: Although the regulation notes that application forms are available on DINAVISA's website, physical submission of the application is the format established by the regulation. It is essential that documents of foreign origin be submitted apostilled or consularized and legalized. Documentation must be submitted in the order detailed in the regulatory resolution.
q_3_2_fuente: Resolución DINAVISA N.º 238/2024 (Article 47, Article 47.a.4, final paragraph).
q_3_3_directa: Yes. The general time frame for DINAVISA to rule on (authorize, deny, or raise objections to) clinical trial applications is 60 business days.
q_3_3_ampliada: This 60-business-day time frame governs the application evaluation process. In public health emergencies, the time frame for expedited clinical trial authorization is reduced to 15 business days. If DINAVISA raises objections, the sponsor has 30 business days to respond, and if it does not, the application will be deemed withdrawn.
q_3_3_fuente: Resolución DINAVISA N.º 238/2024 (Article 18.b, Article 51).
q_3_4_directa: Yes. Authorization of a pharmaceutical specialty, which includes the clinical trial, is subject to payment of fees, and proof of fee payment must be submitted with the application.
q_3_4_ampliada: The national health authority has the power to determine which activities require fee payment and to regulate its fee-setting methodology. At the time of the application, a fee-exemption request may be submitted where applicable. However, the specific amount or fee schedule applicable to the clinical trial authorization procedure before DINAVISA is not detailed in a specific public resolution. Resolución DINAVISA N.º 219/2025, for its part, approves the fee for accrediting Health Research Ethics Committees (CEIS) with DINAVISA, a cost borne by the CEIS, not the trial's sponsor.
q_3_4_fuente: Ley N.º 1119/97 de Productos para la Salud y Otros (Title V, Article 41); Resolución DINAVISA N.º 238/2024 (Article 47.a.1, 47.a.2); Resolución DINAVISA N.º 219/2025.
q_3_5_directa: Yes, registering the clinical trial in a registry that is part of WHO's International Clinical Trials Registry Platform (ICTRP) is a requirement for authorization.
q_3_5_ampliada: Submitting proof of registration in an ICTRP registry is a mandatory documentary requirement that must be attached to the clinical trial authorization application. This requirement aligns with the National Ethics Policy, which seeks research transparency and requires clinical trials to be registered in an ICTRP-affiliated registry.
q_3_5_fuente: SOLICITUD DE ENSAYO CLÍNICO (FOR-DI-02) (Section 4.14); Resolución DINAVISA N.º 238/2024 (Article 47.a.17); Política Nacional de Ética en la Investigación para la Salud Paraguay 2023 (Section 8, Investigators).
q_3_6_directa: DINAVISA may base its guidelines on high-surveillance international bodies such as ICH, CIOMS, EMA, and FDA, but the regulation does not establish a formal mechanism for automatically recognizing or exempting foreign evaluations.
q_3_6_ampliada: Although the regulatory authority is empowered to take regulatory action based on information and decisions from foreign agencies classified as PAHO Regional Reference Authorities, the initial authorization process requires full submission of documentation (Protocol, Investigator's Brochure, etc.), as well as ethical approval from a local CEIS. Adherence to ICH and CIOMS guidelines is a fundamental principle guiding DINAVISA.
q_3_6_fuente: Resolución DINAVISA N.º 238/2024 (Article 59, Article 60).
q_3_7_directa: The process involves selecting a qualified site/investigator, obtaining ethical approval from the local CEIS, and the final regulatory submission and evaluation by DINAVISA.
q_3_7_ampliada:
The sequential order of key steps is:

Capacity Assurance and Contracting: The sponsor must select a Principal Investigator (PI) with adequate qualifications and experience, and a research site meeting GCP standards. The sponsor must sign a contract with the institution and the PI, including a mandatory clause on regulatory compliance.

Documentation Preparation: The sponsor prepares the research Protocol, the Investigator's Brochure (including non-clinical studies), and the Informed Consent/Assent, all in Spanish and in the original language.

Prior Ethical Approval: The PI must request and obtain prior approval of the protocol and informed consent/assent from a duly accredited CEIS.

Public Registry Registration: The clinical trial must be registered in a registry that is part of WHO's ICTRP platform.

Legal and Financial Documentation: The sponsor must secure the insurance policy, the GMP declaration, and, if foreign, delegation of functions to its legal representative in Paraguay.

Application and Payment: The sponsor or its representative submits the formal application (in printed format) to DINAVISA, attaching all documentary requirements (including proof of fee payment).

DINAVISA Regulatory Evaluation: DINAVISA reviews the application and evaluates the product's and study's quality and safety. The maximum response time frame is 60 business days.

Final Authorization: DINAVISA issues the authorization ruling, allowing the trial to begin.
q_3_7_fuente: SOLICITUD DE ENSAYO CLÍNICO (FOR-DI-02) (Section 4); Resolución DINAVISA N.º 238/2024 (Article 18, Article 22.a, Article 34, Article 47).
q_4_1_directa: Yes. The design artwork for primary (label) and secondary (box) packaging materials, as applicable, is required in Spanish.
q_4_1_ampliada: DINAVISA requires submission of information related to the investigational product, including the packaging artwork design. Generally, the text on packaging, containers, package inserts, and labels of pharmaceutical specialties must be in Spanish and contain the precise information needed for correct use.
q_4_1_fuente: SOLICITUD DE ENSAYO CLÍNICO (FOR-DI-02) (Section 4.10); Ley N.º 1119/97 de Productos para la Salud y Otros (Title II, Chapter I, Article 11.1, 11.2); Resolución DINAVISA N.º 238/2024 (Article 47.a.12).
q_4_2_directa: Yes. A sworn statement from the sponsor or a certification that the investigational product complies with Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) requirements for investigational products is required.
q_4_2_ampliada: Submitting this sworn statement or certification is a key requirement for trial authorization. The sponsor must guarantee that the investigational product is manufactured in accordance with GMP for investigational products. Ley 1119/97 defines Good Manufacturing and Control Practices as the standards that regulate manufacturing and control processes to guarantee quality.
q_4_2_fuente: SOLICITUD DE ENSAYO CLÍNICO (FOR-DI-02) (Section 4.7); Resolución DINAVISA N.º 238/2024 (Article 41.b, Article 47.a.10).
q_4_3_directa: No. Approval of the clinical trial (execution authorization) is only a prerequisite. Importing and using the investigational product require submitting a specific import authorization application after the trial's approval.
q_4_3_ampliada: The sponsor must submit the application form for import authorization of the investigational product, comparator, and/or complementary products. This application must be accompanied by the commercial invoice, donation letter or equivalent document, packing list, transport document (air, land, sea, or river), and quality control certificate. DINAVISA is responsible for authorizing the import for research purposes only.
q_4_3_fuente: Resolución DINAVISA N.º 238/2024 (Article 18.h, Article 48).
q_5_1_directa: Yes. The Principal Investigator must report Serious Adverse Events (SAEs) to the sponsor within 24 hours. The sponsor must report Serious Unexpected Adverse Drug Reactions (RAMSI) occurring inside or outside the country to DINAVISA, the CEIS, and investigators, within 10 calendar days of becoming aware of them.
q_5_1_ampliada: The principal investigator must also promptly report SAEs to the corresponding CEIS. The sponsor must also report any information from animal studies suggesting significant risk (such as carcinogenicity or teratogenicity) within 10 calendar days. The sponsor is responsible for reporting any information of immediate importance, including reports from the Independent Data Monitoring Committee (CIMD), within the same 10-calendar-day time frame.
q_5_1_fuente: Resolución DINAVISA N.º 238/2024 (Article 29.a, 29.b, Article 42.1, 42.2, 42.3).
q_5_2_directa: Yes, submission of an annual Development Safety Update Report (DSUR) is required, whose content must align with ICH guidelines.
q_5_2_ampliada: The DSUR is an annual report the sponsor must submit to DINAVISA, presenting a review of the safety information collected during the reporting period to determine the investigational product's benefit/risk profile. In addition to DINAVISA, serious adverse events occurring at authorized sites in the country must be included in the progress report and the final report.
q_5_2_fuente: Resolución DINAVISA N.º 238/2024 (Article 28, Article 29, Article 42.4).
q_5_3_directa: Yes, the Principal Investigator is required to submit the progress report to the CEIS and the sponsor, and the sponsor to DINAVISA.
q_5_3_ampliada: The sponsor's frequency for submitting the progress report to DINAVISA and the CEIS is once, if the clinical trial is shorter than 12 months, and once a year, if longer than 12 months. The progress report is a periodic document detailing the clinical trial's status, including the number of participants, serious adverse events, deviations, and amendments. DINAVISA must evaluate these reports within 60 business days. In addition, Resolución DINAVISA N.º 56/2026 (Article 3) requires that, once the trial is complete, the sponsor or its legal representative in Paraguay submit to DINAVISA — in addition to the final reports required under Resolución 238/2024 — the study's global reports within no more than twelve (12) months, aligned with the structure and content of the ICH E3 Guideline (Clinical Study Reports); failure to comply is grounds for sanction.
q_5_3_fuente: Resolución DINAVISA N.º 238/2024 (Article 18.l, Article 26, Article 28.a); Resolución DINAVISA N.º 56/2026 (Article 3).
q_5_4_directa: Yes. Substantial amendments require the prior approval of both the CEIS and DINAVISA.
q_5_4_ampliada: An amendment is classified as substantial if it involves changes to the design, population, procedures, or product. Non-substantial amendments (such as administrative or contact-information changes) do not require prior approval. DINAVISA has a 15-business-day time frame to authorize or deny substantial amendments. However, if modifications are absolutely necessary to prevent risks to participants, they may be implemented immediately, with the authorities notified within the following 24 hours.
q_5_4_fuente: Resolución DINAVISA N.º 238/2024 (Article 17, Article 18.f, Article 12.g).
q_5_5_directa: No. Paraguay's current regulatory framework does not establish an explicit legal obligation for the sponsor to guarantee participants access to the investigational product once the clinical trial ends.
q_5_5_ampliada: Unlike other regional regulations, neither Ley 1119/97 nor Resolución DINAVISA N.º 238/2024 details a specific mechanism or mandate on post-trial access. Resolución 238/2024 does, however, require trials to adhere to the ethical principles of the Declaration of Helsinki and the CIOMS Guidelines. The CIOMS Guidelines (Guideline 6) establish that sponsors and investigators must make provisions for post-trial access to interventions shown to be beneficial. Consequently, although not a codified regulatory requirement, this becomes a fundamental ethical requirement that will be rigorously assessed by the local CEIS. The sponsor must clearly describe, in the protocol and informed consent form, its post-trial access policy in order to obtain ethical approval. The absence of such a policy is a likely reason for CEIS objection.
q_5_5_fuente: Resolución DINAVISA N.º 238/2024 (Article 8); International Ethical Guidelines for Health-Related Research Involving Humans (CIOMS, 2016).
q_6_1_directa: Yes. Until the new general law takes effect, the directly applicable regulation is Ley N.º 6534/2020, "De Protección de Datos Personales Crediticios" [On the Protection of Credit-Related Personal Data], whose general provisions protect sensitive personal data — a category that includes health data. On November 27, 2025, Ley N.º 7593/2025, "De Protección de Datos Personales en la República del Paraguay" [On the Protection of Personal Data in the Republic of Paraguay], was enacted, the country's first general data protection legal framework, with a 24-month vacatio legis period (taking effect in November 2027).
q_6_1_ampliada:
Despite its title focusing on credit matters, Ley N.º 6534/2020 currently functions as the main personal data protection regulation in Paraguay and is directly applicable to clinical trials. Its Article 2 defines a general scope of application for all processing of personal data within national territory. Article 3 defines "Sensitive Personal Data," explicitly including "data relating to health... genetic data, or biometric data." The law establishes fundamental principles such as the need for free, express, and informed consent from the data subject for processing their data (Article 6), the duty of confidentiality for those handling data (Article 11), and the obligation to implement security measures to protect the integrity and confidentiality of information (Article 10). The sponsor, the CRO, and investigators must therefore ensure strict compliance with this law throughout all phases of collecting, storing, and processing participants' data.

In November 2025, Ley N.º 7593/2025, "De Protección de Datos Personales en la República del Paraguay," was enacted — the country's first general regulatory framework on the subject, inspired by standards such as the European GDPR. The new law expressly recognizes health-related, genetic, and biometric data as sensitive; establishes data subject rights (access, rectification, erasure, objection, portability); imposes security, confidentiality, and transparency obligations; and creates the Agencia Nacional de Protección de Datos Personales (National Personal Data Protection Agency, ANPDP) as the oversight authority. Ley N.º 7593/2025 establishes a 24-month vacatio legis period from its enactment, so it will become fully enforceable in November 2027; in the meantime, Ley N.º 6534/2020 remains in force and will coexist with the new law.
q_6_1_fuente: Ley N.º 6534/2020 de Protección de Datos Personales Crediticios (Articles 2, 3, 4, 6, 10, 11); Ley N.º 7593/2025 de Protección de Datos Personales en la República del Paraguay.
q_6_2_directa: Vaccines are explicitly included within the scope of Resolución DINAVISA N.º 238/2024, under the same authorization regime as medicines, and are considered a type of "special medicine" under Ley 1119/97.
q_6_2_ampliada: Resolución 238/2024 establishes that its requirements apply to clinical trials involving medicines, vaccines, medical devices, and in vitro diagnostic products. Paraguay also has Ley N.º 4621/2012, the "National Vaccines Law," which guarantees citizens' protection against vaccine-preventable diseases. The regulation requires the same documentation and GCP compliance as for other investigational products.
q_6_2_fuente: Ley N.º 1119/97 de Productos para la Salud y Otros (Title II, Chapter II, Article 24.2); Resolución DINAVISA N.º 238/2024 (Article 1, Recitals).
q_6_3_directa: Yes. Resolución DINAVISA N.º 238/2024 regulates the use of biological materials and data for future research, requiring specific informed consent.
q_6_3_ampliada: Informed consent must be appropriate, ensuring that if the future use of biological materials is known at the time of collection, specific authorization for that purpose is obtained. If the future use is unknown, a collection consent process must still be carried out, without specifying the final use, while guaranteeing privacy.
q_6_3_fuente: Resolución DINAVISA N.º 238/2024 (Article 14).
q_6_4_directa: Yes. Specific regulations exist for Post-Authorization Safety Studies (EPA/PASS), governed by Resolución DINAVISA N.º 359/2024, expedited procedures for trials during public health emergencies, and emergency use of unproven interventions (the MEURI framework).
q_6_4_ampliada: EPA/PASS studies are observational studies aimed at identifying, characterizing, or quantifying risks associated with the safety of registered medicines, and require prior CEIS approval. For emergency situations, DINAVISA implements expedited clinical trial authorization processes within 15 business days. DINAVISA is also empowered to authorize emergency use of unproven interventions under WHO's MEURI framework, also within 15 business days.
q_6_4_fuente: Resolución DINAVISA N.º 238/2024 (Article 51, Article 52); Resolución DINAVISA N.º 359/2024 (Recitals, Article 5).

q_1_1_directa: The National Regulatory Authority (NRA) for clinical trials is the Instituto Nacional de Salud (National Institute of Health, INS), through its Dirección de Investigación e Innovación en Salud (Directorate of Health Research and Innovation, DIIS).
q_1_1_ampliada: The DIIS is the INS's technical-regulatory line body and has the primary responsibility of regulating, authorizing, and overseeing clinical trials conducted nationwide. Within the DIIS operates the Subdirección de Ensayos Clínicos (Clinical Trials Sub-Directorate, SUDEC), responsible for formulating policies, strategies, and regulations, and for technically evaluating, authorizing, and overseeing studies. The regulation establishes that the DIIS must protect participants' rights and the quality of the data generated.
q_1_1_fuente: Decreto Supremo N° 021-2017-SA, Article 5.
q_1_2_directa: The main regulations include the Ley General de Salud, which promotes scientific research in the health field, and the Documento Técnico de Consideraciones Éticas para la Investigación en Salud con Seres Humanos [Technical Document on Ethical Considerations for Health Research Involving Human Subjects].
q_1_2_ampliada: The Ley General de Salud (Ley N° 26842) provides that the State promotes scientific and technological research in the health field. In addition, the Technical Document approved by Resolución Ministerial N.° 233-2020-MINSA sets out ethical considerations, based on international standards, to ensure that all health research involving human subjects in Peru is conducted ethically.
q_1_2_fuente: Ley N° 26842, Preliminary Title, item XV; Resolución Ministerial N° 233-2020-MINSA, approving the Documento Técnico "Consideraciones Éticas para la Investigación en Salud con Seres Humanos".
q_1_3_directa: Clinical trial authorization is governed primarily by the Reglamento de Ensayos Clínicos approved by Decreto Supremo N° 021-2017-SA and its amendments. The process is further detailed in the Manual de Procedimientos de Ensayos Clínicos and in the INS's Texto Único de Procedimientos Administrativos (Single Text of Administrative Procedures, TUPA).
q_1_3_ampliada: The central regulatory framework is Decreto Supremo N° 021-2017-SA, amended by Decreto Supremo N° 028-2023-SA and Resolución Directoral N° 184-2023-DIIS/INS, which govern substantial aspects and minor protocol changes. Technical implementation of authorization applies the Manual de Procedimientos de Ensayos Clínicos, updated through Resolución Jefatural N° 252-2022-J-OPE/INS. Administrative time frames, requirements, and fees for authorization are set out in Decreto Supremo N° 010-2025-SA, which approves the INS's TUPA. These regulations define the ethical and technical review criteria, including the binding opinion of the Autoridad Nacional de Productos Farmacéuticos (National Pharmaceutical Products Authority, ANM) on the safety and quality of investigational products.
q_1_3_fuente: Decreto Supremo N° 021-2017-SA; Decreto Supremo N° 028-2023-SA; Decreto Supremo No. 010-2025-SA; Resolución Jefatural N.° 252-2022-J-OPE/INS.
q_1_4_directa: Yes, in Peru obtaining approval from an accredited Comité Institucional de Ética en Investigación (Institutional Research Ethics Committee, CIEI) is a mandatory requirement. No clinical trial or health research involving human participants may begin without this formal approval.
q_1_4_ampliada: The regulatory framework requires every research project involving human subjects to be reviewed and approved by a CIEI before it is conducted, to safeguard participants' rights, safety, and well-being. For clinical trials specifically, the CIEI must be registered and accredited with the INS. CIEIs carry out an independent, competent, and timely evaluation of all ethical aspects of the protocol and the informed consent process. These committees must also continuously monitor approved trials, with a frequency based on risk level and never less than once a year. In the event of uncontrolled risk, they may suspend or cancel the study.
q_1_4_fuente: Decreto Supremo N° 021-2017-SA. Resolución Ministerial N° 233-2020-MINSA.
q_1_5_directa: Yes, approval from an accredited CIEI must be obtained prior to the regulatory application. The sponsor must include proof of this ethical approval within the file submitted to the National Regulatory Authority.
q_1_5_ampliada: Peruvian regulations, including the Reglamento de Ensayos Clínicos and the Manual de Procedimientos, explicitly prohibit ethical review and regulatory authority review from running in parallel. The INS makes its review conditional on receiving a copy of the research protocol and the informed consent form, duly stamped and fully signed by the CIEI. This documentation serves as evidence that the version submitted to the INS is exactly the same as the one that has already passed ethical scrutiny. Once CIEI approval and the research institution's authorization are obtained, the sponsor or CRO may submit the complete dossier to the DIIS for final authorization.
q_1_5_fuente: Decreto Supremo N° 021-2017-SA. Resolución Jefatural N.° 252-2022-J-OPE/INS. Resolución Ministerial N° 233-2020-MINSA, item 7.2.1(b) and item 8.4.3.
q_1_6_directa: Yes, an official accreditation system exists for CIEIs. This accreditation is mandatory and is granted by the DIIS of the INS.
q_1_6_ampliada: Every CIEI seeking to evaluate clinical trials involving pharmaceutical products must be registered and accredited by the INS through the Registro Peruano de Ensayos Clínicos (Peruvian Clinical Trials Registry, REPEC v2.0). The accreditation process requires the committee to demonstrate compliance with the standards detailed in the Manual de Procedimientos de Ensayos Clínicos and to submit its bylaws, procedures manual, and members' curricula vitae. Decreto Supremo N° 010-2025-SA establishes that the accreditation certificate granted by the INS is no longer subject to periodic renewal, unlike the former requirement to renew it every three years. The INS may also conduct inspections or audits of committees to verify that accreditation conditions are maintained.
q_1_6_fuente: Decreto Supremo N° 021-2017-SA, Title IV, Chapter 7; Manual de Procedimientos de Ensayos Clínicos (INS-CTManual); Decreto Supremo N° 010-2025-SA.
q_1_7_directa: Yes, an official public registry exists, called the Registro Nacional de Comités de Ética en Investigación [National Registry of Research Ethics Committees]. This registry is managed by the DIIS through the REPEC online platform.
q_1_7_ampliada: The National Registry brings together all CIEIs formally registered and accredited by the INS. Through the REPEC system (version v2.0), research institutions can electronically initiate the registration process for their committees. Depending on the type of research the committee evaluates, registration may be immediate or progressive. However, for the specific evaluation of drug clinical trials, being listed as a fully accredited CIEI in this national database is essential, and this information can be accessed and verified by sponsors and the public.
q_1_7_fuente: Decreto Supremo N° 021-2017-SA; Resolución de Presidencia Ejecutiva N° 006-2023-PE/INS; Resolución Ministerial N° 233-2020-MINSA.
q_1_8_directa: Yes. All interventional research classified as a clinical trial (Phases I through IV) must be authorized by the INS before it begins. This covers studies determining the efficacy and safety of registered or unregistered pharmaceutical products.
q_1_8_ampliada: The scope of mandatory NRA authorization includes clinical trials evaluating medicines, herbal medicines and other complementary products, dietary products, sweeteners, biological products, and galenic (compounded) products. The INS approves this research through the DIIS, ensuring compliance with Good Clinical Practice. The investigational product must meet certain conditions, such as being approved in high sanitary surveillance countries, being a national public health priority, or being required to establish therapeutic equivalence. Research involving human subjects that does not use medicines or devices is also governed by ethical standards, but clinical trials in the strict sense require express technical, legal, and ethical authorization through a Resolución Directoral.
q_1_8_fuente: Decreto Supremo N° 021-2017-SA, Article 1 (Purpose), Article 2 (item 11), Article 3 (Scope of Application), and Fourth Final Supplementary Provision.
q_2_1_directa: Yes. Peruvian regulations define the sponsor as a natural or legal person, company, institution, or organization, including academic ones, with legal representation in the country. The sponsor takes responsibility for the initiation, management, completion, and financing of a clinical trial.
q_2_1_ampliada: Decreto Supremo N° 021-2017-SA establishes that the sponsor must be registered in the corresponding public registries and have legal representation within national territory. Before applying for clinical trial authorization, the sponsor must register on the REPEC electronic platform. The regulation provides that when an independent investigator initiates and assumes full responsibility for a trial, they take on the role and obligations of a sponsor. Although the sponsor may delegate operational functions to a CRO, it retains ultimate responsibility for the protocol's execution and the data generated. Failure to fulfill its duties results in penalties.
q_2_1_fuente: Decreto Supremo N° 021-2017-SA.
q_2_2_directa: Yes, the sponsor is required to have a legal representative or a legal entity domiciled in the country. Foreign sponsors must appoint a legal representative residing within national territory for the entire duration of the study.
q_2_2_ampliada: Under the Reglamento de Ensayos Clínicos, every sponsor must have legal representation in the country and be registered in Peruvian public registries. For international sponsors, this legal representative channels all communication with the INS's DIIS. The regulation allows this communication and representation responsibility to be delegated to a CRO established in the country. When registering on the REPEC platform, the sponsor must submit documentation certifying the validity of this power of attorney or representation. Even when it delegates functions to a local entity or a CRO, the principal sponsor retains legal responsibility for the trial before the Peruvian State.
q_2_2_fuente: Decreto Supremo N° 021-2017-SA. Formulario FOR-DIIS-020: Solicitud para Registro de Patrocinador, items 2.3 and 2.4; Solicitud de Ampliación o Modificación del Listado de Suministros, item I.
q_2_3_directa: Yes. To act as such, the sponsor must complete mandatory administrative registration on the REPEC platform (v2.0) before requesting any clinical trial authorization. It must also submit the required institutional documentation and appoint a legal representative in the country.
q_2_3_ampliada: The regulatory framework requires the sponsor to initiate a registration procedure in the REPEC electronic system, managed by the INS. In this process, it must submit the sponsor registration form, presented in Spanish or accompanied by its translation. The documentation must include structural and institutional information, objectives, experience history, and, for international sponsors, consular authentication of the delegation of functions. The Reglamento de Ensayos Clínicos and the Manual de Procedimientos establish that approval of this registration is a prior, indispensable step before submitting any clinical study's dossier. Once registration is complete, the sponsor obtains the credentials to submit files through the INS's Mesa de Partes Virtual (Virtual Filing Desk, MPV).
q_2_3_fuente: Decreto Supremo N° 021-2017-SA; Resolución Jefatural N.° 252-2022-J-OPE/INS; Resolución Directoral No. 393-2021-OGITT-INS.
q_2_4_directa: Yes. Peruvian regulations allow the sponsor to fully or partially delegate its functions to a CRO. However, this CRO must have legal status and an established office in Peru, and must undergo prior registration in REPEC.
q_2_4_ampliada: Decreto Supremo N° 021-2017-SA authorizes sponsors to transfer a clinical trial's operational work and various regulatory obligations to a CRO domiciled in the country. Like the sponsor, the CRO must complete its own electronic registration on REPEC (v2.0), submit institutional forms, and provide credentials for its legal representative and monitoring staff. Delegated functions must be detailed in writing through contracts between both entities. Despite the transfer of tasks, the legislation establishes that the principal sponsor retains ultimate responsibility for the protocol's execution. In the event of violations or DIIS inspections, both parties are subject to audits and administrative penalties.
q_2_4_fuente: Decreto Supremo N° 021-2017-SA; Resolución Jefatural N.° 252-2022-J-OPE/INS. Formulario FOR-DIIS-021: Solicitud para Registro de Organización de Investigación por Contrato, Instructions, item 1.4, and item 2.
q_2_5_directa: Yes. The sponsor or the CRO selects research institutions based on their fitness and the physical availability of their facilities. Institutions must also hold an enabling registration in REPEC.
q_2_5_ampliada: Selecting research sites must comply with the Good Clinical Practice (ICH GCP) requirements adopted nationally, so the site has adequate resources and emergency equipment to protect participants. Before hosting a study, institutions must register in the INS's REPEC electronic system. This institutional registration requires submitting an enabling code issued by the Registro Nacional de Instituciones Prestadoras de Servicios de Salud (National Registry of Health Service Providers, RENIPRESS) and demonstrating its categorization level based on the clinic's or hospital's complexity. Under Decreto Legislativo N° 1452, amending Ley N° 27444, the Research Site Registration Certificate (RCI) has indefinite validity: certificates valid as of September 16, 2018, and those issued afterward, are exempt from the three-year renewal required under the Reglamento de Ensayos Clínicos, without prejudice to audits and possible revocation by the INS. Finally, sponsors must verify that the site holds active authorization in the medical specialty the trial will evaluate.
q_2_5_fuente: Decreto Supremo N° 021-2017-SA, Article 3; Decreto Legislativo N° 1452, amending Ley N° 27444; Resolución Ministerial No. 546-2011/MINSA.
q_2_6_directa: Yes. Investigators must be qualified through their education, professional training, and demonstrated clinical experience to take responsibility for a clinical trial. The sponsor must ensure their technical competence and time availability to conduct the study.
q_2_6_ampliada: Peru's regulatory framework adopts Good Clinical Practice (ICH GCP) standards and requires the sponsor to carefully select both the principal investigator and sub-investigators. These professionals must demonstrate technical fitness in their medical specialty and certify they have sufficient time to supervise subjects and conduct the study. It is a regulatory requirement for investigators to provide documented proof of having completed training in Good Clinical Practice and research ethics involving human subjects within the last three years. The sponsor compiles and submits to the INS the undocumented curricula vitae of all local team members. In addition, the principal investigator must sign sworn statements on the absence of financial conflicts of interest and their commitment to follow the approved protocol.
q_2_6_fuente: Decreto Supremo N° 021-2017-SA; Resolución Ministerial N° 233-2020-MINSA; Manual de Procedimientos de Ensayos Clínicos (INS-CTManual).
q_2_7_directa: Yes. It is a legal requirement for the sponsor or the CRO to take out a valid insurance policy covering any unforeseen injury suffered by participants. The sponsor must also guarantee, under a sworn statement, the immediate availability of a financial fund for compensatory care.
q_2_7_ampliada: The regulation requires the sponsor to take out insurance coverage established in Peru or, if the policy belongs to an international company, to have a legal representative in the country assume that insurance jurisdiction. The policy must remain active until the National Final Report is submitted to the health authority. In addition to insurance, the sponsor must submit a notarized document certifying an immediate financial fund intended to guarantee free medical care and cover unforeseen harm. When harm arises from participation in the trial, including complications during pregnancies begun during the study, the sponsor must provide fair monetary compensation. This financial and indemnity responsibility remains regardless of the policy's term or maximum limits.
q_2_7_fuente: Decreto Supremo N° 021-2017-SA, Title III, Chapter II, Article 41; Formulario FOR-DIIS-029.
q_3_1_directa: Yes. The essential content includes the formal application, the research protocol, and the informed consent form approved by the Ethics Committee, in addition to the host institution's authorization. Technical documentation for the investigational product, valid insurance policies, and sworn statements on the team's fitness are also required.
q_3_1_ampliada: Submitting the file for clinical trial authorization involves several documentary and technical requirements. The sponsor must include proof of payment of the processing fee and the printed, signed electronic form. It must submit the updated Investigator's Brochure, the protocol, and the informed consent, all in Spanish, accompanied by the stamped, signed approval from the CIEI. The technical file must attach the team's Good Clinical Practice (GCP) training certificates, curricula vitae, the detailed list of supplies to be imported, and the national budget. Finally, sworn statements on the absence of conflicts of interest, the site's readiness, and the existence of a compensation fund are required, along with the active insurance policy.
q_3_1_fuente: Resolución Jefatural N.° 252-2022-J-OPE/INS, Annexes 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, and 9; Formulario FOR-DIIS-063; Formulario FOR-DIIS-064; Formulario FOR-DIIS-032; Formulario FOR-DIIS-031; Formulario FOR-DIIS-023. Decreto Supremo N° 021-2017-SA. Decreto Supremo No. 010-2025-SA.
q_3_2_directa: Yes. The submission process is entirely electronic and uses two official INS platforms. The application is first generated on REPEC (v2.0) and then the complete documentation is submitted through the Mesa de Partes Virtual (MPV).
q_3_2_ampliada: The sponsor or CRO must have prior registration and credentials on REPEC v2.0. After starting the application on the platform and receiving registration approval notification, a form is generated that must be signed to formalize the procedure. Then, the entire documentary file, including the protocol, annexes, and translations, is submitted through the MPV in PDF format, editable where applicable. This platform channels the process's official notifications and replaces general email or physical communications. Documents whose original language is not Spanish must be submitted with a plain translation.
q_3_2_fuente: Decreto Supremo N° 021-2017-SA. Resolución Jefatural N.° 252-2022-J-OPE/INS.
q_3_3_directa: Yes. The regulation establishes that the INS has a maximum legal time frame of 30 business days to complete the review and approve a clinical trial application. This period also covers the time allotted to the national medicines authority to issue its technical opinion.
q_3_3_ampliada: The evaluation timeline, set out in the TUPA updated in 2025, requires the DIIS to issue an official decision within no more than 30 business days. Within that same time frame, the ANM assesses the investigational product's safety and quality to issue its binding technical ruling. In the initial phase, if omissions or formal errors are found in the file, the applicant has two business days to correct them. If there are substantial technical observations, the time frame is suspended until the sponsor submits the corresponding responses. Finally, if the DIIS denies authorization or misses the deadline, the sponsor may file an appeal within the following 15 business days.
q_3_3_fuente: Decreto Supremo N° 021-2017-SA, Article 69 and Article 70. Decreto Supremo No. 010-2025-SA; Resolución Jefatural N.° 252-2022-J-OPE/INS.
q_3_4_directa: Yes. The sponsor or the CRO must pay an administrative fee to begin the clinical trial's evaluation. Current amounts are set out in the INS's TUPA.
q_3_4_ampliada: Evaluating clinical trials and related procedures, such as protocol amendments, site expansions, or investigator changes, requires prior payment of fees to the State. Decreto Supremo N° 010-2025-SA updated these rates and set costs in soles for each regulatory procedure administered by the INS. For multicenter clinical trials, Resolución Ministerial N° 655-2019/MINSA, amending the Reglamento de Ensayos Clínicos, allows the sponsor to submit a single consolidated payment receipt for the processing fee, instead of requiring a separate payment for each participating site. Payments may be made in person or by electronic transfer to the official Banco de la Nación account. Proof of this transaction is a documentary requirement to be uploaded when submitting the file through the MPV.
q_3_4_fuente: Decreto Supremo N° 021-2017-SA; Decreto Supremo No. 010-2025-SA; Resolución Ministerial No. 655-2019/MINSA.
q_3_5_directa: Yes. Registering the study in REPEC (v2.0) is mandatory as an initial administrative step to process authorization. Once the health authority approves the trial, its status is updated on this publicly accessible platform.
q_3_5_ampliada: REPEC is the country's official database, managed by the DIIS. The sponsor must begin the application by uploading the protocol's main data, investigators, and sites into this system. Once the technical, ethical, and legal review is complete, the health authority issues its ruling and the clinical trial is made public on the portal. The published information follows the international transparency standards of WHO's Trial Registration Data Set. During the study's conduct, the public registry is updated with notifications and authorized amendments.
q_3_5_fuente: Decreto Supremo N° 021-2017-SA; Registro Peruano de Ensayos Clínicos (REPEC); Manual de Procedimientos de Ensayos Clínicos, items 7.4.5 and 7.4.6.
q_3_6_directa: Yes, mechanisms exist for partially recognizing quality and registration documentation for products from "High Sanitary Surveillance Countries," as well as inspection coordination with these foreign regulatory agencies.
q_3_6_ampliada: The Reglamento de Ensayos Clínicos establishes that an investigational product is eligible for authorization in Peru if it has prior approval for human use issued by High Sanitary Surveillance entities. Decreto Supremo N° 016-2011-SA classifies within this status the agencies of France, the Netherlands, the United Kingdom, the United States, Canada, Japan, Switzerland, Germany, Spain, Australia, Denmark, Italy, Norway, Belgium, and Sweden. This provision grants partial recognition to safety and quality evaluations and streamlines the import process for research that the Peruvian ANM processes. In terms of clinical oversight and inspection, the regulation establishes international cooperation channels. If a high-level foreign regulatory agency is going to audit a national clinical site, the sponsor must notify it so the INS can officially attend the proceeding.
q_3_6_fuente: Decreto Supremo N° 021-2017-SA, Annex 5, item 2, items a), b), and c); Decreto Supremo N° 021-2017-SA, Definitions, item 31; Decreto Supremo N° 021-2017-SA, Article 123. Decreto Supremo No. 016-2011-SA.
q_3_7_directa: The process unfolds in three stages: registering the entities, ethical and institutional evaluation, and government authorization. The cycle concludes with the INS issuing a Resolución Directoral and the trial's activation on the public portal.
q_3_7_ampliada: First, the sponsor, clinical institutions, and ethics committees must register on the REPEC platform (v2.0). Then, the principal investigator submits the study design to the accredited ethics committee to obtain its approval and that of the host institution. With these approvals, the sponsor processes the regulatory application by uploading the entire documentary file to the INS's MPV. During this period, the agency requests a binding technical ruling from the ANM to validate the product's manufacture and safety. Once the technical audit is complete and the time frame for correcting documentary errors has expired, the Directorate issues the final ruling authorizing recruitment to begin.
q_3_7_fuente: Decreto Supremo N° 021-2017-SA; Resolución Jefatural N.° 252-2022-J-OPE/INS, flowcharts and annexes (Annex 2, Annex 3, Table N° 04).
q_4_1_directa: Yes. Labeling of investigational products must be printed in indelible ink, in Spanish or English. It must include the product's essential information, the sponsor's details, and statements indicating exclusive use for clinical research.
q_4_1_ampliada: The Reglamento de Ensayos Clínicos requires labeling to contain the sponsor's name and address, the trial's number or code, the product's name, batch, expiry date, and route of administration. It must also include special storage instructions and the warning "For research use only" or "Sale prohibited." In double-blind trials, the immediate label may omit the batch number and manufacturer's name to avoid breaking the blind; in such cases, the main package must include a document allowing treatments to be identified in a medical emergency. Internal primary labels or containers must also detail the active ingredient's concentration and the pharmaceutical form.
q_4_1_fuente: Decreto Supremo N° 021-2017-SA, Annex 5 (Investigational Product Labeling).
q_4_2_directa: Yes. The sponsor or the CRO must submit a current Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) certificate for the investigational product's manufacturer as part of the initial authorization file. The ANM evaluates this certificate when issuing its binding technical opinion on the product's quality.
q_4_2_ampliada: Under the Reglamento de Ensayos Clínicos, the sponsor must include in the technical file a current GMP certificate issued by the competent health authority of the country of origin. The ANM evaluates this certificate as a quality guarantee before issuing its binding technical opinion. If manufacturing takes place locally, Peruvian laboratories must hold GMP certification issued by DIGEMID. During the study's conduct, if the sponsor needs to change the manufacturer or country of origin of authorized supplies, it must submit an application with an updated GMP certificate covering the new origin.
q_4_2_fuente: Decreto Supremo N° 021-2017-SA; Decreto Supremo No. 016-2011-SA. Documentos de modificación del Listado de Productos y Suministros (Annex 2); Ley General de Salud, Ley N° 26842, Article 56.
q_4_3_directa: No. The INS's clinical trial authorization ruling does not automatically authorize customs clearance. The sponsor must apply for a separate, exclusive import authorization from the ANM.
q_4_3_ampliada: Peru's regulatory framework establishes a staged process in which the INS's authorization is a prior requirement, but not an import permit. Once the INS's approving Resolución Directoral for the trial is obtained, the sponsor must submit an import application to the ANM (DIGEMID). This file must include a copy of the trial's ruling and the official list of supplies approved by the technical authority. After receiving the application, the ANM reviews the documentation and issues the import authorization for research purposes within three business days. Customs authorities require this ANM certificate to allow clearance and physical entry of the products into national territory.
q_4_3_fuente: Decreto Supremo N° 021-2017-SA; Decreto Supremo No. 016-2011-SA.
q_5_1_directa: Yes. The regulation sets reporting time frames: the investigator must notify the sponsor within a maximum of one day. Since 2025, the sponsor must report every new adverse event to the regulatory authority exclusively through the REPEC v2.0 digital platform, within a maximum of seven calendar days.
q_5_1_ampliada: The regulation requires the principal investigator to immediately document and report any Serious Adverse Event (SAE) or SUSAR to the sponsor and the accredited Ethics Committee. The sponsor must submit this report to the DIIS within the following seven calendar days. Since the August 2025 regulatory update, all new safety reports are submitted through the REPEC system (v2.0), and the former REAS-NET portal remains only as a historical, reference repository. For international events, the sponsor must submit periodic reports using CIOMS Form I. The sponsor and the site also have an additional eight-day time frame to issue and record a detailed follow-up report.
q_5_1_fuente: Decreto Supremo N° 021-2017-SA, Title III, Chapter II; DIIS communiqué on REPEC v2.0 (August 2025); Guía para el Reporte de Seguridad en Ensayos Clínicos (G-SafeRpt).
q_5_2_directa: Yes. The sponsor or the CRO has a regulatory obligation to generate an annual Development Safety Update Report (DSUR) for the investigational product. This comprehensive report must be sent to both the clinical trials agency (DIIS) and the medicines authority (ANM).
q_5_2_ampliada: Peruvian regulations require preparing an annual safety report (DSUR) counted from the trial's international first worldwide authorization date (DIBD). Its technical structure must follow the pharmacovigilance guidelines of the ICH E2A guideline. For submission, the sponsor completes an electronic form in Spanish and submits a translated summary to the DIIS. In parallel, it must send a complete electronic copy of the DSUR to the ANM.
q_5_2_fuente: Decreto Supremo N° 021-2017-SA. G-SafeRpt (Guía para el Usuario Externo de Reporte de Seguridad).
q_5_3_directa: Yes. The sponsor must submit clinical trial progress reports on a quarterly or semi-annual basis, counted from the authorization date. These reports are recorded in the electronic system for each authorized research site.
q_5_3_ampliada: The Reglamento de Ensayos Clínicos provides that progress reports must first be entered into the INS through REPEC (v2.0), within seven calendar days after the evaluated period closes. This obligation applies even if sites are not enrolling patients. Once uploaded to the system, the sponsor has 20 business days to print, sign, and submit the validated form through the document filing procedure. The report must break down the study's statistics, including the number of participants screened, enrolled, and withdrawn. It must also attach a summary of adverse events and the history of protocol deviations.
q_5_3_fuente: Decreto Supremo N° 021-2017-SA. Resolución Jefatural N.° 252-2022-J-OPE/INS.
q_5_4_directa: Yes. Substantial modifications classified as amendments require mandatory prior evaluation and authorization by the INS and the Ethics Committee. By contrast, "minor changes" require only ethical approval and a formal notification to the regulatory authority.
q_5_4_ampliada: Decreto Supremo N° 028-2023-SA amended the regulation to distinguish between amendments and minor changes to protocols. Amendments are substantial modifications affecting the study's safety, design, or statistics, and the sponsor must wait up to 30 business days for DIIS approval. Minor changes, defined as typographical corrections or operational adjustments as described by the authority, do not generate a new version of the main document. In such cases, only approval from the accredited CIEI is required. The sponsor must then notify the minor change in writing to the DIIS within 10 business days before its implementation.
q_5_4_fuente: Decreto Supremo N° 021-2017-SA; Decreto Supremo N° 028-2023-SA; Decreto Supremo No. 010-2025-SA.
q_5_5_directa: Yes. The sponsor has an explicit obligation to ensure research subjects' access to the investigational product after the study's completion, in accordance with the considerations set out in Title X of the Reglamento de Ensayos Clínicos.
q_5_5_ampliada:
Several conditions must be considered for this post-trial access to be required. These include: the severity of the subject's medical condition, whether discontinuing treatment could affect their health or well-being, the absence of satisfactory therapeutic alternatives for that condition in the country, and sufficient efficacy and safety information for the intervention's benefit-risk balance to be positive. In addition, the product must have proved beneficial for the subject, in the principal investigator's judgment, and its use will continue for as long as that benefit persists. If the condition falls under the management of a MINSA Dirección General, the sponsor must ensure access to the product until it becomes available through those directorates. This obligation must be specified in the informed consent.

Post-trial access may be authorized through two mechanisms:
Authorization of a clinical trial classified as an extension study, granted by the DIIS.
Authorization to use an investigational product, granted by the Autoridad Nacional de Productos Farmacéuticos, Dispositivos Médicos y Productos Sanitarios (ANM).
q_5_5_fuente: Decreto Supremo N° 021-2017-SA, Title X: Post-Trial Access; Article 40, item p); Article 115; Article 116.
q_6_1_directa: Yes. Trial participants' privacy is protected by the Ley de Protección de Datos Personales (Ley N° 29733) and its subsequent amendments. Decreto Supremo N° 016-2024-JUS regulates the procedures for protecting health data and its cross-border transfer.
q_6_1_ampliada: The legal framework classifies all volunteers' clinical, diagnostic, and biological information as sensitive personal data (DPS) in the health sector. Statistical processing requires the participant's express, documented, unequivocal consent, given through a handwritten or electronic signature. The 2024 regulation penalizes security failures and requires the sponsor to notify the National Personal Data Protection Authority within 48 hours of any breach or leak. In addition, transferring clinical trial databases to foreign entities is only authorized if the receiving country guarantees the same level of protection as Peru. If the sponsor plans to use this data for publications or secondary analyses, records must undergo anonymization or de-identification processes.
q_6_1_fuente: Ley N° 29733, Ley de Protección de Datos Personales; Decreto Supremo N° 016-2024-JUS; Directiva Administrativa No. 294-MINSA/2020/OGTI.
q_6_2_directa: Yes. Peru's regulatory framework has specific guidelines in Resolución Ministerial N° 686-2020/MINSA, which approves the "Norma Técnica de Salud para la investigación y desarrollo de vacunas contra enfermedades infecciosas" [Health Technical Standard for the Research and Development of Vaccines against Infectious Diseases].
q_6_2_ampliada: Vaccine clinical studies involving human participants are governed by Resolución Ministerial N° 686-2020-MINSA, which approves the Health Technical Standard for vaccine research and development against infectious diseases, complementing the Reglamento de Ensayos Clínicos. This standard adds specific ethical review criteria for this product category. In the ethical review of vaccine studies, CIEIs must meet the ethical criteria set out in Resolución Ministerial N° 233-2020-MINSA and base their approval or disapproval decision on CIOMS guidelines. These criteria include the research's social value and scientific validity, a favorable risk-benefit balance with risk minimization, equitable selection of participants, the informed consent process, and community engagement. Vaccine studies must be conducted in accordance with the ICH E6(R2) Good Clinical Practice Guideline and current national clinical trial regulations (Decreto Supremo N° 021-2017-SA).
q_6_2_fuente: Resolución Ministerial N° 686-2020-MINSA, approving NTS N° 165-MINSA/2020/INS; Decreto Supremo N° 021-2017-SA.
q_6_3_directa: Yes. The collection, preparation, or use of biological materials is included within the scope of the ethical framework. In addition, the cross-border flow of data derived from these samples is regulated by the Ley de Protección de Datos Personales, which permits it under specific conditions.
q_6_3_ampliada: Health research includes the collection, preparation, or use of biological materials. If the clinical trial contemplates collecting and storing biological samples for future use, this must be made explicit in an additional informed consent form. As for the derived data, which is sensitive data, cross-border transfer is permitted when necessary for epidemiological or similar studies, provided appropriate de-identification procedures are applied. It is also permitted if the data subject has given prior, informed, express, and unequivocal consent. However, current regulations do not detail specific NRA (INS) forms or procedures for the physical import and export of biological samples (biorepositories, transfer agreements, etc.).
q_6_3_fuente: Resolución Ministerial N° 233-2020-MINSA, item 7.1; Decreto Supremo N° 016-2024-JUS; Ley N° 29733, Article 15, item 6; Decreto Supremo N° 021-2017-SA, Article 34.
q_6_4_directa: Yes. Peruvian legislation devotes specific chapters to regulating trials in vulnerable populations and particular situations. It establishes enhanced requirements for research involving pediatric populations, pregnant women and the fetus, subordinate or indigenous groups, and for pharmaceutical equivalence studies.
q_6_4_ampliada:
Vulnerable populations: The Reglamento de Ensayos Clínicos regulates trials in persons with disabilities who cannot give consent; it requires the CIEI to include experts and consent to be given by the legal representative, under Chapter II. It also sets requirements for minors, who must give assent from age 8. Subordinate groups (students, healthcare workers, military personnel) are expressly defined and require special protection, since their participation may be influenced by hierarchical structures.

Special products: The Regulation applies on a transitional basis to trials with herbal medicines, dietary products and sweeteners, galenic products, and medical devices, until specific supreme decrees are issued.

Bioequivalence studies: When bioequivalence studies are required for sanitary registration in Peru, the ANM must issue a binding opinion on the research protocol.
q_6_4_fuente: Decreto Supremo N° 021-2017-SA, Article 2, item 21, Article 19, Article 20, Article 36; Fourth Final Supplementary Provision; Article 69. Resolución Ministerial N° 233-2020-MINSA.

q_1_1_directa: The main authority responsible for the ethical-scientific evaluation, approval, and monitoring of research protocols involving human subjects is the Consejo Nacional de Bioética en Salud (National Council of Bioethics in Health, CONABIOS).
q_1_1_ampliada: CONABIOS is a permanent body of the Ministerio de Salud Pública y Asistencia Social (MSP) whose fundamental mandate is to ensure compliance with national and international bioethical principles and standards in all biomedical research involving human subjects in the country. In addition, the Dirección General de Medicamentos, Alimentos y Productos Sanitarios (General Directorate of Medicines, Food and Health Products, DIGEMAPS), as successor to the Dirección General de Drogas y Farmacias, holds regulatory authority over investigational products, including authorizing their import [Decreto No. 246-06, Art. 116].
q_1_1_fuente: Manual de Normas y Procedimientos Operativos del Consejo Nacional de Bioética en Salud (CONABIOS) (Chapter 1); Decreto No. 246-06 (Reglamento para el Control Sanitario de los Medicamentos y Productos Afines), Article 116.
q_1_2_directa: Health research is governed by the Ley General de Salud No. 42-01, which requires research to adhere to nationally and internationally approved scientific and bioethical principles, and by CONABIOS's Manual de Normas y Procedimientos Operativos.
q_1_2_ampliada: Ley General de Salud No. 42-01 establishes the legal framework for health in the Dominican Republic and mandates that regulations be developed for implementing research activities. CONABIOS's Manual complements this, specifically regulating and standardizing the processes for evaluating, approving, and following up on health research protocols.
q_1_2_fuente: Ley General de Salud No. 42-01, Article 32, Paragraph II; Manual de Normas y Procedimientos Operativos del Consejo Nacional de Bioética en Salud (CONABIOS) (Chapter 4).
q_1_3_directa: The main regulations are CONABIOS's Manual de Normas y Procedimientos Operativos, Decreto No. 246-06 (Reglamento para el Control Sanitario de los Medicamentos y Productos Afines), and Decreto 351-25.
q_1_3_ampliada: Clinical trial authorization involves a dual review: CONABIOS focuses on the research protocol's ethical and methodological evaluation, while the provisions of Decreto No. 246-06 and Ley General de Salud No. 42-01 govern aspects related to medicines' sanitary registration and authorization to import products in the clinical research phase. Decreto 351-25 further reaffirms CONABIOS's role in the ongoing monitoring of biomedical research.
q_1_3_fuente: Manual de Normas y Procedimientos Operativos del Consejo Nacional de Bioética en Salud (CONABIOS) (Chapter 3); Decreto No. 246-06 (Reglamento para el Control Sanitario de los Medicamentos y Productos Afines), Article 116; Decreto No. 351-25, Articles 1 and 4.
q_1_4_directa: Yes, approval from the Research Ethics/Bioethics Committee (CEI/CBI) of the institution where the research will be conducted, or from a recognized independent one, is a mandatory requirement for the protocol file to be considered complete when submitted to CONABIOS.
q_1_4_ampliada: A protocol's evaluation by the institutional CEI/CBI is an initial bioethical evaluation that is indispensable for CONABIOS's final evaluation. The CEI is an independent body whose main function is to ensure the protection of participants' rights, safety, and well-being.
q_1_4_fuente: Decreto No. 351-25, Article 10, Paragraph III; Manual de Normas y Procedimientos Operativos del Consejo Nacional de Bioética en Salud (CONABIOS) (Chapter 3, Section 3.1).
q_1_5_directa: Yes, the CEI's approval must be obtained beforehand and must be submitted as part of the file presented to CONABIOS for its final evaluation.
q_1_5_ampliada: The research file will not be considered complete, and will therefore not be formally accepted by CONABIOS, if it does not include the approval of the corresponding CEI/CBI. The CEI's function is to carry out an initial bioethical evaluation that serves as the basis for CONABIOS's evaluation and ruling process.
q_1_5_fuente: Manual de Normas y Procedimientos Operativos del Consejo Nacional de Bioética en Salud (CONABIOS) (Chapter 3, Section 3.1, and Chapter 4, Section 4.1).
q_1_6_directa: Yes, the regulation includes an accreditation and registration system for Research Ethics Committees (CEIs), managed exclusively by CONABIOS. This body has the duty to regulate, register, and certify public and private institutions' research committees so they can legitimately operate in the country.
q_1_6_ampliada: Every Research Ethics Committee operating within national territory must submit to CONABIOS a series of documents for registration, including its founding charter, internal bylaws, standard operating procedures, and members' curricula vitae. It is also strictly required that at least two of its members have proven training in ethics or bioethics and in research methodology. After documentary evaluation and a verification visit by CONABIOS staff, an identification code is assigned, certifying the committee to operate under national endorsement. The recent Decreto 351-25 reaffirms this requirement, stipulating that accreditation by this council is an indispensable requirement for committees to carry out the initial bioethical evaluation of any clinical study.
q_1_6_fuente: Manual de Normas y Procedimientos Operativos del Consejo Nacional de Bioética en Salud (CONABIOS) (Chapter 8).
q_1_7_directa: Current regulations require CONABIOS to maintain an official registry and assign an identification code to all duly accredited Research Ethics Committees. However, current operational legal frameworks do not specify that this online committee registry is unrestrictedly publicly accessible.
q_1_7_ampliada: CONABIOS bears the unavoidable obligation to regulate, register, and provide ongoing support to research committees, certifying them through formal registration. Although the institution maintains up-to-date databases on biomedical research and protocol status that are publicly available through its portal, the Manual de Normas y Procedimientos Operativos does not explicitly mandate publishing an open directory of ethics committees.
q_1_7_fuente: Manual de Normas y Procedimientos Operativos del Consejo Nacional de Bioética en Salud (CONABIOS) (Chapter 8).
q_1_8_directa: Yes. Prior CONABIOS authorization is required for: projects involving human subjects or human material where some type of intervention takes place; observational projects without direct intervention that handle participants' confidential information; and projects that modify medical care processes or institutional health services policy.
q_1_8_ampliada: CONABIOS's function is to evaluate, approve, and provisionally or permanently suspend any research protocol involving human participation in the Dominican Republic. Even for non-interventional research, obtaining a No-Objection Communication from CONABIOS is recommended, though not mandatory, as it provides the scientific regulatory standing needed for publications.
