q_1_8_fuente: Manual de Normas y Procedimientos Operativos del Consejo Nacional de Bioética en Salud (CONABIOS) (Chapter 4, Section 4.2).
q_2_1_directa: The regulation does not provide an explicit, formal definition of the term "sponsor" or "sponsor/funder," though it mentions it as the national or international entity that must submit an original letter addressed to CONABIOS.
q_2_1_ampliada: The sponsor or funder is responsible for the study's financial guarantee, including providing insurance or indemnity for treating subjects in the event of injury or death attributable to the clinical trial. Any attempt by sponsors to personally influence a submitted protocol must also be reported by CONABIOS members.
q_2_1_fuente: Manual de Normas y Procedimientos Operativos del Consejo Nacional de Bioética en Salud (CONABIOS) (Chapter 4, Section 4.1, on submission requirements).
q_2_2_directa: The bioethics regulation governing protocol submission to CONABIOS does not explicitly require a foreign sponsor to appoint a legal representative or establish a legal entity in the Dominican Republic. However, for importing the investigational product, having a locally licensed importing entity is a practical and regulatory requirement.
q_2_2_ampliada: The regulatory analysis is split into two areas. For the ethical and scientific evaluation before CONABIOS, the international sponsor can act directly. However, for the logistical phase, the "Procedimiento para la Importación para Ensayos Clínicos" (IEC-PD-01) managed by DIGEMAPS requires the import permit application to be made by a local importer. This importer must hold an establishment operating license issued by the Ministerio de Salud Pública. In practice, this role is taken on by a local sponsor affiliate, a CRO with import capacity, or a contracted pharmaceutical distributor. The absence of a local entity would therefore prevent importing the investigational product, effectively halting the trial.
q_2_2_fuente: Manual de Normas y Procedimientos Operativos del Consejo Nacional de Bioética en Salud (CONABIOS); Procedimiento de Importación para Ensayos Clínicos (IEC-PD-01).
q_2_3_directa: Yes. The sponsor/funder, whether national or international, must issue an original letter addressed to CONABIOS as part of the mandatory documentation for submitting the protocol.
q_2_3_ampliada: As part of its role, the sponsor must ensure the file includes a civil liability and/or health/research insurance policy for participants, and must guarantee provision for treatment and compensation in the event of injury or death attributable to the clinical trial. It must also submit the detailed budget contracted for the research.
q_2_3_fuente: Manual de Normas y Procedimientos Operativos del Consejo Nacional de Bioética en Salud (CONABIOS) (Chapter 4, Section 4.1).
q_2_4_directa: Dominican regulations do not have a specific rule defining or setting exclusive registration requirements for Contract Research Organizations (CROs). However, their role is formally recognized in the protocol submission process.
q_2_4_ampliada: Although no specific regulation exists for CROs, the official protocol submission form before CONABIOS includes a field to identify the CRO involved in the study. This constitutes formal recognition of its involvement. Acting on the sponsor's behalf, the CRO implicitly assumes responsibility for ensuring all activities under its management comply with the obligations set out in CONABIOS's Manual de Normas y Procedimientos Operativos, Good Clinical Practice, and other applicable legislation. Any non-compliance by the CRO will be treated as non-compliance by the sponsor.
q_2_4_fuente: Manual de Normas y Procedimientos Operativos del Consejo Nacional de Bioética en Salud (CONABIOS), Formulario para Someter Proyectos de Investigación al CONABIOS.
q_2_5_directa: Yes. Clinical research sites must undergo an evaluation of their infrastructure and technical capacity as part of the protocol approval process before the competent authority. In addition, every health facility or laboratory where a clinical study is conducted must hold a current sanitary operating license.
q_2_5_ampliada: During a protocol's internal evaluation process, CONABIOS formally assesses the executing site's capacity, examining the available infrastructure to ensure optimal, safe conditions exist for conducting the research. Beyond technical infrastructure, sites must hold the operating license issued by the Ministerio de Salud Pública y Asistencia Social (MISPAS), certifying they meet structural and biosafety requirements. Submitting a copy of this health facility's or laboratory's operating license is an indispensable requirement in parallel procedures, such as importing investigational products through DIGEMAPS's IEC-PD-01 procedure. In this way, site fitness is controlled through two channels: the bioethical-technical and the administrative.
q_2_5_fuente: Manual de Normas y Procedimientos Operativos del Consejo Nacional de Bioética en Salud (CONABIOS) (Chapter 4, Section 4.1, and Chapter 7).
q_2_6_directa: Yes. Selecting investigators requires documented proof of their experience, research capacity, and technical competencies. All must submit current Good Clinical Practice (GCP) training certificates as a mandatory requirement.
q_2_6_ampliada: CONABIOS requires the submission of each investigator's detailed curriculum vitae as part of the essential documentation for starting the file's evaluation. The authority rigorously assesses the research team's capacity, considering prior experience and ensuring their clinical duties and commitments to other current research protocols do not interfere. The principal investigator bears the non-delegable duty of conducting the research exactly as designed in the protocol, and must therefore demonstrate the skills needed to protect participants' integrity. All this personnel is subject to ongoing oversight by the regulatory body to ensure strict ethical and scientific compliance.
q_2_6_fuente: Manual de Normas y Procedimientos Operativos del Consejo Nacional de Bioética en Salud (CONABIOS) (Chapters 4, 6, and 7).
q_2_7_directa: Yes. Submitting an insurance policy (civil liability and/or health/research) is mandatory, along with proof of the provision for compensating and treating subjects in the event of injury or death attributable to the clinical trial.
q_2_7_ampliada: Compensation for participants (for transportation, meals, or other expenses) must be submitted for CONABIOS's review and approval. This compensation must not be an excessively high amount, as it could compromise participants' voluntary participation. For interventional research, compensation for time invested is mandatory.
q_2_7_fuente: Manual de Normas y Procedimientos Operativos del Consejo Nacional de Bioética en Salud (CONABIOS) (Chapter 4, Section 4.1, and Chapter 7, Section 7.2).
q_3_1_directa: Yes. Essential documents include: the printed research protocol (original and a faithful Spanish translation, if applicable), a CONABIOS cover letter, the CONABIOS submission form, an original letter from the sponsoring/funding institution, a letter from the executing institution, the CEI's approval, the Informed Consent Form, investigators' curricula vitae with current GCP certificates, an insurance policy, and a detailed budget, plus an identical digital version.
q_3_1_ampliada: A file must be complete to be accepted, including the No-Objection Letter from the Servicio Nacional de Salud (National Health Service, SNS) if the executing site belongs to that service. The printed protocol must be properly bound, and an original copy must be submitted.
q_3_1_fuente: Manual de Normas y Procedimientos Operativos del Consejo Nacional de Bioética en Salud (CONABIOS) (Chapter 4, Section 4.1).
q_3_2_directa: Yes. Protocols must be submitted for evaluation in person at the Council's offices. A physical printed version (properly bound, in original) and an identical digital version (CD or USB) are required.
q_3_2_ampliada: Once the complete file is received, a registration number is assigned, which becomes its permanent identification. Documents that must be stamped after approval must be submitted in a separate folder, in addition to those already bound.
q_3_2_fuente: Manual de Normas y Procedimientos Operativos del Consejo Nacional de Bioética en Salud (CONABIOS) (Chapter 3, Section 3.1).
q_3_3_directa: Yes. The Council must notify the responsible investigator of the evaluation's final outcome within no more than 45 business days of the application.
q_3_3_ampliada: For protocols considered urgent, the time frame is reduced to 21 calendar days from the application date. Internally, the protocol is sent to an expert consulting advisor, who has a maximum of 2 weeks (or 7 days for urgent protocols) to issue an evaluation report before it is discussed at a session by the Council's members.
q_3_3_fuente: Manual de Normas y Procedimientos Operativos del Consejo Nacional de Bioética en Salud (CONABIOS) (Chapter 4).
q_3_4_directa: Yes, legally established fees exist for the sanitary registration application (Ley General de Salud No. 42-01, Para. VIII, Art. 115).
q_3_4_ampliada: The Ley General de Salud states that the cost of evaluations by reference laboratories (in cases where SESPAS cannot meet regulatory time frames) must be covered by the applicant, without this offsetting the fees already established for sanitary registration. However, the specific amount of fees or charges for CONABIOS's evaluation of clinical trial protocols is not detailed in the official regulations available.
q_3_4_fuente: Ley General de Salud No. 42-01, Article 115, Paragraph VIII.
q_3_5_directa: Dominican regulations do not require registering a clinical trial in a national or international public registry before it begins. However, CONABIOS publishes the status of all submitted protocols on its official website.
q_3_5_ampliada: While there is no legal mandate for pre-registering clinical trials — an international standard practice promoted by WHO and the Declaration of Helsinki — CONABIOS ensures transparency by publishing a database on its web portal. This section, called "Estatus del Protocolo" [Protocol Status], functions as a post-submission public registry, where the registration number, study title, sponsor, executing institution, and the Council's ruling can be consulted. This allows public tracking of the regulatory status of research conducted in the country, although it does not fulfill the function of a WHO primary registry, which seeks to prevent publication bias and study duplication.
q_3_5_fuente: Sitio web oficial del Consejo Nacional de Bioética en Salud (CONABIOS) ("Estatus del Protocolo" section).
q_3_6_directa: Yes. CONABIOS can facilitate registering Research Bioethics Committees (CBIs) under its oversight in the FWA (Federal Wide Assurance), recognizing them as certified to operate under the endorsement of the United States' Office for Human Research Protections.
q_3_6_ampliada: Beyond recognizing international ethical accreditations, DIGEMAPS's technical regulation for biotechnology medicines is based on current published international guidelines from the FDA, EMA, ICH, and/or WHO for submitting registration dossiers. CONABIOS also evaluates requests to modify protocols, especially common in multicenter and multinational studies, recognizing the variation in regulations and logistics between countries.
q_3_6_fuente: Manual de Normas y Procedimientos Operativos del Consejo Nacional de Bioética en Salud (CONABIOS) (Chapter 8); Resolución No. 000018-16 (Reglamento Técnico para Registro Sanitario de Medicamentos Biotecnológicos), Articles 6.1 and 8.1.1.
q_3_7_directa: The process is sequential, beginning with local ethical approval, followed by central bioethical evaluation, and concluding with the product's import authorization, if applicable.
q_3_7_ampliada:
Institutional ethical approval: The protocol must be evaluated and approved by the executing institution's CEI/CBI, or a recognized independent one. This evaluation is indispensable for submission to CONABIOS.

Document preparation and collection: The principal investigator (with support from the sponsor/institution) must prepare and gather all mandatory documents, including the printed protocol (original and translation, if applicable), letters from the sponsor and the executing site, informed consent, curricula vitae with current GCP certificates, the insurance policy, and the budget.

In-person submission: The complete file must be submitted in person at CONABIOS's offices.

Registration with CONABIOS: The file is registered and assigned a permanent identification number.

Evaluation by a consulting expert: The protocol is sent to an expert consulting advisor (maximum 2 weeks; 7 days for urgent cases) for methodological and bioethical review, who issues a report for the Council.

Council session and decision: Council members review, analyze, and deliberate on the protocol and the expert's comments, deciding the final outcome (approved, subject to revisions, or rejected).

Official notification: The Council notifies the responsible investigator of the final outcome (45 business days for standard review; 21 calendar days for urgent review).

Import application (if applicable): If the study involves unregistered products, the importer must request express authorization from DIGEMAPS, submitting a copy of the current trial approval permit issued by CONABIOS, and obtain the "Reconocimiento Sanitario para los Fines Aduanales" [Sanitary Recognition for Customs Purposes].

Port/Airport inspection: The DIGEMAPS/Customs inspector carries out documentary validation and a physical check of the imported goods.

Study initiation: The principal investigator must notify CONABIOS in writing of the start of participant enrollment.
q_3_7_fuente: Manual de Normas y Procedimientos Operativos del Consejo Nacional de Bioética en Salud (CONABIOS) (Chapters 3 and 4); Decreto No. 246-06 (Reglamento para el Control Sanitario de los Medicamentos y Productos Afines), Article 116; Procedimiento de Importación para Ensayos Clínicos (IEC-PD-01).
q_4_1_directa: Yes. Labeling, package inserts, and packaging materials must contain information in Spanish, and must specify: the brand and International Nonproprietary Name (INN), the qualitative-quantitative formula, the manufacturing batch number, the expiry date, and the sanitary registration number.
q_4_1_ampliada: The package insert must include detailed information for consumers on identification, indications, dosage, contraindications, adverse effects, interactions, and precautions, in addition to instructions for use and storage. For imported products, a Spanish counter-label with all the aforementioned information must be included.
q_4_1_fuente: Ley General de Salud No. 42-01, Article 112; Decreto No. 246-06 (Reglamento para el Control Sanitario de los Medicamentos y Productos Afines), Articles 42, 43, 97, and 98.
q_4_2_directa: Yes, studies and data submitted for medicine registration must be conducted and obtained in accordance with established Good Manufacturing Practice, Good Laboratory Practice, and Good Clinical Practice.
q_4_2_ampliada: For medicines manufactured abroad, a duly legalized Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) Certificate from the manufacturing laboratory, issued by the health authority in the country of origin, is required. DIGEMAPS formally uses a GMP Inspection Guide based on WHO Technical Reports 32 and 37 for pharmaceutical preparations.
q_4_2_fuente: Decreto No. 246-06 (Reglamento para el Control Sanitario de los Medicamentos y Productos Afines), Articles 21, 31, and 86; Resolución No. 000005-2021 (Aprueba Guía de Inspección de BPM).
q_4_3_directa: No. CONABIOS's trial approval does not automatically include authorization to import or use the Investigational Product (IP); this requires a separate procedure before the DDF/DIGEMAPS.
q_4_3_ampliada: Importing unregistered products in the clinical research phase must be expressly authorized by the DDF, culminating in the issuance of the "Reconocimiento Sanitario para los Fines Aduanales" [Sanitary Recognition for Customs Purposes] certificate. Among the documents required for import is a copy of CONABIOS's current trial approval permit, confirming the need for prior ethical/scientific approval.
q_4_3_fuente: Decreto No. 246-06 (Reglamento para el Control Sanitario de los Medicamentos y Productos Afines), Articles 116 and 132; Procedimiento de Importación para Ensayos Clínicos (IEC-PD-01).
q_5_1_directa: Yes. The principal investigator must report Serious Adverse Events (SAEs) and Major/Critical Protocol Deviations to CONABIOS within a maximum of 24 hours of detection. Serious Unexpected Adverse Reactions (SUSARs) must be reported monthly.
q_5_1_ampliada: The main safety reporting obligation during a clinical trial's conduct is defined by CONABIOS's Manual de Normas y Procedimientos Operativos. It requires expedited notification (24 hours) for serious events that could affect participants' safety, enabling continuous ethical oversight. Monthly reports of SUSARs and Non-Serious Adverse Events (AEs) must also be submitted. These requirements are specific to the trial context. In parallel, the National Pharmacovigilance System, governed by the "Reglamento Técnico para la Farmacovigilancia," establishes a general duty for all healthcare professionals to report suspected serious adverse reactions within 48 hours, but within a trial's framework, CONABIOS's regulation takes precedence due to its specificity.
q_5_1_fuente: Manual de Normas y Procedimientos Operativos del Consejo Nacional de Bioética en Salud (CONABIOS) (Chapter 6); Reglamento Técnico para la Farmacovigilancia en el Sistema Nacional de Salud (Section 5.3).
q_5_2_directa: Yes. Holders of medicines' sanitary registration (including biologics/vaccines) are required to submit Periodic Safety Reports (IPS) to DIGEMAPS.
q_5_2_ampliada: IPS submission time frames are: every six (6) months during the first two years from the registration's authorization date, and annually from the third to the fifth year. From the fifth year on, it is submitted every five years, coinciding with the registration's renewal. The IPS's executive summary must be submitted in Spanish.
q_5_2_fuente: Reglamento Técnico para la Farmacovigilancia en el Sistema Nacional de Salud (Section 5.5).
q_5_3_directa: Yes. CONABIOS carries out continuous follow-up of research, and the investigator must allow monitoring visits, and must report the study's completion and issue the final report or results to CONABIOS.
q_5_3_ampliada: CONABIOS's Monitoring Department must conduct a first visit during recruitment to ensure the Informed Consent process is followed, and further visits during the follow-up phase. The official monitoring report is presented at the Council's next session to decide on the study's continued conduct.
q_5_3_fuente: Manual de Normas y Procedimientos Operativos del Consejo Nacional de Bioética en Salud (CONABIOS) (Chapter 5).
q_5_4_directa: Yes. Any formal protocol change, defined as an Amendment, requires prior approval, specifically including obtaining CONABIOS's approval for any advertisement, poster, video, or any new retention strategy before it is used in the research.
q_5_4_ampliada: Since the investigator has a duty to conduct the research exactly as designed in the submitted Protocol and to use only the Informed Consent stamped and authorized by CONABIOS, any relevant modification to the protocol or to materials directed at participants (recruitment or retention) must be approved in advance by the Council.
q_5_4_fuente: Manual de Normas y Procedimientos Operativos del Consejo Nacional de Bioética en Salud (CONABIOS) (Chapter 6).
q_5_5_directa: No. The explicit obligation focuses on participants' right to receive information about the forms of medical treatment available to them after the study ends, if any, in the event complications arise.
q_5_5_ampliada: This requirement ensures subjects know their options if their health is affected by the study once the research period has ended. The regulation does not establish a general requirement for continued supply of the study medicine to all participants post-trial.
q_5_5_fuente: Manual de Normas y Procedimientos Operativos del Consejo Nacional de Bioética en Salud (CONABIOS).
q_6_1_directa: Yes. Ley General de Salud No. 42-01 establishes the confidentiality of participants' information, and Ley núm. 107-13, on the Rights of Persons in Their Relations with the Administration and Administrative Procedure, is also relevant, applying to CONABIOS's suspension powers. Ley No. 172-13, on the Protection of Personal Data, is also applicable, guaranteeing the comprehensive protection of personal data recorded in public and private files, records, or databases, and recognizing every person's right to privacy, honor, and control over the use of their information.
q_6_1_ampliada: Clinical trial participants have the right to confidentiality and security regarding the handling of their personal data and medical records. Confidentiality may only be waived with the patient's authorization, for the collective interest, by court order, or under a special law. Ley No. 172-13 reinforces this principle by establishing that processing personal data, including health-related data, requires the data subject's free, express, informed consent, and that the data controller must adopt technical and organizational measures to guarantee its security and confidentiality. Informed Consent must guarantee confidentiality and indicate how the information will be handled and stored.
q_6_1_fuente: Manual de Normas y Procedimientos Operativos del Consejo Nacional de Bioética en Salud (CONABIOS) (Chapter 7, Section 7.1). Ley No. 172-13.
q_6_2_directa: Yes, the DDF/DIGEMAPS regulates the manufacture, marketing, import, and promotion of biological medicines or vaccines. Specifically, in vaccine research involving minors, the vaccination card from the Dirección de Inmunoprevenibles por Vacunas (DIV) must be submitted.
q_6_2_ampliada: In the event of conflict between mandatory vaccines and the investigational one, the mandatory vaccine will always prevail. The national authority (DDF/DIGEMAPS) must release each vaccine batch entering the country by evaluating documents such as the batch release certificate from the producing country and the summary production and quality control protocol.
q_6_2_fuente: Ley General de Salud No. 42-01, Article 28, item g); Manual de Normas y Procedimientos Operativos del Consejo Nacional de Bioética en Salud (CONABIOS) (Chapter 7, Section 7.1).
q_6_3_directa: Yes, biological samples of human origin intended for research must be securely stored (in a biobank or collection) and require specific written informed consent from the source subject clearly explaining the purpose of such storage.
q_6_3_ampliada: Consent for sample collection and future use may be an additional section or a separate consent, and may be withdrawn at any time. Consent cannot force participation if storage is essential to the study and the participant expresses reservations.
q_6_3_fuente: Manual de Normas y Procedimientos Operativos del Consejo Nacional de Bioética en Salud (CONABIOS) (Chapter 10).
q_6_4_directa: Yes, differentiated regulations exist for urgent protocols, research involving minors, and the registration of innovative and non-innovative biotechnology medicines.
q_6_4_ampliada: For urgent protocols, review and notification time frames are significantly shorter (7 days for the advisor, 21 calendar days for the Council's decision). For minors, parental or guardian consent is complemented by the minor's assent, which must be respected at all times, allowing the minor to stop the procedure if they decide to. For biotechnology products, the regulation requires compliance with international guidelines (ICH, FDA, EMA, WHO) on comparability, efficacy, safety, and immunogenicity studies.
q_6_4_fuente: Manual de Normas y Procedimientos Operativos del Consejo Nacional de Bioética en Salud (CONABIOS) (Chapter 3, Section 3.4, and Chapter 9, Section 9.3.2); Resolución No. 000018-16 (Reglamento Técnico para Registro Sanitario de Medicamentos Biotecnológicos).

q_1_1_directa: The National Regulatory Authority (NRA) for clinical trials is the Ministerio de Salud Pública (Ministry of Public Health, MSP), through its División Evaluación Sanitaria (Health Evaluation Division, DES), the body responsible for their evaluation.
q_1_1_ampliada: The MSP carries out the registration of all research projects involving human subjects. Although initial registration is managed through the Comisión Nacional de Ética de Investigación (National Research Ethics Commission, CNEI), the application for authorization to conduct the research, if it is a Clinical Trial, is evaluated by the DES. By default, the procedure goes to the DES, and if it does not fall within its evaluation scope, it is sent to the CNEI.
q_1_1_fuente: Instructivo de Registro de Proyectos de Investigación.
q_1_2_directa: The main regulation is Decreto N° 158/019, which approves the regulation drawn up by the CNEI on research involving human subjects.
q_1_2_ampliada: Decreto N° 158/019 is the regulation in force, replacing Decreto N° 379/008 of August 4, 2008. This regulation establishes comprehensive protection for human research subjects, requires respect for fundamental ethical principles (autonomy, beneficence, non-maleficence, and justice), and ensures compliance with the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, the Declaration of Helsinki (2000 version), and Ley N° 18.331.
q_1_2_fuente: Decreto N° 158/019 - Investigación en seres humanos; Instructivo de Registro de Proyectos de Investigación; Registro / Autorización de proyectos de investigación en seres humanos.
q_1_3_directa: Clinical trial authorization is governed primarily by Decreto N° 158/019 and the Good Clinical Practice (GCP) standards set out in Resolución MERCOSUR N° 129/96, internalized as Decreto N° 189/998.
q_1_3_ampliada: Decreto N° 158/019 defines a Clinical Trial as a prospective, biomedical or behavioral study designed to answer specific questions about interventions. Investigators must expressly commit to respecting the Declaration of Helsinki (2000 version) and the MERCOSUR N° 129/96 Good Clinical Practice standard. A Clinical Trial requires specific evaluation by the DES.
q_1_3_fuente: Decreto N° 158/019 - Investigación en seres humanos; Decreto N° 189/998 - Buenas Prácticas Clínicas; Formulario FO-13220 - Solicitud de Evaluación de Protocolo de Ensayo Clínico; Instructivo de Registro de Proyectos de Investigación; Resolución MERCOSUR N° 129/96 - Buenas Prácticas de Investigación Clínica.
q_1_4_directa: Yes, obtaining prior approval from the corresponding accredited Institutional Research Ethics Committee (CEII) is mandatory before any research may begin.
q_1_4_ampliada: All institutions, whether public or private, along with sponsors and investigators, must ensure the research complies with the regulation. The CEII's approval must be accompanied by the corresponding research protocol. Research Ethics Committees are interdisciplinary, independent bodies created to defend research subjects' interests, integrity, and dignity.
q_1_4_fuente: Decreto N° 158/019 - Investigación en seres humanos, Article 3.
q_1_5_directa: Yes, approval from the corresponding CEIIs must be obtained before applying for MSP authorization (DES and/or CNEI).
q_1_5_ampliada: The formal authorization application before the MSP (Step 3 of the registration/authorization process) requires, among the mandatory documentation, proof of approval from the accredited CEII(s). In addition, the research protocol and the informed consent form must be submitted in the version already approved by the CEII.
q_1_5_fuente: Instructivo de Registro de Proyectos de Investigación.
q_1_6_directa: Yes, a formal accreditation system exists for CEIIs. This process is managed by the CNEI, and final approval is issued by the Ministry of Public Health. Accreditation is mandatory for committees to evaluate and rule on research protocols.
q_1_6_ampliada: The accreditation process requires every institution conducting research involving human subjects to establish a CEII and apply for its formal accreditation within a stipulated time frame from its creation. To obtain accreditation, the committee must meet specific requirements for multidisciplinary composition, adequate infrastructure, and strict disclosure of conflicts of interest by its members. The CNEI evaluates the technical application and forwards it to the Dirección General de la Salud (General Directorate of Health, DIGESA) for final approval. Once granted, accreditation is valid for three years, after which it must be mandatorily renewed. Committees must also report their activities annually and notify any changes to their composition to maintain this regulatory status before the authorities.
q_1_6_fuente: Decreto N° 158/019 - Investigación en seres humanos, Articles 3 and 49; Ordenanza N° 827/016 Reglamentación sobre Comités de Éticas de Investigación, Annex I and Annex II.
q_1_7_directa: Uruguayan law establishes that Research Ethics Committees must be duly registered with the Ministry of Public Health once accredited. However, current regulations do not expressly specify that this registry must be unrestrictedly, openly accessible to the public. The health authority maintains and manages this registry centrally for controlling and overseeing the scientific ecosystem.
q_1_7_ampliada: National regulations provide that every CEII must apply for accreditation before the CNEI to obtain subsequent official registration. This registry is kept and directly overseen by the Ministry of Public Health, which exercises its governing role over authorized entities. Although investigators and sponsors interact with the health authority to find out which committees hold accreditation, the current Decree contains no explicit mandate requiring an open database to be published on the Ministry's website. In practice, inquiries about a committee's validity and status are channeled through the body's own institutional mechanisms or the CNEI.
q_1_7_fuente: Decreto 158/019 - Información Institucional MSP, Article 49; Ordenanza N° 827/016 Reglamentación sobre Comités de Éticas de Investigación, Article 13.
q_1_8_directa: Yes. Prior MSP authorization, through the DES or the CNEI, is mandatory for Clinical Trials involving new medicines, new indications, vaccines, diagnostic tests, equipment, devices, and invasive procedures, as well as for multicenter studies requiring a single ruling, research involving vulnerable populations, and projects involving biosafety aspects.
q_1_8_ampliada: It is vital to note that, for multicenter studies seeking a single ruling, the competent evaluating authority within the MSP is the CNEI, not the DES, which is the default evaluator for single-site clinical trials. This difference in the review pathway must be carefully considered when planning the regulatory submission strategy, as it involves interacting with a committee of a different composition and focus.
q_1_8_fuente: Decreto N° 158/019 - Investigación en seres humanos, Article 43, item b), items 1) and 4); Annex, Chapter I, item 2), item g); Instructivo de Registro de Proyectos de Investigación, Page 2, Step 3.2.
q_2_1_directa: Yes. It is defined as the individual, company, institution, or organization responsible for the initiation, management, and/or financing of a study.
q_2_1_ampliada: The definition's flexibility, which includes "initiation, management, and/or financing," is relevant for internal agreements between the parties. However, for regulatory purposes before the MSP, the entity formally submitting the clinical trial authorization application is considered ultimately responsible and takes on all the sponsor's legal obligations, without prejudice to its ability to contractually delegate tasks to third parties.
q_2_1_fuente: Decreto N° 158/019 - Investigación en seres humanos; Resolución MERCOSUR N° 129/96 - Buenas Prácticas de Investigación Clínica.
q_2_2_directa: Yes. For transnational research or research with foreign cooperation (specifically, Clinical Trials), non-resident sponsors and investigators must appoint a legal representative domiciled in the country.
q_2_2_ampliada: When research is conducted from abroad, in addition to appointing a legal representative domiciled in the country, sponsors must submit to the jurisdiction of Uruguayan courts. They must also submit the contract with the comprehensive health provider and the documentation constituting the guarantees covering the right to compensation.
q_2_2_fuente: Decreto N° 158/019 - Investigación en seres humanos.
q_2_3_directa: It must fulfill the obligation of taking responsibility for the study's initiation, management, and/or financing. For the Clinical Trial protocol evaluation application, it must provide its name or corporate name, status, legal domicile, MSP registration or license number, and the Technical Director's identity.
q_2_3_ampliada: The sponsor, together with the investigator and the institution, is responsible for providing comprehensive care to subjects for complications and harm resulting from realized risks. It must also ensure the study's oversight through monitoring, and, for the Clinical Trial application, must submit a statement indicating it will be responsible for the trial's costs.
q_2_3_fuente: Decreto N° 158/019 - Investigación en seres humanos; Formulario FO-13220 - Solicitud de Evaluación de Protocolo de Ensayo Clínico; Resolución MERCOSUR N° 129/96 - Buenas Prácticas de Investigación Clínica.
q_2_4_directa: Not specified in official regulations.
q_2_4_ampliada: The regulation defines a Contract Research Organization as an organization to which the sponsor may transfer some of its tasks and obligations. While it states that all transfers of tasks and obligations must be expressed in writing, the regulation does not detail specific registration, licensing, or legal incorporation requirements the CRO must meet to operate in the country.
q_2_4_fuente: No specific information was found in official regulations.
q_2_5_directa: Yes, the regulation establishes specific requirements for selecting and licensing the sites where clinical research is conducted. These establishments must be legitimately incorporated organizations and hold the proper operating license granted by the Ministry of Public Health. They must also demonstrate the availability of suitable infrastructure and equipment to ensure participants' sanitary protection.
q_2_5_ampliada: During a protocol's formal evaluation process, the facilities of the centers, services, or care institutions where the study's various stages will take place must be detailed. The regulation requires documentary proof that the chosen institution has adequate, sufficient infrastructure, not only for the research's methodological conduct but also to handle any medical issues that may arise. Express, signed endorsement from the relevant authorities and services is also required, committing to provide comprehensive care for any harm to recruited subjects. For pharmacological clinical trials specifically, the sponsor must attach current proof of institutional licensing of those operating sites with DIGESA.
q_2_5_fuente: Decreto N° 158/019 - Investigación en seres humanos, Articles 2 (item j), 25 (items b.8, b.9, and f), and 46; Instructivo de Registro de Proyectos de Investigación; Formulario FO-13220 - Solicitud de Evaluación de Protocolo de Ensayo Clínico; Registro / Autorización de proyectos de investigación en seres humanos.
q_2_6_directa: Yes, the regulatory framework requires investigators to have academic and professional qualifications strictly appropriate to the proposed study's complexity. All participating investigators must certify their competence by submitting an up-to-date, detailed curriculum vitae. If they are also healthcare professionals, they must have their degree duly registered and licensed by the national health authority.
q_2_6_ampliada: The regulation determines that involved personnel must guarantee research subjects' full well-being, requiring demonstrable alignment between the responsible investigator's technical competencies and the project's methodological design. During the research authorization procedure, submitting the entire investigative team's curricular background is mandatory, highlighting their prior experience and capacity in similar clinical trials. As an additional ethical safeguard, all scientists involved must sign a sworn statement expressly committing to respect the Declaration of Helsinki, MSP regulations, and Good Clinical Practice (GCP). Physicians and specialists operating in these studies are also required, by organic law, to have their qualifying degrees validated and registered with the Ministry's Departamento de Habilitación y Control de Profesionales de la Salud. In the event of proven shortcomings or negligence, the investigator bears non-delegable responsibility that can result in serious administrative or criminal penalties.
q_2_6_fuente: Decreto N° 158/019 - Investigación en seres humanos, Annex, Articles 6 (item h), 25 (item d), and 37.
q_2_7_directa: Research subjects who suffer harm, whether foreseen or not, resulting from their participation, have the right to comprehensive care and compensation. Before the ethical ruling, an agreement with a comprehensive health provider protecting research subjects must be submitted.
q_2_7_ampliada: The Investigator, the Sponsor, and the Institution are jointly and severally responsible for providing comprehensive care for complications and harm resulting from realized risks. The protocol documentation must identify the insurance covering such harm. In addition, requiring a research subject to waive their right to compensation for harm is strictly prohibited; any clause in the free, informed consent that reduces this responsibility is void.
q_2_7_fuente: Decreto N° 158/019 - Investigación en seres humanos.
q_3_1_directa: Yes. The submission must include proof of registration with the MSP, the CEII-approved research Protocol, the CEII-approved Informed Consent Form, proof of approval from the accredited CEII, investigators' CVs, and investigators' sworn statement of GCP commitment. Specifically for Clinical Trials, the Formulario de Solicitud de Evaluación de Protocolo de Ensayo Clínico (FO-13220-004) and any additional documentation requested by the DES are required.
q_3_1_ampliada: All mandatory documentation (including institutional endorsement, the note to the Minister of Public Health, and the letter from the responsible Pharmaceutical Chemist) must be contained in a single, paginated PDF document identified with the registration number (R) and file version (V) (e.g., R1111-V1), with a maximum size of 5 MB. For studies conducted from abroad, the approval document from the regulatory authority in the country of origin must be attached. The research protocol submitted for approval must explicitly contain two key commitments: 1) a statement on the ownership arrangements for the information generated, ensuring no clauses restrict the public disclosure of results (except for patent protection cases); and 2) a formal statement that all study results, both positive and negative, will be made public within a maximum of two years of the study's completion.
q_3_1_fuente: Formulario FO-13220 - Solicitud de Evaluación de Protocolo de Ensayo Clínico; Instructivo de Registro de Proyectos de Investigación.
q_3_2_directa: Yes. The process is online and is part of AGESIC's e-government procedures system through the MSP. Submitting the documentation for authorization involves uploading the single, paginated, versioned PDF document to the platform, once registration has been validated.
q_3_2_ampliada: To begin the procedure, prior registration with ID Uruguay is required. Once the project registration is complete (Step 2) and validated by the CNEI, the Investigator must access their procedures inbox and request the evaluation/authorization (Step 3). The file must be identified with the registration number and version (e.g., R1111-V1) and not exceed 5 MB.
q_3_2_fuente: Instructivo de Registro de Proyectos de Investigación.
q_3_3_directa: Official regulations do not specify a time frame for the DES to issue a ruling. The CNEI must issue its ruling — approval, rejection, or request for clarifications — within sixty days, which may be extended for justified cause. For CEIIs, the maximum time frame for issuing a substantiated opinion is thirty days.
q_3_3_ampliada: The CNEI's sixty-day time frame begins once all required documentation is received. If modifications are requested, investigators have sixty days to provide them; if they do not respond within that time frame, the protocol will be archived. The expiry of the original time frame or its extension without an express ruling from the CNEI may, in specific cases, result in the research being denied.
q_3_3_fuente: Decreto N° 158/019 - Investigación en seres humanos.
q_3_4_directa: The procedure has no fee set by regulation.
q_3_4_ampliada: The Ministry of Public Health's procedures information explicitly states that the process for Registering/Authorizing Research Projects with Human Subjects "Has no cost." The regulations reviewed do not include a schedule of regulatory fees or charges under Decreto N° 158/019 or Decreto N° 189/998, although the study's costs must be borne by the sponsor.
q_3_4_fuente: Registro / Autorización de proyectos de investigación en seres humanos; Resolución MERCOSUR N° 129/96 - Buenas Prácticas de Investigación Clínica.
q_3_5_directa: Not specified in official regulations.
q_3_5_ampliada: Registering the research proposal with the MSP is mandatory, and is solely for the purpose of learning about research proposals involving human subjects in Uruguay, enabling timely follow-up of registered projects. While systematizing information for disclosure purposes is a goal, the official regulations reviewed do not establish an explicit requirement to register in an international public database (such as ClinicalTrials.gov) before national regulatory authorization.
q_3_5_fuente: Instructivo de Registro de Proyectos de Investigación.
q_3_6_directa: Yes. For Clinical Trials conducted from abroad or with foreign involvement, submitting documentation certifying approval in the country of origin or from the corresponding regulatory authority is mandatory.
q_3_6_ampliada: This foreign approval documentation is required for the local research Ethics Committee's assessment, in addition to local requirements. This ensures the protocol meets the requirements set by international standards applicable to research involving human subjects.
q_3_6_fuente: Decreto N° 158/019 - Investigación en seres humanos; Formulario FO-13220 - Solicitud de Evaluación de Protocolo de Ensayo Clínico.
q_3_7_directa: The sequential order of steps runs from the investigator's and the project's initial online registration, through institutional ethical approval, to the formal authorization application before the MSP's DES, and DIGESA's notification.
q_3_7_ampliada:
User Registration (Investigator): The Investigator must register with ID Uruguay.

Project Registration (Investigator/Sponsor): Registration of the research proposal is requested through the MSP's online system (Step 2), where the project's key information is provided and a registration number (R) is obtained.

Registration Validation (CNEI): The CNEI reviews the initial application and confirms registration validation.

Institutional Ethical Approval (Investigator/Institution): The Investigator and the Institution must obtain approval from the accredited CEII(s) and their respective endorsements, which is mandatory and precedes step 7.

Submission Preparation (Sponsor/Investigator): All necessary documentation is compiled, including Formulario FO-13220 and proof of the CEII's approval, consolidated into a single, paginated, versioned PDF document (Rxxx-Vx) of no more than 5 MB.

Regulatory Authorization Application (Investigator/Sponsor): The portal is accessed, the validated project is selected, YES is marked to request evaluation/authorization (Step 3), and the PDF document is uploaded.

Regulatory Evaluation (MSP/DES/CNEI): The procedure defaults to the DES for evaluation. If there are observations, they are received by email, and a new, consecutively paginated version of the document must be uploaded.

Final Authorization (MSP/DIGESA): Once all observations are resolved, the project is authorized, and a notification is received from DIGESA.
q_3_7_fuente: Instructivo de Registro de Proyectos de Investigación.
q_4_1_directa: Yes. The investigational product or placebo must be labeled with a statement identifying it by its generic name or registration number, and also stating its investigational purpose.
q_4_1_ampliada: The Investigational Product (IP) label must highlight that it is "Material for clinical study." Labeling must apply both to the active ingredients under study and to the placebos used.
q_4_1_fuente: Resolución MERCOSUR N° 129/96 - Buenas Prácticas de Investigación Clínica.
q_4_2_directa: Not specified in official regulations.
q_4_2_ampliada: The regulation for submitting the Clinical Trial protocol evaluation application requires submitting the medicine manufacturer's license. A description of the quality controls applied from raw material to finished product must also be included, ensuring the study is conducted in strict compliance with recognized scientific principles. The license is an indicator of compliance, but current regulations do not expressly require a GMP certificate as a mandatory submission document.
q_4_2_fuente: Formulario FO-13220 - Solicitud de Evaluación de Protocolo de Ensayo Clínico; Resolución MERCOSUR N° 129/96 - Buenas Prácticas de Investigación Clínica.
q_4_3_directa: Yes. The clinical trial authorization issued by the Ministry of Public Health constitutes the "favorable report" that, under Decreto N° 18/020, exempts the investigational product from the sanitary registration requirement for import.
q_4_3_ampliada: Article 19, item b), of Decreto N° 18/020 establishes a clear legal mechanism allowing the import of unregistered medicines when intended for a duly authorized clinical trial. While the import process itself must comply with the corresponding customs procedures, the DES/CNEI's trial authorization is the fundamental regulatory document justifying the exemption and allowing the product to enter the country solely for research purposes.
q_4_3_fuente: Article 19, item b), of Decreto N° 18/020.
q_5_1_directa: Yes. The regulation requires the investigator to "immediately" report serious or unexpected adverse reactions to the sponsor and the CEI. The sponsor, in turn, must inform the health authority. While the study protocol must specify detailed time frames for this reporting, Decreto N° 158/019 and Res. MERCOSUR N° 129/96 do not explicitly establish a numerical time frame (e.g., 48 hours) for the sponsor's notification to the authority. Sponsors must therefore adhere to what is committed in the approved protocol and follow international pharmacovigilance good practices (e.g., 7- and 15-day time frames for SUSARs, depending on severity and outcome).
q_5_1_ampliada: A Serious Adverse Event (SAE) is defined as any harmful occurrence resulting in death, life-threatening effects, the need for hospitalization, permanent disability, or a congenital malformation. The investigator has an obligation to immediately suspend the research if any risk or health harm to the subject is perceived. In MERCOSUR multicenter studies, the Health Authority detecting the serious adverse reaction must report it to the health authorities of the other Member States.
q_5_1_fuente: Decreto N° 158/019 - Investigación en seres humanos; Resolución MERCOSUR N° 129/96 - Buenas Prácticas de Investigación Clínica.
q_5_2_directa: Yes. The Investigator must submit periodic reports at intervals no longer than 6 months to the Ethics Committees and the sponsor, who will forward them to the health authority. In addition, the CEII will assess project progress through investigators' annual reports.
q_5_2_ampliada: The investigator prepares and submits interim and final reports to the Ethics Committee. The concept of Periodic Report is defined as a report submitted every six months (or quarterly, depending on the definition) detailing partial results and the research's degree of progress.
q_5_2_fuente: Decreto N° 158/019 - Investigación en seres humanos; Resolución MERCOSUR N° 129/96 - Buenas Prácticas de Investigación Clínica.
q_5_3_directa: Yes. Submitting interim reports (or periodic reports) at intervals no longer than 6 months is required. A final communication to the health authority must also be submitted within no more than 180 days of the study's completion.
q_5_3_ampliada: The Investigator must submit, at any time, the data requested by the Research Ethics Committee. In addition, clinical trials with psychotropic drugs require a written report to the health authority every 3 months on the trial's progress, detailing enrolled patients and the medicine used.
q_5_3_fuente: Decreto N° 158/019 - Investigación en seres humanos; Resolución MERCOSUR N° 129/96 - Buenas Prácticas de Investigación Clínica.
q_5_4_directa: Yes. Any modification to the protocol and its annexes must be reported to and approved in advance by the CEII. These modifications must also be reported in advance to the authorities enforcing the regulation.
q_5_4_ampliada: The CEII is responsible for reviewing every protocol modification, and its approval is a condition for implementation. If MSP authorization is required, the investigator must submit any modification to the Ethics Committee, which must approve it before proceeding.
q_5_4_fuente: Decreto N° 158/019 - Investigación en seres humanos; Resolución MERCOSUR N° 129/96 - Buenas Prácticas de Investigación Clínica.
q_5_5_directa: Yes. Once the research is complete, all participating patients must be assured that they will have access to the benefits demonstrated by the research, as long as indicated by the treating physician.
q_5_5_ampliada: It is a requirement that the research guarantee subjects the project's resulting benefits, whether in terms of social return or access to the research's procedures and/or products. The protocol must ensure this access to preventive, diagnostic, and therapeutic procedures that have proved beneficial once the trial concludes.
q_5_5_fuente: Decreto N° 158/019 - Investigación en seres humanos; Formulario FO-13220 - Solicitud de Evaluación de Protocolo de Ensayo Clínico.
q_6_1_directa: Yes. Ley N° 18.331 (the Personal Data Protection Law) is the applicable regulation, and accepting its terms is mandatory when registering the project.
q_6_1_ampliada: Health-related information is classified as Sensitive Data. Sensitive data may only be processed with the data subject's express, written consent, or for statistical or scientific purposes when de-identified from their subjects. Ley N° 18.331 requires those responsible for databases to adopt measures guaranteeing the security and confidentiality of personal data.
q_6_1_fuente: Ley N° 18.331 - Protección de Datos Personales; Instructivo de Registro de Proyectos de Investigación.
q_6_2_directa: Not specified in official regulations.
q_6_2_ampliada: Decreto N° 158/019 establishes that vaccine clinical trials are a specific subject area that mandatorily requires a ruling from the CNEI. However, no specialized regulatory body or guideline is provided establishing additional requirements for vaccines beyond the general ones for Clinical Trials.
q_6_2_fuente: Decreto N° 158/019 - Investigación en seres humanos.
q_6_3_directa: Yes. Decreto N° 160/006 establishes the regulatory framework for donating, obtaining, evaluating, processing, storing, distributing, therapeutically using, researching, and disposing of human cells and tissues.
q_6_3_ampliada: This research falls under the authority of the Instituto Nacional de Donación y Trasplante (National Institute of Donation and Transplantation, INDT) for authorization. The regulation covers stem cells, umbilical cord cells, and progenitor cells, and requires the principle of voluntary, unpaid donation, as well as high quality and safety standards.
q_6_3_fuente: Decreto N° 160/006 - Células y tejidos humanos.
q_6_4_directa: Yes. Detailed provisions exist for research involving vulnerable populations, pregnant women, persons with legally defined incapacity, and research involving persons diagnosed with brain death. Special reporting requirements also exist for studies with psychotropic drugs.
q_6_4_ampliada: For vulnerable subjects, their protection from vulnerability or legally defined incapacity must be ensured to prevail, and their selection must be justified in the protocol. Research with psychotropic drugs requires a sworn statement from the sponsoring laboratory's Technical Direction and a list of participating physicians, as well as mandatory quarterly reports to the health authority. For clinical trials involving psychotropic drugs, in addition to the general requirements, Resolución MERCOSUR N° 129/96 requires submitting additional documentation in the initial application. This includes: 1) a sworn statement from the sponsoring laboratory's Technical Direction specifying the production batches to be used; 2) a complete list of the investigating physicians authorized to receive and administer the product; and 3) a statement signed individually by each physician, taking responsibility for the medicine's proper custody and dispensing exclusively to trial participants.
q_6_4_fuente: Decreto N° 158/019 - Investigación en seres humanos; Resolución MERCOSUR N° 129/96 - Buenas Prácticas de Investigación Clínica.

q_1_1_directa: The main authority responsible for authorizing clinical trials is the Ministerio de Salud y Desarrollo Social, acting through the Junta Revisora de Productos Farmacéuticos (Pharmaceutical Products Review Board, JRPF).
q_1_1_ampliada: The Ley de Medicamentos grants the Ministerio de Salud y Desarrollo Social the authority to authorize every clinical trial, delegating this advisory and oversight function to the JRPF. The Instituto Nacional de Higiene "Rafael Rangel" (Rafael Rangel National Institute of Hygiene, INHRR), the Ministry of Health's technical body, is also responsible for evaluating medicines and has the authority to authorize clinical protocols for importing unregistered products.
q_1_1_fuente: Ley de Medicamentos (Gaceta Oficial N° 37.006 del 03 de agosto de 2000) (Title VI, Article 71; Title III, Chapter I, Article 33); Ley de Medicamentos (Gaceta Oficial N° 37.006 del 03 de agosto de 2000) (Title IV, Chapter III, Article 19).
q_1_2_directa: The main regulations governing health research are the Ley de Medicamentos, the Código de Bioética y Bioseguridad, and the Ley sobre Transplante de Órganos y Materiales Anatómicos en Seres Humanos, if the research involves the disposition of such materials.
q_1_2_ampliada: The Ley de Medicamentos governs the regulatory aspects and elevates the Declaration of Helsinki's principles to a binding legal requirement. Article 72 requires clinical trials to be conducted with "strict respect for individuals' fundamental rights and the universally accepted ethical principles... contained in the Declaration of Helsinki," making compliance with it a legal obligation rather than a mere recommendation.
q_1_2_fuente: Ley de Medicamentos (Gaceta Oficial N° 37.006 del 03 de agosto de 2000) (Title VI, Article 72).
q_1_3_directa: Clinical trial authorization is governed primarily by the Ley de Medicamentos and the Normas de la Junta Revisora de Productos Farmacéuticos.
q_1_3_ampliada: The Ley de Medicamentos defines clinical trials and establishes the need for authorization from the Ministerio de Salud y Desarrollo Social, through the JRPF. The Normas de la Junta Revisora de Productos Farmacéuticos (5th Revision), Chapter I, Group A, item 4, establish the JRPF's authority to approve clinical research protocols conducted in the country. Chapter III, Group H, item 1.b of those Normas further conditions the import of unregistered products for research on prior authorization of the protocol by the INHRR.
q_1_3_fuente: Ley de Medicamentos (Gaceta Oficial N° 37.006 del 03 de agosto de 2000) (Title VI, Article 71); Normas de la Junta Revisora de Productos Farmacéuticos (5ta Revisión, Julio de 1998) (Chapter I, Group A, Item 4; Chapter III, Group H, Item 1.b).
q_1_4_directa: Yes, approval from a Research Ethics Committee (CEI), also known as a Bioethics Commission, is mandatory. The regulation requires institutions to establish these commissions to evaluate projects.
q_1_4_ampliada: The Ley de Medicamentos requires respect for ethical principles such as the Declaration of Helsinki. More specifically, the Código de Bioética y Bioseguridad establishes that institutions executing MCT/FONACIT-funded projects must establish bioethics and biosafety commissions. These commissions must issue a reasoned written opinion on the project's bioethical aspects. Although the legal basis is tied to public funding, the ethical approval requirement applies to all clinical trials. Expectations regarding these committees' composition and operation align with international standards, as detailed in the draft GCP Standards, which stipulate a minimum of five members, with representation from healthcare professionals, scientists, and non-scientific community members.
q_1_4_fuente: Ley de Medicamentos (Gaceta Oficial N° 37.006 del 03 de agosto de 2000) (Title VI, Article 72); Código de Bioética y Bioseguridad (Part III, Section D, Items 1 and 2).
q_1_5_directa: Current regulations do not explicitly specify whether the CEI's approval must precede submission to the Regulatory Authority. However, this is standard, recommended practice.
q_1_5_ampliada: While the primary regulations do not define the exact sequence, international practice and the direction indicated by Venezuela's draft GCP Standards suggest the CEI's approval should be obtained before submitting the application to the regulatory authority (INHRR/JRPF). Submitting the application without prior ethical approval could result in the procedure not being accepted or in significant delays.
q_1_5_fuente: No specific regulation was identified on this point.
q_1_6_directa: Official Venezuelan regulations do not provide for a centralized accreditation system for Research Ethics Committees (CEIs). Although establishing these commissions at sites is mandatory, neither the Ministry of Health nor the INHRR details a national certification or registration process.
q_1_6_ampliada: In the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela, conducting clinical trials mandatorily requires protocols to be evaluated and ruled on. The Código de Bioética y Bioseguridad stipulates that institutions conducting research must establish bioethics commissions. These bodies are typically structured based on recognized international ethical guidelines. However, under the current legal framework, comprising the Ley de Medicamentos and the Normas de la Junta Revisora, no formal accreditation system for these committees has been implemented. The national regulatory authority does not issue centralized fitness or operating certifications for CEIs. They therefore operate in a decentralized manner, under the strict endorsement of the medical or academic institution hosting them.
q_1_6_fuente: Código de Bioética y Bioseguridad, Part III.
q_1_7_directa: Current Venezuelan regulations do not provide for an official public registry of Research Ethics Committees (CEIs). The laws require ethical review of clinical trials, but do not specify a government mechanism for a listing open to the public.
q_1_7_ampliada: Venezuela's regulatory framework requires all biomedical research to have the endorsement of an institutional bioethics commission. Regulations such as the Ley de Medicamentos and the Código de Bioética y Bioseguridad set out these primary requirements to protect subjects. However, health authorities, such as the Ministerio del Poder Popular para la Salud or the INHRR, do not manage a centralized platform consolidating these bodies. Consequently, no free, publicly accessible national registry exists listing approved or active committees. The burden of proof falls directly on each institution and sponsor, who must justify the committee's composition before the JRPF when submitting their protocols.
q_1_7_fuente: Ley de Medicamentos (Gaceta Oficial N° 37.006 del 03 de agosto de 2000), Title VI.
q_1_8_directa: Yes. Every clinical trial, defined as the experimental evaluation of a substance or medicine in human subjects, must be authorized by the Ministerio de Salud y Desarrollo Social, through the JRPF.
q_1_8_ampliada: A clinical trial is defined as the experimental evaluation of a substance or medicine through its administration or application in human subjects, aiming to demonstrate its pharmacodynamic effects, collect absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion (ADME) data, establish its efficacy, or determine its safety profile. Conducting these studies must be authorized by the NRA. In addition, if an unregistered pharmaceutical product is to be imported for Clinical Research purposes, the import requires prior authorization of the clinical protocol by the INHRR.
q_1_8_fuente: Ley de Medicamentos (Gaceta Oficial N° 37.006 del 03 de agosto de 2000) (Title VI, Articles 70 and 71); Normas de la Junta Revisora de Productos Farmacéuticos (5ta Revisión, Julio de 1998) (Chapter III, Group H, Item 1.b).
q_2_1_directa: Venezuelan regulations do not explicitly define the term "sponsor" in the clinical trial context, either in the Ley de Medicamentos or the Normas de la JRPF. However, they clearly distinguish between the entity responsible for the trial (the de facto sponsor) and its local legal representative (the Farmacéutico Patrocinante). The sponsor is the organization that initiates, manages, and/or finances the study.
q_2_1_ampliada: Venezuela's regulatory framework establishes two distinct roles that must not be confused. The Sponsor, in line with international standards (ICH-GCP), is the entity taking ultimate responsibility for the clinical trial, including its financing, design, and guaranteeing compensation to participants in the event of harm, as required by the Código de Bioética y Bioseguridad. The Farmacéutico Patrocinante [Sponsoring Pharmacist], on the other hand, is an administrative requirement: a Venezuelan pharmaceutical professional who acts as attorney-in-fact and legal representative of the product's owner before the health authority (INHRR) for registration procedures. While the Farmacéutico Patrocinante manages submitting the application, the international or national Sponsor retains ultimate responsibility for the trial's ethical and scientific conduct.
q_2_1_fuente: Código de Bioética y Bioseguridad (Part III, Section C, Item 7.5); Instructivo SREF-0007 (Documentos Requeridos: AL06); Annex 13 of the EU Good Manufacturing Practice Standards (definition of sponsor).
q_2_2_directa: Yes, the sponsor must appoint a Farmacéutico Patrocinante holding a Venezuelan degree, and the owner must grant power of attorney to a Casa de Representación [Representation House] legally authorized in the country.
q_2_2_ampliada: The Farmacéutico Patrocinante must hold a Venezuelan degree and comply with the Ley de Colegiación Farmacéutica. For the registration application or other procedures, the Sponsorship Power of Attorney and the Representative Power of Attorney are required, the latter granted by the Owner to the Casa de Representación. The Casa de Representación must hold an Installation and Operation Certificate issued by the National Health Authority, implying its legal establishment in the country.
q_2_2_fuente: Instructivo SREF-0007 (Documentos Requeridos: AL06 and AL07); Instructivo SREF-0007 (Documentos Requeridos: AL08).
q_2_3_directa: Yes. The clinical trial's sponsor, whether an individual or a legal entity, must appoint a Sponsor Representative in Venezuela (the "Farmacéutico Patrocinante"), who must be a Venezuelan pharmacist, registered with a professional association and the health authorities, and must hold a Sponsorship Power of Attorney specifically authorizing them to act on the sponsor's behalf before the JRPF.
q_2_3_ampliada: The Farmacéutico Patrocinante is not the trial's sponsor, but rather its legal representative before the regulatory authority in Venezuela. To act as such, they must hold a Venezuelan degree under the Ley del Ejercicio de la Farmacia and comply with the Ley de Colegiación Farmacéutica. The Sponsorship Power of Attorney authorizing them must be legible and include registration details such as national ID number, MPPS registration number, professional association number, and IPREF registration number, explicitly stating that the designated person acts as the study's sponsor representative.
q_2_3_fuente: Instructivo SREF-0007 (Documentos Requeridos: AL06); Solicitud de Autorización de Protocolo Clínico (SAPC) para Especialidades Farmacéuticas - INHRR.
q_2_4_directa: Venezuelan regulations do not contain a specific rule for Contract Research Organizations (CROs). However, the sponsor may delegate functions to them, provided this is documented in writing.
q_2_4_ampliada: No law or regulation in Venezuela specifically defines or governs CROs. However, their involvement is recognized. The sponsor may delegate any or all of its trial-related functions to a CRO. This delegation must be formalized in a written contract. It is essential to understand that, even when tasks are transferred, ultimate responsibility for the quality and integrity of the trial's data and the protection of research subjects always remains, non-delegably, with the sponsor.
q_2_4_fuente: No specific regulation was identified on this point.
q_2_5_directa: Yes, the regulation requires research sites to have adequate facilities and qualified staff to respond to potential emergencies. To authorize the study, the INHRR requires submitting an official document certifying this adequacy, in addition to the express approval of the medical institution's highest authority.
q_2_5_ampliada: Selecting institutions for clinical trials is contingent on their having proven research experience and comprehensive care response capacity. Under the official guide for the Solicitud de Autorización de Protocolos Clínicos (Form F-RCDM 011), submitting the site's "resource adequacy" documentation is unavoidable. This technical requirement certifies the hospital facility's potential in terms of infrastructure and qualified staff to promptly address any injury a participant might suffer. The file must also contain a formal statement of awareness and approval of the trial issued by the institution's highest governing authority.
q_2_5_fuente: Instructivo para el llenado del formulario F-RCDM 011, Annex 4, Items 13.4 and 13.5.
q_2_6_directa: Yes. Clinical trials must be conducted by duly trained, registered medical professionals or health specialists, who must certify their technical and ethical fitness before the INHRR.
q_2_6_ampliada: Venezuelan regulation entrusts the conduct of clinical research exclusively to healthcare professionals with proven training and experience in the therapeutic area under study. During the formal Solicitud de Autorización de Protocolos Clínicos (S.A.P.C.) procedure before the INHRR, official documentation certifying the principal and secondary investigators must be submitted. Among these requirements, each physician's curriculum vitae stands out, which must be updated within the last two years and formally certified by the corresponding Medical Association. Proof of clinical specialty endorsed by the relevant professional body must also be attached. Finally, submitting a current Deontological Certification, issued no more than three months prior, is essential, thereby guaranteeing the professional's ethical fitness and unblemished record in their jurisdiction.
q_2_6_fuente: Instructivo para el llenado del formulario F-RCDM 011, Annex 5, Items 14.1, 14.3, and 14.4.
q_2_7_directa: Yes. The sponsor must state in writing its commitment to duly compensate research subjects who suffer injury from accidents or death at the site where the studies are conducted.
q_2_7_ampliada: If a pharmaceutical company sponsors, funds, or conducts a project (and consults Venezuela's Bioethics and Biosafety Commission), it must guarantee compensation through immediate medical care (financial or otherwise) for temporary or permanent disability. In the event of death, family members are entitled to material compensation set under the Republic's laws. In addition, the Informed Consent document must explicitly state the funding agencies' commitments regarding insurance and other indemnities, especially in higher-risk studies.
q_2_7_fuente: Código de Bioética y Bioseguridad (Part III, Section C, Item 7.5; Annex 1, Section A, Item 7).
q_3_1_directa: Yes. The essential content for preclinical/clinical evaluation must include the Summary Statement, the Submitted Material Report (with risk/benefit balance), and the preclinical and clinical studies (Phase I, II, III) justifying the product's safety and efficacy.
q_3_1_ampliada: If the clinical trial is submitted for approval of a New Category A Product (an active ingredient not approved in the country), the application requires a thorough evaluation including: the Submitted Material Report (a faithful summary of the scientific work, including tables, graphs, and statistical evaluations to establish the risk/benefit balance); Preclinical Studies (acute, subacute, chronic, and special toxicology studies, such as teratogenicity and carcinogenesis); and Clinical Studies (Phase I, Phase II — early and late — and Phase III).
q_3_1_fuente: Normas de la Junta Revisora de Productos Farmacéuticos (5ta Revisión, Julio de 1998) (Chapter II, Group E, Sections 5.1 and 5.2).
q_3_2_directa: Yes. The submission process is done virtually through the Sistema Venezolano de Registro, Control de Medicamentos y Evaluación de Productos Sanitarios (Venezuelan System for the Registration, Control, and Evaluation of Medicines and Health Products, SIVERC) version 2.0, followed by submitting a paginated physical file bearing fiscal stamps.
q_3_2_ampliada: All applications for the sanitary registration of pharmaceutical products (including clinical evaluation) must be submitted exclusively through SIVERC 2.0. Documents must be uploaded in PDF format, with a maximum size of 120KB per page. The physical file submitted at the Receiving office must include the printed copy of the procedure form generated by the system, with the Farmacéutico Patrocinante's handwritten signature and fiscal stamps, plus a CD containing the preclinical and clinical information.
q_3_2_fuente: Circular RC N° 005 (23/05/2025); Circular RC N° 006 (05/08/2025); Instructivo SREF-0007 (Page 3, Recommendations; Page 8, Points 9 and 15).
q_3_3_directa: Although no official maximum time frame is specified for evaluating and authorizing a clinical trial protocol, the regulation does set key procedural time frames, such as 15 business days to respond to information requests and 180 days of validity for fee payment.
q_3_3_ampliada:
Venezuela's regulatory framework does not set a maximum legal time for the authority (INHRR/JRPF) to issue a decision on a clinical trial application. However, critical time frames the applicant must meet do exist:
Correcting Deficiencies: The sponsor has 15 business days to correct or submit missing documents notified by the INHRR. Failure to meet this time frame may result in the application's rejection.
Payment Validity: Payment of the fees corresponding to the procedure is valid for 180 continuous days. The physical file must be submitted within this period to avoid having to make a new payment.
q_3_3_fuente: Instructivo SREF-0007.
q_3_4_directa: Yes, applications' evaluation is subject to the current fee schedule. However, the Ley de Medicamentos exempts sanitary registration of essential medicines in their generic denomination from fee payment.
q_3_4_ampliada: The applicant must make payment according to the current fee schedule, and the payment is valid for 180 continuous days. The NRA reserves the right to adjust and apply new prices for its services. Sanitary registration authorization procedures for essential medicines in their generic denomination are exempt from paying evaluation and analysis fees.
q_3_4_fuente: Instructivo SREF-0007 (Page 7, Point 7); Ley de Medicamentos (Gaceta Oficial N° 37.006 del 03 de agosto de 2000) (Title II, Chapter II, Second Paragraph of Article 14).
q_3_5_directa: No, current Venezuelan regulations do not explicitly require registering a clinical trial in a public registry platform before it begins, as a condition for authorization.
q_3_5_ampliada: While the Ley de Medicamentos promotes creating medicine information systems, and the JRPF aims to effectively oversee clinical trials, current regulations do not explicitly require registering the clinical trial in a national or international public platform before it begins.
q_3_5_fuente: No specific regulation was identified on this point.
q_3_6_directa: Yes, for research funded by foreign entities, submitting the project's technical approval issued by the funding body is required. In addition, bioequivalence studies conducted under foreign regulations may be accepted if certified by the health authorities of origin.
q_3_6_ampliada: In the context of consultations to the Comisión de Bioética y Bioseguridad (CoBioBios) regarding research funded by international agencies, submitting the project's technical approval by the funding body is required. For pharmacokinetic bioequivalence studies, missing data (such as the batch number and certificate of analysis) may be replaced by a certificate issued by the health authorities of the country where the study was conducted, provided it confirms the study was conducted under their authorization and in compliance with Good Clinical Research Practice.
q_3_6_fuente: Código de Bioética y Bioseguridad (Part III, Section C, Items 7 and 7.1); Normas Venezolanas de Biodisponibilidad y Bioequivalencia de Productos Farmacéuticos (Resolución No 212, Gaceta Oficial N° 38.499) (Article 5, Section a.5).
q_3_7_directa: The process begins with institutional ethical approval. For trials requiring the import of an unregistered product, a critical step prior to the import application is obtaining clinical protocol authorization from the INHRR. Finally, formal trial authorization is obtained from the Ministry of Health through the JRPF.
q_3_7_ampliada:
The sequence of steps must account for a key branch if the investigational product is imported.

Institutional ethical approval: Obtaining the institutional Bioethics Commission's favorable opinion.

Dossier preparation: Preparing the protocol and the technical, legal, and financial documentation.

Protocol authorization for import (Critical Step): Submitting the protocol to the INHRR to obtain its authorization. Under the JRPF's Normas, this authorization is an indispensable, prior condition for processing the product's import.

Submission to the JRPF: Once the previous steps are complete, the formal clinical trial authorization application is submitted to the JRPF (through the SIVERC system and in physical form).

Evaluation and final authorization: The JRPF evaluates the complete file and issues its recommendation to the Ministry of Health for the trial's final authorization.
q_3_7_fuente: Normas de la Junta Revisora de Productos Farmacéuticos (5ta Revisión, Julio de 1998) (Chapter III, Group H, Item 1.b); Ley de Medicamentos (Gaceta Oficial N° 37.006 del 03 de agosto de 2000) (Title VI, Article 71).
q_4_1_directa: Not specified in official regulations for the Investigational Product (IP) in the context of a clinical trial.
q_4_1_ampliada: While detailed regulations exist for labeling and packaging pharmaceutical products for sale, including declaring the active ingredient, strength, pharmaceutical form, batch number, and expiry date, the regulations available do not establish specific requirements for labeling an Investigational Product (IP), especially when used under blinded conditions in a clinical trial.
q_4_1_fuente: No specific regulation was identified on this point.
q_4_2_directa: Yes, submitting the Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) Certificate of the manufacturers involved in the process is a mandatory requirement.
q_4_2_ampliada: The GMP Certificate is a legal document required for processing applications before the INHRR (Document AL01), and must correspond to the requested manufacturer(s), be current, and be legalized. The Ley de Medicamentos supports this requirement by establishing that laboratories must base their activity on Good Manufacturing Practice.
q_4_2_fuente: Instructivo SREF-0007 (Documentos Requeridos: AL01); Ley de Medicamentos (Gaceta Oficial N° 37.006 del 03 de agosto de 2000) (Title IV, Chapter I, Article 49).
q_4_3_directa: No. Importing pharmaceutical products without Sanitary Registration for Clinical Research purposes requires prior authorization of the clinical protocol by the INHRR.
q_4_3_ampliada: Pharmaceutical Products may only be imported without prior sanitary registration for Clinical Research purposes, but this import is conditional on the protocol's prior authorization by the INHRR. The applicant must subsequently request the corresponding authorization from the JRPF.
q_4_3_fuente: Normas de la Junta Revisora de Productos Farmacéuticos (5ta Revisión, Julio de 1998) (Chapter III, Group H, Items 1.b and 2).
q_5_1_directa: Yes. Venezuelan regulations establish the obligation to report adverse events and any relevant information related to medicines' safety to the health authority.
q_5_1_ampliada:
Venezuelan legislation on medicines provides for the obligation to report information on adverse events and risks associated with medicine use to the competent health authority. Within clinical research, this obligation translates into the duty to report serious adverse events and any relevant adverse reaction detected during the study's conduct.

Current provisions establish the responsibility of pharmaceutical product holders, manufacturers, or those responsible to report identified adverse effects or safety issues to the health authority. However, the regulations reviewed do not specifically detail the operational procedures or exact time frames for reporting adverse events in the context of clinical trials.
q_5_1_fuente: Ley de Medicamentos (Gaceta Oficial N° 37.006 del 03 de agosto de 2000), Title IV, Chapter I, Article 49. Normas de la Junta Revisora de Productos Farmacéuticos (5ta Revisión, Julio de 1998), (Chapter III, Group H).
q_5_2_directa: Venezuelan regulations provide for submitting periodic safety reports for medicines subject to sanitary surveillance.
q_5_2_ampliada:
Venezuela's regulatory provisions on medicines establish the obligation to report information related to pharmaceutical products' safety to the health authority.
