q_5_1_directa: No. Pharmacovigilance is an activity of the Pharmacy Directorate (DPM/MT). However, the sources do not specify the detailed requirements, channels, or time frames for reporting Serious Adverse Events (SAEs) or Serious Unexpected Adverse Reactions (SUSARs).
q_5_1_ampliada: When an investigator requests an extension from the CNB, the progress note must include details of doléances reçues (complaints received), their description, and anticipated harm and side effects, implying safety follow-up.
q_5_1_fuente: Standards for Sanitary Registration and Laboratory Accreditation (DPM/MT) / Enregistrement d'un laboratoire et obtention d'AMM (page 4), Procédures du Comité National de Bioéthique Pour approbation De protocole de recherche (Décembre 2014) (page 4).
q_5_2_directa: Not specified in official regulations.
q_5_2_ampliada: The regulation does not explicitly require submitting annual safety reports (DSUR). However, if a study extension is requested, a detailed progress note summarizing the study's status, the number of subjects enrolled, and preliminary results must be submitted.
q_5_2_fuente: No specific regulation was identified on this point.
q_5_3_directa: Yes. The investigator must indicate the report drafting deadlines in the initial submission to the CNB. In addition, submitting a "note de progrès" (progress note) is mandatory when requesting an extension of the approval's duration.
q_5_3_ampliada: The "progress note" submitted for extensions must detail the research's status, whether it is in progress or has not started (and why), the number of subjects enrolled, complaints received, and preliminary results.
q_5_3_fuente: Procédures du Comité National de Bioéthique Pour approbation De protocole de recherche (Décembre 2014) (page 3, page 4).
q_5_4_directa: Yes. Amendments changing the protocol's meaning or objectives, or altering the limitations experienced or risks incurred by participants, must be submitted for the CNB's ruling before being implemented.
q_5_4_ampliada: The investigator must submit these amendments to the CNB well in advance, since review can take up to 3 months. It is recommended that any protocol modifications be flagged by highlighting them in color in the new version.
q_5_4_fuente: Procédures du Comité National de Bioéthique Pour approbation De protocole de recherche (Décembre 2014) (page 3, page 4).
q_5_5_directa: Not specified in official regulations.
q_5_5_ampliada: The CNB requires the consent form to cover what is planned in the event of harm during participation, but the regulations reviewed do not establish obligations for the sponsor regarding access to the investigational product once the clinical trial ends.
q_5_5_fuente: No specific regulation was identified on this point.
q_6_1_directa: Not specified in official regulations.
q_6_1_ampliada: While the Constitution guarantees the freedom and privacy of communications, and the informed consent form must clearly state that the participant's confidentiality will be respected, no specific law or dedicated regulation on personal data protection directly applicable to clinical trials exists.
q_6_1_fuente: Procédures du Comité National de Bioéthique Pour approbation De protocole de recherche (Décembre 2014) (page 3), Constitution de la République d'Haïti (1987, amendée 2012) (Article 49).
q_6_2_directa: Yes, the 2005 Décret establishes the Coordination Nationale du Programme de Vaccination, whose mission is to define vaccination standards and procedures, and to oversee the introduction of new vaccines based on the epidemiological profile.
q_6_2_ampliada: This coordination body is responsible for promoting, coordinating, and controlling vaccination activities throughout the national territory. This suggests a specific regulatory mechanism for introducing new vaccines, relevant to conducting clinical trials in this field, although the specific regulation is not cited.
q_6_2_fuente: Décret du 28 décembre 2005 portant Organisation du Ministère de la Santé Publique et de la Population (MSPP) (Article 28, Article 41).
q_6_3_directa: Not specified in official regulations.
q_6_3_ampliada: The DELR has the mandate to develop and apply standards and procedures on safe blood transfusion, and to ensure medical laboratories' quality control. However, no specific regulations or guidelines are cited for the general collection and use of human biological samples for research, beyond the blood transfusion area.
q_6_3_fuente: Décret du 28 décembre 2005 portant Organisation du Ministère de la Santé Publique et de la Population (MSPP) (Article 36).
q_6_4_directa: Yes. Special requirements exist for documenting studies involving illiterate participants, where the consent methodology must be specified. In addition, for submitting generics, bioequivalence documentation is required for antibiotics, antibacterials, and antivirals.
q_6_4_ampliada: The DPM/MT requires generics' technical dossiers to include bioequivalence tests for these product classes before granting sanitary registration (AMM). The CNB also requires a mentor or counterpart to be named in dissertation research.
q_6_4_fuente: Procédures du Comité National de Bioéthique Pour approbation De protocole de recherche (Décembre 2014) (page 2), Standards for Sanitary Registration and Laboratory Accreditation (DPM/MT) / Enregistrement d'un laboratoire et obtention d'AMM (page 3).

q_1_1_directa: The National Regulatory Authority (NRA) for clinical trials conducted for marketing-authorization purposes is the National Administration of Drugs, Foods and Medical Devices (ANMAT).
q_1_1_ampliada: ANMAT is a decentralized agency with jurisdiction throughout the national territory. It is responsible for controlling and overseeing drugs and medicines and is empowered to grant their marketing authorization (sanitary registration). Within this authority, the Directorate of Clinical Research and Drug Registry Management (Dirección de Investigación Clínica y Gestión del Registro de Medicamentos) holds specific competence to evaluate, authorize, and oversee protocols for pharmacological clinical trials conducted for marketing-authorization purposes.
q_1_1_fuente: Decreto 1490/1992 (Article 3, item a); Disposición ANMAT 7516/2025, Art. 5; Annex VI (Abbreviations).
q_1_2_directa: The main ethical and health-research regulations are Resolución 1480/2011 of the Ministry of Health, which approves the Guide for Research in Human Health (Guía para Investigaciones en Salud Humana), and the Civil and Commercial Code of the Nation (Código Civil y Comercial de la Nación).
q_1_2_ampliada: Resolución 1480/2011 sets out ethical and operational guidelines that are mandatory for Clinical Pharmacology Studies conducted for marketing-authorization purposes before ANMAT, seeking to guarantee respect for the dignity, well-being, and physical and mental integrity of participants. For its part, the Civil and Commercial Code of the Nation introduced specific requirements for medical research involving human subjects, including the requirement of a clear protocol and prior approval by an accredited research ethics committee.
q_1_2_fuente: Resolución 1480/2011 del Ministerio de Salud (Articles 1 and 3); Disposición ANMAT 7516/2025 (Recitals). Código Civil y Comercial de la Nación (Articles 58 and 59).
q_1_3_directa: The main regulation is Disposición 7516/2025, which approves the rules on Good Clinical Practice (GCP) for the Evaluation and Oversight of Clinical Pharmacology Studies conducted for Marketing-Authorization Purposes, and adopts the ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice, supplemented by local regulatory requirements.
q_1_3_ampliada: The adoption of the ICH E6(R3) Guideline seeks to harmonize Argentina with global standards, facilitating data acceptance and participation in international research. This regulation applies to Phase I, II, and III studies, as well as to protocol phase variations conducted for marketing-authorization purposes.
q_1_3_fuente: Disposición ANMAT 7516/2025, Recitals and Articles 1, 3, and 4.
q_1_4_directa: Yes. Every medical research project involving human subjects must have the prior approval of an accredited research ethics committee.
q_1_4_ampliada: The requirement for prior ethical review is a fundamental requirement, established in the Civil and Commercial Code of the Nation, to guarantee the protection of participants' rights, safety, and well-being. The Research Ethics Committee (REC) must be independent of the sponsor and the investigator, and its prior approval is necessary before study activities begin at the site.
q_1_4_fuente: Código Civil y Comercial de la Nación, Article 58; Disposición ANMAT 7516/2025 (Recitals); Annex VI (Institutional Review Board/Independent Ethics Committee/Research Ethics Committee); Annex II (Section 2.3.1).
q_1_5_directa: No. Approval by a Research Ethics Committee (REC) is not a mandatory requirement for the initial submission of the Protocol Authorization Application (Formulario EFCA 1), but it must be obtained before ANMAT authorizes or is notified of each individual site and investigator.
q_1_5_ampliada: ANMAT's current regulations establish a two-stage process: first, authorization of the study's general protocol (initial filing), and then the individual submission and evaluation of sites/investigators. The list of documentation required for the initial study authorization application (Formulario EFCA 1) does not include the REC approval opinion. However, ethical approval is an indispensable requirement for the subsequent submission of investigators and research sites (Formulario EFCA 2) and must be submitted at that stage. In addition, the Civil and Commercial Code of the Nation establishes, as a fundamental requirement, that every medical research project involving human subjects must have the prior approval of an accredited research ethics committee before it may be carried out.
q_1_5_fuente: Disposición ANMAT 7516/2025, Annex II (Section 2.3.1); Annex III (Section 2.1); Annex III (Appendix C, Section C.2.1(f)).
q_1_6_directa: Yes. Research Ethics Committees (RECs) must be accredited by a central jurisdictional accreditation body in order to evaluate clinical pharmacology studies.
q_1_6_ampliada: Current regulations require the REC to be accredited in order to act. If the jurisdiction where the study is conducted does not have a central accreditation body, the protocol must be evaluated by an accredited REC from another jurisdiction.
q_1_6_fuente: Disposición ANMAT 7516/2025, Annex II, Section 1.2.1.
q_1_7_directa: Yes. The National Registry of Health Research (RENIS) exists, along with jurisdictional registries, where information on RECs is systematized.
q_1_7_ampliada: Resolución 1480/2011 sets out the guidelines for registering and overseeing Research Ethics Committees (RECs) to provide public assurance of the process. Due to Argentina's federal organization, responsibility for registering and overseeing RECs lies with the authorities of each province. At the national level, RENIS systematizes this information, complementing local registries with centralized oversight for regulatory studies.
q_1_7_fuente: Resolución 1480/2011 del Ministerio de Salud, Articles 2 and 5.
q_1_8_directa: Yes. ANMAT must grant prior authorization before the start of all clinical pharmacology studies conducted for marketing-authorization purposes (except Phase IV studies).
q_1_8_ampliada: The scope of application includes Phase I, II, and III studies, as well as protocol phase variations conducted for marketing-authorization purposes. It also covers studies of already-registered medicines evaluating, for marketing-authorization purposes, a new indication, a new strength (if higher than the one already registered), a new dosage regimen, a new pharmaceutical form, or any other post-registration change requiring clinical trial data. Bioequivalence and bioavailability studies, non-interventional studies, and studies not conducted for marketing-authorization purposes are excluded.
q_1_8_fuente: Disposición ANMAT 7516/2025 (Article 4).
q_2_1_directa: Yes. The sponsor is the legal entity responsible for the initiation, management, and financing of a clinical trial.
q_2_1_ampliada: The sponsor assumes responsibility for the initiation, management, and financing of a clinical study. Throughout the entire life cycle of the trial, the sponsor is responsible for protecting participants' rights, safety, and well-being, as well as for the reliability of the results. If an independent investigator assumes full responsibility, that investigator takes on the role of sponsor.
q_2_1_fuente: Disposición ANMAT 7516/2025, Glossary (Sponsor); Annex VI (Sponsor); ICH E6(R3) Guideline (Section 3).
q_2_2_directa: Yes, the conduct of the study in Argentina and the submission to ANMAT, whether by the sponsor or its representative, must be carried out by a firm legally established in the country.
q_2_2_ampliada: This entity must be a firm legally established in Argentina and must have a quality assurance and quality control system in place. If the sponsor is a foreign firm that delegates the conduct and performance of the study to a Contract Research Organization (CRO), the CRO becomes subject to the regulations in its capacity as representative, assuming administrative, regulatory-offense, and civil liability.
q_2_2_fuente: Disposición ANMAT 7516/2025, Annex II (Sections 3.6.1 and 3.6.3).
q_2_3_directa: Yes. The sponsor must be a legal entity established in the country or act through a local representative, must have a quality assurance and quality control system in place, and must ensure that sufficient resources are available to carry out the trial.
q_2_3_ampliada: The sponsor must ensure compliance with GCP, local regulations, and contractual agreements, retaining ultimate responsibility for protecting participants' rights and for the reliability of the data. The financial aspects of the trial must be documented in an agreement with the investigator/institution.
q_2_3_fuente: Disposición ANMAT 7516/2025, Annex II (Section 3.6.1); ICH E6(R3) Guideline (Sections 3.2, 3.5, and 3.6.6).
q_2_4_directa: Yes. The CRO must be a firm legally established in the country, must assume the sponsor's administrative, regulatory-offense, and civil liability, and the transferred tasks must be set out in a written agreement signed by the parties.
q_2_4_ampliada: Although the sponsor may transfer functions to the CRO, it retains ultimate legal responsibility for participant care and for the quality and integrity of the trial data. The agreement between the parties must clearly define roles and responsibilities, and any functions not specified in the agreement must be carried out by the sponsor.
q_2_4_fuente: Disposición ANMAT 7516/2025, Annex II (Sections 3.6.2, 3.6.3, and 3.6.4).
q_2_5_directa: Yes. Sites must hold a valid health-operating license, adequate infrastructure for the study population and phase, and authorization from the institution's highest authority.
q_2_5_ampliada: Site selection requires verifying that the site has the facilities, equipment, and supplies necessary for the study, including emergency-care arrangements if the study is outpatient. For Phase I studies, sites are specifically required to be level 2 or 3 inpatient institutions, registered in the federal registry (REFES), with immediate access to intensive care.
q_2_5_fuente: Disposición ANMAT 7516/2025, Annex II, Section 2.3.3, and Annex V, Section 1.1.
q_2_6_directa: Yes. A professional degree, a valid professional license, a curriculum vitae demonstrating experience in the study phase, and certified training in Good Clinical Practice and local regulations are required.
q_2_6_ampliada: The Principal Investigator (PI) must demonstrate competence through specific training and experience (for example, prior Phase I/II experience for Phase I studies). In addition, the PI must submit a signed commitment to comply with the protocol and ethical standards, and must not have conflicts of interest that could affect the research.
q_2_6_fuente: Disposición ANMAT 7516/2025, Annex III, Appendix C, Section C.2.1.
q_2_7_directa: Yes. The sponsor must obtain insurance issued in the country to guarantee coverage for medical care and compensation to participants in the event of harm, injury, or damage arising from the study.
q_2_7_ampliada: The insurance policy must be taken out in the country to guarantee coverage for risks or potential harm. The sponsor commits to ensuring that the participant receives the necessary and immediate medical care and treatment in the event of harm related to the study medication or procedures. The Informed Consent Form must include specific language detailing this coverage, stating that signing the document does not imply a waiver of the participant's legal rights.
q_2_7_fuente: Disposición ANMAT 7516/2025, Annex II (Section 3.14.2); Annex II (Appendix D, Section D.3.2(o)); Annex II (Section 3.14.1).
q_3_1_directa: Yes. The essential content for the authorization application includes the completed Formulario EFCA 1, the study protocol, the Investigational Product Monograph (MPI), a sworn statement of GMP compliance, the import/export application for materials and samples, and proof of fee payment.
q_3_1_ampliada: Proof of the delegation of functions to the sponsor's representative (if applicable) and evidence that the study is being conducted in countries with high sanitary surveillance standards must also be attached. For the MPI, in studies involving already-registered products, the summary of product characteristics or the package insert is accepted.
q_3_1_fuente: Disposición ANMAT 7516/2025, Annex III (Appendix A); Annex III (Appendix A, Section A.1(b), (c), (d), and (e)).
q_3_2_directa: Yes. The submission process for a Clinical Pharmacology Study (EFCA) authorization application is electronic and must be carried out through the Remote Filing System (TAD) or the Clinical Trial Management System (SIGEC).
q_3_2_ampliada: Regulations require that submissions be made electronically through the authorized official platforms, currently the Remote Filing System (TAD) or the Clinical Trial Management System (SIGEC). This imposes mandatory digitalization on all sponsors, who must have authorized user accounts to manage the upload of required documentation, such as the protocol, the product monograph, and proof of fee payment.
q_3_2_fuente: Disposición ANMAT 7516/2025, Annex III (Section 2).
q_3_3_directa: The maximum time frame for protocol evaluation by the technical areas varies depending on the study classification: 20 business days for studies with low regulatory risk and special studies (extensions, orphan studies, etc.), and 35 business days for studies with non-low risk.
q_3_3_ampliada: An additional 10 business days are added to these time frames for the administrative areas. The Directorate of Clinical Research carries out an initial review of the documentation within 2 administrative business days, and if the documentation is inaccurate or incomplete, the application may be denied. The time frame is interrupted if the sponsor submits an amendment or if ANMAT communicates substantiated objections (the sponsor has 15 business days to respond to the objections).
q_3_3_fuente: Disposición ANMAT 7516/2025; Annex III (Sections 1.2.4 and 1.2.5); Annex III (Sections 1.4 and 1.6).
q_3_4_directa: Yes, the authorization application for clinical pharmacology studies requires payment of a fee, and proof of payment is a mandatory document. The exact amount must be verified against the current fee schedule published by ANMAT at the time of submission.
q_3_4_ampliada: Payment of the fee is a requirement for initiating the application procedure. Fee amounts are updated on a dedicated section of ANMAT's website (https://www.argentina.gob.ar/anmat/regulados/aranceles).
q_3_4_fuente: Disposición ANMAT 7516/2025, Annex III (Appendix A); ANMAT Fee Schedule; Decreto 1490/1992 (Article 8, item m).
q_3_5_directa: Yes, proof of registration in the National Registry of Health Research (RENIS) must be submitted before the first participant is enrolled in the study.
q_3_5_ampliada: By adopting ICH GCP principles, ANMAT promotes clinical trial transparency, including timely registration in recognized, publicly accessible databases. RENIS, created by Resolución 1480/2011, aims to systematize and consolidate information on human health research. In addition, each local jurisdiction may create its own registries (for example, the PRIISA.BA platform of the City of Buenos Aires).
q_3_5_fuente: Disposición ANMAT 7516/2025, Annex III (Section 5.6.1); ICH E6(R3) Guideline (Principle 9.6); Resolución 1480/2011 del Ministerio de Salud (Article 2).
q_3_6_directa: Yes, ANMAT uses the reliance mechanism and requires evidence that the study is being conducted in countries with high sanitary surveillance standards or regulatory convergence.
q_3_6_ampliada: Reliance is a principle that allows ANMAT to give significant weight to evaluations carried out by another regulatory authority or trusted institution, while retaining independence and responsibility for the final decision. For classification as a low regulatory-risk study, it is considered a requirement that the study be approved and ongoing in countries with high sanitary surveillance standards or in countries recognized by PAHO/WHO as a Reference National Regulatory Authority. Evidence of this may be demonstrated through documents such as proof of an FDA IND application or a European Union EudraCT number.
q_3_6_fuente: Disposición ANMAT 7516/2025 (Article 5(p)); Annex VI (Reliance); Annex III (Section 1.2.1); Annex III (Appendix A).
q_3_7_directa: The process is sequential and requires general protocol authorization from ANMAT, followed by the authorization or notification of each individual investigator/site before activities begin at the site.
q_3_7_ampliada:
The sequence of steps is as follows:

1. Regulatory preparation and prior ethical review (Sponsor/Investigator): The sponsor must request a pre-submission meeting with ANMAT, which is mandatory for Phase 1 studies, advanced therapies, innovative investigational products, and local developments (Annex III, 1.8.1). The Principal Investigator (PI) initiates the evaluation of the protocol and the Informed Consent Form (ICF) before an accredited Research Ethics Committee (IRB/IEC), and verifies the site's operating license.

2. Protocol authorization application (Sponsor): The sponsor submits the study authorization application to ANMAT (Formulario EFCA 1 and technical documentation). ANMAT verifies the documentation within 2 business days and evaluates the study within 20 business days (low regulatory risk) or 35 business days (all other studies), plus an additional 10 administrative business days in each case.

3. General study authorization (ANMAT): ANMAT issues the Disposición granting general protocol authorization.

4. Authorization or notification of investigators and sites (Sponsor/ANMAT): After study authorization, the sponsor submits the documentation for each investigator and site (Formulario EFCA 2), for which the IRB/IEC approval opinion is an indispensable requirement. The applicable pathway depends on the jurisdiction's ethical accreditation status:
– Evaluation and approval by ANMAT (15 administrative business days): when sites are located in jurisdictions that do not have a central IRB/IEC accreditation body; when the investigational product falls into highly innovative categories, regardless of phase; or when ANMAT determines that, in addition to IRB/IEC evaluation, its own authorization is required.
– Notification (5 administrative business days): when the jurisdiction has a central IRB/IEC accreditation body and ANMAT authorization is not required; in that case, ANMAT issues an expedited acknowledgment of receipt.

5. Start of study activities (Investigator/Sponsor): The investigator must have documented approval from both ANMAT and the IRB/IEC before starting activities. The sponsor must submit proof of RENIS registration before enrolling the first participant (Annex III, 5.6.1).
q_3_7_fuente: Disposición ANMAT 7516/2025, Annex III (Sections 1.8, 1.2.4, 1.2.5, 1.4, 2.1, 2.3, 2.4, and 5.6.1); Annex II (Section 2.3.1); Annex III (Appendix C).
q_4_1_directa: Labeling of the Investigational Product (IP) must be in Spanish and must include identification of the study, sponsor, and investigator, the product name or code, the dosage/strength, and the batch number.
q_4_1_ampliada: The label or secondary packaging must include the warnings "for clinical research use only" and "keep out of reach of children" (where applicable). It must also show the name, address, and telephone number of the contact person for product information and emergency unblinding, storage conditions, and the expiry date (month/year). If the expiry date is updated, an additional label must be affixed showing the batch number and both the previous and new dates, and this process must be documented.
q_4_1_fuente: Annex II (Sections 3.15.1, 3.15.2, and 3.15.3) of Disposición ANMAT 7516/2025.
q_4_2_directa: Yes, an original sworn statement signed by the sponsor must be submitted, certifying that the manufacturing, handling, and storage of the IP are carried out in accordance with applicable Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) principles.
q_4_2_ampliada: The sworn statement must be accompanied by the GMP certificate or an equivalent document. For locally developed investigational products, documentation issued by ANMAT certifying GMP compliance under current regulations must be attached. In addition, the ICH E6(R3) Guideline requires that investigational products be manufactured in accordance with applicable GMP standards.
q_4_2_fuente: Annex III (Appendix A, Section A.1(e)) of Disposición ANMAT 7516/2025; ICH E6(R3) Guideline (Principle 11.1).
q_4_3_directa: Yes, ANMAT's authorization of the study includes authorization for the import or export of study materials, since the import/export application is a requirement of the initial submission.
q_4_3_ampliada: ANMAT, through the Directorate of Clinical Research and Drug Registry Management, has the authority to intervene, through the Foreign Trade office, to authorize or reject the import or export of materials. The quantities of drugs and biological samples requested must be justified by the protocol schedule, their intended use, and the expected number of participants in the country.
q_4_3_fuente: Disposición ANMAT 7516/2025 (Article 5(e)); Annex III (Appendix A, Section A.1(f)).
q_5_1_directa: Yes. The sponsor must report all Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reactions (RAMSIS/SUSAR) occurring in Argentina through ANMAT's electronic Pharmacovigilance reporting system. Safety information originating from other countries need only be reported if it implies a change in the benefit-risk profile, within ten (10) administrative business days.
q_5_1_ampliada: Reports must be submitted individually and follow the ICH E2A Guideline. The sponsor must promptly notify investigators of findings that could affect safety, including an updated assessment of the benefit-risk balance. In blinded studies, if the sponsor receives a report of an unexpected serious adverse event (SAE), the blind must be broken in accordance with the ICH E2A guidelines.
q_5_1_fuente: Annex III (Sections 5.1.2, 5.1.4, and 5.1.5) of Disposición ANMAT 7516/2025.
q_5_2_directa: Yes, an annual Development Safety Update Report (DSUR) must be submitted, with a data-lock point no later than 90 days after the close of the reporting period.
q_5_2_ampliada: The DSUR submission must assess the safety of the investigational medicine based on all available information. If, during the course of the trials, an increase in risks relative to observed benefits is detected (for example, through Data Monitoring Committee (DMC) reports), the sponsor must inform ANMAT of the finding within ten (10) administrative business days.
q_5_2_fuente: Annex III (Sections 5.2.1 and 5.2.2); Annex III (Appendix F, Section F.1.1) of Disposición ANMAT 7516/2025.
q_5_3_directa: Yes, the sponsor must submit a periodic report for each investigator at least once a year, counted from the date of ANMAT authorization.
q_5_3_ampliada: The periodic report must be signed and dated by the investigator and the sponsor's representative and must be submitted within a maximum of 60 calendar days after the close of the reporting period. The investigator must inform the IRB/IEC of the study's progress at least once a year.
q_5_3_fuente: Annex III (Sections 5.4.1 and 5.4.3); Annex II (Section 2.4.1) of Disposición ANMAT 7516/2025.
q_5_4_directa: Yes. Substantial amendments to the protocol (changes that affect the safety, physical or mental integrity of participants, or the validity of the data) require the prior approval of the IRB/IEC and of ANMAT before they may be implemented.
q_5_4_ampliada: Only those changes necessary to eliminate an immediate risk to participants are exempt from prior approval. Administrative amendments need only be attached to the next periodic report. The time frame for evaluating amendments is 15 business days, subject to suspension in the event of objections or very high complexity.
q_5_4_fuente: Annex III (Sections 3.2, 3.4, and 3.6); Annex VI (Substantial Protocol Amendment) of Disposición ANMAT 7516/2025.
q_5_5_directa: Yes, at the end of the study, participants who need to continue treatment must have access to the intervention that proved beneficial, or to an alternative intervention or other appropriate benefit, approved by the IRB/IEC.
q_5_5_ampliada: This provision must be maintained for the period determined by the IRB/IEC, or until access to treatment is guaranteed by other means. ANMAT authorizes the import of the medication/treatment for post-trial access, and this authorization has an initial validity of twelve months from the date the procedure is approved.
q_5_5_fuente: Annex III (Sections 6.1 and 6.3) of Disposición ANMAT 7516/2025. Resolución 1480/2011 del Ministerio de Salud (P19).
q_6_1_directa: Yes. The applicable law is Ley 25.326 on the Protection of Personal Data.
q_6_1_ampliada: The sponsor is obligated to implement measures to protect the privacy and confidentiality of participants' personal information, in accordance with this law. Health-related information is considered sensitive data, which may only be collected and processed for reasons of general interest authorized by law, or for statistical or scientific purposes when data subjects cannot be identified.
q_6_1_fuente: Ley 25.326 de Protección de los Datos Personales (Articles 1, 2, and 7); Disposición ANMAT 7516/2025, Annex I, Section 4; Annex II (Section 3.16.1 and Section 4); Annex VI (Glossary).
q_6_2_directa: No. Vaccine trials must follow the guidelines set out in the general regulatory regime. However, Disposición 705/2005 establishes the Lineamientos para la Evaluación de Productos Biológicos: Vacunas y Hemoderivados (ANMAT-SG006/2014) [Guidelines for the Evaluation of Biological Products: Vaccines and Blood Products].
q_6_2_ampliada: Disposición 705/2005 sets out the requirements for submitting technical documentation, including preclinical-clinical information. For Novel (Innovative) Vaccines, original Phase I, II, and III clinical studies must be submitted. For Conventional Vaccines, however, original clinical studies are not essential, and efficacy documentation based on available international literature is sufficient.
q_6_2_fuente: Disposición ANMAT 705/2005 (Title and Recitals); Lineamientos para la Evaluación de Productos Biológicos: Vacunas y Hemoderivados (ANMAT) (Title, Introduction, Chapters IV and V).
q_6_3_directa: Yes, Resolución 2940/2020 del Ministerio de Salud approved the Guía para Biobancos de Muestras Biológicas de Origen Humano con Fines de Investigación [Guide for Biobanks of Human Biological Samples for Research Purposes].
q_6_3_ampliada: This Guide addresses the ethical and technical guidelines for the collection, processing, storage, and distribution of biological samples and associated data. The use of samples for future research (storage in biobanks) requires broad, advance informed consent, and the biobank must guarantee custody, quality, and respect for the donor's rights at all times.
q_6_3_fuente: Resolución 2940/2020 del Ministerio de Salud (Article 1 and Recitals); (Section B.2.2).
q_6_4_directa: Yes, specific guidelines or requirements exist for Phase I and First-in-Human studies, Decentralized Clinical Trials (DCTs), and public health emergencies (e.g., COVID-19).
q_6_4_ampliada: For first-in-human Phase I sites, prior ANMAT authorization through inspection is required, and sites must be level 2 or 3 inpatient healthcare facilities guaranteeing immediate access to an intensive care unit. The DCT guideline addresses the use of telemedicine, home visits, or direct shipment of the IP, requiring the sponsor to describe these operational aspects in the protocol along with a risk-benefit analysis. Resolución 908/2020 allows for expedited ethical review procedures in public health emergency contexts, prioritizing a rapid response to the pandemic.
q_6_4_fuente: Annex V (Title and Chapter 6) of Disposición ANMAT 7516/2025; Guía para Uso de Elementos Descentralizados en EFC (ANMAT) (Introduction and Chapter 1.a); Resolución 908/2020 del Ministerio de Salud (Article 1 and Recitals).
